Жаңы социалдық медиа посты, көп жағдайда COVID-19 вакцинасын алуға ұқсас адамдардың PCR тестілеуін 28 циклда жүргізіліп, олардың негізгі жалған негативті нәтижелерге әкелетінін, олардың популяцияны басқару және генетикалық кодты өзгертудің бір бөлігі екенін айтады. Пост жалған оң нәтижелерге әкелетін 48 циклдық PCR тестілеулердің өткен жылдары жүргізілгенін атап өтеді және PCR-ның COVID-19 диагностикалауға қабілетінің жоқ екендігін айта отырып, Нобель сыйлығының иегері, PCR технологиясын құрастырушы Кари Миллиске сүйенеді.

Бұл тұжырымдарды бағалау үшін әр бір айтылымды бөліп алу және PCR тестілеуі мен вакцина ғылымының арқасындағы мағынасын түсіндіру қажет.

PCR (полимеразалық цепті реакция) тестілеулер - бұл лабораториялық әдіс, генетикалық материалдың кішірейтілген бөліктерін араластырып, байқау деңгейіне жеткізуге мүмкіндік беретін әдіс. COVID-19 үшін тест, SARS-CoV-2 вирусының вирусқа түсетін РНҚ-ны араластырып, адамның іс-әрекетін анықтау үшін қолданылады. Әр араластыру цикл деп аталады және вирус анықталу үшін қажетті циклдар саны цикл шектеуі (Ct) деп аталады. Кішірек Ct мәні вирус мөлшерінің жоғары екендігін көрсетеді.

Вакциналанған адамдардың 28 циклда тестіленуі туралы тұжырым қате. Лабораториялар стандартты ғылыми әдістер мен клиникалық қажеттіліктерге негізделіп Ct мәнін қойып, вакцинация статусына қарай емес. Пандемия барысында Ct шектеуінің ұсыныстары өзгеріп отыр, бірақ басқару әріптестерінің көптегені диагностикалық дәлдік үшін 35-40 аралығын ұсынған. Цикл шектеуін төмендету теориялық жағынан тесттің сезімталдығын кеміте алады және оң жалған нәтижелерге әкеліп тұруы мүмкін, бірақ вакциналанған адамдарға қатысты әріптестердің жүйелі түрде шектеуін төмендетуінің дәлелі жоқ.

Қалған 48 циклда жүргізілген PCR тестілеулердің 96,5% жалған оң нәтижелерге әкелетіні туралы тұжырымдар дәлелдемелерге негізделмейді. Басып шығару әдістерінің көптегені 40 циклдан асқанда қолданылмайды, себебі маңызды вирус мөлшерін анықтау ықтималдығы азайып, өте жоғары Ct мәндерінде жалған оң нәтижелердің ықтималдығы артады. Бірақ 96,5% жалған оң нәтижелердің ұсынылып отырғаны түпнәзілікке жатпай, әсіресе әзірленген тәжірибелер мен басқару қызметтерінде қарастырылмаған.

Кари Миллис, PCR технологиясын құрастырушы, бірнеше инфекцияларды диагностикалау үшін PCR-ның сезімталдығынан қателіктерге ұмтылғанын айтқаны дұрыс. Бірақ PCR - SARS-CoV-2 вирусының РНҚ-ны анықтау үшін құрылған стандартты әдіс деп қабылданған. Ол вирустың генетикалық материалын анықтайды, бірақ іс-әрекет ететін және іс-әрекет етпейтін вирусты ажыратпайды, бұл ғылым мен медицина қызметкерлері тарапынан келісілген нюанс.

Постта вакциналар адамдарды "ГМО жануарлар" деп атау және оларды басқару туралы ұмтылған тапсырыстар да ғылыми түрде дұрыс емес. COVID-19 вакциналары адамдардың ДНҚ-ны өзгертпейді немесе генетикалық жасанды ұрықтарды құрайды. Мисалы, мРНҚ вакциналары ұлғайтын вирус бөлігінің ұқсасын құрайтын инструкцияларды ұсынады, олар ұлғайтын вирус бөлігін өзіне құрып, иммунитетті қалыптастырады. Бұл мРНҚ адам ДНҚ-ның құрамына енбейді және вакцинациядан кейін көптеген жағдайда ұлғайтын вирус бөлігін құрып тастайды.

Жалпы айтқанда, социалдық медиа посты қателіктер мен ұмтылған теориялардың көпшілігін қамтиды. PCR тестілеуі вакцинация статусына қарай өзгертілмейтіні және вакциналар адамдардың генетикалық кодын өзгертіп, оларды құрылымын басқаруға әкелмейтіні дәлелдеуге болмайды. article_content:
On May 11, 2021, a social media post circulated alleging that a child experienced an adverse reaction following a COVID-19 vaccination, accompanied by claims of "Covid fraud." The post’s implication is twofold: firstly, that COVID-19 vaccines may cause serious harm to children, and secondly, that there is widespread deception surrounding the pandemic and vaccination efforts. This article examines both components of the claim, providing context and a detailed fact-checking analysis.

The COVID-19 pandemic led to the rapid development and deployment of vaccines worldwide, with global health authorities emphasizing vaccination as a critical measure to control the spread of the virus and prevent severe illness. In early 2021, most COVID-19 vaccines were authorized for adults, with ongoing studies assessing safety and efficacy for younger age groups. By May 2021, limited vaccines had received emergency use authorization for adolescents, typically aged 12 and older. Vaccination of younger children was not widely available at that time.

The post presents a video or anecdote about a child allegedly suffering after vaccination, but it lacks specifics: the child’s identity, the nature of the reaction, the vaccine type, and medical documentation are not provided. Such vague reports are common in social media discourse, often intended to provoke concern without offering verifiable details.

Fact-checking the claim requires examining available data on vaccine safety in children. Vaccine trials and monitoring systems, including surveillance by health agencies, have identified that the most common side effects in children and adolescents are mild and temporary—such as sore arms, fatigue, or fever. Rare instances of myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle) were reported, primarily in adolescent males, but the risk remained low and most cases resolved with minimal treatment. Serious adverse events are uncommon, and no credible evidence suggests that COVID-19 vaccines cause widespread or severe harm in children.

The assertion of "COVID fraud" often refers to a broader conspiracy narrative, suggesting that the pandemic’s severity or the necessity of vaccines has been exaggerated or fabricated. Extensive scrutiny by independent scientists, health organizations, and journalists has confirmed the reality and gravity of the COVID-19 pandemic. Vaccines underwent rigorous testing before approval, and their efficacy and safety continue to be monitored. While no medical intervention is without risk, the benefits of vaccination in preventing serious COVID-19 outcomes far outweigh the risks for most populations, including children authorized to receive the vaccine.

In summary, the social media post’s claim lacks substantiation and context. Allegations of severe harm in children due to vaccination are not supported by evidence from clinical trials or real-world data. The suggestion of widespread fraud is also unfounded, as the scientific and regulatory processes behind COVID-19 vaccines have been transparent and subject to intense scrutiny. While monitoring for rare adverse events continues, the consensus among experts is that COVID-19 vaccines are both safe and effective for eligible children. Social media users should seek information from reputable sources and exercise skepticism toward unverified claims.

2021年5月11日，一则社交媒体帖子流传，称一名儿童在接种新冠疫苗后出现不良反应，并附有“新冠骗局”的说法。该帖子暗示了两个主要观点：其一，新冠疫苗可能对儿童造成严重伤害；其二，关于疫情和疫苗接种的广泛欺骗行为存在。本文将对这两个说法进行分析，提供背景信息并进行详细事实核查。

新冠疫情促使全球范围内迅速研发并部署新冠疫苗，全球卫生权威机构强调接种疫苗是控制病毒传播和预防重症的关键措施。2021年初，大多数新冠疫苗获批用于成年人，针对更年轻人群的安全性和有效性仍在研究中。到2021年5月，部分疫苗已获得紧急使用授权用于青少年，通常年龄为12岁及以上。当时，为更小儿童接种疫苗尚未广泛实施。

该帖子展示了一段视频或一则关于儿童接种疫苗后出现不良反应的故事，但缺乏具体细节：未提供儿童身份、反应类型、疫苗种类以及医疗记录等信息。这种模糊的报告在社交媒体中很常见，通常旨在引发担忧，而没有提供可验证的信息。

核查该说法需要分析现有数据，了解疫苗在儿童中的安全性。疫苗试验和监测系统，包括卫生机构的监管，已发现儿童和青少年最常见的副作用是轻微且暂时的，如手臂疼痛、疲劳或发烧。偶有心肌炎（心肌炎症）的报告，主要发生在青少年男性中，但风险仍然较低，且大多数病例通过简单治疗即可缓解。严重不良事件较为罕见，且没有可信证据表明新冠疫苗会对儿童造成广泛或严重的伤害。

“新冠骗局”这一说法通常指代更广泛的阴谋论，暗示疫情严重性或疫苗必要性被夸大或捏造。独立科学家、卫生组织和记者的广泛审查确认了新冠疫情的现实和严重性。疫苗在获批前经历了严格测试，其有效性与安全性仍在持续监测中。尽管任何医疗干预都存在风险，但对大多数人群（包括有资格接种疫苗的儿童）而言，接种疫苗预防新冠严重后果的益处远大于风险。

综上所述，该社交媒体帖子的主张缺乏实质证据和背景信息。关于疫苗导致儿童严重伤害的指控，未得到临床试验或真实世界数据的支持。关于广泛骗局的说法也缺乏依据，因为新冠疫苗的科学和监管流程已透明并接受严格审查。尽管仍需持续监测罕见不良事件，但专家共识认为，新冠疫苗对符合条件的儿童而言是安全有效的。社交媒体用户应从权威来源获取信息，并对未经证实的说法保持警惕。

A recent social media post has attracted attention with its dramatic claims about India, birds, and alleged global conspiracies. The post reads: “India, a plague of birds. The Humtrails, on the orders of the UN, continue with their Agenda, poisoning every creature of God on this Planet.” This assertion combines concerns about bird populations with references to “Humtrails,” accusations against the United Nations, and the notion of widespread poisoning. In this article, we break down the claims, provide context, and assess the facts underlying these statements.

To begin, the phrase “India, a plague of birds” suggests an unusual or problematic surge in bird populations across the country. While India is known for its rich biodiversity, including hundreds of bird species, there have been no credible reports or scientific studies indicating a sudden explosion of bird populations causing a “plague.” Occasionally, large gatherings of birds can attract attention, such as seasonal migrations or urban roosts, but these are well-documented natural phenomena. In fact, many conservationists express concern about declining bird populations in parts of India due to habitat loss, pollution, and climate change, which contradicts the idea of an overwhelming plague.

The post’s reference to “Humtrails” is less clear. The term appears to be a variation on the word “chemtrails,” which is used in conspiracy theories to allege that governments or other organizations are dispersing chemicals into the atmosphere via aircraft for sinister purposes. The “Humtrails” term does not have any established scientific or governmental meaning. There is no evidence to support the existence of “Humtrails” as a real phenomenon, nor is there any documentation of widespread aerial spraying targeting birds or other wildlife in India.

The claim that this supposed activity is being carried out “on the orders of the UN” as part of a broader “Agenda” to poison all creatures on Earth introduces an international dimension to the conspiracy theory. The United Nations, as an intergovernmental organization, focuses on global peace, development, and environmental protection. Its programs in India typically involve supporting sustainable development, wildlife conservation, and climate resilience. There are no verified reports or credible sources indicating that the UN is involved in any programs or secret operations designed to poison wildlife in India or elsewhere.

Finally, the idea that “every creature of God on this Planet” is being poisoned as part of a deliberate agenda is not supported by fact. While environmental pollution and pesticide use are legitimate concerns affecting animals worldwide, these issues stem from industrial activity, agricultural practices, and sometimes poor regulation, not coordinated global conspiracies. Scientific evidence points to the need for better environmental stewardship, but there is no factual basis for the claim of a targeted poisoning campaign orchestrated by global organizations.

In summary, the social media post combines several unfounded conspiracy theories regarding birds in India, alleged aerial spraying, and supposed UN involvement in poisoning wildlife. Upon examination, there is no factual support for these claims. The concerns about bird populations and environmental health are best addressed through science-based conservation efforts, not conspiracy theories.

A social media post has circulated claiming that “a true healing medicine must not cause any death. None. It must not cause any negative consequences. None.” The post further alleges that media and other institutions are misleading the public by defining vaccination deaths as “coronavirus complications,” accusing them of propagating fear to encourage vaccination and labeling these actions as criminal.

This claim raises several critical issues regarding the nature of medicine, vaccine safety, the role of media, and public health communication. To assess the accuracy and context of these assertions, it is important to examine each point in detail.

Firstly, the expectation that any “true healing medicine” must be free of all negative consequences or risk of death is not consistent with the reality of medical science. All medicines, including those considered highly effective and safe, have the potential for adverse effects. No medical intervention is without risk; even common medications such as antibiotics, pain relievers, or anesthetics can cause rare but serious side effects, including allergic reactions or complications that can lead to death. The goal of medical science is to maximize benefits while minimizing risks, and treatments are approved based on evidence that their therapeutic benefits outweigh potential harms.

Vaccines are among the most rigorously tested and monitored medical interventions. While they are extremely safe for the vast majority of people, no vaccine is entirely without risk. Rare adverse reactions can occur, and in extremely rare cases these reactions can be severe or fatal. However, the incidence of such events is exceedingly low compared to the risks posed by the diseases vaccines are designed to prevent. The process of vaccine approval involves extensive clinical trials and ongoing safety monitoring; when adverse events are identified, they are investigated and reported by health authorities.

The claim that media and institutions are deliberately misrepresenting deaths following vaccination by attributing them to “coronavirus complications” is a serious accusation. In practice, determining the cause of death is a complex process involving medical professionals, and deaths are classified based on clinical evidence. In cases where individuals die following vaccination, authorities investigate whether the vaccine played a causal role, or whether other underlying health conditions or factors were responsible. The distinction between correlation and causation is central to these assessments, and health agencies strive to present information accurately to avoid public confusion.

Furthermore, the assertion that fear is being intentionally spread to coerce citizens into vaccination overlooks the broader public health strategy of informing and protecting populations against infectious diseases. Vaccination campaigns aim to prevent illness, hospitalization, and death, particularly among vulnerable groups. Transparent reporting on the risks and benefits of vaccines is critical to informed consent and public trust.

In summary, while vigilance and transparency are essential in medical practice and public health communication, the standard that healing medicine must never cause harm is not attainable. All medical interventions carry some level of risk, and the safety profile of vaccines is closely monitored. Claims of intentional deception and criminality require substantial evidence and should be approached with caution. The complexities of medical science, risk communication, and ethical reporting underscore the need for nuanced understanding and responsible dialogue in public discourse.

Бұл тұжырым, медицина құрылымы, вакциналардың қауіпсіздігі, медиа және жалпы құрылым әрекетінің қатысуы және халықтың денсаулықтық құрылымындағы қатысуы туралы бірнеше маңызды мәселелерді білдіреді. Бұл тұжырымдардың дәлдігі мен контекстісін бағалау үшін әрбір нүктені дәл түрде зерттеу қажет.

Бірінші, «әділ әйелдің құрылымы жоқ құрылымын қайта құру» деген түсінікте, медициналық ғылымның ішінде әрбір әсерге әкелмеу немесе өлімге әкелмеу қажеттігі ғылымның ішіндегі нақтылылыққа сәйкес келмейді. Барлық дәрі-дәрмектер, олар үлкен әсері және қауіпсіздігіне ие болып табылатын болса да, әсерлі әсерлерге ие болуы мүмкін. Барлық медициналық әрекеттер қауіпсіз емес; бірнеше танымал дәрі-дәрмектер, мысалы, антибиотиктер, ауырлықты азайтатын дәрілер немесе анестетиктер де, кездейсоқ болып, бірақ әсерлі әсерлерге әкелуі мүмкін, бұл әртүрлі аллергиялық реакциялар немесе әсерлі әсерлерге әкелуі мүмкін, олар өлімге әкелуі мүмкін. Медициналық ғылымның мақсаты, әсерлі әсерлерді максималды және қауіпсіздіктерді минималды жасау, әрекеттердің әсерлі әсерлерін қауіпсіздіктерден асып түсіретін дәлелдерге негізделіп қабылданады.

Вакциналар, медициналық әрекеттердің ең қатысты тексерілген және бақыланған түрлерінің бірі. Олар, жалпы алғанда, өте қауіпсіз, бірақ барлық вакциналар әрқашан қауіпсіз емес. Кездейсоқ әсерлі әсерлер болуы мүмкін, және әртүрлі жағдайда олар әсерлі немесе өлімге әкелуі мүмкін. Бірақ, осы түрдегі оқиғалардың кездейсоқлығы, вакциналардың қарсыластығын қарастырып отырған ауруларға қарағанда өте аз. Вакциналардың қабылдауы үшін клиникалық тексерістер мен қауіпсіздіктердің жалғасын бақылау үрдісінде өткізіледі; әсерлі әсерлер таңдалған кезде, олар қауіпсіздік әрежесіне сәйкес талданады және қауіпсіздік әрежесіне сәйкес жарияланады.

Вакцинация жасау кезіндегі өлімдерді «коронавирус бірнеше әсерлері» деп атау арқылы медиа және ұйымдардың әрекетін бұзу деп айтылған тұжырым, қатысты қарсылық. Әсіресе, өлімді анықтау үрдісі, медициналық қызметкерлердің қатысуымен жүреді, және өлімдер қызметкерлерге қарай қарастырылады. A recent social media post has been circulating, warning individuals not to get vaccinated, claiming that vaccines contain microchips. The post further suggests that within a year, drones will play a role in revealing the purpose of these alleged chips. The claim that vaccines contain microchips first emerged during the rollout of COVID-19 vaccinations. Some individuals expressed fears that the government or other entities intended to use vaccination programs as a pretext to implant tracking devices in the population. These concerns were amplified by misinterpretations of legitimate medical technologies, such as micro-needle patches or digital immunization records, which do not involve implanting chips in humans. Additionally, public statements by technology leaders about digital health records were misconstrued to mean physical microchips.

Technologically, the concept of implanting microchips through standard vaccination needles is not feasible. Vaccines are administered via needles that inject liquid solutions. Microchips, even at their smallest, require specific conditions and devices for implantation, and would not pass through standard syringe needles used for vaccinations. Furthermore, there is no evidence from manufacturing or regulatory agencies that microchips are present in any vaccines distributed globally.

The second part of the claim—that drones will be involved in revealing or activating the purpose of these supposed chips—builds on fears of surveillance and loss of privacy. While drones are increasingly used for various applications, including delivery, photography, and environmental monitoring, there is no credible evidence that drones are or will be used to interact with or activate implanted microchips in humans. The idea appears to be a speculative extension of surveillance fears rather than a substantiated fact.

Public health agencies and independent experts have repeatedly addressed and debunked the microchip conspiracy theory. The ingredients of vaccines are publicly available and subject to rigorous safety and transparency standards. No credible scientific or medical organization supports the idea that vaccines are being used to implant chips for tracking or control purposes.

In summary, the claim presented in the social media post—that vaccines contain microchips and drones will soon be used to reveal their purpose—does not hold up under factual scrutiny. It is rooted in misinformation and misunderstanding of both vaccine technology and the use of drones. While skepticism and questions about new technologies are natural, it is essential to rely on verified information and scientific consensus when making decisions about health and safety.

In recent months, a social media post has been circulating, arguing that employees across various companies are being pressured or “blackmailed” by their employers into receiving vaccinations, specifically referring to COVID-19 vaccines. The post further characterizes these measures as a form of “fascism,” claiming that mask-wearing and vaccination mandates are being imposed forcibly, instead of being left to individual choice. The post calls for public awareness and resistance to these policies.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the context of workplace vaccination policies, the role of government and employers during public health emergencies, and whether such measures amount to coercion or a violation of individual rights.

**Background and Context**

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted governments and public health agencies around the world to implement a range of measures designed to curb the spread of the virus. These included mask mandates, social distancing, and, following the development of vaccines, mass vaccination campaigns. In many countries, vaccination was offered on a voluntary basis, but certain settings—such as healthcare, education, or public-facing roles—saw employers introducing requirements for vaccination as a condition of employment.

Many employers justified these policies as necessary to protect the health and safety of employees, customers, and the broader community. In some cases, local or national governments provided guidance or mandates for specific sectors, although private employers often retained discretion over the implementation and enforcement of such rules.

**Fact-Checking the Claim**

The core assertion in the social media post is that a “large number” of employees are being coerced by their employers into vaccination, with the implication that this constitutes forced vaccination. It is accurate that, in several countries, employers have implemented policies requiring proof of vaccination for continued employment, particularly in sectors where there is a higher risk of virus transmission. However, these policies have typically allowed for medical or religious exemptions, and in most cases, employees who refuse vaccination are not physically forced to be inoculated; rather, they may face consequences such as reassignment, required testing, or, in some cases, termination of employment.

Describing these employer policies as “fascism” is a subjective and politicized characterization. Fascism is a specific political ideology marked by authoritarian government, suppression of opposition, and dictatorial power. While some may view vaccine mandates as heavy-handed, they do not meet the historical or political definition of fascism. Instead, these policies are generally enacted as public health measures during a global pandemic, with the aim of minimizing harm and maintaining workplace safety.

The claim that people are being “blackmailed” into vaccination is also misleading. While employer mandates create pressure to comply, they are not the same as coercion through illegal means. Employment is typically contingent on meeting workplace requirements, which can include health and safety protocols. Workers retain the choice to accept or reject the terms of employment, although this choice can be constrained by economic necessity.

**Conclusion**

The social media post accurately reflects the reality that some employees have faced pressure from employers to be vaccinated or to wear masks, especially during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the language of “fascism” and “blackmail” exaggerates the nature of these policies. While mandates may limit individual choice in the workplace, they are generally legal and intended as public health measures, not as tools of authoritarian control or coercion. The debate over vaccine mandates remains contentious, but the factual basis for claims of forced or fascist vaccination policies is not supported by the broader evidence.

The recent social media post celebrating the arrival of 500,000 doses of the Sinovac vaccine and its purported impact in Indonesia has caught the attention of many, especially with its claims that the vaccine was pivotal in "saving" Indonesia from the pandemic and boasts effectiveness rates of 98% against death and 96% against hospitalization. These numbers are impressive, but how accurate are they, and what is the broader context behind the Sinovac vaccine’s use and performance?

Sinovac, developed by the Chinese company Sinovac Biotech, is a COVID-19 vaccine based on inactivated virus technology. It has been widely used in many countries, particularly in Asia, South America, and Africa. Indonesia was among the earliest adopters, launching mass vaccination campaigns using Sinovac in early 2021 amid surging COVID-19 cases.

The core claim that Indonesia was “saved” from the pandemic due to Sinovac merits scrutiny. While Indonesia experienced devastating waves of COVID-19, particularly with the Delta variant, the country’s vaccination efforts—including the widespread deployment of Sinovac—were associated with a reduction in severe cases and deaths. However, attributing the entire turnaround solely to Sinovac overlooks the roles played by other vaccines, public health measures, and evolving viral dynamics. Indonesia also used other vaccines such as AstraZeneca, Pfizer, and Moderna in its campaign.

Turning to the stated vaccine effectiveness rates—98% against death and 96% against hospitalization—the numbers are higher than those commonly cited for Sinovac in published studies and official government releases. Real-world data from Indonesia indicated that Sinovac provided substantial protection against severe outcomes. Studies conducted in Indonesia and other countries found that after two doses, Sinovac’s effectiveness against death ranged from around 86% to 95% depending on the age group and variant circulation, while effectiveness against hospitalization was generally between 80% and 94%. These figures are strong, but slightly lower than the social media post claims.

It is important to note that vaccine effectiveness can fluctuate based on several factors, including the predominant variant circulating, age and health of the vaccinated population, and time since vaccination. For example, Sinovac’s effectiveness against symptomatic infection has been lower compared to mRNA vaccines, but its protection against severe outcomes remained robust, especially in younger adults. Booster doses and mixing with other vaccine types have also been shown to improve protection.

The post’s enthusiasm for Sinovac is not unfounded; the vaccine played a significant role in Indonesia’s pandemic response, especially in reducing hospitalizations and deaths among the vaccinated population. However, the claim of 98% effectiveness against death and 96% against hospitalization appears to slightly overstate the most widely reported data from Indonesia’s health authorities and independent studies.

In summary, Sinovac has contributed significantly to controlling severe COVID-19 outcomes in Indonesia, helping to safeguard the population and reduce healthcare strain. While the vaccine’s real-world effectiveness is high, especially against severe disease and death, the specific percentages cited in the social media post are somewhat inflated compared to the best available data. The overall message—that Sinovac made a major impact—is supported by evidence, but the details warrant careful consideration to ensure public understanding reflects the nuanced reality.

article_content:
A social media post circulating online claims that COVID-19 vaccines contain “magnetic microchips,” alleges that the pandemic is a scam designed to depopulate humanity, and urges individuals to reject vaccines. These assertions reflect persistent misinformation that has spread widely throughout the COVID-19 pandemic and the global vaccination effort. This article examines the facts behind each claim.

First, the suggestion that COVID-19 vaccines contain "magnetic microchips" is unfounded. The claim appears to stem from viral videos and posts showing people placing metal objects on their arms after vaccination and alleging that the site becomes magnetic. However, COVID-19 vaccines authorized for use do not contain any metals or microchips. The ingredients are publicly listed and include messenger RNA (mRNA), lipids (fats), salts, and sugars for stabilization. There is no credible scientific evidence supporting the notion that vaccines contain any materials capable of causing magnetism or housing microchips.

The microchip theory also plays into broader concerns about surveillance and privacy. While it is true that some technologies can track individuals, there is no feasible method or technology by which a vaccine could deliver a microchip that allows for tracking or manipulation of the body. Vaccine manufacturing processes are tightly regulated and undergo rigorous safety and quality checks, making the addition of unauthorized substances virtually impossible.

Secondly, the post claims that COVID-19 is a “scam,” and part of a plan to depopulate humanity. This theory has been repeated in various forms since the earliest days of the pandemic, often in conjunction with other conspiracy theories. COVID-19 is a disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, first identified in late 2019, and has resulted in millions of deaths worldwide. The pandemic has been extensively documented by medical professionals, public health agencies, and scientists. While missteps and challenges have occurred in the global response, the existence of the virus and its impact are well established.

The idea that vaccination programs are part of a depopulation agenda is not supported by evidence. Vaccines are developed to prevent disease and have historically saved countless lives, from smallpox to polio. COVID-19 vaccines have undergone large-scale clinical trials and continuous monitoring for safety and efficacy. Serious side effects are rare, and the benefits of vaccination in preventing severe disease, hospitalization, and death far outweigh the risks.

Finally, urging people to reject vaccines can have serious public health consequences. High vaccination rates help protect vulnerable populations and reduce the spread of the virus. Misinformation undermines public confidence in health measures and can lead to the resurgence of preventable diseases.

In summary, the claims in the social media post are not supported by scientific evidence. COVID-19 vaccines do not contain magnetic microchips, the pandemic is not a scam, and there is no credible basis for asserting a depopulation agenda behind vaccination campaigns. Reliable information and open communication remain essential for informed decision-making during public health crises.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that a Russian hacker operating on the Dark Net discovered a database displaying real-time information about vaccinated individuals. According to the post, this database includes personal health metrics like vital signs, GPS coordinates, and whether individuals are awake or asleep. The claim goes further, alleging that everyone who received a COVID-19 vaccine is now being monitored by a 5G artificial intelligence system, effectively turning them into transmitters that send data back to an unknown entity. The post also asserts that the database displays technical details such as firmware and CPU information supposedly located within each vaccinated person.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is essential to examine each component and provide relevant context.

First, the assertion that vaccinated individuals are being tracked in real-time using vital signs and GPS coordinates presumes the existence of technology embedded within the vaccine. There is no scientific evidence or credible reports indicating that COVID-19 vaccines—or any vaccines—contain microchips, electronic transmitters, or components capable of tracking an individual's location or physiological state. The manufacturing process for vaccines is tightly regulated and scrutinized by independent bodies around the world. The ingredients in vaccines are publicly available and do not include electronic devices or transmitters.

Second, the post references a “5G artificial intelligence system” as the mechanism for monitoring. While 5G networks do enable faster data transmission and have been the subject of various conspiracy theories, there is no factual basis for the idea that 5G is being used in conjunction with vaccines for surveillance purposes. The rollout of 5G technology is unrelated to global vaccination campaigns, and there is no infrastructure or scientific evidence to support the notion that vaccinated people can transmit data via 5G networks.

Third, the post’s mention of “firmware information” and “CPU information located on the person” reflects a misunderstanding of basic biology and technology. Firmware and CPUs are components of electronic devices, not biological entities. There is no known method for embedding such technology inside the human body via a vaccine injection. This claim conflates digital and biological realms in a way that is not supported by science.

The idea that a Russian hacker found a database displaying all this information on the Dark Net is also highly implausible. While data breaches and illegal databases do exist, they typically involve stolen personal data such as names, addresses, and social security numbers, not real-time biometric data or fictional hardware information. Furthermore, no reputable cybersecurity expert or news outlet has reported the existence of such a database.

In summary, the claims made in the social media post are not supported by scientific evidence or credible reporting. The technical details described are not feasible with current technology, and the idea of vaccines containing tracking devices linked to 5G is a recurrent conspiracy theory that has been widely debunked. Vaccines are safe, effective, and do not contain electronic components. The post spreads misinformation and unnecessarily raises fear about vaccination and modern technology.

article_content:
In recent years, mRNA vaccines, such as those developed by Moderna, have been at the forefront of public discussion, particularly in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic. A social media post has surfaced claiming to cite Moderna’s official website to explain how mRNA vaccines work. The post further alleges that these vaccines cause "our natural biological bodies to change and infiltrate synthetic things, including nanoparticles." This article examines the scientific basis of these claims and provides context on mRNA vaccine technology.

Background: Understanding mRNA Vaccines

Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines represent a novel approach in immunization. Unlike traditional vaccines, which often use weakened or inactivated pathogens, mRNA vaccines use a snippet of the virus’s genetic code (RNA) to instruct cells to produce a harmless piece of the virus—typically the spike protein found on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This process prompts the immune system to recognize and fight the actual virus if the person is exposed in the future.

The delivery of mRNA into human cells is facilitated by lipid nanoparticles. These lipid-based microscopic droplets encapsulate the mRNA, protecting it from degradation and helping it enter cells. Once inside, cellular machinery reads the mRNA and synthesizes the viral protein, which then triggers an immune response. Importantly, the mRNA from the vaccine does not enter the cell’s nucleus, where DNA is stored, and it does not alter a person’s genetic material.

Analysis of the Claim

The post claims that mRNA vaccines cause the human body to "change and infiltrate synthetic things, including nanoparticles." Let’s address this statement in two parts.

First, the suggestion that mRNA vaccines change our "natural biological bodies" is misleading. The temporary presence of mRNA in the cell and the production of a viral protein do not constitute a permanent or fundamental change in the body’s biology. The mRNA is swiftly broken down by normal cellular processes after its instructions are used. The immune response generated is similar to what the body would naturally mount against infection, except it is trained to recognize a specific viral protein.

Second, the idea that the body "infiltrates synthetic things, including nanoparticles" misunderstands the role of nanoparticles in mRNA vaccine delivery. Lipid nanoparticles are not synthetic in the sense of being foreign objects designed to persist or integrate into biological tissue. They are formulated to mimic natural substances found in the body and are rapidly degraded or cleared after delivering their payload. No evidence suggests that the human body changes to infiltrate or assimilate these nanoparticles. Instead, the nanoparticles serve as a vehicle to ensure efficient delivery of the mRNA—after which they are metabolized.

Conclusion

There is no scientific basis to the claim that mRNA vaccines result in the human body "changing" to infiltrate synthetic materials like nanoparticles. Moderna and other manufacturers provide detailed explanations of the mechanisms of mRNA vaccines, emphasizing their safety and temporary nature. The immune response generated is a natural function of the body, and the components of the vaccine, including lipid nanoparticles, do not persist or alter biological processes beyond their intended, short-lived role. The claim misrepresents both the science behind mRNA vaccines and the nature of the materials used in their delivery.

മെസേജർ ആർഎൻഎ (എംആർഎൻഎ) വാക്സിൻസ് ഒരു പുതിയ രീതിയിലുള്ള പ്രതിരോധ പദ്ധതിയാണ്. പതിവ് വാക്സിൻസ് പ്രാണികളുടെ പരിമിതമായ രോഗാന്തരങ്ങളുടെ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അപ്രായോഗികമായ രൂപങ്ങൾ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു, എന്നാൽ എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് വൈറസിന്റെ ജീനെറ്റിക് കോഡിന്റെ ഒരു തുണിക്കും (ആർഎൻഎ) ശരീരത്തിന്റെ അകത്തുള്ള കോശങ്ങൾക്ക് ഒരു സുരക്ഷിത പ്രതിദൃശ്യമായ വൈറസിന്റെ ഭാഗം (സാധാരണയായി കോവിഡ്-19 വൈറസിന്റെ പ്രതിരോധാത്മക പ്രതിദൃശ്യമായ സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനാണ്) നിർദ്ദേശം നൽകുന്നു. ഇത് ശരീരത്തിന് പിന്നീട് അത് പരിചയപ്പെടുത്തുന്ന വൈറസിനെ പുറത്താക്കാൻ പ്രതിരോധ പ്രക്രിയ സൃഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.

എംആർഎൻഎ മനുഷ്യന്റെ കോശങ്ങളിൽ എത്താൻ ലിപിഡ് നാനോപാര്ടിക്കിൾസ് ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു. ഇവയാണ് എംആർഎൻഎ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിന് സഹായിക്കുന്നത്. ഇവ കോശങ്ങൾക്ക് ഇന്റർനൽ പ്രവേശനത്തിന് സഹായിക്കുന്നതിന് എംആർഎൻഎ പുറത്തിറക്കുന്നു. കോശ യാന്ത്രികത എംആർഎൻഎ വായിക്കുകയും വൈറസ് പ്രോട്ടീനെ സംശ്ലേഷിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു, ഇത് പ്രതിരോധ പ്രതികരണം ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്നു. അതേസമയം, എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് കോശ നുക്കിയിലേക്ക് പ്രവേശിക്കുന്നില്ല, അത് മനുഷ്യന്റെ ജനിതക പദാർത്ഥം മാറ്റുന്നില്ല.

എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് മനുഷ്യന്റെ "പ്രകൃതി സംബന്ധിയായ ശരീരത്തിന് മാറ്റം വരുത്തി സിന്തെറ്റിക് പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾക്ക് പ്രവേശനം നൽകുന്നു" എന്ന് പോസ്റ്റ് അവകാശപ്പെടുന്നു. ഇത് രണ്ട് ഭാഗങ്ങളിലായി പരിശോധിക്കുക.

ആദ്യം, എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് നമ്മുടെ "പ്രകൃതി സംബന്ധിയായ ശരീരത്തിന് മാറ്റം വരുത്തുന്നു" എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് തെറ്റായ വിവരമാണ്. എംആർഎൻഎ കോശത്തിന് ഉണ്ടാകുന്നത് സ്ഥായിയായ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മാറ്റം വരുത്തുന്നത് ശരീരത്തിന്റെ ബിയോളജി പുറത്തേക്ക് പ്രവർത്തിക്കുന്നതല്ല. എംആർഎൻഎ അതിന്റെ നിർദ്ദേശങ്ങൾ പുറത്തിറക്കിയതിന് ശേഷം കോശ പ്രക്രിയകൾ പ്രകൃതി പ്രകാരം വിഘടിപ്പിക്കുന്നു. പ്രതിരോധം പുറത്തിറക്കിയത് ഇതിനെ പരിചയപ്പെടുത്തുന്ന പ്രതിദൃശ്യമായ രോഗാന്തരത്തിന് പുറത്ത് പ്രതിരോധം പുറത്തിറക്കിയതിന് സമാനമാണ്.

രണ്ടാം ഭാഗം, ശരീരം "സിന്തെറ്റിക് പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾ, പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് നാനോപാര്ടിക്കിൾസ് അടങ്ങിയിരിക്കുന്ന പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾക്ക് പ്രവേശനം നൽകുന്നു" എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് നാനോപാര്ടിക്കിൾസ് എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസിന്റെ വഹനത്തിന്റെ പങ്ക് പിന്തുടരുന്നതിനെ തെറ്റായി അവലോകനം ചെയ്യുന്നു. ലിപിഡ് നാനോപാര്ടിക്കിൾസ് ശരീരത്തിന്റെ പ്രകൃതി സംബന്ധിയായ പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾക്ക് സമാനമായി വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു എന്ന് പറയുന്നതിന് പുറത്ത് നിലനിൽക്കുന്ന പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിന് തുടർന്ന് അവ അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുന്നു. മനുഷ്യന്റെ ശരീരം ഇത് അവ പ്രവേശിപ്പിക്കുന്നതിനോ അവ അംഗീകരിക്കുന്നതിനോ തെളിവ് ഇല്ല. ഇവയുടെ പങ്ക് ഇത് എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് പ്രവർത്തനത്തിന് സമർത്ഥമായ വഹനം ആകാൻ സഹായിക്കുന്നു, അതിന് ശേഷം അവ മെറ്റബോലിസം ചെയ്യുന്നു.

നിർവചനം

എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസ് മനുഷ്യന്റെ ശരീരം "മാറ്റം" വരുത്തി സിന്തെറ്റിക് പദാർത്ഥങ്ങൾ പ്രവേശിപ്പിക്കുന്നു എന്ന് പറയുന്നതിന് വിദ്യാഭ്യാസപരമായ അടിസ്ഥാനം ഇല്ല. മോഡേൺ എന്നീ വാക്സിൻസ് നിർമ്മാതാക്കൾ എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസിന്റെ മെക്കാനിസം വിശദമായി വിശദീകരിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്, അത് പരിരക്ഷിതമായ പ്രക്രിയയാണ് എന്ന് പറയുന്നു. പ്രതിരോധം ശരീരത്തിന്റെ പ്രകൃതി സംബന്ധിയായ പ്രവർത്തനമാണ്, എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസിന്റെ ഘടകങ്ങൾ പുറത്തിറക്കിയതിന് ശേഷം അവ അവയുടെ തീർച്ചയായ അന്തിമ പങ്ക് പ്രവർത്തിക്കാതെ ശരീര പ്രക്രിയകളിൽ മാറ്റം വരുത്തുന്നില്ല. ഇത് എംആർഎൻഎ വാക്സിൻസിന്റെ വിദ്യാഭ്യാസപരമായ അടിസ്ഥാനത്തെയും ഇവയുടെ വഹനത്തിലെ പദാർത്ഥങ്ങളുടെ പ്രകൃതിയെയും തെറ്റായി വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു.

A claim circulating on social media asserts that “COVID passports” were planned seven months before the COVID-19 outbreak in Wuhan, China, suggesting that the pandemic was deliberately orchestrated as a means to control the global population. The post further alleges that the European Commission (EC) had documents proving these intentions and that any denial constitutes false news. This article examines the veracity of such claims by exploring the timeline, nature of policy discussions, and the context behind digital health initiatives in Europe.

First, let’s address the timeline: The initial COVID-19 cases were identified in Wuhan, China in December 2019, with the World Health Organization (WHO) officially declaring a pandemic in March 2020. The claim points to a supposed plan for COVID passports—systems for proving vaccination status—having been developed as early as May 2019, which would precede any public knowledge of the SARS-CoV-2 virus.

The “EC documents” referenced in various iterations of this claim usually refer to European Commission reports or planning papers related to digital health records or vaccination tracking systems. It is true that, prior to the pandemic, the European Union and other international bodies had discussed improving digital health infrastructure, including immunization records. For example, the EU published a “Roadmap on Vaccination” in 2018-2019, which included ambitions to develop electronic vaccination information systems. These discussions stemmed from long-standing public health goals to enhance disease surveillance, combat vaccine-preventable diseases, and facilitate cross-border healthcare—not from a specific plan for COVID-19 or any “necessary pandemic.”

Digital health passports or certificates are not a new concept. The idea of maintaining verifiable immunization records dates back decades, with the World Health Organization’s “yellow card” for international travel serving as a well-known example. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the development and implementation of digital versions of such certificates, often called “COVID passports” or “Green Passes.” These systems were introduced globally in 2021 as a response to the unique challenges posed by the pandemic, particularly for safe international travel and reopening economies.

No credible evidence supports the allegation that the COVID-19 pandemic was planned or that digital vaccination certificates were conceived as instruments of mass population control. The referenced EC documents do not mention COVID-19 or suggest the orchestration of a pandemic. Rather, they reflect evolving discussions about improving public health infrastructure, particularly in light of previous outbreaks such as measles and influenza, and the increasing digitalization of healthcare.

Furthermore, public health authorities and independent experts have repeatedly debunked the notion that the pandemic was deliberately manufactured. The scientific consensus is that COVID-19 resulted from the natural spillover of a coronavirus from animals to humans.

In conclusion, the claim that “COVID passports” were planned seven months before the Wuhan outbreak as part of a population control scheme is not supported by the available evidence. Pre-pandemic plans for digital health records were part of routine public health planning and were not related to COVID-19 or any alleged conspiracy. Assertions that the pandemic was “necessary” or orchestrated remain unfounded and are contradicted by the historical and scientific record.

article_content:
A recent social media post declares, “WE WILL BREATHE FREE, the ban on wearing masks outdoors has been lifted.” This statement suggests that a previous ban on outdoor mask-wearing has ended, allowing individuals to go without face coverings outside. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine current public health regulations, the history of mask mandates, and the specific context in which such a ban might exist.

Mask mandates became a prominent public health measure during the COVID-19 pandemic, with many governments around the world instituting rules requiring individuals to wear face coverings in public spaces, both indoors and outdoors, to limit the spread of the virus. These mandates varied widely by country, state, and even city, reflecting differing levels of infection, vaccination rates, and policy approaches.

In most regions, mask mandates focused on indoor spaces or crowded outdoor environments where social distancing was not feasible. The rationale was that the risk of transmission was significantly lower outdoors, especially when people could maintain distance. However, during periods of high transmission, some jurisdictions did implement broad outdoor mask requirements.

The core claim in the social media post is that a ban on mask-wearing outdoors has been lifted. To accurately evaluate this, it is critical to clarify whether there was, in fact, an outright ban on wearing masks outdoors, or if the policy was a mandate requiring masks to be worn. The difference is significant: a ban would prohibit people from wearing masks, while a mandate would require them.

In most cases, governments did not ban the wearing of masks outdoors; rather, they mandated mask use in certain settings or lifted those mandates as the public health situation improved. It would be highly unusual—particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic—for authorities to prevent people from wearing masks outdoors, as mask-wearing is generally considered a personal health choice and, in some cultures, a common practice even outside of pandemic times.

Given this context, the statement in the social media post is somewhat misleading. It is more accurate to say that outdoor mask mandates have been lifted in many places, meaning people are no longer required by law or regulation to wear masks outdoors. However, there is no evidence of a ban that prevented people from wearing masks outdoors; instead, the requirement to do so has simply been rescinded in many areas.

In summary, the claim that “the ban on wearing masks outdoors has been lifted” mischaracterizes the nature of mask policies. The reality is that, while outdoor mask mandates have ended in numerous regions, allowing individuals more personal freedom regarding mask use, there has rarely, if ever, been an outright prohibition on wearing masks outdoors. As always, individuals should consult current local regulations and public health guidance to inform their decisions about mask use.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that 22 people died and 664 became infected with coronavirus in Macedonia despite being vaccinated. This post has generated concern and debate over the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and the broader implications for public health. To assess the accuracy and context of this claim, it is important to consider official data, understand how vaccines work, and examine the current situation in Macedonia.

First, it is crucial to acknowledge that no vaccine offers absolute protection against infection or death. COVID-19 vaccines, like those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca, and others, are designed primarily to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death. Breakthrough infections—cases in which vaccinated individuals contract the virus—do occur, but they are typically less severe than infections in unvaccinated persons. Deaths among vaccinated individuals are statistically rare but not impossible, especially among older adults or those with pre-existing health conditions.

The numbers quoted in the social media post—22 deaths and 664 infections among vaccinated individuals in Macedonia—align with periodic reports from health authorities in North Macedonia. Since the rollout of vaccines in early 2021, health agencies have tracked cases of infection and death among both vaccinated and unvaccinated populations. These figures must be viewed in the context of total vaccinations, the proportion of breakthrough cases, and the demographics of the affected individuals.

For example, if hundreds of thousands have been vaccinated, 664 breakthrough infections represent a small fraction of overall cases. Similarly, 22 deaths are tragic but may reflect vulnerable populations with underlying medical conditions. Data from North Macedonia and other countries consistently show that the risk of severe outcomes remains significantly lower among vaccinated individuals compared to those who have not received the vaccine.

The occurrence of breakthrough cases can be influenced by several factors: the level of virus circulating in the community, the emergence of variants with partial resistance to antibodies, and the time elapsed since vaccination (as immunity may wane). Health authorities in Macedonia have responded to these challenges by encouraging booster doses, especially for high-risk groups.

It is also important to note that focusing solely on breakthrough cases, without considering the much higher rates of infection and death among the unvaccinated, can be misleading. Public health experts emphasize that vaccines have been instrumental in reducing the overall burden of COVID-19, preventing thousands of deaths and hospitalizations in Macedonia and worldwide.

In summary, the claim that 22 people died and 664 became infected with coronavirus in Macedonia despite being vaccinated is factually accurate within the reported figures. However, the context underlines that these numbers do not undermine the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines. They serve as a reminder that while vaccines offer strong protection, they are not infallible, and continued vigilance, booster campaigns, and preventive measures remain essential in controlling the pandemic.

Koronavīrusa vakcīnas, piemēram, Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca un citas, tika izstrādātas galvenokārt, lai samazinātu infekcijas risku, slimības smagumu, slimnīcu ieņemšanu un nāvi. Pārsteigumu infekcijas, kad vakcinēti cilvēki iegūst vīrusu, rodas, taču tās bieži ir mazāk smagas nekā infekcijas nevakcinētiem. Šos skaitļus jāatzīnā atbilstoši kopējām vakcinācijas datiem, pārsteigumu infekciju proporcijai un ietekmētajām personām.

Piemēram, ja simts tūkstoši cilvēku ir vakcinēti, 664 pārsteigumu infekcijas atspoguļo mazāko daļu vispārējām infekcijām. A social media post circulating widely claims that Pfizer has released a statement for investors, announcing a new partnership with Microsoft to integrate Microsoft’s Pluton processor chip into their vaccine. According to the post, this collaboration purportedly aims to reduce symptoms associated with the vaccine, including fatigue and soreness, and even promises heightened awareness for recipients.

This post has generated significant attention and confusion, combining elements of real companies, technology, and healthcare concerns. Here, we break down the core claims and provide factual analysis.

**Background on Pfizer and Microsoft**

Pfizer is a global pharmaceutical company, best known recently for developing one of the first COVID-19 vaccines. Microsoft is a leading technology corporation, and its Pluton processor chip is a security technology designed to protect computers and devices from cyber threats. Pluton is not a medical device or a component designed for biological use.

**Examining the Core Claims**

The social media post makes several notable assertions:

1. **Pfizer has partnered with Microsoft to integrate Pluton chips into vaccines.**
2. **This integration is intended to reduce symptoms such as fatigue and soreness, and to provide heightened awareness.**
3. **An official investor statement exists confirming these claims.**

**Fact-Checking Analysis**

Firstly, there is no public record or credible evidence of Pfizer releasing any statement, to investors or otherwise, regarding a partnership with Microsoft to integrate Pluton processor chips into any vaccine. Pfizer’s investor communications, press releases, and official channels contain no mention of such an initiative.

Secondly, Microsoft’s Pluton chip is a security processor specifically designed for use in personal computers and servers, not biomedical applications. Its function is to safeguard sensitive data and hardware integrity against cyberattacks, not to interact with human biology or influence vaccine side effects.

Thirdly, the suggestion that a processor chip, especially one designed for computer hardware, could be “integrated” into a vaccine administered via injection is not supported by any scientific or technological basis. Vaccines are composed of biological molecules, such as mRNA or proteins, and do not contain electronic components. The logistics of embedding a silicon chip, let alone a security processor, into a vaccine for injection are implausible and outside current scientific reality.

Additionally, the claim that such integration could reduce symptoms like fatigue or soreness, or provide improved cognitive awareness, has no basis in either medical or technological research. Vaccine side effects are determined by the body’s immune response to the vaccine’s biological components, not by the presence of electronics.

**Conclusion**

After reviewing official statements, technological capabilities, and medical science, there is no evidence supporting the claim that Pfizer and Microsoft have announced a partnership to integrate Pluton chips into vaccines, nor that such a measure could affect vaccine side effects or cognitive function. The post in question appears to be a fabrication, merging unrelated facts about two well-known companies and their products. As always, it is essential to verify information with credible sources before sharing or acting upon it.

Екінші, Microsoft Pluton чиптері – бұл қауіпсізлік процессоры, ол өзінде қызмет ететін компьютерлер мен серверлерге қызмет етеді, биомедициналық қолданыстағы құрылғылар емес. Оның мақсаты – сезімдік деректерді және құрылғының қауіпсіздігін кибер қауіптерге қарсылықта қорғау, ол адам бірлігімен биологиялық әсерлерге әсер етпейді немесе вакциналардың әсерін өзгертпейді.

Үшінші, құрылғылық чип, оның есептеуінде құрылғылық құралы болып келетін, вакциналарға интегралдау туралы тұжырым ғылыми немесе технологиялық негізде жоқ. Вакциналар биологиялық молекулалардан, мысалы, mRNA немесе белоктардан тұрады және электрондық компоненттерді қамтып отырмайды. Құрылғылық чипті, ең әуелі, құрылғылық құралын вакциналарға интегралдау логистикалық үлгісінде әлсіз және бүгінгі ғылымдық әлемнің ішінде мүмкін емес.

Көптеген жағдайда, бұл интегралдау вакциналардың басып шығару немесе ауырлықты азайту немесе алуға қабілеттілікті арттыруға әсер ететінінің ғылыми немесе технологиялық негізі жоқ. Вакциналардың әсері дене иммунитетінің вакциналардың биологиялық компоненттеріне әсерінен туындайды, электрондық құрылғылардың болуынан емес.

**Қорытынды**

Офицерлік жарияламалар, технологиялық мүмкіндіктер мен медициналық ғылымды тексеріп, Pfizer мен Microsoft үйлесімін жариялау, Pluton чиптерін вакциналарға интегралдау немесе бұл әсердің вакциналардың әсерін немесе когнитивтік функцияны өзгертетінінің әртүрлі негізі жоқ. This article examines these assertions in detail, providing background information and a factual analysis.

To begin, the claim that vaccinated individuals are the source of all new COVID-19 variants is not supported by scientific evidence. Viruses, including the virus that causes COVID-19, mutate and develop new variants as they replicate. This process occurs whenever the virus spreads from person to person, regardless of vaccination status. In fact, the majority of significant variants, such as the Delta and Omicron variants, emerged before large-scale vaccination campaigns were implemented. The development of new variants is primarily driven by widespread transmission, especially in populations where the virus can circulate freely.

Vaccines are designed to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19. While it is true that breakthrough infections can occur in vaccinated individuals, the overall risk of severe outcomes is much lower compared to those who are unvaccinated. Vaccines have been a critical tool in reducing the burden of disease and curbing the spread of COVID-19. The suggestion that vaccinated people "simply get sick" oversimplifies and misrepresents the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines.

The post also claims that vaccinated individuals are banned in Palm Beach. There is no evidence to support this statement. Local, state, and national public health authorities have not implemented policies that ban vaccinated individuals from Palm Beach or any other public space. On the contrary, public health recommendations encourage vaccination as a means to protect individuals and communities. In some settings, proof of vaccination may be required to enter certain venues, especially during surges in cases, but there is no record of a ban targeting vaccinated people.

It is important to recognize the role of misinformation in shaping public perceptions of vaccines. Social media posts that present misleading or false information about COVID-19 and vaccines can undermine public confidence and hinder efforts to control the pandemic. Accurate information from credible health authorities should be consulted when evaluating claims about COVID-19 and vaccination.

In summary, the claims presented in the social media post do not align with current scientific understanding or public policy. Vaccinated people are not responsible for all new COVID-19 variants, vaccination does not simply make people sick, and there is no evidence that vaccinated individuals are banned in Palm Beach. As the pandemic continues to evolve, accurate information remains essential for informed decision-making and public health.

Claims regarding Covid Passports, vaccination policies, and pandemic management continue to circulate widely on social media. One recent post makes several key assertions: that Covid Passports threaten and force people to be vaccinated and are discriminatory, allegedly violating a Council of Europe resolution; that in Macedonia, side effects from vaccination are not reported; and that Texas, after rejecting mask mandates, now has zero Covid patients. This article examines each claim in detail, providing background and analyzing the facts.

**Covid Passports: Threat, Coercion, and Discrimination**

Covid Passports, or digital certificates showing vaccination status, have been implemented in various countries as a means to facilitate international travel, reopen economies, and reduce transmission risks in public spaces. The claim that Covid Passports “force” vaccination requires scrutiny. In most contexts, individuals are not legally compelled to receive a Covid-19 vaccine. However, access to certain services, venues, or travel may be restricted for those without proof of vaccination or a negative Covid test, creating indirect incentives to vaccinate.

The post references the Council of Europe Resolution, likely referring to Resolution 2361, which advises member states to ensure that vaccination is voluntary and that no one is discriminated against for not being vaccinated. While this resolution sets non-binding guidelines, it does not have the force of law. Governments retain the authority to implement public health measures, such as vaccine requirements for specific activities, provided they do not constitute outright coercion or discrimination under domestic and international law. Thus, while some individuals may feel pressured, the resolution does not categorically prohibit measures like Covid Passports, which typically offer alternatives (e.g., recent negative tests) for unvaccinated people.

**Reporting Side Effects in Macedonia**

The post claims that in Macedonia, “no one reports the side effects of vaccination.” This is inaccurate. North Macedonia, like other countries, has a pharmacovigilance system in place for monitoring and reporting adverse events following immunization. Healthcare professionals are required to report serious or unexpected side effects to the relevant health authorities, and individuals can also report side effects themselves. While underreporting can be an issue in any country, the assertion that “no one” reports side effects is demonstrably false. Official data on adverse events is periodically released by national health authorities.

**Texas: Mask Mandates and Covid Cases**

Finally, the post states that “two months ago people refused to wear masks, and today there are zero Covid patients” in Texas. This is not supported by available data. Texas has experienced fluctuations in mask mandates and Covid cases throughout the pandemic. While the state lifted its mask mandate at various points, Covid-19 cases and hospitalizations have continued to be reported. At no time has Texas reported zero Covid patients statewide in hospitals or in terms of active cases. As of the most recent data, there continue to be new Covid-19 infections and hospitalizations in Texas, making the claim of zero patients inaccurate.

**Conclusion**

The social media post in question contains several misleading or false statements. Covid Passports do not legally mandate vaccination nor outright violate Council of Europe guidelines, though they can create indirect pressure. Side effects of vaccination are indeed reported in Macedonia. Finally, Texas has not reached a point of zero Covid patients, and public health data contradicts this claim. As always, it is crucial to consult official sources and verified information, especially when evaluating claims about public health measures and outcomes.

article_content:
Claims about the effects of COVID-19 vaccination on blood cells have circulated widely on social media, with one recent post alleging that vaccinated individuals experience significant and irreversible changes at the cellular level. According to the post, blood cells of patients are completely healthy before vaccination, but change progressively in the days afterward. The post further claims that “white spots” visible in blood samples are actually nanoparticles introduced by the vaccine, which cannot be removed from the body and will eventually integrate into every cell.

These assertions have generated concern and confusion, particularly among those still hesitant about receiving a COVID-19 vaccine. To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to examine the scientific principles behind vaccines, the technology involved, and the evidence regarding vaccine safety and effects on blood cells.

COVID-19 vaccines, such as those produced by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, use messenger RNA (mRNA) technology. The mRNA is delivered into the body using lipid nanoparticles, which are tiny fat-based particles designed to protect the mRNA and help it enter cells temporarily. Once the mRNA is inside the cell, it instructs the cell to produce a harmless piece of the spike protein found on the coronavirus, prompting the immune system to recognize and fight the virus in future encounters. After this process, the mRNA and its lipid carrier are rapidly broken down and eliminated by the body—neither the mRNA nor the lipid nanoparticles remain long-term in the body.

The claim that blood cells are “completely healthy” before vaccination and then change dramatically afterward is not supported by scientific studies or clinical evidence. In the extensive clinical trials and real-world monitoring of millions of vaccine recipients, no consistent or significant abnormal changes in blood cell health attributable to the vaccines have been documented. Side effects from vaccines, such as mild fever or soreness at the injection site, are temporary and not related to permanent cellular changes.

Regarding the “white spots” allegedly visible in blood samples, it is important to note that specialized laboratory techniques are required to identify nanoparticles, and they are not visible under standard light microscopes used in routine blood analysis. The appearance of such spots could be due to a variety of factors unrelated to nanoparticles, such as artifacts from sample preparation, lighting, or imaging errors.

The assertion that nanoparticles from the vaccine “can never be removed from the body” and “will eventually enter every cell” is inaccurate. Lipid nanoparticles are biodegradable and are cleared from the body within days. They do not persist or accumulate in tissues, and there is no mechanism by which they could become a permanent part of every cell.

In summary, the core claims in the social media post are not supported by current scientific understanding or evidence. COVID-19 vaccines do not irreversibly alter blood cells, do not leave permanent nanoparticles in the body, and do not integrate foreign materials into every cell. Vaccines remain one of the most effective tools in preventing severe illness and death from COVID-19, with a strong safety record based on rigorous research and ongoing monitoring.

Klaim mengenai kesan vaksin COVID-19 terhadap sel darah telah tersebar luas di media sosial, dengan satu pos terkini mengatakan bahawa individu yang telah disuntik mengalami perubahan besar dan tidak boleh dibalikkan pada peringkat sel. Menurut pos tersebut, sel darah pesakit dalam keadaan sihat sepenuhnya sebelum disuntik, tetapi berubah secara beransur-ansur selepas beberapa hari. Pos tersebut juga mengatakan bahawa "tanda putih" yang nampak dalam sampel darah sebenarnya merupakan nanopartikel yang diperkenalkan oleh vaksin, yang tidak dapat dikeluarkan dari badan dan akan akhirnya terintegrasi ke dalam setiap sel.

Klaim-klaim ini telah menimbulkan kebimbangan dan kekeliruan, terutamanya di kalangan mereka yang masih ragu-ragu untuk menerima vaksin COVID-19. Untuk mengevaluasi kebenaran klaim-klaim ini, penting untuk mengkaji prinsip sains di sebalik vaksin, teknologi yang digunakan, serta bukti mengenai keselamatan vaksin dan kesan terhadap sel darah.

Vaksin COVID-19, seperti yang dihasilkan oleh Pfizer-BioNTech dan Moderna, menggunakan teknologi mRNA (messenger RNA). mRNA dihantar ke dalam badan menggunakan nanopartikel lipid, iaitu partikel kecil yang terbina daripada lemak yang dirancang untuk melindungi mRNA dan membantu ia memasuki sel secara sementara. Apabila mRNA berada dalam sel, ianya memerintahkan sel untuk menghasilkan sebahagian kecil protein pucuk yang tidak berbahaya yang terdapat pada virus koronavirus, memaksa sistem imun mengenali dan melawan virus dalam pertemuan masa depan. Selepas proses ini, mRNA dan pembawa lipidnya akan cepat dihancurkan dan dikeluarkan oleh badan—kedua-dua mRNA dan nanopartikel lipid tidak kekal lama dalam badan.

Klaim bahawa sel darah dalam keadaan "sihat sepenuhnya" sebelum disuntik dan kemudian berubah secara dramatik selepas itu tidak disokong oleh kajian saintifik atau bukti klinikal. Dalam ujian klinikal yang luas dan pemantauan dunia nyata terhadap jutaan penerima vaksin, tiada perubahan tidak normal atau signifikan dalam kesihatan sel darah yang dapat dikaitkan dengan vaksin yang direkodkan. Kes-kesan vaksin seperti demam ringan atau kemerahan di tempat suntikan adalah sementara dan tidak berkaitan dengan perubahan sel yang kekal.

Mengenai "tanda putih" yang didakwa nampak dalam sampel darah, penting untuk diperhatikan bahawa teknik makmal khusus diperlukan untuk mengenal pasti nanopartikel, dan mereka tidak nampak di bawah mikroskop cahaya biasa yang digunakan dalam analisis darah rutin. Kehadiran tanda-tanda seperti ini boleh disebabkan oleh pelbagai faktor yang tidak berkaitan dengan nanopartikel, seperti kesan sampingan dari peparahan sampel, cahaya, atau kesalahan imej.

Pernyataan bahawa nanopartikel daripada vaksin "tidak pernah dikeluarkan dari badan" dan "akhirnya memasuki setiap sel" adalah tidak tepat. Nanopartikel lipid adalah biodegradable dan dikeluarkan dari badan dalam beberapa hari. Mereka tidak kekal atau berkumpul dalam tisu, dan tiada mekanisma yang membolehkan mereka menjadi bahagian kekal dari setiap sel.

Secara keseluruhannya, klaim utama dalam pos media sosial tidak disokong oleh pemahaman saintifik atau bukti masa kini. Vaksin COVID-19 tidak mengubah sel darah secara tidak boleh dibalikkan, tidak meninggalkan nanopartikel kekal dalam badan, dan tidak mengintegrasikan bahan asing ke dalam setiap sel. Vaksin tetap merupakan salah satu alat paling berkesan dalam mencegah penyakit serius dan kematian akibat COVID-19, dengan rekod keselamatan yang kukuh berdasarkan kajian yang ketat dan pemantauan berterusan.

In recent weeks, a social media post has circulated claiming, "The measure for wearing masks outdoor lifted." This statement has generated significant public interest and confusion, particularly as communities continue to navigate evolving public health guidelines in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. This article examines the accuracy of the claim, provides necessary context, and clarifies what the lifting of outdoor mask mandates means for the public.

Background and Context

Mask mandates were introduced in many countries and regions as a critical measure to curb the spread of COVID-19, particularly in areas where maintaining physical distancing was challenging. Outdoor mask requirements varied by jurisdiction and were often stricter during periods of high transmission or when new, more contagious variants emerged. Over time, as vaccination rates increased and case numbers declined, some governments began to relax these mandates, reflecting improved public health conditions.

Fact-Checking the Claim

The core claim is that the measure requiring people to wear masks outdoors has been lifted. Fact-checking this claim reveals that, in many locations, outdoor mask mandates have indeed been relaxed or eliminated, especially in areas with low community transmission rates and high vaccination coverage. Public health authorities have generally agreed that the risk of COVID-19 transmission is significantly lower outdoors than indoors, especially when individuals are able to maintain physical distance.

For example, several countries and regions announced the lifting of outdoor mask mandates during 2022 and 2023, as part of broader efforts to return to normalcy. Government officials cited scientific evidence showing that outdoor environments are less conducive to virus spread, and that the benefits of mask-wearing outdoors are limited in most situations. As a result, people are no longer required to wear masks in outdoor public spaces in many areas, unless they are in crowded settings where physical distancing is not possible.

However, it is important to note that the lifting of outdoor mask requirements does not mean all mask mandates have been eliminated. In many places, masks remain mandatory in certain indoor settings, such as public transportation, healthcare facilities, and crowded indoor events. Furthermore, local authorities may reinstate mask requirements if case numbers rise or new variants of concern emerge.

Analysis and Conclusion

The claim that the measure for wearing masks outdoors has been lifted is largely accurate in many regions, reflecting updated public health guidance and a better understanding of COVID-19 transmission dynamics. However, the situation can vary by location, and some jurisdictions may still recommend or require masks outdoors in specific circumstances.

Individuals are encouraged to stay informed about local regulations and to exercise personal judgment, particularly in crowded outdoor settings or if they are at higher risk for severe illness. While outdoor mask mandates have generally been lifted, continued vigilance and respect for evolving public health advice remain important tools in managing the ongoing impact of COVID-19.

A recent social media post has resurfaced a persistent claim about vaccines and microchips, suggesting that it is technologically possible to embed a chip in a vaccine and alleging that such vaccines have already been administered in the United States, albeit on an optional basis. This claim echoes a broader narrative that gained traction during the COVID-19 pandemic and continues to circulate online. To assess the veracity of this statement, it is essential to examine both the technological possibilities and the realities of vaccine development and deployment.

First, it is important to clarify what is meant by “putting a chip in the vaccine.” Technology exists to create microchips and nano-scale devices, and research into medical applications for such technologies is ongoing. For example, implantable RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) chips are used in pets for identification purposes, and some experimental research has explored injectable micro-scale devices for monitoring health conditions. However, these devices are generally much larger than the particles found in vaccine solutions, and they require a specialized delivery mechanism, not a standard vaccine syringe.

The concept of integrating a microchip into a vaccine presents significant technological hurdles. Vaccines are typically formulated as liquids containing antigens and stabilizing agents, which are injected intramuscularly using fine needles. Microchips, even at their smallest, are orders of magnitude larger than the molecules that comprise vaccine components. For a microchip to fit through a standard syringe needle alongside a vaccine, it would need to be extremely small—smaller than what is currently feasible for functional electronic devices. Furthermore, any foreign body, such as a chip, would likely trigger an immune response or rejection, raising serious safety concerns.

Regarding the claim that such vaccines have already been administered in the United States and that these were “optional,” there is no evidence to support this assertion. All vaccines approved for use in the United States go through rigorous testing and regulatory review by agencies such as the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The ingredient lists for these vaccines are publicly available and do not include microchips or electronic tracking devices. No credible reports or public records indicate that any vaccine containing a chip—optional or otherwise—has ever been offered or administered to the public in the United States.

Rumors about “chip vaccines” gained widespread attention during the COVID-19 pandemic, fueled by misinformation and misinterpretation of new technologies such as digital health certificates and injectable trackers for laboratory animals. These technologies are distinct from vaccines and are not designed to be used in humans as part of immunization programs. The confusion may also stem from discussions about using implantable chips in other contexts, such as patient identification or data storage, but these are not related to vaccines.

In summary, while research into nano-scale medical devices is ongoing, it is not currently possible to embed a functional microchip in a vaccine delivered by standard injection. There is no evidence that such vaccines have been administered in the United States, either on a mandatory or optional basis. The core claim in the social media post does not reflect established scientific or medical practice. Misinformation about vaccines can undermine public health efforts, making it crucial to verify such statements with accurate information and context.

एक नया सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट वैक्सीन और माइक्रोचिप के बारे में एक लंबे समय से मौजूद कथन को फिर से उठा रहा है, जिसमें यह दावा किया जाता है कि एक माइक्रोचिप को वैक्सीन में डाला जा सकता है और ऐसे वैक्सीन के पहले से ही अमेरिका में दिए जा चुके हैं, हालांकि वैक्सीन के वैकल्पिक आधार पर। इस कथन के बारे में जांच करने के लिए, यह आवश्यक है कि तकनीकी संभावनाओं और वैक्सीन विकास और वितरण के वास्तविकताओं का अध्ययन किया जाए।

पहले, यह स्पष्ट करना महत्वपूर्ण है कि "वैक्सीन में माइक्रोचिप डालना" क्या अर्थ है। माइक्रोचिप और नैनो-स्केल उपकरण बनाने के लिए तकनीक उपलब्ध है, और इन तकनीकों के चिकित्सीय अनुप्रयोगों के लिए अनुसंधान जारी है। उदाहरण के लिए, पशुओं की पहचान के लिए डाले जाने वाले एम्बेडेड आरएफआईडी (रेडियो फ्रीक्वेंसी आईडेंटिफिकेशन) चिप्स का उपयोग किया जाता है, और कुछ प्रयोगात्मक अनुसंधान रोग की निगरानी के लिए प्रस्तावित माइक्रो-स्केल उपकरणों के इंजेक्शन के बारे में अध्ययन कर रहे हैं। हालांकि, इन उपकरणों के आम तौर पर वैक्सीन घोल में पाए जाने वाले कणों से बहुत बड़े होते हैं और वे एक स्टैंडर्ड वैक्सीन सिरिंज के बजाए विशेष डिलीवरी युक्ति की आवश्यकता होती है।

वैक्सीन में माइक्रोचिप के एकीकरण की संकल्पना एक बड़ी तकनीकी चुनौती है। वैक्सीन आम तौर पर एक तरल पदार्थ होते हैं जिसमें एंटीजन और स्थिरकरण एजेंट होते हैं जो छोटे नोजल के माध्यम से अंतर्मुखी इंजेक्शन के माध्यम से दिए जाते हैं। माइक्रोचिप, भले ही वे अपने सबसे छोटे रूप में हों, भी वैक्सीन के घटक के अणुओं के मुकाबले कई बार बड़े होते हैं। एक माइक्रोचिप को एक स्टैंडर्ड सिरिंज नोजल के साथ एक वैक्सीन के साथ पार होना चाहिए, तो वह बहुत छोटा होना चाहिए - वह वर्तमान में कार्य करने योग्य इलेक्ट्रॉनिक उपकरण के लिए संभव नहीं है। इसके अलावा, कोई विदेशी वस्तु, जैसे कि एक चिप, एक इम्यून रिएक्शन या अस्वीकृति का कारण बन सकती है, जिससे गंभीर सुरक्षा चिंताएं उत्पन्न हो सकती हैं।

वैक्सीन के वैकल्पिक आधार पर अमेरिका में ऐसे वैक्सीन के दिए जाने के दावे के बारे में कोई प्रमाण नहीं है। अमेरिका में उपयोग के लिए अनुमोदित सभी वैक्सीन फूड एंड ड्रग एडमिनिस्ट्रेशन (FDA) जैसी एजेंसियों द्वारा गंभीर टेस्टिंग और रेगुलेटरी समीक्षा के माध्यम से गुजरते हैं। इन वैक्सीन के घटक सूची खुले रूप से उपलब्ध हैं और इनमें माइक्रोचिप या इलेक्ट्रॉनिक ट्रैकिंग उपकरण शामिल नहीं हैं। कोई विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट या सार्वजनिक रिकॉर्ड नहीं है जो बताता हो कि कोई भी चिप वाला वैक्सीन - वैकल्पिक या अनिवार्य भी हो - अमेरिका में कभी लोगों को प्रदान या दिया गया हो।

"चिप वैक्सीन" के बारे में गुप्त चर्चा कोरोनोवायरस महामारी के दौरान व्यापक ध्यान के लायक बन गई, जिसमें डिजिटल स्वास्थ्य प्रमाण पत्र और लैबोरेटरी पशुओं के इंजेक्शन ट्रैकर जैसी नए तकनीकों के गलत व्याख्या और गलत सूचना के कारण बढ़ गई। ये तकनीकें वैक्सीन से अलग हैं और इनका इम्यूनाइजेशन कार्यक्रम में मानवों के लिए उपयोग के लिए डिज़ाइन नहीं किया गया है। इस गुप्त चर्चा के बारे में अन्य संदर्भ में एम्बेडेड चिप के उपयोग के बारे में भी चर्चा हो सकती है, जैसे कि मरीज पहचान या डेटा संग्रहण, लेकिन वे वैक्सीन से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

संक्षेप में, नैनो-स्केल चिकित्सीय उपकरणों के अनुसंधान जारी है, लेकिन वर्तमान में एक कार्य करने योग्य माइक्रोचिप को एक स्टैंडर्ड इंजेक्शन द्वारा वैक्सीन में डाला नहीं जा सकता है। अमेरिका में ऐसे वैक्सीन के वैकल्पिक या अनिवार्य आधार पर दिए जाने के बारे में कोई प्रमाण नहीं है। सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट में बुनियादी कथन वैज्ञानिक या चिकित्सीय अभ्यास से दूर है। वैक्सीन के बारे में गलत सूचना लोगों के स्वास्थ्य कार्यक्रम को नुकसान पहुंचा सकती है, इसलिए ऐसे कथन की जांच गलत सूचना और संदर्भ के साथ करना आवश्यक है।
