കോവിഡ്-19 പാന്റിഡം ആരംഭിച്ചതിനു ശേഷം, വാക്സിനുകൾ വികസിപ്പിച്ചെടുക്കുകയും വ്യാപകമായി നിയമിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തിട്ടുണ്ട്, ഇത് രോഗം പടരുന്നതിനും ഗുരുതരമായ രോഗം വരുന്നതിനും പ്രചാരണം നേരിടുന്നതിനും സാധ്യതയെ കുറയ്ക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു. ഉപയോഗത്തിന് അനുമതി നൽകിയിരിക്കുന്ന വാക്സിനുകൾക്ക് തുടർച്ചയായ ആരോഗ്യ പരിശോധനകൾ നടത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. ആരോഗ്യ അധികാരികൾ നിർണ്ണയിച്ച ഒരു പ്രധാന വസ്തുത എന്നതാണ് കോവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനുകൾക്ക് ജീവിത വൈറസ് ഉൾപ്പെടുത്താൻ കഴിയാത്തതാണ്, അത് പ്രതിരോധകരായ വ്യക്തികളിലേക്ക് രോഗം പടരുകയോ മറ്റുള്ളവർക്ക് പരോപകാരം നൽകുകയോ ചെയ്യാനാവില്ല. എംആർഎൻഎ പിന്തുണയും വെക്ടർ തരം വാക്സിനുകളും വൈറസിനെ അനുവദിക്കുന്നതിനും പ്രതിരോധ പ്രവർത്തനം നടത്തുന്നതിനും ശാസ്ത്രം പ്രാപിക്കുന്നു, അത് പ്രകോപന പദാർത്ഥം പരിചയപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതല്ല.

**വാദം പരിശോധന: "പഠനപരിശീലകർ വാക്സിനീകരിക്കുകയും വിദ്യാർത്ഥികളെ പ്രകോപിപ്പിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും"**

പോസ്റ്റിന്റെ പ്രധാന വാദം വാക്സിനീകരിച്ച പഠനപരിശീലകർ വിദ്യാർത്ഥികളെ പ്രകോപിപ്പിക്കുന്ന പ്രതിരോധ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങളായി മാറുകയും പറയുന്നു. ഈ പ്രമേയം പ്രസ്താവനയുടെ സാധാരണ സാമ്പത്തിക അനുമാനത്തിനു വിരോധമാണ്. വാക്സിനീകരിച്ച വ്യക്തികൾ അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും അതിനാൽ പ്രചാരണം നേരിടുകയും കുറവാണ്, അതുപോലെ അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും കുറവാണ്, അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും കുറവാണ്, അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും കുറവാണ്, അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും കുറവാണ്, അനുബന്ധ രോഗം പടരുകയും കുറവാണ്. വാക്സിനീകരിക്കുന്നതിന്റെ കാര്യം പ്രചാരണ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിന്റെ കാരണം കൂടി വാക്സിനീകരിക്കുന്ന വ്യക്തികളെ പ്രചാരണ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങളാക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നില്ല. വാക്സിനീകരിക്കുന്നത് പ്രചാരണ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങൾ രൂപപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിനു വിരോധമാണ്, അത് പ്രചാരണ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങൾ രൂപപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിനു വിരോധമാണ്.

**വാദം പരിശോധന: "കബ്ബലാ വിദ്യാർത്ഥികളെ വാക്സിനീകരിക്കാൻ ബലപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിനെ കാരണമാകുന്നില്ല"**

പോസ്റ്റ് കബ്ബലാ എന്ന ഒരു യിഹൂദ മാന്ത്രികതയെ കൂടി പരിഗണിക്കുന്നു, അത് വാക്സിനീകരണ നയങ്ങളിലോ വിദ്യാർത്ഥികളെ ബലപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിലോ പങ്കെടുക്കുന്നു. വാസ്തവത്തിൽ, ജനാധിപത്യ പരിശോധന വാക്സിനുകളുടെ നിർണ്ണയത്തിന് ജനാധിപത്യ അധികാരികളും വിദഗ്ധ അധികാരികളും തീരുമാനങ്ങൾ എടുക്കുന്നു, അതുപോലെ ധർമ്മിക അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മാന്ത്രിക സംഘങ്ങളും പങ്കെടുക്കുന്നില്ല. കബ്ബലാ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അതിനു സമ്പർക്കമുള്ള സംഘം വിദ്യാർത്ഥികളെ വാക്സിനീകരിക്കുന്നതിന് പുറത്തുകളും നിയമങ്ങളും എടുക്കുന്നതിന് തെളിവ് ഇല്ല.

**പരിഗണനയുടെ നിലപാട്**

സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയ പോസ്റ്റിൽ പ്രസ്താവിച്ച ആരോപണങ്ങൾ വിദഗ്ദ്ധ തെളിവുകളോ പുസ്തകങ്ങളിൽ നിന്നും പ്രസ്താവിച്ച നയങ്ങളോ അടിസ്ഥാനമാക്കി പ്രസ്താവിച്ചിട്ടില്ല. വാക്സിനീകരിച്ച പഠനപരിശീലകർ പ്രകോപന കേന്ദ്രങ്ങളോ പ്രതിരോധ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങളോ അല്ല, അവർക്ക് കോവിഡ്-19 പ്രചാരണം ചെയ്യാനുള്ള സാധ്യത കുറവാണ്. ഈ പരിസ്ഥിതിയിൽ കബ്ബലാ സംബന്ധിച്ച പരാമർശം അടിസ്ഥാനമാക്കി പ്രസ്താവിച്ചിട്ടില്ല അല്ലെങ്കിൽ തെറ്റായി പ്രസ്താവിച്ചിട്ടില്ല. പാന്റിഡം സമയത്ത് സ്കൂളിൽ പരിസ്ഥിതികളെ പരിശോധിക്കുന്നതിന് പൊതു വിവരങ്ങളെ അടിസ്ഥാനമാക്കി പ്രസ്താവിച്ച ആരോഗ്യ വിവരങ്ങൾ അനുസരിച്ച് പൊതു വിശ്വസനീയ വിവരങ്ങൾ ആശ്രയിക്കുക അത്യാവശ്യമാണ്.

article_content:
A recent social media post has raised alarm by suggesting that vaccines contain “the blood of small children,” and that their use separates humans from God. The post further claims that vaccine inventors have acknowledged this, and encourages readers to reject vaccines, framing the issue in stark moral and religious terms.

To address these assertions, it is necessary to examine both the factual basis of the claims and the broader context in which they are made.

**Understanding Vaccine Ingredients**

Vaccines are developed using a variety of scientific methods, and their ingredients are subject to strict regulatory oversight. The claim that vaccines contain “the blood of small children” is a misrepresentation of how vaccines are made. Most vaccines contain antigens (such as inactivated viruses or pieces of viruses), adjuvants to enhance immune response, stabilizers, and preservatives. None of the common vaccines in use contain human blood.

Some confusion may arise from the fact that, historically, certain vaccines have been developed using human cell lines. These cell lines, such as WI-38 and MRC-5, were originally derived from fetal tissue obtained from elective abortions in the 1960s. However, these cells do not form part of the final vaccine product. Instead, the cell lines serve as a medium to grow viruses used in vaccines. The cells themselves are filtered out during the manufacturing process. There is no blood or tissue from children, living or deceased, in the vaccines administered today.

**Acknowledgement by Vaccine Developers**

The assertion that vaccine inventors “acknowledge” the use of children’s blood is inaccurate. Vaccine manufacturers and health authorities are transparent about the sources of cell lines used in some vaccine production, but they do not claim that blood or tissue from children is present in vaccines. This transparency allows individuals to make informed decisions based on accurate information.

**Religious and Ethical Considerations**

The post frames vaccine use as a spiritual issue, suggesting it could “kill our soul and body.” Many religious organizations and leaders have issued statements addressing concerns about vaccines developed with historical fetal cell lines. In many cases, religious authorities have determined that receiving such vaccines is morally permissible, especially given the substantial public health benefits.

For individuals with personal or religious objections, alternative vaccines that do not use these cell lines may be available. Health professionals are encouraged to discuss these options with patients.

**Conclusion**

The central claim of the post—that vaccines contain the blood of small children—is not supported by scientific evidence or by statements from vaccine developers. Vaccines do not contain human blood or tissue, and their composition is subject to rigorous safety standards. While ethical discussions continue regarding the use of historical cell lines in vaccine development, the suggestion that vaccination constitutes a grave spiritual or physical danger is not supported by established facts. It is important for individuals to consult with medical and religious authorities and to rely on accurate information when making decisions about vaccination.

article_content:
A recent social media post has stirred debate by claiming that “many people knew what was to come,” asserting that governments are intent on taking “full control of the population” and “wipe out the middle class.” Such sweeping statements resonate with widespread anxieties about government overreach and economic inequality, but do these claims stand up to closer scrutiny?

To fact-check this assertion, it’s important to break down its core elements: the alleged inevitability of government control, and the purported plan to eliminate the middle class.

**Government Control: Perceptions vs. Reality**

The idea that governments seek to “take full control of the population” is a recurring theme in conspiracy theories, especially during times of crisis. Events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, economic recessions, and political unrest have fueled concerns about increased surveillance, emergency powers, and restrictions on personal freedoms. Governments around the world have, at times, implemented policies such as lockdowns, digital tracking for health purposes, and expanded police powers.

However, most democratic governments operate under constitutional frameworks that limit the scope of executive power and provide checks and balances. While it is true that some temporary measures have expanded government authority, these are usually subject to judicial review, public debate, and, in many cases, reversal once the crisis abates. There is little concrete evidence to support the claim of a coordinated effort by governments globally to assert “full control” over populations in a permanent fashion.

**Wiping Out the Middle Class: Economic Trends and Policy Impacts**

The second part of the claim—that the middle class is being deliberately wiped out—taps into real concerns about economic inequality. Over the past several decades, many developed countries have seen the middle class shrink in proportion to the overall population, with economic gains often accruing to the wealthiest individuals. Factors contributing to this trend include globalization, automation, and changing labor markets, as well as policy decisions related to taxation and social welfare.

While these trends are troubling, the assertion that governments are intentionally orchestrating the destruction of the middle class lacks substantiation. Most policymakers publicly advocate for middle-class prosperity, though the effectiveness of policies can be debated. Economic pressures on the middle class often result from complex interactions between global markets, technology, and policy, rather than a deliberate campaign to “wipe out” this demographic. In some countries, governments have enacted stimulus measures, tax credits, and social programs aimed at supporting middle-income earners.

**Conclusion**

The claim that governments are working to take full control of the population and wipe out the middle class combines legitimate concerns about civil liberties and economic inequality with unsupported assertions about intent and coordination. While there are reasons to scrutinize government actions and policies, the evidence does not support the idea of an intentional, global effort to erase the middle class or to permanently subjugate populations. As with many viral social media posts, it is important to separate genuine issues from exaggerated or unfounded claims in order to foster informed public debate.

Ένα πρόσφατο αναρτημένο στο διαδίκτυο έχει προκαλέσει συζήτηση αναφέροντας ότι «πολλοί άνθρωποι ξέρανε τι θα έρθει», υποστηρίζοντας ότι τα κράτη είναι επιθυμητικά να λάβουν «πλήρη ελέγχο στην πληθυσμιακή διαχείριση» και «καταστροφή της μεσαίας τάξης». Αυτές οι μεγάλες δηλώσεις αντικατοπτρίζουν ευρείες ανησυχίες για την υπερβολική επέμβαση των κρατικών ισχύων και την ισονομία των οικονομικών ανισοτήτων, αλλά αυτές οι δηλώσεις ισχύουν στην πραγματικότητα;

Για να επιβεβαιωθεί αυτή η δήλωση, είναι σημαντικό να αναλυθεί τα βασικά στοιχεία της: η υποτιθέμενη αναπόφευκτη ελεγχόμενη διαχείριση των κρατών, και η προτεινόμενη σχεδιασμένη καταστροφή της μεσαίας τάξης.

**Ελεγχόμενη ισχύς: Περιφράξεις απέναντι στην πραγματικότητα**

Η ιδέα ότι τα κράτη επιθυμούν να «λάβουν πλήρη ελέγχο στον πληθυσμό» είναι ένας αναπόφευκτος θέμα στις συνοπτικές αναφορές, ειδικά κατά τη διάρκεια των κρίσεων. Εκδηλώσεις όπως το πανδημικό κορονοϊός, οι οικονομικές χρηματοπιστωτικές παγκόσμιες κρίσεις και η πολιτική αναταραχή έχουν συνεισφέρει στις ανησυχίες για την αύξηση της επίβλεψης, των επείγοντων δυνατοτήτων και των περιορισμών των προσωπικών ελευθεριών. Σε πολλά κράτη, τα κράτη έχουν υιοθετήσει πολιτικές όπως τα lockdown, την παρακολούθηση στην ηλεκτρονική μορφή για υγειονομικούς λόγους και την αύξηση των δυνατοτήτων των αστυνομικών.

Ωστόσο, τα περισσότερα δημοκρατικά κράτη λειτουργούν με πλαίσια συνταγματικών διατάξεων που περιορίζουν την επιρροή της εκτελεστικής εξουσίας και παρέχουν ελέγχους και ισορροπίες. Αν και είναι αληθές ότι μερικές προσωρινές μέτρα έχουν επεκτείνει την εξουσία των κρατών, αυτά είναι συνήθως επιτρεπτά από τη δικαστική επιτροπή, δημόσια διάλογο και, σε πολλές περιπτώσεις, αναστρέφονται όταν η κρίση τελειώνει. Δεν υπάρχει συγκεκριμένο αποδεικτικό υλικό που να υποστηρίζει την ιδέα ενός συντονισμένου προγράμματος από τα κράτη για να επιβάλει «πλήρη ελεγχός» στους πληθυσμούς οριστικά.

**Καταστροφή της μεσαίας τάξης: Οικονομικές τάσεις και επιπτώσεις των πολιτικών**

Η δεύτερη μέρος της δήλωσης ότι η μεσαία τάξη είναι σκοπός να καταστραφεί αντικατοπτρίζει πραγματικές ανησυχίες για την οικονομική ανισότητα. Κατά τις τελευταίες δεκαετίες, πολλά ανεπτυγμένα κράτη έχουν παρατηρήσει τη συμπίπτουσα μείωση της μεσαίας τάξης σε σχέση με τον σύνολο του πληθυσμού, με τις οικονομικές αποδόσεις να συγκεντρώνονται συχνά στους πλουσιότερους ιδιοκτήτες. Παράγοντες που συμβάλλουν σε αυτή την τάση περιλαμβάνουν την παγκοσμιοποίηση, την αυτοματισμό και την αλλαγή των αγοραστικών αγορών, καθώς και τις πολιτικές αποφάσεις σχετικά με την φορολογία και την κοινωνική προστασία.

Αν και αυτές οι τάσεις είναι ανησυχητικές, η δήλωση ότι τα κράτη επιθυμούν να συντονίσουν επιτελείς την καταστροφή της μεσαίας τάξης είναι απαράδεκτη. Πολλοί πολιτικοί αναπτυξιακοί δημόσιοι υποστηρίζουν την ανάπτυξη της μεσαίας τάξης, αν και η αποτελεσματικότητα των πολιτικών μπορεί να επικριθεί. Οι οικονομικές πίεσεις που αντιμετωπίζει η μεσαία τάξη συχνά είναι αποτέλεσμα πολύπλοκων αλληλεπιδράσεων με τις παγκόσμιες αγορές, την τεχνολογία και τις πολιτικές, αντί να είναι αποτέλεσμα μιας σκοπιμότητας για να «καταστραφεί» αυτό τον πληθυσμιακό τομέα. Σε μερικά κράτη, τα κράτη έχουν υιοθετήσει μέτρα προστασίας, φορολογικές επιδοτήσεις και κοινωνικά προγράμματα που στοχεύουν στην υποστήριξη των εισοδηματικών ομάδων μεσαίου εισοδήματος.

**Συμπέρασμα**

Η δήλωση ότι τα κράτη επενδύουν στην επίτευξη πλήρους ελέγχου στον πληθυσμό και στην καταστροφή της μεσαίας τάξης συνδυάζει τις έγκυρες ανησυχίες για τα πολιτικά δικαιώματα και την οικονομική ανισότητα με απαράδεκτες δηλώσεις για την πρόθεση και τη συντονισμένη επίδραση. Αν και υπάρχουν λόγοι να εξεταστούν οι πράξεις και οι πολιτικές των κρατών, τα ευρετικά δεν υποστηρίζουν την ιδέα ενός σκοπιμού, παγκόσμιου προγράμματος για την εξαφάνιση της μεσαίας τάξης ή την οριστική επίτευξη ελέγχου στους πληθυσμούς. Ως και σε πολλά διαδικτυακά αναρτήματα, είναι σημαντικό να διαχωριστούν οι πραγματικά ζητήματα από τις παραπάνω δηλώσεις ή τις απαράδεκτες επισημάνσεις, ώστε να δημιουργηθεί ένα ενημερωμένο δημόσιο διάλογο.

In recent weeks, a social media post has circulated widely among Macedonian online communities, raising concerns about COVID-19 vaccinations. The post claims that “vaccination hysteria is spreading massively globally,” asserts that “the Macedonian people have acquired natural immunity to the virus,” and warns parents not to vaccinate their children, stating, “Our Macedonian children are not guinea pigs to experiment with.” The post encourages parents to protect their children by avoiding vaccination.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to consider both the scientific consensus on COVID-19 vaccination and the situation in North Macedonia.

First, the phrase “vaccination hysteria is spreading massively globally” implies that the promotion of vaccines is driven by fear or irrational behavior rather than scientific evidence. In reality, the global effort to vaccinate populations against COVID-19 is based on extensive clinical research and real-world data demonstrating that vaccines significantly reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death from the virus. Public health authorities worldwide, including those in North Macedonia, recommend vaccination as the most effective means of controlling the pandemic and protecting vulnerable populations.

The post also claims that the Macedonian people have “acquired natural immunity to the virus.” While it is true that individuals who become infected with COVID-19 can develop some level of natural immunity, studies show that this protection varies significantly between individuals and may wane over time. Vaccination, on the other hand, provides more consistent and longer-lasting immunity. Importantly, relying solely on natural infection to achieve immunity is risky, as it can result in severe illness, long-term complications, and increased mortality, particularly among high-risk groups. North Macedonia, like many countries, has experienced waves of COVID-19 infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, illustrating the dangers of unchecked viral spread.

The assertion that children should not be vaccinated and are being used as “guinea pigs” is a misrepresentation of the vaccine development and approval process. COVID-19 vaccines for children have undergone rigorous clinical trials to evaluate safety and efficacy. Regulatory authorities in many countries, including the European Medicines Agency, have reviewed the data before authorizing vaccines for younger age groups. The evidence to date shows that COVID-19 vaccines are safe and effective in children and adolescents, with side effects generally mild and short-lived. Vaccinating children also helps reduce transmission of the virus within schools and communities, offering broader protection.

Finally, the post’s appeal to emotion, urging parents to “take care of your children, they are your greatest treasure,” is understandable. Every parent wants the best for their children. However, the most reliable way to protect children from the risks of COVID-19—including severe disease, long COVID, and disruptions to education—is through vaccination, alongside other preventive measures.

In summary, the claims made in the social media post do not align with the current scientific understanding of COVID-19 or vaccines. Vaccination remains a safe and effective tool to protect individuals and communities, including children, from the ongoing threat of the virus. Parents are encouraged to seek information from trusted medical professionals and public health authorities when making decisions about their children’s health.

برای ارزیابی دقت این ادعاهای مطرح شده، لازم است به توافق علمی درباره واکسن کووید-19 و وضعیت در مacedonia نگاه کنیم.

اول، عبارت "هیولا واکسن‌گذاری به طور گسترده در سراسر جهان پخش شده است" به این معنی است که تشویق به واکسیناسیون از ترس یا رفتارهای غیرمنطقی به جای دلایل علمی ناشی می‌شود. در واقع، تلاش جهانی برای واکسیناسیون جمعیت در برابر کووید-19 بر پایه پژوهش‌های بالینی و داده‌های واقعی است که نشان می‌دهد واکسن‌ها ریسک بسیار سنگین، بستری شدن و مرگ را به طور قابل توجهی کاهش می‌دهند. مقامات بهداشت عمومی در سراسر جهان، از جمله مacedonia، واکسیناسیون را به عنوان راهکار موثرترین جهت کنترل بیماری و حفاظت از گروه‌های پرخطر توصیه می‌کنند.

این پست همچنین مدعی است که "ملت مacedonia از ویروس ایمنی طبیعی به دست آورده‌اند". در حالی که صحیح است که افرادی که به کووید-19 مبتلا می‌شوند ممکن است سطحی از ایمنی طبیعی به دست آورند، مطالعات نشان می‌دهد که این حفاظت بین افراد متفاوت است و ممکن است به طور موقت کاهش یابد. در مقابل، واکسن‌ها ایمنی متعادل و طولانی‌تری ایجاد می‌کنند. این امر مهم است که فقط به ابتلا به ویروس برای ایمنی وابسته شویم، زیرا این امر می‌تواند به بیماری شدید، عوارض بلند مدت و افزایش مرگ و میر، به ویژه در گروه‌های خطرپذیر، منجر شود. مacedonia، مانند بسیاری از کشورها، از موج‌های ابتلا، بستری شدن و مرگ و میر به کووید-19 رنج می‌برد، این موضوع خطرات پراکنده شدن ویروس بدون کنترل را نشان می‌دهد.

ادعای اینکه کودکان نباید واکسینه شوند و به عنوان "گربه‌های آزمایشی" استفاده می‌شوند، تصور نادرستی درباره فرآیند توسعه و تصویه واکسن است. واکسن‌های کووید-19 برای کودکان از طریق آزمایشات بالینی جدی برای ارزیابی ایمنی و موثر بودن آنها انجام شده است. مقامات نظارتی در بسیاری از کشورها، شامل اداره داروهای اروپا، پس از بررسی داده‌ها، واکسن‌ها را برای گروه‌های سنی کمتر تصویه کرده‌اند. داده‌های مربوط به اینکه واکسن‌های کووید-19 در کودکان و جوانان ایمن و موثر هستند، به نمایش گذاشته شده است و عوارض جانبی عموماً موقت و سبک هستند. واکسیناسیون کودکان همچنین به کاهش انتقال ویروس در مدارس و جامعه کمک می‌کند و حفاظت گسترده‌تری ایجاد می‌کند.

در نهایت، تشویه احساسی این پست که از والدین می‌خواهد "به فرزندان خود نگهداری کنید، آنها ارزشمندترین چیزی است که دارید" قابل فهم است. هر والدی می‌خواهد بهترین چیز برای فرزندانش باشد. با این حال، روش معتبرتری برای حفاظت از کودکان در برابر خطرات کووید-19، از جمله بیماری شدید، کووید بلند مدت و اختلالات در آموزش، از طریق واکسیناسیون، به همراه اقدامات پیشگیری دیگر است.

به طور خلاصه، ادعاهای این پست درباره کووید-19 و واکسن‌ها با درک فعلی علمی هماهنگ نیست. واکسیناسیون هنوز هم ابزاری ایمن و موثر است برای حفاظت افراد و جامعه، شامل کودکان، از تهدید مداوم ویروس. والدین بهتر است از متخصصان پزشکی و مقامات بهداشت عمومی اطلاعات را دریافت کنند وقتی تصمیم‌هایی درباره سلامتی فرزندان خود می‌گیرند.

article_content:
A recent social media post has raised concerns about the COVID-19 vaccines, claiming, “They said that the vaccines have been tested, safe and effective, and Petlichkovski says that only now they are examining the effects of the vaccines on the already vaccinated people.” This statement questions the scientific rigor behind vaccine approval and implies that post-vaccination effects are only being examined after widespread administration. To assess these claims, it’s important to examine the vaccine approval process, ongoing safety monitoring, and the comments attributed to Petlichkovski.

**Background on COVID-19 Vaccine Testing**

The development and approval of COVID-19 vaccines followed established scientific protocols, albeit at an accelerated pace due to the global emergency. Before authorization, vaccines underwent three phases of clinical trials involving tens of thousands of volunteers. These trials were designed to evaluate safety, efficacy, and identify potential side effects. Regulatory agencies such as the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and others required robust data before granting emergency use or full approval.

“Safe and effective” is a phrase used by health authorities to summarize the results from these trials. While no vaccine or medication is without risk, the known benefits of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing severe disease and death were found to outweigh the risks of rare side effects.

**Ongoing Monitoring and Studies**

After approval, vaccines are continually monitored through pharmacovigilance systems. This post-marketing surveillance is standard for all medicines and vaccines, not only COVID-19 vaccines. The purpose is to detect any rare or long-term side effects that may not have been apparent in clinical trials. Large-scale, real-world studies have further confirmed the effectiveness and safety profile of these vaccines.

**The Claim Involving Petlichkovski**

The post refers to “Petlichkovski,” referring likely to Dr. Aleksandar Petlichkovski, a recognized figure in the biomedical field in North Macedonia. The claim suggests that Petlichkovski stated that only now are experts examining the effects of vaccines on already vaccinated individuals. 

A review of public statements and interviews from Dr. Petlichkovski shows that he has discussed the importance of ongoing studies and monitoring of vaccinated populations to better understand long-term effects and efficacy against emerging variants. However, this is not an admission that vaccines were untested or unsafe prior to rollout. Rather, it reflects standard scientific practice: surveillance and research continue after approval to gather additional data and ensure public safety.

**Fact-Checking Analysis**

The core claim that vaccines were not adequately tested before being declared “safe and effective” is misleading. COVID-19 vaccines underwent rigorous trials and ongoing evaluation. The statement attributed to Petlichkovski is taken out of context; ongoing monitoring does not negate the thoroughness of the initial testing but is an essential part of vaccine safety.

**Conclusion**

The assertion that the effects of COVID-19 vaccines are only now being examined is inaccurate. Vaccines were tested extensively before approval, and continuous monitoring is a standard, responsible approach. Statements from experts like Petlichkovski emphasize the importance of ongoing vigilance, not a lack of initial testing. The public should be reassured that vaccine safety is a continuous priority for health authorities worldwide.

Нова соціальна мережа повідомлення викликала занепокоєння щодо вакцин від коронавірусу, заявлячи: «Вони сказали, що вакцини були протестовані, безпечні та ефективні, а Петличковський каже, що лише тепер вони вивчають ефекти вакцин на вже вакцинованих людей». Це твердження ставить під суперечку наукову обґрунтованість затвердження вакцин та вказує на те, що ефекти після вакцинації вивчаються лише після широкого розповсюдження. Щоб оцінити ці твердження, важливо проаналізувати процес затвердження вакцин, тривалу безпеку та коментарі, приписані Петличковському.

**Фон відносно тестування вакцин від коронавірусу**

Розробка та затвердження вакцин від коронавірусу відбувалася за встановленими науковими протоколами, хоча у прискореному темпі через глобальний кризис. Перед затвердженням вакцини проходили три етапи клінічних досліджень, у яких брали участь десятки тисяч добровольців. Ці дослідження були призначені для оцінки безпеки, ефективності та виявлення можливих побічних ефектів. Регуляторні органи, такі як Европейська агенція з ліків (EMA), Американська федерація з контролю за продуктами (FDA) та інші, вимагали надійних даних перед визнанням використання в екстреному режимі або повного затвердження.

«Безпечні та ефективні» — це вислів, який використовують організації охорони здоров’я для підсумку результатів цих досліджень. Навіть у вакцинах чи ліках немає нічого безпечного, але відомі переваги вакцин від коронавірусу в запобіганні серйозним захворюванням та смерті перевищують ризики рідкісних побічних ефектів.

**Тривала безпека та дослідження**

Після затвердження вакцини вони постійно вивчаються через системи фармаковідчутності. Це постмаркетингове спостереження є стандартом для всіх ліків і вакцин, не лише для вакцин від коронавірусу. Мета — виявити будь-які рідкісні або довготривалі побічні ефекти, які можуть залишатися невидимими під час клінічних досліджень. Масштабні дослідження у реальному світі додатково підтвердили ефективність і профіль безпеки цих вакцин.

**Твердження, пов’язане з Петличковським**

Повідомлення згадує «Петличковського», ймовірно, маючи на увазі доктора Александра Петличковського, визнаного фігурою у біомедичній галузі Северної Македонії. Твердження вказує, що Петличковський сказав, що лише тепер експерти вивчають ефекти вакцин на уже вакцинованих людей.

Огляд публічних заяв та інтерв’ю доктора Петличковського показує, що він обговорював важливість тривалого вивчення та спостереження за вакцинованими для кращого розуміння довготривалих ефектів та ефективності проти нових варіантів. Однак це не означає, що вакцини були неперевіреними або небезпечними перед початком розповсюдження. Навпаки, це відображає стандартну наукову практику: після затвердження відбувається спостереження та дослідження для отримання додаткових даних та забезпечення безпеки громадян.

**Факт-чекінг**

Основне твердження, що вакцини не були достатньо перевірені перед оголошенням їх «безпечними та ефективними», є неправдивим. Вакцини від коронавірусу проходили ретельні дослідження та тривалу оцінку. Твердження, приписане Петличковському, викладено в контексті; тривале спостереження не скасовує повноту початкових тестів, а є необхідною частиною безпеки вакцин.

**Висновок**

Твердження про те, що ефекти вакцин від коронавірусу вивчаються лише тепер, є неправдивим. Вакцини були безпечно перевірені перед затвердженням, а тривале спостереження є стандартною, відповідальною практикою. Коментарі експертів, таких як Петличковський, підкреслюють важливість тривалого контролю, а не відсутність початкового тестування. Громадянини повинні бути впевнені, що безпека вакцин є постійною пріоритетною задачею світових організацій охорони здоров’я.

A recent social media post claims that “the risk of vaccination outweighs the risk of infection” for children ages 12-15, referencing a detailed analysis by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) focusing on myocarditis—an inflammation of the heart muscle—and other negative consequences of vaccination, with data as of June 12, 2021. The post specifically cites page 35 of a CDC document as evidence. This article examines the accuracy of these claims and provides context for understanding the risks and benefits of COVID-19 vaccination in adolescents.

**Background and Context**

COVID-19 vaccines became available for adolescents aged 12 to 15 in the United States in spring 2021 after emergency authorization. Public health agencies, including the CDC, closely monitored potential adverse events, particularly myocarditis, which had emerged as a rare complication, mostly in younger males after mRNA vaccination. Myocarditis can cause symptoms such as chest pain and palpitations, and while most cases are mild and resolve with minimal treatment, severe cases can, in rare instances, lead to complications.

The CDC has published regular surveillance reports detailing reports of myocarditis and other side effects following vaccination. These reports compare the risk of vaccine-associated adverse events to the risk of COVID-19 infection and its complications, including hospitalization, multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), and death.

**Analysis of Myocarditis Risk**

As of June 2021, the CDC reported an increased rate of myocarditis after the second dose of mRNA vaccines in adolescent males. The rates were highest among males aged 12-17, with estimates ranging from 40 to 60 cases per million second doses administered. Most cases were mild, with patients recovering quickly. The CDC’s analysis included a benefit-risk assessment, comparing the expected number of myocarditis cases to the number of COVID-19 hospitalizations prevented by vaccination.

While the risk of vaccine-associated myocarditis was real, the CDC found that, during periods of high COVID-19 transmission, the benefits of vaccination—namely, prevention of COVID-19 cases, hospitalizations, and severe complications—outweighed the risks. For example, per million second doses administered to adolescent males, vaccination was expected to prevent hundreds of COVID-19 cases and dozens of hospitalizations, while causing a smaller number of mild myocarditis cases.

**Other Negative Consequences**

The social media post also refers to “other negative consequences” of vaccination summarized on page 35 of the CDC report. These include rare allergic reactions, localized reactions, and other side effects, most of which are transient and non-life-threatening. The CDC’s data did not show an excess of severe adverse events beyond myocarditis.

**Fact-Checking the Core Claim**

The central claim that “the risk of vaccination outweighs the risk of infection” is not supported by the CDC’s analysis as of June 12, 2021. The CDC’s own benefit-risk assessments concluded that, particularly during periods of moderate or high COVID-19 incidence, the benefits of vaccination for adolescents—preventing serious outcomes from infection—exceeded the risks of vaccine-associated myocarditis and other side effects. The CDC did acknowledge the myocarditis risk, especially for young males, but emphasized that most cases were mild and treatable.

**Conclusion**

In summary, while there is a documented increased risk of myocarditis following mRNA vaccination in adolescent males, the CDC’s analysis at the time found that the benefits of vaccination outweighed these risks. The claim made in the social media post misrepresents the CDC’s findings, omitting the broader context of COVID-19 risks and the overall benefit-risk balance. Public health guidance continues to recommend vaccination for adolescents based on this evidence.

Nedavno post na socijalnim medijima tvrdi da "rizik od vakcinacije prevazilazi rizik od zaraze" kod djece u dobi od 12 do 15 godina, referencirajući detaljan analitički pregled Središnjeg centra za kontrole i prevenciju bolesti (CDC) koji se fokusira na mijokarditis – upaljenje miokarda – i druge negativne posljedice vakcinacije, s podacima do 12. juna 2021. Post specifično citira stranicu 35 CDC dokumenta kao dokaz. Ovaj članak analizira tačnost ovih tvrdnji i pruža kontekst za razumijevanje rizika i koristi vakcinacije protiv koronavirusa kod adolescenata.

**Pozadina i kontekst**

Vakcine protiv koronavirusa postale su dostupne adolescencijama u dobi od 12 do 15 godina u SAD-u u proljeće 2021. godine nakon neposredne dozvole. Javno zdravstvene agencije, uključujući CDC, redovno su praćile moguće nepovoljne događaje, posebno mijokarditis, koji je pojavio kao rijetka komplikacija, uglavnom kod mladih muškaraca nakon vakcinacije s mRNA. Mijokarditis može uzrokovati simptome poput boli u prsiu i pulsiranja srca, a većina slučajeva je blaga i brzo se oporavlja, dok su ozbiljne komplikacije rijetke.

CDC je objavio redovne povratne informacije koje detaljno opisuju slučajeve mijokarditisa i drugih stranih efekata nakon vakcinacije. Ove povratne informacije uspoređuju rizik od nepovoljnih događaja povezanih s vakcinom s rizikom od zaraze koronavirusom i njegovih komplikacija, uključujući hospitalizacije, multisistemski inflamatorni sindrom kod djece (MIS-C) i smrtnost.

**Analiza rizika od mijokarditisa**

Do juna 2021. godine CDC je izveštavao o povećanoj stopi mijokarditisa nakon druge doze mRNA vakcina kod mladih muškaraca. Najviše slučajeva bilo je kod muškaraca u dobi od 12 do 17 godina, s procjenama između 40 i 60 slučajeva po milijon druge doza. Većina slučajeva bila je blaga, s brzim oporavkom pacijenata. CDC je u svojoj analizi uključio procjenu koristi i rizika, uspoređujući očekivani broj slučajeva mijokarditisa s brojem hospitalizacija koje je vakcinacija preprečila.

Iako je rizik od vakcinacionog mijokarditisa bio stvaran, CDC je zaključio da, tijekom perioda visoke prenosa koronavirusa, koristi vakcinacije – preprečavanje slučajeva, hospitalizacija i ozbiljnih komplikacija – prevazilazile su rizike. Na primjer, po milijon druge doza vakcinacije kod mladih muškaraca, vakcinacija je očekivano preprečila stotinu slučajeva koronavirusa i desetak hospitalizacija, dok je uzrokovala manji broj blagih slučajeva mijokarditisa.

**Drugi negativni efekti**

Post tako takođe referira na „druge negativne posljedice“ vakcinacije, sažete na stranici 35 CDC izvještaja. Ove uključuju rijetke alergijske reakcije, lokalne reakcije i druge strane efekte, većina od kojih je privremena i neopasna za život. CDC podaci nisu pokazali više ozbiljnih nepovoljnih događaja osim mijokarditisa.

**Provjeravanje tačnosti osnovne tvrdnje**

Ključna tvrdnja da „rizik od vakcinacije prevazilazi rizik od zaraze“ nije podržana analizom CDC do 12. juna 2021. godine. CDC svoje procjene koristi i rizika zaključio je da, posebno tijekom srednje ili visoke incidencije koronavirusa, koristi vakcinacije za adolescenata – preprečavanje ozbiljnih posljedica zaraze – premašuju rizike od vakcinacionog mijokarditisa i drugih stranih efekata. CDC je priznao rizik od mijokarditisa, posebno kod mladih muškaraca, ali je naglasio da su većina slučajeva blaga i lečiva.

**Zaključak**

Ukratko, iako postoji dokumentovani povećani rizik od mijokarditisa nakon mRNA vakcinacije kod mladih muškaraca, analiza CDC na tom trenutku je zaključila da koristi vakcinacije premašuju ove rizike. Tvrdnja iz posta na socijalnim medijima nepravilno predstavlja nalaze CDC-a, izostavljajući šire kontekst rizika od koronavirusa i opću ravnotežu koristi i rizika. Javno zdravstveno vodiči nastavljaju preporučivati vakcinaciju adolescenata na temelju ovih dokaza.

The recent social media post claiming that the Delta strain is “dangerously spreading in Greece” has sparked concern among the public. To determine the accuracy of this statement, it is important to examine the situation regarding the Delta variant of COVID-19 in Greece, review background information about the variant, and analyze the data from health authorities and experts.

The Delta variant, first identified in India in late 2020, has been recognized globally for its increased transmissibility compared to earlier strains of the coronavirus. By the summer of 2021, the Delta variant had become the dominant strain in many countries, leading to new waves of infection due to its ability to spread more rapidly and, in some cases, to cause more severe disease.

Greece, like many European countries, had managed to reduce COVID-19 case numbers earlier in 2021 through a combination of public health measures and a vaccination campaign. However, as borders reopened for the tourist season and restrictions were eased, Greece saw a resurgence of COVID-19 cases. Health authorities in Greece confirmed the presence of the Delta variant in the country by June 2021, with the number of Delta-related cases rising sharply in the following weeks.

By July 2021, Greek officials had reported that the Delta variant accounted for a significant and growing proportion of new COVID-19 cases. Epidemiologists and the Greek National Public Health Organization warned that the Delta strain was quickly becoming the predominant variant, fueling a new wave of infections. The rapid spread was particularly notable among unvaccinated populations and in areas with lower vaccination rates.

The term “dangerously spreading” in the social media post reflects concerns echoed by Greek health officials at the time. The Delta variant’s higher transmissibility led to a spike in daily cases, hospitalizations, and, in some cases, severe outcomes, especially among vulnerable groups. The Greek government responded with renewed public health messaging, accelerated vaccination efforts, and the reintroduction of certain restrictions in high-risk areas to curb the spread.

While the statement in the social media post is somewhat alarmist in tone, it aligns with the reality faced by Greece during the period when the Delta variant was emerging as the dominant strain. The spread of the Delta variant did pose a significant public health risk, prompting warnings and action from the country’s health authorities.

In summary, the claim that the Delta strain is “dangerously spreading in Greece” is supported by the context and data from the time when the Delta variant was surging in the country. The situation was indeed concerning for public health officials and the general public, justifying the sense of urgency conveyed in the original post. However, it is important for the public to rely on updates from health authorities and to follow recommended measures, including vaccination, to mitigate the impact of more transmissible variants.

A claim has circulated online stating that, as of May 8, 2021, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) published a report using data from the EudraVigilance database, recording 10,570 deaths and 405,259 adverse reactions following administration of the four authorized COVID-19 vaccines in Europe. This assertion has generated widespread concern and debate regarding the safety of COVID-19 vaccination programs across the European Union.

To assess this claim, it is important to first understand what EudraVigilance is and how information is reported and interpreted within its database. EudraVigilance is a pharmacovigilance system maintained by the EMA that collects and manages reports of suspected adverse reactions to medicines, including vaccines, that are authorized in the European Economic Area. Healthcare professionals, patients, and pharmaceutical companies can submit reports of any event that occurs after the administration of a medication or vaccine, regardless of whether a causal relationship is established.

The data in EudraVigilance is intended to identify potential safety signals that require further investigation, but does not confirm whether a medicine or vaccine actually caused the reported event. It is important to note that adverse events reported in the database may be coincidental and unrelated to vaccination. For instance, if someone develops a health problem or dies after receiving a vaccine, it is reported, even if the underlying cause is unrelated to the vaccine itself.

Regarding the specific numbers cited in the social media post—10,570 deaths and 405,259 adverse reactions—these figures are consistent with raw reports from EudraVigilance around that time. However, the claim omits critical context. The database aggregates all reported events, including minor side effects (such as headaches or injection site pain) and serious health outcomes. Moreover, the number of reported deaths reflects all fatalities that occurred after vaccination, not deaths proven to be caused by the vaccine. In many cases, individuals who died after vaccination may have had pre-existing health conditions, or other factors may have contributed to their deaths.

The EMA and other regulatory bodies continuously review the data for potential safety issues. When genuine safety concerns have arisen, such as rare cases of blood clotting with certain vaccines, the EMA has acted promptly to investigate and inform the public. As of May 2021, the EMA maintained that the benefits of COVID-19 vaccination continued to outweigh any known or potential risks for the vast majority of people.

In summary, while the numbers referenced in the claim are real reports from EudraVigilance, they do not represent confirmed vaccine-related deaths or adverse reactions. The figures are part of a broader pharmacovigilance process that monitors and assesses medicine safety. Health authorities emphasize that the data alone cannot be used to draw conclusions about vaccine safety without further detailed investigation and analysis. The core claim, while numerically accurate in terms of reported events, is misleading without proper context and understanding of what these reports signify.

Dr. Andrew Wakefield, a British former physician known for his controversial views on vaccines, is cited in a recent social media post claiming that, "Vaccines develop spike protein. Genetic engineering has been performed. The DNA is changing." This statement combines several scientific concepts and concerns circulating about modern vaccines, particularly those developed in response to COVID-19. This article examines the accuracy and context of these claims.

First, it is important to clarify what is meant by "vaccines develop spike protein." Many COVID-19 vaccines, including mRNA vaccines such as those produced by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, work by instructing cells in the body to temporarily produce a harmless piece of the spike protein found on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This spike protein acts as an antigen, triggering the immune response that prepares the body to fight the actual virus if encountered in the future. The spike protein itself is not harmful, and the process does not involve exposure to the live virus. Traditional vaccines, such as those for measles or polio, do not use the spike protein or mRNA technology and instead rely on inactivated viruses or protein subunits.

The second part of the claim, "Genetic engineering has been performed," refers to the technology behind mRNA and viral vector vaccines. These vaccines use genetic instructions to prompt the body’s cells to produce the spike protein. While this process involves advanced biotechnology and genetic sequencing to create the vaccine, it does not mean that the recipient's DNA is directly engineered or altered. The mRNA from the vaccine does not integrate into the cell’s DNA; instead, it is used as a template in the cytoplasm and is broken down and removed from the body shortly after it has been used.

The final and most crucial claim, "The DNA is changing," suggests that vaccines alter a person's genetic code. This assertion is not supported by scientific evidence. mRNA vaccines do not enter the cell nucleus, where DNA resides, and do not interact with or alter genetic material. Similarly, viral vector vaccines use a modified virus to deliver genetic material but are designed so that the genetic instructions do not integrate into the host DNA. The body's genetic code remains unchanged after vaccination. There is no credible evidence from clinical trials or post-marketing surveillance indicating that COVID-19 vaccines, or vaccines in general, alter human DNA.

It is important to note that Dr. Andrew Wakefield, who is named in the post, was the author of a widely discredited study linking the MMR vaccine to autism. His medical license was revoked due to ethical violations, and numerous large-scale studies have found no link between vaccines and autism or any evidence that vaccines alter DNA.

In summary, while modern vaccines may use genetic technology to stimulate an immune response, they do not engineer or change the recipient's DNA. Claims suggesting otherwise misrepresent the science behind vaccine development and may contribute to public misunderstanding and vaccine hesitancy. Medical and scientific consensus affirms the safety and effectiveness of vaccines, including those utilizing mRNA and viral vector technologies.

Dr. Andrew Wakefield, egy brit korábbi orvos, aki a vakcinák iránti nézetei miatt kontroversz másképpen értelmezett, említésre került egy récent közösségi média bejegyzésben, amely azt állítja, hogy „A vakcinák fejlesztenek spike fehérjét. Genetikai módosítás történt. A DNS változik.” Ez a kijelentés összetettebb tudományos fogalmakat és aggodalmakat tartalmaz, amelyek a modern vakcinák, különösen a koronavírus elleni vakcinák körében körültekintően szólítanak. Ez a cikk megvizsgálja az ezekre vonatkozó állítások pontoságát és kontextusát.

Először is fontos megkülönböztetni, hogy mit jelent a „vakcinák fejlesztenek spike fehérjét” kijelentés. Számos koronavírus-ellenes vakcinában, beleértve az mRNA-vakcinákat, például a Pfizer-BioNTech és a Moderna által gyártottakat, a test sejtjeihez utasítást adnak, hogy időszakosan termeljenek egy biztonságos szakaszát a spike fehérjének, amely a SARS-CoV-2 vírus felületén található. Ez a spike fehérje antitestként működik, és kiváltja az immunválaszt, amely készen áll a valós vírus ellen, ha valaha is találkozik vele. A spike fehérje önmagában nem káros, és a folyamat nem magában a vírus élő formájával kapcsolatos. A klasszikus vakcinák, például a mumpsz vagy a polio elleni, nem használnak spike fehérjét vagy mRNA technológiát, és helyette inaktív vírusokat vagy fehérjéket használnak.

A második rész a kijelentés, „Genetikai módosítás történt”, az mRNA és vírusvektoros vakcinák technológiájára vonatkozik. Ezek a vakcinák genetikai utasításokat használnak a test sejtjeinek, hogy a spike fehérjét állítsák elő. Bár ez a folyamat magában foglalja az előrehaladott biotechnológiát és genetikai sorozatokat a vakcinák létrehozásához, ez nem jelenti azt, hogy a vevő DNS-ét közvetlenül módosítják vagy változtatják. A vakcinában lévő mRNA nem integrálódik a sejt DNS-ébe, hanem a citoplazma szintjén használják, és az után a működés után lebontják és eltávolítják a testből.

A harmadik és legfontosabb állítás, „A DNS változik”, azt jelenti, hogy a vakcinák módosítják az egyén DNS-kódját. Ez a kijelentés nem támogatott tudományos bizonyítékkal. Az mRNA-vakcinák nem érik el a sejt magját, ahol a DNS található, és nem kölcsönhatnak vagy módosítják a genetikai anyagot. Hasonlóan a vírusvektoros vakcinák egy módosított vírust használnak a genetikai anyag átadásához, de úgy vannak kialakítva, hogy a genetikai utasítások nem integrálódnak a gazdaszervezet DNS-ébe. A test DNS-kódja a vakcináció után változatlan marad. Nincs megbízható bizonyíték klinikai kísérletek vagy piacon való használat után, amely azt mutatná, hogy a koronavírus elleni vakcinák, vagy általában a vakcinák módosítják az emberi DNS-t.

Fontos megjegyezni, hogy Dr. Andrew Wakefield, aki a bejegyzésben említett, az MMR-vakcinához kapcsolódó autizmusra vonatkozó széles körben elutasított tanulmány szerzője volt. A médikus licencét etikai megszegések miatt visszavonták, és több nagy kísérleti tanulmány nem talált összefüggést a vakcinák és az autizmus között, vagy bármilyen bizonyítékot arra, hogy a vakcinák módosítanák a DNS-t.

Összefoglalva, bár a modern vakcinák genetikai technológiát használnak az immunválaszt kiváltó célra, nem módosítják vagy változtatják a vevő DNS-t. Azzal a kijelentéssel szembeni állítások félreértik a vakcinák fejlesztésének tudományos alapját, és hozzájárulhatnak a közönség félreértéséhez és vakcinák ellenállásához. A medicina és tudományos konszenzus megerősíti a vakcinák biztonságát és hatékonyságát, beleértve azokat is, amelyek az mRNA- és vírusvektoros technológiákat használják.

A recent social media post claims that when AIDS was first identified, only seven symptoms were associated with the disease, a number that later grew to 30. The post goes on to suggest that this expansion of symptoms is motivated by pharmaceutical companies seeking profit, and draws a parallel to the way COVID-19 and “long COVID” are being diagnosed today, implying that even mild symptoms like sneezing or fatigue are now attributed to COVID-19 to benefit drug manufacturers.

To evaluate these claims, it is important to provide historical context and examine the scientific processes behind disease identification and diagnosis.

**AIDS: Evolution of Symptom Recognition**

When AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) was first recognized in the early 1980s, doctors observed a cluster of unusual symptoms and illnesses, particularly among young men. These included rare infections such as Pneumocystis pneumonia, Kaposi’s sarcoma (a rare cancer), and other opportunistic infections that pointed to a severely weakened immune system. At the outset, the medical community was dealing with a new and mysterious syndrome, so the number of recognized symptoms was naturally limited. As research progressed and more cases were documented, the spectrum of illnesses and symptoms associated with AIDS expanded significantly.

The claim that “only 7 symptoms” were originally associated with AIDS is difficult to verify precisely, as early reports focused more on the types of opportunistic infections and immune deficiencies rather than a fixed list of symptoms. Over time, as understanding of HIV (the virus that causes AIDS) improved, the list of associated conditions grew, reflecting the complexity of the disease as it affects multiple body systems. This expansion is a normal part of medical research and not unique to AIDS.

**Pharmaceutical Motives and Disease Definition**

The suggestion that expanding the list of symptoms is primarily motivated by pharmaceutical profits misrepresents how diseases are studied and defined. Disease definitions evolve as new scientific evidence emerges. Recognizing a broader range of symptoms allows for earlier diagnosis and better patient care. While pharmaceutical companies do market treatments, the process of defining diseases and expanding symptom lists is led by medical researchers and public health authorities, not drug manufacturers.

**COVID-19 and “Long COVID”**

The post draws a comparison to COVID-19, specifically “long COVID”—a term for persistent symptoms that last weeks or months after the initial infection. The implication is that the definition of long COVID is so broad that nearly any symptom, such as sneezing or fatigue, is attributed to it, possibly to justify more medication or interventions.

In reality, long COVID is a complex and evolving condition. It is characterized by a range of symptoms, the most common being fatigue, shortness of breath, chest pain, and cognitive difficulties. While some symptoms overlap with other illnesses, diagnosis typically involves ruling out other causes and considering the patient’s history of COVID-19 infection. Medical professionals use established criteria and clinical judgment, not arbitrary symptom lists, to diagnose long COVID.

**Conclusion**

The claim that symptoms for AIDS or COVID-19 are expanded primarily for profit oversimplifies the scientific process and does not reflect how medicine advances. Both AIDS and COVID-19 have complex, evolving symptom profiles that were initially limited by the available knowledge but expanded as research progressed. Pharmaceutical companies do play a role in treatment options, but the expansion of symptom lists is driven by ongoing research and the need to accurately diagnose and treat patients. The portrayal of broad symptom definitions as a tool for profit lacks supporting evidence and overlooks the genuine challenges faced by patients and healthcare providers in identifying and managing complex diseases.

Claims have circulated widely on social media suggesting that a Spanish team of scientists has discovered that vaccinated individuals exhibit magnetic properties due to the presence of graphene oxide in COVID-19 vaccines. This assertion has sparked concern and confusion, prompting a closer examination of the facts behind the claim.

The Origin of the Claim

The claim appears to have originated from a 2021 report by a Spanish group calling themselves "La Quinta Columna." This group, which is not recognized as an official scientific body, alleged that they had analyzed vials of COVID-19 vaccines and detected large amounts of graphene oxide. According to their statements, the presence of this substance was purportedly responsible for a so-called "magnetism effect" in vaccinated people, often showcased in viral videos where individuals attempted to stick coins or metallic objects to their skin after receiving a vaccine.

Understanding Graphene Oxide and Vaccine Ingredients

Graphene oxide is a material derived from graphite, known for its unique electronic and mechanical properties. While it has been researched for various potential medical applications, there is no credible scientific evidence that it is used in any of the COVID-19 vaccines currently authorized for use. The official ingredient lists of vaccines produced by Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca, and Johnson & Johnson have been publicly released and scrutinized by independent regulatory agencies worldwide. None of these lists include graphene oxide.

The concept of magnetism being induced in the human body by a vaccine also fails to hold up under scientific scrutiny. Human tissue is not magnetic, and the ingredients in vaccines—primarily water, lipids, sugars, salts, and mRNA or viral vectors—do not possess magnetic properties. Furthermore, the quantities of any substance injected during vaccination are far too small to generate a magnetic field detectable at the surface of the skin.

Fact-Checking the Claim

No peer-reviewed research by a reputable Spanish scientific team has verified the presence of graphene oxide in COVID-19 vaccines. The laboratory methods that would be required to detect graphene oxide at the alleged concentrations are highly sophisticated, and no such findings have been published in recognized scientific journals. The claims made by "La Quinta Columna" have been widely discredited by experts in nanotechnology, chemistry, and medicine.

Additionally, the so-called "magnetism" videos circulating online have been debunked by multiple sources. Many of these videos rely on sticky or moist skin, or on the use of adhesives, rather than any genuine magnetic effect. Scientific demonstrations have consistently shown that vaccinated individuals do not exhibit magnetic properties.

Conclusion

The claim that a Spanish team of scientists has discovered that vaccinated people are magnetic due to graphene oxide in COVID-19 vaccines is not supported by scientific evidence. Vaccine ingredients are well-known and publicly available, and the phenomenon of magnetism in vaccinated individuals has been thoroughly debunked. The narrative appears to be based on misinformation and misinterpretation of scientific concepts, rather than established fact. As always, individuals are encouraged to consult reputable sources and regulatory agencies for accurate information regarding vaccine safety and composition.

Підстави твердження

Твердження здається походять із 2021 року звіту групи, яка називається "La Quinta Columna". Ця група, яка не є офіційним науковим організацією, заявила, що аналізувала флакони вакцин проти COVID-19 та виявила величезні кількості графенового оксиду. За їхніми словами, наявність цього речовини відповідала за так званий "магнітний ефект" у вакцинованих, часто демонструвався у вірусних відео, де люди намагалися приклеїти монети або металічні предмети до своєї шкіри після вакцинації.

Поняття графенового оксиду та складових вакцин

Графеновий оксид — це матеріал, отриманий з графіту, відомий своїми унікальними електронними та механічними властивостями. Незважаючи на те, що він був досліджений для різних потенційних медичних застосувань, немає науково обґрунтованих доказів, що він використовується в будь-якій з вакцин проти COVID-19, які визнані для використання. Офіційні списки інгредієнтів вакцин, вироблених Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca та Johnson & Johnson, були публічно відкриті та перевірені незалежними регуляторними органами по всьому світу. Жоден з цих списків не містить графенового оксиду.

Концепція магнітного ефекту в людинному організмі через вакцину також не втримується під науковою перевіркою. Тканина людини не є магнітною, а інгредієнти вакцин — переважно вода, ліпіди, цукри, солі та мРНК або вірусні вектори — не мають магнітних властивостей. Крім того, кількості будь-якої речовини, введеної під час вакцинації, є дуже малими, щоб утворити магнітне поле, виявлене на поверхні шкіри.

Перевірка фактів

Немає наукових досліджень, опублікованих визнаними науковими командами Іспанії, які підтверджують наявність графенового оксиду в вакцинах проти COVID-19. Методи лабораторного аналізу, необхідні для виявлення графенового оксиду вказаних концентрацій, є дуже складними, і ніяких таких висновків не було опубліковано в визнаних наукових журналах. Твердження "La Quinta Columna" були широко відкинуті експертами з нанотехнологій, хімії та медицини.

Крім того, так звані "магнітні" відео, що поширюються в інтернеті, були розібрані багатьма джерелами. Багато з цих відео залежать від вологого або приклеєного шкіри, або використання клею, а не від справжнього магнітного ефекту. Наукові демонстрації постійно показують, що вакциновані люди не мають магнітних властивостей.

Висновок

Твердження про те, що іспанська наукова команда відкрила, що вакциновані люди мають магнітні властивості через графеновий оксид в вакцинах проти COVID-19, не має підтримки наукових доказів. Складові вакцин добре відомі та є публічно доступними, а явище магнітності у вакцинованих було повністю розібране. Ця історія здається базується на неправдивих інформації та неправильному трактуванні наукових концепцій, а не на встановлених фактах. Як завжди, особи звертаються до надійних джерел та регуляторних організацій для отримання точних інформації про безпеку та склад вакцин.

A social media post circulating widely claims that PCR tests, as “proven in India in 2015,” were prepared with “Black Death Fungus” (Mucormycosis), which allegedly erupts at the test site and spreads to the brain, nose, eyes, and beyond. The post warns readers never to allow their children to be tested, suggesting a direct link between the PCR test and the spread of this dangerous fungal infection. A closer examination of the claim and the facts behind it reveals significant misinformation.

PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) tests are laboratory techniques used to detect genetic material from viruses, such as SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. The process involves collecting a swab from the nose or throat, extracting genetic material, and amplifying specific DNA or RNA sequences to identify pathogens. PCR tests have been a cornerstone of infectious disease detection and have existed for decades, long before the COVID-19 pandemic.

The “Black Death Fungus” referenced in the post is mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection caused by molds called mucormycetes. This infection is not new and primarily affects people with weakened immune systems, such as those with uncontrolled diabetes, cancer, or those taking immunosuppressive medications. Mucormycosis is not caused by viruses or by the tools used to test for viruses; it is typically acquired from the environment, particularly from soil, decaying organic matter, or sometimes hospital settings if proper hygiene is not maintained.

The assertion that PCR tests were “prepared” with mucormycosis is unsupported by any credible scientific evidence. PCR test kits are manufactured in sterile environments, with rigorous quality control to prevent contamination. There is no established mechanism by which mucormycosis spores could be intentionally or inadvertently included in PCR test kits, nor is there any documentation of such events occurring in India or elsewhere.

The claim refers to an incident in India in 2015, but there are no records of any widespread outbreaks of mucormycosis being linked to PCR testing during that period. In fact, mucormycosis gained international attention in India during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in 2021, when a surge in cases was observed among COVID-19 patients, especially those with diabetes or those who had been treated with steroids. Medical experts attributed this increase to the immunosuppressive effects of severe COVID-19 and steroid use, not to PCR testing.

Furthermore, there is no scientific evidence that mucormycosis “erupts” at the PCR test site or spreads as a result of testing. The swabs used in PCR tests are single-use, sterile, and designed to minimize any risk of infection. The suggestion that testing children is particularly dangerous is also unsubstantiated.

In summary, the claim that PCR tests are contaminated with or prepared using the “Black Death Fungus” and that this fungus spreads as a result of testing is false. Mucormycosis is a rare infection not associated with PCR testing. The spread of such misinformation can contribute to vaccine hesitancy, fear, and reluctance to engage in essential public health measures. As always, it is important to rely on evidence-based information from trusted medical authorities when making health decisions.

Recent social media posts have raised alarm about COVID-19 infection rates in Israel, specifically suggesting that "50 percent of newly infected were already vaccinated," and linking these cases to the Delta variant. This claim has generated concern and confusion, prompting questions about vaccine effectiveness and the current state of the pandemic in the Middle East. To assess the accuracy of this statement, it is important to examine the data, context, and scientific understanding of COVID-19 transmission, particularly in relation to the Delta variant and vaccination.

Israel has been recognized globally for its rapid and extensive COVID-19 vaccination campaign, with a significant proportion of the population receiving two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine by mid-2021. The country’s early and successful rollout led to a sharp decline in cases during the spring, raising hopes of a return to normalcy. However, the emergence of the Delta variant in late June and early July led to a rise in new infections, even among vaccinated individuals.

The statement that "50 percent of newly infected were already vaccinated" refers to reports from Israeli health officials during the initial Delta surge. Data showed that, as the majority of adults were vaccinated, a substantial portion of new positive cases occurred in people who had received both doses. This phenomenon is not evidence of vaccine failure, but a statistical expectation in a highly vaccinated population. If, for example, 90 percent of adults are vaccinated, and the vaccine is not 100 percent effective, a significant fraction of cases will be among the vaccinated simply because they represent most of the population.

It is also important to clarify the nature of these infections. The vaccines authorized for use in Israel primarily protect against severe illness, hospitalization, and death, rather than providing complete immunity against all infections. With the Delta variant being more transmissible and partially able to evade immune responses, breakthrough infections—cases in vaccinated individuals—became more common. However, studies and real-world data show that vaccinated individuals are far less likely to develop severe symptoms or require hospitalization compared to those who are unvaccinated.

The claim further labels the situation as a "delta plague," which is an exaggeration. While the Delta variant did fuel a spike in cases, Israeli health authorities responded quickly by reintroducing public health measures and launching booster vaccine campaigns to curb transmission. The country did not experience a catastrophic surge akin to the earliest months of the pandemic. Instead, the new wave highlighted the need for ongoing vigilance, adaptation of vaccine strategies, and global cooperation to address emerging variants.

In summary, the claim that 50 percent of new Israeli COVID-19 cases were among vaccinated individuals reflects a statistical reality in a highly immunized population during the Delta variant surge. It does not indicate widespread vaccine failure. Vaccines remain highly effective at preventing severe disease and death, and continued monitoring and public health measures are essential to managing COVID-19, especially in the face of evolving variants. The situation in Israel underscores the importance of clear communication, nuanced interpretation of data, and the ongoing need for global vaccination efforts.

Sydney, Australia, has been at the forefront of the country’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic, with strict lockdowns and public health measures implemented to control outbreaks. A recent social media post has made several claims about the current state of Sydney, the rationale for lockdowns, the death toll from COVID-19 in Australia in 2021, the percentage of the population infected, and the intent behind vaccination campaigns. We examine these claims for accuracy and provide context.

The post asserts that “Sydney today. The busiest place in town is a wasteland. The two-week quarantine has been extended for another week. 5mil. residents imprisoned because of a virus from which no one has died this year in Australia, and with a percentage of infected of 0.018% of the population.” It further suggests that vaccination is being used as a tool to restore freedom, quoting the “Prime Minister of New South Wales,” and concludes with the assertion that the pandemic is not real but rather a pretext for forced vaccination.

First, regarding the lockdown: In mid-2021, Sydney, the capital of New South Wales, was placed under a citywide lockdown due to an outbreak of the Delta variant of COVID-19. The initial lockdown began in June 2021, for two weeks, but was extended multiple times as case numbers increased. At the time, Greater Sydney was home to approximately 5 million residents, who were required to stay at home except for essential reasons such as grocery shopping, medical care, or essential work.

The post describes the city as a “wasteland,” a subjective characterization likely referencing the empty streets and closed businesses resulting from movement restrictions. This language, while emotive, reflects observable changes in public life during strict lockdowns.

The claim that “no one has died this year in Australia” from COVID-19, however, is inaccurate. While Australia managed to keep case numbers and deaths low in 2020 and early 2021 through border controls and quarantine measures, there were recorded COVID-19 deaths in Australia in 2021, particularly during the Delta outbreak in New South Wales and Victoria. By July 2021, several deaths had been reported in Sydney alone.

The post claims a “percentage of infected of 0.018% of the population.” This figure significantly underestimates the impact. By mid-2021, thousands of cases had been reported in New South Wales, and while this still represents a small fraction of the total population, the number was higher than cited, especially as outbreaks accelerated.

The post attributes a quote to the “Prime Minister of New South Wales,” a title that does not exist; the correct title is Premier. Premier Gladys Berejiklian did emphasize that high vaccination rates were critical to easing restrictions, aligning with public health advice that widespread vaccination reduces transmission, severe illness, and deaths.

Finally, the assertion that the pandemic is not real and is “proof that the virus was imposed for forced vaccination” is a conspiracy theory without basis in fact. COVID-19 is a global pandemic, recognized by health authorities worldwide. Measures such as lockdowns and vaccination campaigns are standard public health responses to infectious disease outbreaks.

In summary, while Sydney’s strict lockdowns and low case numbers reflect Australia’s aggressive response to COVID-19, the social media post contains inaccuracies and misleading statements about the pandemic’s reality and public health measures. The claim that there were no deaths in 2021 and the infection rate cited are both incorrect, and suggestions that the pandemic was manufactured for forced vaccination are unfounded.

article_content:
A social media post circulating online expresses strong opposition to childhood vaccination, specifically targeting parents who consent to having their children vaccinated. The post claims that vaccines are part of an "experiment" conducted by "chronic liars, globalist runners, and traitors to their own people," and accuses them of waging "biological warfare against humanity." This article examines the core assertions of the post, provides context about vaccines, and analyzes the accuracy of the claims.

**Context and Background**

Vaccines have played a vital role in public health for decades, preventing the spread of diseases such as measles, polio, diphtheria, and more recently, COVID-19. Most vaccines undergo rigorous clinical trials, regulatory review, and ongoing safety monitoring before being approved for use in children and adults. Despite this, vaccine hesitancy has grown in some communities, fueled by misinformation, distrust in institutions, and concerns about side effects or long-term impacts.

The COVID-19 pandemic amplified debates about vaccine safety and government policies. Some individuals and groups have accused authorities and pharmaceutical companies of pushing unproven medical interventions for profit or control, labeling them as "globalist" or as betraying their populations. The post in question draws from this narrative, alleging not only malfeasance but also intentional harm.

**Analysis of the Claims**

*Vaccines as an Experiment:*  
The claim that children are being given to an "experiment" misrepresents how vaccines are developed and administered. Before authorization, vaccines typically go through multiple phases of clinical testing involving tens of thousands of participants. These trials are designed to ensure safety and efficacy. Once approved, vaccines continue to be monitored for adverse effects. While the initial rollout of COVID-19 vaccines was expedited due to urgent need, they still underwent substantial safety evaluations. For routine childhood vaccinations, decades of data support their safety profiles.

*Accusations Against Authorities:*  
The post refers to vaccine proponents as "chronic liars, globalist runners, and traitors," implying deliberate deception and betrayal. While skepticism and demands for transparency from public institutions are healthy in a democracy, broad accusations without supporting evidence do not constitute proof of wrongdoing. Regulatory agencies, scientific communities, and international organizations publish data and updates about vaccine safety and efficacy, and independent oversight is built into the system.

*Biological Warfare Allegation:*  
The assertion that vaccines constitute "biological warfare against humanity" is a serious accusation. Biological warfare involves the intentional release of harmful biological agents to cause illness or death. Vaccines, by contrast, are intended to prevent disease and reduce mortality. There is no credible evidence to suggest that vaccines approved for use are designed or used as weapons against the public.

*Parental Rights and Responsibilities:*

article_content:
A social media post circulating online claims that individuals have experienced increased body magnetism following vaccination, suggesting that this phenomenon is occurring worldwide. This claim has gained traction alongside videos and testimonials purporting to show coins, keys, or other small metal objects sticking to the skin of recently vaccinated individuals.

Background and Context

The claim about increased body magnetism after vaccination emerged prominently during the global rollout of COVID-19 vaccines. Videos on various platforms have shown people pressing metallic objects against their arms and asserting that these items adhere due to a magnetic effect caused by the vaccine. The implication is that the vaccine either contains magnetic materials or somehow alters the body’s properties to create magnetism.

Fact-Checking Analysis

To assess this claim, it is essential to understand both the composition of vaccines and the science of magnetism.

First, vaccines, including those developed for COVID-19, do not contain magnetic ingredients. The main components of these vaccines are active ingredients (such as mRNA or viral proteins), lipids, salts, and stabilizers. None of these substances are magnetic, nor are they present in quantities that would create a magnetic field detectable by the human body or capable of attracting metal objects.

Second, the human body is not capable of producing a magnetic field strong enough to attract or hold metal objects. Even if a vaccine contained a minuscule amount of metallic material—which it does not—such an amount would be far too small to create any noticeable magnetic effect.

Videos and posts showing objects sticking to skin can often be explained by other factors. Skin oils, sweat, and surface tension can cause small, light objects like coins or paperclips to temporarily adhere to the skin, especially if the skin is slightly moist or sticky. This effect occurs regardless of vaccination status and has been demonstrated by people who have not been vaccinated.

Scientific authorities and health organizations worldwide have addressed these claims, confirming that vaccines do not cause magnetism. There is no credible scientific evidence that receiving a vaccine can make a person magnetic in any way.

Conclusion

The assertion that increased body magnetism occurs after vaccination is not supported by scientific evidence. The ingredients in vaccines do not possess magnetic properties, and the human body cannot generate a magnetic field strong enough to attract metal objects. Videos and testimonials purporting to show this effect can be attributed to natural adhesion of objects to the skin, not to any change caused by vaccines. Claims of increased magnetism post-vaccination are unfounded and do not reflect established scientific understanding.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has generated a vast amount of discussion and speculation on social media, particularly regarding immunity to the virus and its variants. Recently, a social media post claimed: "It was revealed which people are immune to the Covid-19 delta variant." This statement suggests that a specific group of individuals has been identified as immune to the Delta variant of the virus. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine the scientific understanding of immunity to COVID-19 and its variants, specifically Delta.

The Delta variant, first identified in India in late 2020, quickly became the dominant strain worldwide due to its increased transmissibility. Concerns about its ability to evade immunity, whether from previous infection or vaccination, led to significant research and public health responses. Immunity to SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, is generally acquired through vaccination or prior infection. The degree and duration of immunity can vary based on factors such as the individual’s immune response, age, underlying health conditions, and the specific variant encountered.

Current scientific consensus has not identified any specific population that is categorically immune to the Delta variant. Some groups may have a reduced risk of severe disease due to vaccination or previous infection, but immunity is not absolute. Vaccines, particularly mRNA vaccines, have been shown to provide significant protection against severe illness and death caused by the Delta variant, though breakthrough infections can still occur. People who have recovered from COVID-19 may also possess some level of natural immunity; however, this immunity can wane over time and may not fully protect against new variants, including Delta.

There have been no credible reports or scientific revelations pinpointing a particular subset of people who are naturally immune to the Delta variant without prior infection or vaccination. Claims that certain individuals—such as those with specific genetic traits or blood types—are completely immune to Delta remain unsubstantiated by peer-reviewed research. Immunity is a complex and dynamic process, and while some people may experience milder symptoms or avoid infection due to a robust immune response, this does not equate to guaranteed immunity.

It is important to note that public health recommendations emphasize vaccination as the most effective tool for reducing the risk of COVID-19 infection and its complications. Relying on unverified claims about immunity can contribute to misinformation and undermine efforts to control the spread of the virus. The evolving nature of SARS-CoV-2 means that new variants may arise with different characteristics, making continued vigilance and adherence to scientific guidance crucial.

In summary, the claim that it has been revealed which people are immune to the COVID-19 Delta variant is not supported by current scientific evidence. No specific group has been identified as categorically immune to the Delta variant. Immunity depends on a range of factors, and vaccination remains the most reliable method of protection. Social media users are encouraged to seek information from reputable sources and to be cautious of sweeping claims regarding immunity to COVID-19 and its variants.
