A recent social media post claims that the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported on June 24, 2021, that only 6% of reported COVID-19 cases resulted in death, and further asserts, “There is no pandemic.” The post suggests that the real impact of COVID-19 has been overstated, urging readers to “prepare for the truth.” This fact-check will examine the accuracy of these claims, provide necessary context, and analyze the interpretation of the CDC’s data.

First, it is important to clarify what the CDC actually reported regarding COVID-19 fatalities. The 6% figure refers to a specific data point in the CDC’s weekly updates on COVID-19 deaths. In August 2020, the CDC indicated that “for 6% of the deaths, COVID-19 was the only cause mentioned” on death certificates. The remaining 94% of deaths listed additional conditions or comorbidities, such as diabetes, heart disease, or respiratory illnesses, alongside COVID-19.

This statistic has been widely misinterpreted. Some have used it to argue that only 6% of reported COVID-19 deaths were truly caused by the virus, implying that the pandemic’s severity has been exaggerated. However, this interpretation is misleading. Medical experts explain that most people who die from any disease often have multiple health conditions. The presence of comorbidities does not mean that COVID-19 was not the primary cause of death; rather, it reflects the reality that the virus can be especially deadly for those with underlying health issues.

In practice, COVID-19 often exacerbates pre-existing conditions, leading to severe complications or death. The CDC’s data shows that, as of June 2021, hundreds of thousands of Americans had died with COVID-19 listed as a cause of death, regardless of comorbidities. The presence of other health problems does not negate the role that COVID-19 played in these deaths.

The claim that “only 6% of reported cases die from Covid-19” is also inaccurate. The post appears to confuse the percentage of deaths with the case fatality rate. The actual case fatality rate—the proportion of confirmed COVID-19 cases that result in death—has varied over time and by location but has consistently been lower than 6%. Importantly, the 6% figure in the CDC report pertains to death certificates, not to the percentage of cases resulting in death.

Lastly, the assertion that “there is no pandemic” is demonstrably false. The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020, and since then, the virus has led to millions of deaths worldwide, strained healthcare systems, and caused significant social and economic disruption. The existence of comorbidities among those who died does not diminish the scale or seriousness of the pandemic.

In summary, the social media post misrepresents CDC data and distorts the actual impact of COVID-19. The 6% statistic cited is taken out of context and does not support the claim that the pandemic is not real or serious. The pandemic has had a profound effect on global health, and the data from the CDC underscores, rather than undermines, the severity of COVID-19’s impact.

בנוסף, הטענה כי "אין פנדמיה" היא שקר באופן מובהק. הארגון הבינלאומי לבריאות (WHO) הכריז על הקורונה כפנדמיה במרץ 2020, ומאז הקורונה גרמה ל数千万 מקרי מות בזירה גלובלית, לחץ על 시스טיים רפואיים, וגרמה להפרעה חמורה בקשר חברתי וכלכלי. הקיום של תנאים רפואיים среди אלו שמתו לא מפחית את היקף או אופי הפנדמיה.

בקיצור, הפרסום במדיה החברתית מטעה את נתוני CDC ומעורר את ההשפעה האמיתית של הקורונה. ה-6% שמבוסס על הטענה נלקח מתוך הקשר, ומאפשר את הטענה שהפנדמיה אינה אמיתית או חמורה. הפנדמיה השפיעה על בריאותה הגלובלית, והנתונים של CDC מציינים את האיום הגדול של הקורונה, ולא מפחיתים אותו.

A social media post has recently circulated, claiming that only large corporations make huge profits and that this phenomenon represents a massive transfer of capital from the middle class to “globalists.” The post further asserts that the ultimate goal is the financial destruction of the middle class, referencing the distribution of “an experimental vaccine for free” as part of this alleged agenda. This article examines these claims by providing context, background, and a fact-based analysis.

First, the assertion that only large corporations make huge profits oversimplifies the dynamics of the global economy. It is true that many of the world’s largest corporations have reported record profits in recent years, especially in sectors like technology, pharmaceuticals, and retail. During the COVID-19 pandemic, some corporations, particularly those equipped for online commerce or essential goods, saw their revenues soar. However, the claim disregards the fact that profit is not exclusive to large corporations. Many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) also generate significant profits, though on a different scale, and contribute substantially to employment and economic growth. The pandemic affected SMEs adversely, with many struggling or closing, but the blanket statement that only large companies profit is inaccurate.

The post suggests that these profits are a result of a deliberate transfer of capital from the middle class to “globalists.” While wealth inequality has indeed grown, with much of the world’s wealth concentrated among a small group of individuals and corporations, this is the outcome of complex economic factors such as globalization, automation, tax policy, and investment trends. The term “globalists” is often used in conspiracy theories to suggest a coordinated effort among elites to control resources. However, there is no credible evidence of a deliberate, orchestrated plan to destroy the middle class for the benefit of global corporate interests. Economic shifts have resulted from policy decisions, market forces, and technological changes, not from a unified conspiracy.

The claim that the “goal is the financial destruction of the middle class” is also misleading. While the middle class in many countries faces challenges such as wage stagnation, rising costs of living, and reduced economic mobility, attributing this solely to an intentional strategy by corporations or elites is speculative. Many governments and organizations actively implement policies aimed at supporting the middle class, such as stimulus packages, minimum wage laws, and small business aid.

Lastly, the post references the distribution of “an experimental vaccine for free,” implying ulterior motives. COVID-19 vaccines were developed rapidly due to global collaboration and significant investment, but they underwent clinical trials and regulatory review before approval for emergency use. The term “experimental” is misleading, as vaccines were authorized based on evidence of safety and efficacy. Providing vaccines for free was a public health measure designed to reduce transmission and protect populations, not a covert tactic to harm the middle class.

In summary, while there are valid concerns about wealth concentration and middle-class stability, the claims in this post are exaggerated and not supported by credible evidence. The interplay between large corporate profits, economic policy, and public health measures is complex and cannot be reduced to a simple narrative of intentional harm.

A recent social media post has raised concerns about the prevalence and severity of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS) among children in India, particularly associating the condition with Covid-19 and Covid-19 vaccination. The post claims that over 2,000 children across India are suffering from MIS as an adverse reaction to Covid-19, and that in Jaipur, 17 out of 154 children diagnosed with the syndrome have died in the past two months. It also alleges a spike in MIS cases at Jaekelon Hospital in Jaipur following Covid-19 vaccination.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to understand what Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome is. MIS, more specifically referred to as MIS-C (Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children), is a rare but serious condition characterized by inflammation affecting multiple organ systems. It has been observed in children following exposure to the Covid-19 virus, typically appearing weeks after infection. The syndrome’s symptoms include persistent fever, abdominal pain, rashes, and in severe cases, shock or organ failure. The condition is recognized by health authorities worldwide as a possible complication of Covid-19 infection in children, though it remains uncommon.

The first core claim is that more than 2,000 children in India are currently suffering from MIS as a result of Covid-19. While there have been documented cases of MIS-C in India, especially during the peak of the Covid-19 pandemic, the number of active cases at any given time is much lower than 2,000. Official data and reports from pediatric associations indicate that the total number of MIS-C cases reported since the beginning of the pandemic is in the low thousands, but these are cumulative figures over several years, not active cases at present. Furthermore, MIS-C is considered rare relative to the total number of Covid-19 infections among children.

The post also asserts that in Jaipur, 17 out of 154 children with MIS have died in the last two months, suggesting a mortality rate of over 10%. This figure appears unusually high. Medical experts report that with early recognition and appropriate treatment, the vast majority of children with MIS-C recover. Reported mortality rates for MIS-C in India and globally are typically less than 2%. Hospitals in Jaipur, including Jaekelon Hospital, have treated children with MIS-C, but there is no public evidence to support as high a death toll as claimed in the post.

Lastly, the post alleges a rise in MIS cases at Jaekelon Hospital in Jaipur after Covid-19 vaccination. There is currently no scientific evidence that Covid-19 vaccines cause MIS-C in children. On the contrary, health authorities have found that the risk of MIS-C is far greater following natural Covid-19 infection than after vaccination. The World Health Organization and national health agencies continue to recommend vaccination for eligible children to prevent severe Covid-19 outcomes, including MIS-C.

In summary, while MIS-C is a real and serious medical condition linked to Covid-19 infection in children, the numbers and mortality rates cited in the social media post appear to be exaggerated. Additionally, the claim linking increased MIS-C cases to Covid-19 vaccination is not supported by current scientific evidence. Parents are encouraged to seek accurate information from trusted medical sources and healthcare professionals.

A recent social media post has sparked concern and debate by claiming that a significant and underreported act—referred to vaguely as “poisoning with the new technology”—is occurring in Japan. The post suggests that mainstream news and television have ignored this issue, but that evidence is available on the Internet, including videos purportedly showing the affected individuals. It further asserts that the Japanese response has been inadequate, but doctors are beginning to organize and take action to “stop the madness.” This article examines these claims, provides relevant context, and analyzes their validity.

Firstly, the post’s central claim revolves around alleged “poisoning with the new technology.” While the post does not specify the technology in question, similar language has previously been used online to refer to a range of modern developments, such as 5G networks, COVID-19 vaccines, or other recent advances. These topics have been targets of misinformation, with some social media users alleging health risks without credible scientific evidence.

Japan is known for its rigorous public health standards and robust technological infrastructure. When new technologies—such as 5G or vaccines—are introduced, Japanese regulatory bodies conduct extensive safety evaluations. For example, the COVID-19 vaccination campaign in Japan followed international protocols and was monitored for adverse effects. No credible scientific evidence has linked technological advancements like 5G networks or vaccines to widespread “poisoning” in Japan or elsewhere.

The claim that this alleged act is ignored by mainstream news and television is also misleading. Japanese media, as well as international outlets, regularly report on public health issues and technological developments. If there were substantiated cases of widespread poisoning linked to a new technology, these would be the subject of significant media scrutiny and public debate, not secrecy. Doctors and health experts in Japan have been active in discussing and addressing health concerns related to new technologies, and their findings are typically published and discussed openly.

The post further alleges that videos online show “these people,” implying visual evidence of victims. However, viral videos on the Internet can be misleading or taken out of context. Without specific details or verifiable sources, such claims remain anecdotal and do not constitute reliable evidence of a widespread phenomenon.

Lastly, the post suggests that doctors in Japan are mobilizing against this alleged “madness.” While it is true that medical professionals in Japan are vigilant about public health and may raise concerns if new risks emerge, there is no documented movement among Japanese doctors to combat a technological “poisoning.” In fact, Japanese medical associations have often spoken out to dispel misinformation, particularly regarding vaccines and telecommunications.

In summary, the social media post repeats familiar themes seen in conspiracy theories around technology and health, amplifying fears without providing verifiable evidence. Public concern about new technology is understandable, but extraordinary claims require clear, credible proof. As of now, no substantiated reports support the existence of a covert poisoning event tied to new technology in Japan, nor a corresponding movement among doctors to oppose it. Claims to the contrary are not supported by available facts or the current consensus in the scientific and medical communities.

Acest articol analizează aceste afirmații, oferă contextul relevant și analizează validitatea lor.

În primul rând, afirmația centrală a postului se referă la „toxificare cu noua tehnologie”. Deși postul nu specifică tehnologia în cauză, limbajul similar a fost folosit înainte pe internet pentru a se referi la o varietate de dezvoltări moderne, cum ar fi rețelele 5G, vaccinurile împotriva coronavirusului sau alte progresii recente. Aceste subiecte au fost obiectul unor informații false, cu unii utilizatori ai rețelelor sociale susținând riscuri pentru sănătate fără dovezi științifice credibile.

Japonia este cunoscută pentru standardele sale riguroase în domeniul sănătății publice și infrastructura sa tehnologică robustă. Când sunt introduse tehnologii noi – cum ar fi 5G sau vaccinurile – autoritățile japoneze efectuează evaluări extinse privind siguranța lor. De exemplu, campania de vaccinare împotriva coronavirusului în Japonia a urmat protocolurile internaționale și a fost monitorizată pentru efecte adverse. Nu există dovezi științifice credibile care să lege dezvoltări tehnologice precum rețelele 5G sau vaccinurile cu o „toxificare” generală în Japonia sau în alte locuri.

Afirmația că acest act este ignorat de mass-media și televiziunea de masă este, de asemenea, inexactă. Mass-media japoneză, precum și publicații internaționale, raportează în mod regulat probleme de sănătate publică și dezvoltări tehnologice. Dacă ar exista cazuri documentate de toxificare generală legate de o nouă tehnologie, acestea ar fi subiectul unor investigații presiunilor media și al unor dezbatere publice, nu a unui secret. Medicii și experții în sănătate din Japonia au fost activi în discuții și abordarea preocupărilor privind tehnologiile noi, iar concluziile lor sunt publicate și discutate deschis.

Postul afirmă, de asemenea, că videoclipurile disponibile pe internet ar arăta „aceste persoane”, sugerând dovezi vizuale ale victimelor. Totuși, videoclipurile virale pe internet pot fi înșelătoare sau preluate din context. Fără detalii specifice sau surse verificabile, aceste afirmații rămân anecdotice și nu reprezintă dovezi credibile ale unui fenomen general.

În sfârșit, postul susține că medicii din Japonia se mobilizează împotriva acestei „nebunii”. Deși este adevărat că profesionii medicali din Japonia sunt vigilanți în privința sănătății publice și pot ridica alarme în cazul apariției unor riscuri noi, nu există un mișcare documentat printre medicii japonezi pentru a combate o „toxificare” tehnologică. În fapt, asociațiile medicale japoneze au adesea emis declarații pentru a dezamăgi informațiile false, în special privind vaccinurile și telecomunicațiile.

În concluzie, postul de pe rețelele sociale repetă teme cunoscute din teorii conspirative privind tehnologia și sănătatea, amplificând friciile fără a oferi dovezi verificabile. Preocuparea publică față de tehnologie nouă este înțeleptă, dar afirmații extraordinare necesită dovezi clare și credibile. În prezent, nu există rapoarte documentate care să susțină existența unui eveniment de toxificare secretă legat de tehnologie nouă în Japonia, nici o mișcare corespunzătoare printre medicii japonezi pentru a se opune acestui fapt. Afirmațiile contrare nu sunt susținute de fapte disponibile sau de consensul actual din comunitatea științifică și medicală.

In recent days, a social media post has been circulating, raising concerns about funeral ceremonies held for COVID-19 victims without the presence of a body. The post expresses anxiety and anger among the population towards authorities, questioning the rationale behind holding ceremonies for empty coffins and implying possible mishandling of deceased coronavirus patients.

To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to understand the procedures and challenges associated with the management of COVID-19 fatalities, especially during the height of the pandemic.

**Background and Context**

During the COVID-19 pandemic, many countries faced unprecedented challenges in handling the bodies of those who succumbed to the virus. Strict public health protocols were implemented to minimize the risk of further transmission. In some cases, restrictions included limiting contact with the deceased, special handling requirements for bodies, and bans on traditional funeral gatherings.

In certain regions, authorities required that victims of COVID-19 be buried or cremated promptly, often under supervision, and sometimes with minimal or no attendance by family members. In rare instances, logistical complications, such as overwhelmed morgues or delays in transportation, led to funerals being held before the body could be present, or with an empty coffin symbolizing the deceased.

**Fact-Checking the Claim**

The central claim in the social media post is that authorities are organizing funerals for COVID-19 victims with empty coffins, sparking public outrage and anxiety over the fate of the bodies. While such occurrences have been reported, they are not widespread and are usually the result of exceptional circumstances rather than standard policy.

In some documented cases, funeral ceremonies without bodies have taken place when the body was not released from hospital or morgue due to biohazard concerns, or when the family was unable to retrieve the body because of quarantine restrictions or bureaucratic delays. These situations, while distressing, were typically communicated to families as necessary precautions based on public health guidance.

It is important to note that the vast majority of COVID-19 victims were buried or cremated according to protocols, often with modified ceremonies to ensure safety. The use of an empty coffin, while symbolic and emotionally difficult for families, was not intended to deceive or disrespect the deceased. Rather, it reflected the extraordinary circumstances and the priority given to preventing further spread of the virus.

**Public Reaction and Official Response**

Anxiety and anger from the public in response to these protocols are understandable, given the emotional significance of funerals and the pain of losing loved ones. Many families felt deprived of closure, and some questioned the transparency of authorities regarding the handling of bodies.

Officials in various regions have acknowledged these concerns and, in many cases, sought to clarify procedures and offer support to grieving families. As the pandemic evolved, protocols were adapted to allow for safer, more compassionate handling of funerals, including virtual attendance and, where possible, limited in-person participation.

**Conclusion**

While there have been isolated instances of COVID-19 funeral ceremonies being held without the physical presence of the deceased, these were largely a consequence of necessary health precautions during an unprecedented crisis. The claim raised in the social media post reflects real anxieties and frustrations, but does not indicate a widespread or intentional practice by authorities to hold funerals with empty coffins. The situation underscores the broader impact of the pandemic on social and cultural rituals, and the need for sensitivity and transparency in public health decision-making.

De siste dagene har en sosialmedieinnlegg blitt delt, som oppsøker bekymring rundt begravelsesceremonier for koronavirusets offer uten tilstedeværelse av kroppen. Innlegget uttrykker angst og opprørt blant befolkningen mot myndighetene, spørsmål om grunnen til å holde begravelsesceremonier for tomme kasser og antyder mulig feilbehandling av døde koronaviruspasienter.

For å vurdere gyldigheten av disse påstandene er det viktig å forstå prosedyrene og utfordringene forbundet med håndtering av koronavirusoffer, spesielt under toppen av pandemien.

**Baground og kontekst**

Under koronaviruspandemien møtte mange land uventede utfordringer ved håndtering av kroppene til de som døde av viruset. Strenge offentlige helseprotokoller ble innført for å minimere risikoen for videre spredning. I noen tilfeller innebar restriksjoner begrensning av kontakt med de døde, spesifikke håndteringskrav for kroppene og forbud mot tradisjonelle begravelsesmøter.

I visse regioner kravde myndighetene at koronavirusoffer skulle begravs eller kremeres raskt, ofte under overvåkning, og noen ganger med minimal eller ingen tilstedeværelse fra familiemedlemmer. I sjeldne tilfeller førte logistiske utfordringer, som overbelasted morgue eller forsinkelser i transport, til at begravelsesceremonier ble holdt før kroppen kunne være til stede, eller med en tom kasse som symbol på den døde.

**Faktaundersøkelse av påstanden**

Sentralen påstand i sosialmedieinnlegget er at myndighetene arrangerer begravelsesceremonier for koronavirusoffer med tomme kasser, noe som fører til offentlig opprørt og angst over hva som skjer med kroppene. Selv om slike hendelser har vært rapportert, er de ikke utbredt og er vanligvis resultatet av unormalle omstendigheter i stedet for standardpolitikk.

I noen dokumenterte tilfeller har begravelsesceremonier uten krop skjedd når kroppen ikke kunne frigjøres fra sykehus eller morgue på grunn av biohazardkonsekvenser, eller når familiene ikke kunne hente kroppen på grunn av karantænebegrænsninger eller byraderet forsinkelser. Disse situasjonene, selv om de var skadelige, ble typisk kommunisert til familier som nødvendige forholdsregler basert på offentlig helseveiledning.

Det er viktig å merke seg at den meste av koronavirusoffer ble begravt eller kremeret i henhold til protokoller, ofte med tilpassede begravelsesceremonier for å sikre sikkerhet. Bruken av en tom kasse, selv om den var symbolisk og følelsesmessig vanskelig for familier, hadde ikke formålet å forsvare eller mista respekt for de døde. Det reflekterte snarere de unormale omstendigheter og prioriteringen av å forhindre videre spredning av viruset.

**Offentlig reaksjon og myndighetsrespons**

Angst og opprørt fra befolkningen i forbindelse med disse protokollene er forståelig, gitt den følelsesmessige betydningen av begravelsesceremonier og smerten ved å miste kjære. Mange familier følte seg utelukket fra en avslutning, og noen foreslo gjennomgående kommunikasjon fra myndighetene om håndtering av kroppene.

Myndigheter i ulike regioner har anerkjent disse bekymringene og, i mange tilfeller, forsøkt å klargjøre prosedyrer og tilby støtte til sorgende familier. Da pandemien utviklet seg, ble protokoller tilpasset for å tillate tryggere og mer menneskelige håndtering av begravelsesceremonier, inkludert virtuell deltagelse og, hvor det var mulig, begrenset personlig deltagelse.

**Konklusjon**

Selv om det har vært isolerte tilfeller av koronavirusbegravelsesceremonier som ble holdt uten fysiske tilstedeværelse av den døde, var disse i stor grad en konsekvens av nødvendige helseforholdsregler under en uventet krise. Påstanden oppsøkt i sosialmedieinnlegget reflekterer virkelige angst og frustrasjon, men viser ikke til en utbredt eller avsiktsmessig praksis fra myndighetene til å holde begravelsesceremonier med tomme kasser. Situasjonen understreker den brede påvirkningen av pandemien på sosiale og kulturelle ritualer, og behovet for følelsesmessig oppmerksomhet og gjennomsiktighet i offentlige helsebeslutninger.

A recent social media post claims that receiving a COVID-19 vaccine causes immediate and chronic constipation that can last for months, and alleges that commonly used remedies such as castor oil are ineffective against this condition. The post further suggests that while the vaccine may prevent COVID-19 infection, it instead leads to persistent digestive issues. Given the widespread concern about potential vaccine side effects, it is important to examine these claims against available scientific evidence and expert opinion.

First, it is essential to understand the process by which vaccines, including those developed for COVID-19, are tested and monitored. Before approval, vaccines undergo rigorous clinical trials involving tens of thousands of participants. These trials are designed to identify both common and rare side effects. After approval, ongoing surveillance systems continue to monitor for side effects in the general population. This extensive monitoring provides a comprehensive understanding of potential adverse reactions.

Constipation is a common digestive complaint in the general population. It can be triggered by a variety of factors, including diet, medications, dehydration, stress, and underlying medical conditions. However, in the context of COVID-19 vaccines, the most frequently reported side effects are mild and temporary, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, headache, mild fever, and muscle aches. Gastrointestinal side effects, when they occur, are typically mild and short-lived—such as nausea or diarrhea—and are not among the most commonly reported adverse reactions.

There is currently no scientific evidence or credible medical reports linking COVID-19 vaccines to immediate or chronic constipation. The notion that constipation would begin instantly after vaccination and persist for months does not align with known vaccine side effect profiles. Furthermore, the claim that traditional remedies like castor oil would be ineffective against vaccine-induced constipation is speculative and unsupported by clinical data.

It is possible that some individuals may experience changes in bowel habits due to stress or anxiety related to vaccination, or coincidentally develop constipation around the time of vaccination. However, this does not mean the vaccine is the cause. Chronic constipation lasting several months is a significant medical concern that warrants evaluation by a healthcare provider to rule out underlying conditions unrelated to vaccination.

Misinformation about vaccine side effects can contribute to vaccine hesitancy and unnecessary anxiety. Health authorities and medical organizations emphasize the importance of relying on evidence-based information when it comes to vaccine safety. The widespread use of COVID-19 vaccines globally, coupled with robust safety monitoring, has not revealed a causal link between vaccination and chronic constipation.

In summary, the claim that COVID-19 vaccines cause immediate, long-lasting constipation that is resistant to remedies is not supported by scientific evidence or by data from vaccine safety monitoring systems. Anyone experiencing ongoing constipation should seek advice from a healthcare professional, as this is unlikely to be related to vaccination. Vaccines remain a safe and effective tool in the fight against COVID-19.

این اطلاعات اشتباه درباره عوارض جانبی واکسن می‌تواند به اضطراب درباره ایمنی واکسن و مقاومت در برابر واکسیناسیون انجام شود. مقامات بهداشت و سازمان‌های پزشکی اهمیت اطلاعات پایه‌ای درباره ایمنی واکسن را تاکید می‌کنند. استفاده گسترده از واکسن کووید-19 در سراسر جهان به همراه نظارت قوی بر ایمنی، ارتباطی عللی بین واکسیناسیون و اسهال مزمن را نشان نمی‌دهد.

به طور خلاصه، ادعای اینکه واکسن کووید-19 باعث اسهال فوری و طولانی مدتی می‌شود که به داروهای درمانی مقاوم است، توسط دلایل علمی و داده‌های نظارت بر ایمنی واکسن پشتیبانی نمی‌شود. هر فردی که اسهال طولانی مدتی را تجربه کند، نیاز به مشورت با پزشک دارد، زیرا این وضعیت به احتمال زیاد با واکسیناسیون مرتبط نیست. واکسن‌ها هنوز هم ابزاری ایمن و مؤثر در مبارزه با کووید-19 هستند.

A recent Facebook post from a profile known for sharing conspiracy theories has sparked concern among public health experts. The profile’s author claims that a drug called Suramin can cure individuals of supposed negative effects caused by the Covid-19 vaccine, further alleging that the vaccine itself is harmful. This article examines these claims, provides background on Suramin, and evaluates the scientific evidence.

**Background on Suramin**

Suramin is a medication that has been in use since the early 20th century, primarily for treating African sleeping sickness (trypanosomiasis) and river blindness (onchocerciasis). It is a large, complex molecule administered intravenously under strict medical supervision due to its potential for serious side effects. Suramin is not approved for use outside these specific parasitic diseases and is not available over the counter.

**The Claim: Suramin as a Cure for Vaccine Side Effects**

The social media post asserts that Suramin can reverse or cure negative effects allegedly caused by Covid-19 vaccines. This claim has circulated in various online communities since early in the pandemic, often amplified by individuals or groups skeptical of vaccines. These narratives typically lack scientific foundation and are not supported by any major health organization.

**Scientific Analysis and Expert Opinion**

To date, there is no credible scientific evidence that Suramin is effective in treating any side effects associated with Covid-19 vaccines. The vaccines authorized for use against Covid-19 have undergone rigorous testing and monitoring, showing that serious side effects are extremely rare. Most reported vaccine side effects are mild and temporary, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, or mild fever.

Moreover, Suramin itself carries significant health risks. Side effects can include nausea, vomiting, adrenal gland problems, kidney damage, and severe allergic reactions. Its use without medical oversight can be dangerous, and the drug is not intended for general use or self-medication. The idea that Suramin could "detox" or neutralize vaccine components is not supported by any pharmacological or clinical evidence.

**Misinformation and Public Health Impact**

The Facebook profile in question has a history of promoting conspiracy theories, which raises concerns about the reliability of its health recommendations. Promoting unproven and potentially harmful treatments can deter individuals from seeking appropriate medical care and contribute to vaccine hesitancy. Health authorities around the world have repeatedly warned against using unauthorized drugs to treat or prevent Covid-19 or its vaccine side effects.

**Conclusion**

The claim that Suramin is a cure for alleged negative effects of Covid-19 vaccines is not supported by scientific evidence. Suramin is a powerful drug with specific medical uses and serious potential side effects. Self-administering or recommending this medication outside of its approved indications is both dangerous and irresponsible. Individuals concerned about vaccine side effects should consult qualified healthcare professionals rather than relying on unverified social media posts. Public health depends on accurate information and evidence-based medicine, not on conspiracy theories or misinformation.

Ia merupakan molekul besar dan kompleks yang diberikan secara intravena di bawah pengawasan perubatan yang ketat kerana potensi kesan sampingan yang serius. Suramin tidak diluluskan untuk digunakan di luar penyakit parasit tertentu ini dan tidak tersedia untuk dibeli secara bebas.

**Klaim: Suramin sebagai Penyembuh Kesan Sampingan Vaksin**

Post media sosial tersebut menyatakan bahawa Suramin boleh membalikkan atau menyembuhkan kesan negatif yang didakwa disebabkan oleh vaksin Covid-19. Naratif-naratif ini biasanya tidak memiliki dasar saintifik dan tidak disokong oleh mana-mana organisasi kesihatan utama.

Hingga kini, tiada bukti saintifik yang dapat dipercayai menunjukkan bahawa Suramin berkesan dalam merawat sebarang kesan sampingan yang berkaitan dengan vaksin Covid-19. Kebanyakan kesan sampingan vaksin yang dilaporkan adalah ringan dan sementara, seperti kesakitan di tempat suntikan, lemah dan demam ringan.

Selain itu, Suramin itu sendiri membawa risiko kesihatan yang besar. Kesan sampingan termasuk mual, muntah, masalah kelenjar adrenal, keracunan buah pinggang, dan reaksi alahan yang serius. Mempromosikan rawatan yang tidak disahkan dan mungkin berbahaya boleh menghalang individu daripada memohon perkhidmatan kesihatan yang sesuai serta menyumbang kepada keraguan terhadap vaksin. Pihak berkuasa kesihatan di seluruh dunia telah berulang kali memperingatkan supaya tidak menggunakan ubat yang tidak diluluskan untuk merawat atau mencegah Covid-19 atau kesan sampingan vaksinnya.

Membuat penggunaan atau merekomendasikan ubat ini di luar kegunaan yang diluluskan adalah berbahaya dan tidak bertanggungjawab. Individu yang bimbang mengenai kesan sampingan vaksin sepatut berkonsultasi dengan profesional kesihatan yang berkelayakan, bukan bergantung pada kenyataan media sosial yang tidak disahkan. Kesihatan awam bergantung pada maklumat yang tepat dan perubatan berdasarkan bukti, bukan pada teori konspirasi atau pemalsuan maklumat.

A conspiracy theory circulating on social media claims that Bill Gates, the co-founder of Microsoft and a prominent philanthropist, aims to wipe out the world’s population using the Covid-19 vaccination. This alarming assertion has gained notable attention online, especially among communities skeptical of vaccines and global health initiatives. In this article, we examine the origins of this claim, the motivations attributed to Gates, and the available evidence to determine its accuracy.

The roots of this conspiracy theory can be traced back to Bill Gates’s long-standing involvement in global health initiatives through the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The foundation has committed billions of dollars to fight infectious diseases, develop vaccines, and improve healthcare infrastructure, particularly in low-income countries. During the Covid-19 pandemic, Gates became a prominent advocate for vaccine development and equitable access, frequently appearing in interviews and public forums to discuss strategies for combating the virus.

The theory alleges that Gates’s support for vaccination is a cover for a sinister agenda: to use Covid-19 vaccines to reduce the global population. Proponents of this idea often point to statements made by Gates about the role of vaccines and healthcare in reducing population growth. In reality, Gates has discussed how improving child health and reducing mortality rates often leads to lower birth rates, as families do not feel the need to have as many children when child survival improves. This is a well-established concept in public health, not a call for population “reduction” in the sense of mass extermination.

There is no credible scientific evidence to support the claim that Covid-19 vaccines are intended or able to cause mass death or sterilization. The vaccines underwent rigorous clinical trials and were authorized by regulatory agencies worldwide after demonstrating safety and efficacy. Adverse effects are rare and are outweighed by the benefits of preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death due to Covid-19.

Fact-checkers and public health experts have repeatedly debunked the notion that Bill Gates or his foundation is engaged in a plot to harm humanity through vaccines. The theory often relies on misinterpretations, out-of-context quotes, and mistrust of global health institutions. It also echoes broader patterns of misinformation that have historically targeted vaccination campaigns, sometimes leading to real-world harm by fueling vaccine hesitancy.

In conclusion, the claim that Bill Gates seeks to wipe out the world’s population using the Covid-19 vaccination is not supported by any factual evidence. The Gates Foundation’s work in global health is aimed at saving lives and improving health outcomes, not reducing the population through nefarious means. Covid-19 vaccines have proven to be a vital tool in controlling the pandemic and protecting public health. It is essential to approach such extraordinary claims with critical thinking and to rely on verified information from reputable scientific and medical authorities.

A video circulating on social media claims that the Covid-19 pandemic was predicted or exposed in a cartoon from the 1990s. The video suggests that specific references in an animated show from that era directly point to the coronavirus outbreak that began in 2019, implying either prophetic foresight or hidden knowledge being revealed to the public decades in advance.

To assess this claim, it is essential to consider the context in which cartoons from the 1990s were created, as well as the nature of such predictions in popular media. Animated shows, particularly satirical ones, have often been known to lampoon or reference current events, scientific concepts, or general fears about the future. However, these references are typically broad or speculative, rather than specific forecasts of future events.

The claim hinges on the idea that a cartoon specifically named Covid-19, coronavirus, or depicted scenarios that unmistakably parallel the global pandemic, including elements such as mask mandates, worldwide virus spread, or lockdowns. However, a review of well-known cartoons from the 1990s, including episodes frequently cited in such conspiracy theories, reveals no direct references to Covid-19 or the coronavirus. While some animated shows have featured storylines about viruses, plagues, or generic pandemics, these are common plot devices in fiction and not unique to any one show or time period.

For example, "The Simpsons," a show often at the center of such predictions, aired an episode in 1993 titled "Marge in Chains," which depicted a fictional virus called the "Osaka Flu" spreading through Springfield. While some social media users have pointed to this episode as evidence of foreknowledge, the storyline features a fictional flu from Japan and does not mention coronaviruses, Covid-19, or any details specific to the 2019 pandemic. The inclusion of a pandemic plot was meant as a satirical take on public health scares and is not unique to "The Simpsons."

Similarly, other cartoons from the 1990s occasionally referenced viruses or outbreaks in a general sense, usually for comedic or dramatic effect. None, however, contain accurate or explicit predictions regarding the emergence, naming, or characteristics of Covid-19. The term "Covid-19" itself did not exist prior to 2019, when it was designated by the World Health Organization to describe the novel coronavirus disease.

Fact-checking analysis reveals that claims of a 1990s cartoon exposing or predicting the Covid-19 pandemic are unfounded. Such narratives often arise from misinterpretations, selective editing, or the human tendency to find patterns and meaning in coincidental similarities. While cartoons have occasionally touched on themes related to disease outbreaks, there is no credible evidence that any 1990s cartoon specifically predicted or referenced Covid-19.

In conclusion, the assertion that a cartoon from the 1990s exposed or predicted the Covid-19 pandemic is not supported by the content of those shows or by any factual record. Such claims should be regarded with skepticism and understood as examples of misinformation or misremembered cultural references.

ਇਸੇ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ, 1990 ਦੇ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਹੋਰ ਕਾਰਟੂਨ ਅਕਸਰ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਜਾਂ ਉਪਲੱਬਧਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਵਾਲਾ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ, ਅਕਸਰ ਮਜ਼ਾਕ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ੰਸਾ ਦੇ ਲਈ। ਹਾਲਾਂ ਕਿ, ਕੋਈ ਵੀ ਕੋਵਿਡ-19 ਦੇ ਉਦੇਸ਼, ਨਾਮ ਜਾਂ ਵਿਸੂਚਿਤ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਤਾਵਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਸਹੀ ਜਾਂ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਪ੍ਰਗਟੀਸ਼ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। "ਕੋਵਿਡ-19" ਨਾਮ ਨੂੰ 2019 ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਸ਼ਵ ਸਿਹਤ ਸੰਗਠਨ ਦੁਆਰਾ ਇਸ ਨਵੇਂ ਕੋਰੋਨਾਵਾਇਰਸ ਰੋਗ ਦੇ ਵਰਗੀਕਰਣ ਲਈ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ।

article_content:
A recent social media post asserts that the World Health Organization (WHO) has been planning since 1972 to use vaccines as a method to kill, outlining a three-step process: 1) deactivating the immune system, 2) filling every cell with a virus, and 3) reactivating the immune system to trigger a deadly cytokine storm. This claim has circulated in various forms for years, often resurfacing during periods of heightened public attention to vaccines and global health policies.

To assess the accuracy of this assertion, it is important to provide context on the WHO, the history of vaccination, and the origins of the specific claim.

The WHO is an international public health agency established in 1948, dedicated to coordinating global health responses, managing disease outbreaks, and promoting health initiatives. Vaccines are one of the most significant tools in public health, credited with the control and eradication of diseases such as smallpox and the reduction of illnesses like polio, measles, and diphtheria.

The claim references "1972" as the beginning of an alleged plan by the WHO to weaponize vaccines. In reality, 1972 saw the publication of scientific papers on immunology and vaccine development, but there is no evidence of any plot to use vaccines to harm populations. The source of this claim appears to be a misinterpretation of immunological research on immune responses and the phenomenon of cytokine storms—a rare, exaggerated immune reaction that can occur during certain infections or medical treatments.

Breaking down the three points in the post:

1. **Deactivating the immune system:** Vaccines are designed to stimulate, not suppress, the immune system. Their purpose is to safely introduce an antigen, prompting the body to develop immunity by producing antibodies without causing disease. There is no credible mechanism, evidence, or intent within the WHO or the scientific community to use vaccines to deactivate or weaken immune defenses.

2. **Filling every cell with a virus:** Vaccines do not "fill every cell" with a virus. Most vaccines use either inactivated viruses, weakened versions of a virus, or pieces of a virus (such as proteins) to teach the immune system to recognize and fight infections. Live-attenuated vaccines may enter cells to prompt an immune response, but they are engineered to be non-pathogenic and do not infect every cell. Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines temporarily instruct cells to produce a viral protein, but this occurs in a limited number of cells and does not involve a full virus.

3. **Triggering a cytokine storm:** While cytokine storms are a serious medical phenomenon, they are rare and not a typical result of vaccination. Vaccines undergo extensive safety testing and monitoring to ensure they do not provoke such dangerous immune reactions. The occurrence of cytokine storms is primarily associated with severe infections, not vaccines.

In summary, the claim that the WHO has planned to use vaccines as a killing method since 1972 is not supported by any credible evidence. The points outlined in the post misrepresent both the science of immunology and the function of vaccines. Such misinformation can undermine public trust in life-saving health interventions and does not reflect the established facts about the WHO or vaccine development.

article_content:
A social media post circulating online has sparked debate and confusion regarding the purpose and effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines. The post reads, “Think carefully about this and go and get vaccinated if you are a sheep. What does the vaccine protect you from?” Alongside this, the author shares an image that states, “Madhouse. Vaccinate the unvaccinated so as not to infect those who have already been vaccinated.” The implication is clear: the author is questioning the logic behind vaccinating individuals if vaccinated people can still get infected and, by extension, questioning the overall efficacy of vaccines.

To understand and assess the claim, it is important to consider both the science behind vaccines and the intent of broad vaccination campaigns.

**Background on Vaccine Purpose and Function**

Vaccines, including those developed for COVID-19, work by stimulating the immune system to recognize and fight off the virus if exposed in the future. The primary goals of vaccination are to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death, rather than to provide absolute immunity from infection. No vaccine is 100% effective at preventing infection, but most are highly effective at reducing the severity of disease.

**Do Vaccines Prevent Infection and Transmission?**

The post suggests a contradiction: if vaccinated people can still get infected, why vaccinate the unvaccinated? Early in the pandemic, data indicated that COVID-19 vaccines were highly effective at preventing both infection and transmission. However, as the virus evolved and new variants emerged, the vaccines’ ability to prevent infection decreased somewhat, particularly with the Omicron variant and its subvariants. Nevertheless, vaccines have continued to offer strong protection against severe outcomes.

Importantly, vaccinated people who do become infected are generally less likely to experience severe symptoms and are infectious for a shorter period. This means widespread vaccination reduces the overall burden on healthcare systems and helps protect vulnerable populations.

**Why Encourage Vaccination for All?**

The logic behind encouraging everyone to get vaccinated is based on community or herd immunity. When more people are vaccinated, the virus has fewer opportunities to spread, mutate, and cause outbreaks. This protects not only vaccinated individuals, but also those who cannot be vaccinated due to medical reasons and those in whom the vaccine is less effective.

Moreover, while breakthrough infections (cases in vaccinated individuals) do occur, the risk of severe disease is much higher among the unvaccinated. Multiple studies have shown that unvaccinated people are more likely to be hospitalized or die from COVID-19 compared to their vaccinated counterparts.

**Conclusion**

The claim in the social media post misrepresents the goals and benefits of vaccination. COVID-19 vaccines are not only about protecting individuals from infection, but also about reducing the severity of disease, limiting transmission, and protecting the community as a whole. Asking what the vaccine protects you from is a valid question, but the answer is clear: vaccines primarily protect against severe illness, hospitalization, and death, and they contribute to the broader effort to control the pandemic. The recommendation for widespread vaccination is based on scientific evidence and public health principles, not contradiction or illogic.

社交媒体上流传的一则帖子引发了关于新冠疫苗目的和效果的争论和困惑。该帖子写道：“仔细思考一下，如果你是绵羊，就去接种疫苗吧。疫苗能保护你免受什么？”同时，作者分享了一张图片，上面写着：“疯人院。接种未接种者，以免感染已接种者。”其含义明确：作者在质疑，如果接种疫苗的人仍可能感染，那为何要接种疫苗？进而质疑疫苗的整体有效性。

为理解并评估这一说法，有必要同时考虑疫苗的科学原理以及大规模接种计划的意图。

**疫苗的目的与功能背景**

疫苗，包括针对新冠的疫苗，通过刺激免疫系统来识别和对抗病毒，从而在将来暴露于病毒时能够有效应对。疫苗的主要目标是降低重症、住院和死亡的风险，而不是提供绝对的感染防护。没有任何一种疫苗能100%防止感染，但大多数疫苗在降低疾病严重程度方面非常有效。

**疫苗能预防感染和传播吗？**

该帖子暗示了矛盾：如果接种疫苗的人仍可能感染，为何要接种未接种者？在疫情初期，数据显示新冠疫苗在预防感染和传播方面非常有效。然而，随着病毒的演变和新变种的出现，疫苗在预防感染方面的效果有所下降，尤其是在奥密克戎变种及其亚变种的情况下。尽管如此，疫苗仍能有效保护人们免受严重后果。

重要的是，即使接种疫苗的人感染了病毒，他们通常不太可能出现严重症状，并且传染期较短。这意味着广泛接种疫苗可以减少对医疗系统的整体负担，并帮助保护易感人群。

**为何鼓励所有人接种疫苗？**

鼓励所有人接种疫苗的逻辑基于群体免疫。当更多人接种疫苗时，病毒传播、变异和引发疫情的机会减少。这不仅保护了接种疫苗的人，也保护了因医疗原因无法接种疫苗的人，以及疫苗效果较弱的人群。

此外，虽然接种疫苗者出现突破性感染的情况确实存在，但未接种疫苗者发生严重疾病的风险更高。多项研究表明，与接种疫苗者相比，未接种疫苗的人更可能因新冠住院或死亡。

**结论**

该社交媒体帖子对疫苗的目标和益处存在误解。新冠疫苗不仅旨在保护个人免受感染，还旨在减少疾病严重程度、限制传播，并保护整个社区。询问疫苗能保护你免受什么是一个合理的问题，但答案是明确的：疫苗主要保护人们免受重症、住院和死亡，并有助于整体控制疫情。广泛接种疫苗的建议基于科学证据和公共卫生原则，而非矛盾或逻辑错误。

A recent social media post claims that mass vaccination campaigns are a form of subtle brainwashing, leveraging social pressure by implying that those who refuse vaccination are “stupid.” The post further suggests that most people in Macedonia have resisted vaccination, with approximately 85% of citizens remaining unvaccinated, allegedly because they do not trust “unknown experimental (and proven dangerous) ingredients.” This article examines these assertions, providing context and separating fact from misinformation.

First, it is important to address the claim that vaccination campaigns constitute brainwashing or coercion. Public health campaigns, including those promoting vaccination, are designed to inform the public about scientific consensus and evidence regarding disease prevention. Messaging often highlights the benefits of vaccines in reducing the risk of illness, hospitalization, and death. While some campaigns may use strong language to encourage vaccine uptake, the primary goal is public health, not manipulation.

The assertion that vaccines contain “unknown” or “experimental” ingredients is misleading. Vaccines authorized for use by health authorities undergo rigorous testing for safety and efficacy before public distribution. The ingredients of all approved vaccines are publicly listed and monitored for safety. While some COVID-19 vaccines were developed and authorized quickly, the accelerated timeline resulted from unprecedented global collaboration and funding, not from a relaxation of safety standards. Post-authorization monitoring continues to ensure vaccine safety, with rare adverse reactions documented and addressed transparently.

The claim that vaccines are “proven dangerous” does not align with the extensive safety data available. Serious side effects from COVID-19 vaccines are extremely rare. The benefits of vaccination in preventing severe illness and death far outweigh the risks of adverse reactions, according to numerous health authorities worldwide. Millions of people have received these vaccines with a strong safety record.

Turning to the claim about Macedonia’s vaccination rate, the post states that about 85% of citizens have not been vaccinated, implying widespread skepticism or resistance. In reality, vaccination rates in Macedonia have lagged behind some European countries, but not to the extent suggested. As of early 2024, estimates indicate that around 40-45% of Macedonia’s adult population has received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. This means that the unvaccinated proportion is closer to 55-60%, not 85%. The reasons for lower uptake are complex, involving factors such as vaccine hesitancy, misinformation, access challenges, and public trust in institutions.

Finally, the post frames public health messaging as “morbid propaganda” and suggests that only “smart citizens” resist vaccination. This rhetoric misrepresents the purpose of vaccination campaigns and stigmatizes those who choose to get vaccinated. The scientific consensus supports vaccination as a key tool in controlling the COVID-19 pandemic and protecting public health.

In summary, the social media post contains several inaccuracies. Vaccination campaigns are based on scientific evidence, not manipulation. COVID-19 vaccines are not experimental or proven dangerous, and their ingredients are well known. The vaccination rate in Macedonia, while relatively low, is not as low as claimed. Accurate information and open discussion are crucial for informed decision-making about health.

A recent social media post claims that vaccines intended to be stored at -75 degrees Celsius are being distributed in the middle of villages from tractor-trailers in temperatures as high as 40 degrees Celsius. This post raises concerns about vaccine safety and efficacy, suggesting serious breaches in recommended storage protocols.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to first understand the storage requirements for certain COVID-19 vaccines. Notably, the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine was originally required to be stored at ultra-cold temperatures, specifically around -70 to -75 degrees Celsius. This stringent requirement was due to the fragility of the mRNA molecules used in the vaccine, which degrade rapidly if exposed to higher temperatures. Other vaccines, such as the Moderna vaccine, also require cold storage, but at less extreme temperatures—around -20 degrees Celsius. Many other vaccines, including those for influenza or measles, are typically stored between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius.

The distribution of these vaccines has posed logistical challenges worldwide, particularly in remote or rural areas. To address these challenges, governments and health organizations have invested in specialized cold-chain equipment, such as ultra-cold freezers and insulated containers. Mobile vaccination sites, including those set up in trucks or trailers, have been deployed in some regions to reach isolated communities. These vehicles are usually equipped with refrigeration units or portable ultra-cold storage systems designed to maintain the necessary temperature until administration.

The social media post suggests that vaccines requiring ultra-cold storage are being distributed in tractor-trailers at ambient temperatures of 40 degrees Celsius, implying that proper storage protocols are not being followed. This scenario, if true, would result in the vaccines losing their potency and potentially becoming unsafe for use.

Upon closer examination, there is little credible evidence to support the widespread practice described in the post. While it is true that mobile vaccination efforts sometimes involve trucks and trailers, these vehicles are typically outfitted with appropriate cooling technologies. Health authorities have emphasized the importance of maintaining the cold chain throughout the transport and distribution process. In the rare event of a cold chain failure, vaccines are usually discarded rather than administered, as their efficacy cannot be guaranteed.

Reports of vaccines being distributed without cold storage are extremely uncommon and, when they do occur, are investigated and addressed by local health officials. The claim that vaccines requiring -75 degrees Celsius storage are routinely distributed in 40-degree heat is not supported by documented evidence from official sources or reputable news outlets. The suggestion that such practices are widespread or accepted is misleading and does not reflect the standard procedures followed in vaccine distribution.

In summary, while vaccine distribution in rural areas can be challenging, health authorities have established protocols to ensure vaccines are stored and handled safely. The claim that ultra-cold vaccines are being distributed in hot tractor-trailers without proper cooling does not align with established procedures and available evidence. Concerns about vaccine safety are important, but it is equally vital to rely on accurate information when evaluating public health practices.

Денеска социјална мрежа ја изјави дека ваксини кои треба да се зачувуваат на -75 степени Целзии се распоредуваат во средината на селата од трактор-трактори во температури како што е 40 степени Целзии. Оваа изјава предизвикува загриженост за безбедноста и ефикасноста на ваксините, предводени од тврдење дека има сериозни нарушенија на препорачаните протоколи за зачувување.

За да се процени валидноста на ова тврдење, е важно да се разберат захтевите за зачувување на одредени ваксини за коронавирус. Најзначајно, ваксината Pfizer-BioNTech за коронавирус најпрвин треба да се зачувува на ултрависоки температури, конкретно околу -70 до -75 степени Целзии. Овој строг захтев беше поради чувствителноста на молекулите mRNA кои се користат во ваксината, кои се разградуваат брзо ако се изложат на поголеми температури. Други ваксини, како што е Moderna, исто така изискуваат хладно зачувување, но на помалку екстремни температури – околу -20 степени Целзии. Многу други ваксини, вклучувајќи ги ваксините за грип или вакцинација против вирус на огнените вируси, се зачувуваат помеѓу 2 и 8 степени Целзии.

Распоредувањето на овие ваксини предизвикало логистички предизвици ниво глобално, особено во отдалечени или селски зони. За да ги решат овие предизвици, владини и здравствени организации инвестираа во специјализирано зачувување на хладно, како што се ултрависоки фризери и изолирани кутии. Мобилни вакцинирачки места, вклучувајќи ги оните кои се поставени во трактори или трактори, се користат во одредени региони за да достигнат изолирани групи. Овие возила обично се опремени со хладилни единици или портативни ултрависоки системи за зачувување дизајнирани да задржат потребната температура до вакцинацијата.

Социјалната мрежа изјавува дека ваксини кои изискуваат ултрависоки зачувување се распоредуваат во трактори на амбиентни температури од 40 степени Целзии, што предводи дека протоколите за зачувување не се следени. Ако ова е точно, ваксините би губеле својата ефикасност и потенцијално би станале небезбедни за користење.

При детално преглед, постои малка крепка доказ за широка практика како што е описана во изјавата. Исто така, истината е дека мобилни вакцинирачки напори понекогаш вклучуваат трактори и трактори, но овие возила обично се опремени со одговарајќи технологија за охлаждување. Здравствените органи подчертуваат важноста на задржувањето на хладниот ланец постојано во транспортот и распоредувањето. Во случај на ретки нарушенија на хладниот ланец, ваксините обично се одбафуваат, а не се користат, бидејќи нивната ефикасност не може да се гарантира.

Пораките за распоредување на ваксини без хладно зачувување се екстремно ретки, а кога се случува, локалните здравствени органи ги инспектираат и ги решаваат. Тврдењето дека ваксини кои изискуваат зачувување на -75 степени Целзии се распоредуваат на 40 степени Целзии е не поддржано од документирани докази од официјални извори или надежни медиа. Сugerацијата дека такви практики се широки или прифатени е неправилна и не отсликува стандардните процедури за распоредување на ваксини.

Вкупно, докажувањето на ваксини во селски зони може да предизвика логистички предизвици, но здравствените органи имаат уредени протоколи за да се зачувуваат и обработуваат ваксини безбедно. Тврдењето дека ултрависоки ваксини се распоредуваат во трактори на топли температури без одговарајќи охлаждување не се согласно со уредени процедури и достапни докази. Загриженоста за безбедноста на ваксините е важна, но исто така е критично да се користи точна информација кога се проценува здравствени практики.

A photograph circulating widely on Facebook claims to show a scene from Paris on July 17, 2021, depicting a protest against new anti-Covid measures. The post suggests that the image captures demonstrators responding to government policies introduced to curb the spread of COVID-19. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to analyze the context of the protests in France at the time, examine the government's pandemic-related actions, and verify the origin and content of the photograph in question.

In July 2021, France experienced significant public opposition to expanded Covid-19 restrictions announced by President Emmanuel Macron. The government declared that beginning later that month, a health pass would be required to enter restaurants, cafes, shopping centers, and various public venues. This pass, which showed proof of vaccination, recent recovery from COVID-19, or a negative test result, was intended to help control a surge in cases attributed to the Delta variant. The announcement was met with both support and criticism, sparking nationwide demonstrations.

On July 17, 2021, thousands of people took to the streets across France, including Paris, to protest what they viewed as restrictive and coercive measures. Reports from the day describe large crowds marching through Paris, waving signs and chanting slogans against mandatory vaccinations and the health pass. The protests were generally peaceful, though some incidents of tension between demonstrators and police were reported. Images and videos from that day showed notable landmarks such as the Champs-Élysées and Place du Trocadéro filled with protesters.

Fact-checking the specific Facebook post requires a closer look at the photograph’s content. Details such as visible signage, clothing styles, the presence of French-language banners, and recognizable city landmarks can help determine whether the image authentically reflects a Parisian protest. Cross-referencing the photograph with reliable news coverage and official reports from July 17, 2021, is crucial. For instance, many legitimate images from that date show large crowds, and some feature the Eiffel Tower or other Parisian scenery, confirming the location.

However, social media posts sometimes misrepresent images by attributing them to incorrect dates, locations, or events. In this case, if the photograph matches those published by reputable news outlets on July 17, 2021, and includes clear indicators of Paris, the claim is credible. Conversely, if the image omits these details or matches photos from different events or cities, the post would be misleading.

After analyzing publicly available images and accounts from July 17, 2021, it is plausible that the photo in question does depict a protest in Paris against new anti-Covid measures. The timing corresponds with a major demonstration, and the context aligns with widespread public dissent regarding government health policies. Nevertheless, it is always advisable to confirm the authenticity of viral images, as misinformation can easily spread on social media.

In summary, the claim that the photo shared on Facebook was taken in Paris on July 17, 2021, during a protest against new anti-Covid measures is supported by the context of mass demonstrations occurring on that date. While the overall narrative fits historical events, the veracity of the specific photograph ultimately depends on its alignment with confirmed images from that day. Fact-checking remains essential to ensure accurate representation of significant moments in public discourse.

Η κυβέρνηση ανακοίνωσε ότι από την έναρξη της επόμενης εβδομάδας θα ήταν απαραίτητο να παρουσιαστεί ένα πιστοποιητικό υγείας για να εισέλθει κανείς σε εστιατόρια, καφετερίες, καταστήματα αγορών και διάφορα δημόσια χώρα. Αυτό το πιστοποιητικό, το οποίο αποδεικνύει την εμβολιασμένη κατάσταση, την επανάκτηση από τον κορωνοϊό ή το αρνητικό αποτέλεσμα ελέγχου, είχε ως σκοπό να βοηθήσει στην καταπολέμηση της αύξησης των περισσότερων περιστατικών που αποδοκιμάζονταν στον τύπο Δέλτα. Η ανακοίνωση έλαβε και υποστήριξη και κριτική, προκαλώντας διαδηλώσεις σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα.

Στις 17 Ιουλίου 2021, χιλιάδες άνθρωποι πήγαν στους δρόμους σε διάφορες πόλεις της Γαλλίας, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της Παρισινής, για να διαδηλώσουν ενάντια στις μέτρα που θεωρούσαν ότι ήταν περιοριστικά και απαιτητικά. Αναφορές από την ημέρα αυτή περιγράφουν μεγάλα συγκεντρωμένα άτομα που περπατούσαν στη Παρίσι, κρατώντας σημαίες και χειροκρατώντας συνθήματα εναντίον των υποχρεωτικών εμβολιασμών και του πιστοποιητικού υγείας. Οι διαδηλώσεις ήταν συνολικά ειρηνικές, αν και υπήρχαν αναφορές για επιτόπιες συγκρούσεις μεταξύ διαδηλωτών και αστυνομίας. Εικόνες και βίντεο από αυτήν την ημέρα έδειξαν προεδρεύοντα σημεία όπως το Χάμπς-Ελυσέ και το Πλας ντου Τροκαντέρ πληρείς διαδηλωτές.

Η επικύρωση της συγκεκριμένης ανάρτησης στο Facebook απαιτεί μια πιο συγκεκριμένη εξέταση του περιεχομένου της φωτογραφίας. Στοιχεία όπως η ορατή σημαία, η στυλιστική των ενδυμάτων, η παρουσία ηλεκτρονικών σημαίων στα γαλλικά και τα αναγνωρίσιμα παραθαλάσσια χώρα μπορούν να βοηθήσουν να καθοριστεί αν η εικόνα ανταποκρίνεται αληθινά σε μια προστασία στη Παρίσι. Η αντιστοίχιση της φωτογραφίας με πιστοποιημένη έκδοση των ειδήσεων και αποσπάσματα από αξιόπιστες πηγές της 17ης Ιουλίου 2021 είναι σημαντική. Παραδείγματος χάριν, πολλές πιστές εικόνες από την ημέρα εκείνη δείχνουν μεγάλες συγκεντρώσεις, και μερικές από αυτές περιλαμβάνουν την Εικονοστάσιο Εφελύγγιο ή άλλα παραθαλάσσια χώρα που επιβεβαιώνουν την τοποθεσία.

Ωστόσο, τα αναρτήματα στα κοινωνικά δίκτυα μπορεί να εμφανίζουν εικόνες με λανθασμένες ημερομηνίες, τοποθεσίες ή γεγονότα. Σε αυτήν την περίπτωση, αν η φωτογραφία συμπίπτει με αυτές που δημοσιεύθηκαν από αξιόπιστα ιδρύματα ειδήσεων της 17ης Ιουλίου 2021 και περιλαμβάνει σαφείς δείκτες για την Παρίσι, το αίτημα είναι πιθανό να είναι αξιόπιστο. Αντίθετα, αν η εικόνα απουσιάζει αυτά τα στοιχεία ή αντιστοιχεί σε φωτογραφίες από διαφορετικές εκδηλώσεις ή πόλεις, το αναρτημένο αίτημα είναι αμφισημερικό.

Μετά την ανάλυση δημόσιων φωτογραφιών και αποσπασμάτων από την 17η Ιουλίου 2021, είναι πιθανό να είναι αληθινή η φωτογραφία που αναφέρεται στην ιστοσελίδα της Παρισινής ενάντια στις νέες μέτρα κατά της πανδημίας. Η ημερομηνία αντιστοιχεί σε μια μεγάλη διαδήλωση και το πλαίσιο ανταποκρίνεται στη διαδεδομένη δημόσια αντίδραση ενάντια στις πολιτικές υγείας της κυβέρνησης. Ωστόσο, πάντα είναι σύμφωνο να επιβεβαιωθεί η πραγματική αξιοπιστία των διαδεδομένων εικόνων, καθώς η πληροφορία μπορεί εύκολα να διαδοθεί στα κοινωνικά δίκτυα.

Συνοπτικά, το αίτημα ότι η φωτογραφία που αναρτήθηκε στο Facebook έχει ληφθεί στη Παρίσι την 17η Ιουλίου 2021 κατά τη διάρκεια μιας διαδήλωσης εναντίον νέων μέτρων κατά της πανδημίας είναι υποστηριζόμενο από το πλαίσιο των μεγάλων διαδηλώσεων που έγιναν την ημέρα αυτή. Αν και το γενικό πλαίσιο ταιριάζει με τα ιστορικά γεγονότα, η αληθινή αξιοπιστία της συγκεκριμένης φωτογραφίας εξαρτάται από τη συμφωνία με τις επιβεβαιωμένες εικόνες από την ημέρα αυτή. Η επικύρωση της αλήθειας παραμένει απαραίτητη για να διασφαλιστεί η ακριβής αναπαράσταση σημαντικών στιγμών στη δημόσια διάσκεψη.

A social media post circulating online claims that authorities are implementing "remote immunization" using military, police, and "sniper services" to forcibly vaccinate unvaccinated individuals. According to the post, individuals would be hunted and shot with specialized vaccine-loaded ammunition, purportedly using harmless bullets that inject the vaccine upon contact with targeted areas such as the neck, shoulders, or thighs. The post goes on to suggest that this measure would result in complete immunization of the population within three days.

To analyze the veracity of this claim, it's important to consider both the scientific feasibility and the current public health practices regarding vaccination.

First, the notion of "remote immunization" via shooting vaccine ampoules into individuals is not grounded in any established medical or scientific protocol. Vaccines are typically administered via injection by trained healthcare professionals in controlled environments to ensure safety, correct dosage, and proper record-keeping. The description of ammunition carrying a vaccine ampoule, which would inject its contents upon impact, not only lacks any basis in medical practice but also poses obvious risks of injury, infection, and improper dosing.

Furthermore, the idea of deploying military, police, and snipers to forcibly vaccinate individuals is contrary to both ethical standards and legal frameworks governing public health. Mass vaccination campaigns, such as those for COVID-19, measles, or influenza, rely on public education, outreach, and voluntary participation. While some countries have implemented mandates or incentives to increase vaccination rates, none have resorted to using force or weaponized delivery methods.

The claim also raises questions about logistics and safety. Shooting individuals with an arrow or bullet, even if purportedly harmless, could cause trauma, bleeding, and other medical complications. There is no evidence that vaccine delivery via projectile is safe, effective, or in use anywhere in the world. Traditional vaccine delivery systems, such as syringes or needle-free jet injectors, are designed to minimize discomfort and maximize safety, and are administered by trained personnel.

Moreover, the assertion that such a measure would result in 100 percent immunization in three days is unrealistic. Achieving full immunization coverage, even under optimal circumstances, requires careful planning, consent, follow-up, and monitoring for adverse effects. Public health authorities emphasize the importance of transparency, informed consent, and community engagement in vaccination campaigns.

In summary, the claim that authorities are hunting down unvaccinated individuals and using "sniper services" to shoot vaccine-loaded ammunition is entirely unfounded. There is no evidence, scientific basis, or official policy supporting such an approach. The post appears to be either satirical, misleading, or part of misinformation. Vaccination remains a critical tool for public health, but it is administered in accordance with established medical standards, not through forced remote delivery by armed personnel.

Et sosialt medierende innlegg som kretser på nettet påstår at myndigheter implementerer «ferdig immunisering» ved hjelp av militær, politi og «sniperservices» for å tvangsimmunisere uimmuniserte personer. Ifølge innlegget vil personer bli jaktet og skutt med spesialladede vaccineampuller, hvor det påstås at de bruker ubærenge skudd som injiserer vaksinen ved kontakt med målområder som halsen, skulrene eller lårene. Innlegget går videre og foreslår at dette tiltaket vil føre til full immunitet blant befolkningen innen tre dager.

For å analysere påstanden om året, er det viktig å ta hensyn til både den vitenskapelige muligheten og de nåværende offentlige helsepraksisene rundt vaksinering.

Først og fremst er idéen om «ferdig immunisering» gjennom å skute vaksinampuller inn i personer ikke basert på noen opprettet medisinsk eller vitenskapelig protokoll. Vaksiner administreres typisk ved injeksjon av utdannete helsepersonell i kontrollerte miljøer for å sikre sikkerhet, korrekt dosering og riktig registrering. Beskrivelsen av ammunition som bærer en vaksinampull, som skal injisere innholdet ved treff, har ikke noen basis i medisinsk praksis og gir også opplyste risiko for skader, infeksjoner og feil dosering.

Enda mer, idéen om å bruke militær, politi og snipers for å tvangsimmunisere personer er motstridende både med etiske standarder og lovgivning som regulerer offentlig helse. Massetiltak for vaksinering, som for eksempel for covid-19, milt, eller influensa, bygger på offentlig opplæring, utvikling og frivillig deltagelse. Selv om noen land har innført krav eller incentiv for å øke vaksineringssatsen, har ingen brukt kraft eller våpenetiserte leveringsmetoder.

Påstanden opptrer også spørsmål om logistikk og sikkerhet. Å skute personer med en pil eller skudd, selv om det påstås å være ubærenge, kan forårsake trauma, blødning og andre medisinske komplikasjoner. Det er ingen bevis på at vaksinlevering gjennom projektiler er sikker, effektiv eller brukt noen sted i verden. Tradisjonelle vaksinleveringssystemer, som nåleløse jet-injectorer, er designet for å minimere ubehag og maksimere sikkerhet, og administreres av utdannede personell.

Enda mer, påstanden om at slik tiltak vil føre til 100 % immunitet innen tre dager er urealistisk. Å oppnå fullt immunisering, selv under optimale forhold, krever nøye planlegging, samtykke, oppfølging og overvåking av bivirkninger. Offentlige helsemyndigheter understreker betydningen av gjennomsiktighet, informert samtykke og samarbeid med samfunnet i vaksineringstiltak.

I alt, påstanden om at myndigheter jaktet ned uimmuniserte personer og brukte «sniperservices» for å skute vaksinladede ammunition er helt upåvirket. Det er ingen bevis, vitenskapelig basis eller offentlig politikk som støtter slik tilnærming. Innlegget virker å være enten satirisk, misvisende eller del av feilinformasjon. Vaksinering er fortsatt en kritisk verktøy for offentlig helse, men det utføres i samsvar med opprettet medisinske standarder, ikke gjennom tvangsferdig levering av våpenedde personell.

In recent weeks, a social media post has circulated widely featuring a short video clip in which a person claims that, after receiving a COVID-19 vaccine, a metal object—a spoon—can stick to their shoulder. The person demonstrates this by pressing a spoon against their skin, where it appears to adhere without support. The implication is that something in the vaccine, such as metals or magnetic materials, allows objects to stick to the skin, suggesting unusual or harmful ingredients in the vaccine.

This claim is not new and has surfaced repeatedly since COVID-19 vaccination campaigns began. Videos and photos of coins, keys, and other metallic objects allegedly sticking to vaccinated individuals’ arms or shoulders have proliferated on platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and TikTok. The core assertion remains that something in the vaccines is making people "magnetic," fueling speculation and concern about vaccine safety and transparency.

To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to examine several aspects: the composition of COVID-19 vaccines, the physics of adhesion, and the broader context of misinformation during the pandemic.

First, COVID-19 vaccines authorized for use contain no metals or magnetic ingredients. The main ingredients in mRNA vaccines (such as those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) include messenger RNA, lipids (fats), salts, and sugars. Other vaccines may use traditional methods like inactivated viruses or protein subunits, but none use metals or magnetic particles. Vaccine ingredient lists are made publicly available by manufacturers and regulatory agencies.

Second, from a scientific standpoint, it is not possible for any component of these vaccines to make the human body magnetic. The doses are tiny—measured in micrograms or milliliters—and contain only biologically relevant compounds. Even if trace metals were present (which they are not), the quantities would be far below anything capable of causing objects to adhere magnetically to skin.

The phenomenon seen in the videos can be readily explained by basic physics and properties of human skin. Skin can be slightly sticky, especially if it is moist or oily, allowing lightweight objects like spoons to temporarily adhere due to friction and surface tension. This effect can be replicated by pressing objects against clean, dry skin, regardless of vaccination status. In some cases, individuals may exaggerate the effect through subtle tilting or by using adhesive substances.

Health authorities and scientific experts have repeatedly debunked claims of "magnetic" vaccines. These demonstrations rely on misdirection, misunderstanding of science, or intentional deception. The continued spread of this myth contributes to vaccine hesitancy and undermines public trust in vaccination campaigns, which are essential for controlling the spread of COVID-19 and protecting public health.

In conclusion, the claim that COVID-19 vaccination causes metal objects like spoons to stick to the skin is not supported by scientific evidence. The ingredients in the vaccines cannot induce magnetism or cause objects to adhere to the body. Such viral videos and posts are misleading and should be regarded with skepticism.

මෙම අභියෝගය නව නොවේ සහ කොවිඩ්-19 වාක්‍ය ප්‍රමාණ අවසන් වීමෙන් පසුව සිදු විය යුතු අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇති අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇති අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇති අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇති අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇති අතර ඒ අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත. 

මෙම අභියෝගය අත්හැරීමට සිදු කරන්නේ මෙම ප්‍රමාණයේ තරම් ප්‍රමාණය, ප්‍රමාණයේ ස්ථායී විද්‍යාත්මක සාධක සහ ප්‍රචාරණයේ මිතිකරණය අතර සියලුම තරම් ප්‍රචාරණය වී ඇත.

පළමුව, කොවිඩ්-19 ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් මිනිසුන් ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. mRNA ප්‍රමාණය (උදා: පොෆිර්-බයෝන්ටෙක් සහ මෝඩර්නා) ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රධාන අභියෝගයන් ඇති විද්‍යුත් පරිපථය, ප්‍රමාණය, ප්‍රමාණය සහ ප්‍රමාණය. අනෙකුත් ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රමාණයන් සහ ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රමාණයන් සහ ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රමාණයන් සහ ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රමාණයන් සහ ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ. ප්‍රමාණයේ ප්‍රමාණයන් සහ ප්‍රමාණයන් ප්‍රමාණය සමඟ ප්‍රමාණයක් ප්‍රමාණයක් නොවේ.
