A recent social media post claims that Dr. Zarko Karadzovski, Chairman of the Commission for Infectious Diseases and a longtime epidemiologist at the Institute of Public Health, is "on the payroll of the Rockefeller Foundation." This assertion has sparked discussion online, with some users expressing concerns about potential conflicts of interest within North Macedonia's public health leadership. We examine the origins and validity of this claim, providing necessary background and context.

Who is Dr. Zarko Karadzovski?

Dr. Zarko Karadzovski has served as a prominent figure in North Macedonia’s public health system for decades. He is widely recognized for his role as Chairman of the Commission for Infectious Diseases, leading the country’s response to outbreaks such as COVID-19, and has held a longstanding position at the Institute of Public Health in Skopje. His expertise as an epidemiologist has made him a visible public health spokesperson, especially during times of crisis.

The Rockefeller Foundation and Public Health

The Rockefeller Foundation is a global philanthropic organization based in the United States. Since its founding in 1913, it has funded a range of health initiatives worldwide, including programs to combat infectious diseases. As a major donor, the foundation often provides grants to governmental agencies, research institutions, and non-governmental organizations. These grants may support research, capacity-building, or direct public health interventions, but recipients are typically institutions rather than individuals.

Analyzing the Claim

The social media post suggests that Dr. Karadzovski is “on the payroll” of the Rockefeller Foundation, implying a direct employment or financial relationship between the foundation and the Macedonian public health official. To evaluate this claim, it is important to distinguish between individual employment and institutional grants.

An examination of available public records, including the Rockefeller Foundation’s grant disclosures and employment rosters, reveals no direct evidence that Dr. Karadzovski has ever been employed or personally compensated by the foundation. There are no public reports of his name appearing on the foundation’s payroll. While the Rockefeller Foundation has historically provided funding to various health initiatives in Eastern Europe and the Balkans, these grants are typically made to institutions, not individual public health officials.

Possible Sources of Confusion

It is possible that the claim stems from misunderstandings about the nature of international funding in public health. For example, if the Institute of Public Health, where Dr. Karadzovski works, has received project funding or support from the Rockefeller Foundation, some may interpret this as a personal financial link. However, institutional grants are not the same as personal employment or remuneration.

Conclusion

There is no verifiable evidence to support the claim that Dr. Zarko Karadzovski is personally “on the payroll” of the Rockefeller Foundation. While the foundation has a long history of supporting public health initiatives globally, including in the Balkans, such support is generally directed to organizations, not individual employees. The assertion circulating on social media appears to conflate institutional funding with personal employment, leading to an inaccurate representation of Dr. Karadzovski’s relationship with the Rockefeller Foundation.

A social media post has recently circulated, making sweeping claims about the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccination efforts, and alleged global conspiracies. The post asserts that the pandemic is a manufactured event—a "biological, terrorist operation" orchestrated as part of a global project designed to usher in a "totalitarian, communist order." It further alleges that an organization referred to as the "World Hospital (Bank)" has calculated that the project will be completed in March 2025, and that, until then, there are plans to vaccinate everyone, "at any cost."

To assess these claims, it is important to examine each assertion for accuracy and context.

The claim that COVID-19 is a "false corona pandemic" and part of a coordinated terrorist operation has been a persistent narrative among conspiracy theorists since early 2020. COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, was declared a pandemic by the World Health Organization (WHO) in March 2020 after rapid global spread and mounting evidence of its health impact. The scientific consensus, supported by extensive peer-reviewed research, has confirmed the origin of the virus as natural, most likely emerging from zoonotic transmission. There is no credible evidence supporting the idea that the pandemic was deliberately engineered or staged as a terrorist act.

The post further claims that the pandemic is being used as a pretext to establish a "totalitarian, communist order" worldwide. Throughout the pandemic, governments have imposed varying degrees of restrictions, such as lockdowns, mask mandates, and vaccination requirements, aiming to limit the spread of the virus and protect public health. These measures have sparked debates about civil liberties and government overreach. However, labeling these public health responses as part of a global plot to install communism is unsubstantiated. Democracies around the world have implemented COVID-19 policies within legal frameworks, and no evidence indicates a coordinated movement towards global communism or totalitarianism as a result of pandemic management.

A key part of the post references the "World Hospital (Bank)," a term that does not correspond to any known international organization. It is possible the post conflates the World Health Organization (WHO) and the World Bank, both of which have played roles in the global response to COVID-19. The WHO provides public health guidance and technical support, while the World Bank has allocated funding to aid countries in coping with the economic and health impacts of the pandemic. Neither organization has announced a project timeline culminating in March 2025, nor any plan to forcibly vaccinate the entire global population "at any cost."

The global vaccination campaign has been a central strategy in managing the pandemic, aiming to reduce transmission, severe illness, and death. Vaccination policies vary by country, with some mandating vaccines for specific groups, such as healthcare workers, but no credible plan exists to vaccinate every person worldwide through coercion.

In summary, the social media post recycles several unfounded conspiracy theories about COVID-19, vaccines, and international organizations. None of its core claims are supported by credible evidence. The pandemic remains a public health crisis addressed by international cooperation, scientific research, and vaccination—not as part of a clandestine plot for global domination.

A social media post circulating widely claims that French scientists have demonstrated, via a video available in English and Russian, the discovery of "new components of graphene" in the blood of vaccinated individuals—components purportedly never seen before. This assertion has sparked concern and confusion, especially among those wary of COVID-19 vaccines and their ingredients. This article examines the origins and accuracy of the claim, providing context and a thorough fact-check.

The claim centers on the alleged presence of graphene, specifically graphene oxide or related nanomaterials, in the blood of people who have received COVID-19 vaccines. Graphene is a form of carbon arranged in a single layer of atoms and has been researched for various technological applications. However, it is not a recognized or approved component in any COVID-19 vaccine authorized for use in France or elsewhere.

The viral post refers to a video supposedly produced by French scientists, showing microscopic images and purported analysis of blood samples from vaccinated individuals. In the video, the narrators claim to observe unusual structures in the blood, which they identify as graphene or graphene-related substances. These observations are contrasted with blood samples from unvaccinated people, which allegedly do not exhibit the same features.

To assess the credibility of this claim, it is important to consider the scientific consensus and regulatory oversight surrounding vaccine ingredients. The manufacturing processes for vaccines, including those produced by Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, and AstraZeneca, are transparent and subject to rigorous review by health authorities such as the European Medicines Agency and the French National Agency for the Safety of Medicines and Health Products. The full list of ingredients for these vaccines is publicly available and does not include graphene or graphene oxide.

Additionally, the scientific method requires that extraordinary claims—such as the presence of novel nanomaterials in the bloodstream—be supported by peer-reviewed research, validated methods, and reproducible results. The video cited in the post does not appear in any recognized scientific journal, nor is it associated with known scientific institutions in France. The methods by which the supposed "graphene components" were identified are not described in detail, and the images provided lack the context and specificity needed for scientific validation.

Medical experts and professional societies have repeatedly debunked the idea that COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene. No credible studies have demonstrated the presence of graphene in vaccinated individuals' blood. Furthermore, the physical and chemical properties of graphene make it unlikely to be mistaken for common biological structures under a microscope without specialized detection equipment and techniques.

In conclusion, the claim that French scientists have demonstrated the existence of new graphene components in the blood of vaccinated people is not supported by scientific evidence. The video referenced in the social media post lacks transparency, methodological rigor, and endorsement from the scientific community. Assertions about undisclosed vaccine ingredients should be treated with skepticism and verified through reputable sources. The available evidence confirms that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain graphene, and there is no substantiated link between vaccination and graphene presence in human blood.

A claim circulating on social media alleges that Israel has announced intentions to begin microchipping its citizens, with a particular focus on children. This assertion has gained traction online, raising concerns about privacy, civil liberties, and governmental overreach. However, a thorough review of official statements, media reports, and available evidence reveals that this claim is misleading and not supported by credible information.

The origin of this claim appears to trace back to various social media posts and online forums, where it is often presented without substantiation or direct references to government announcements. The core of the allegation is that Israeli authorities are planning to insert microchips into people, particularly minors, purportedly for purposes such as tracking, identification, or health monitoring.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to examine recent actions and statements by Israeli officials. There have been no official announcements or policies from the Israeli government indicating plans to microchip citizens or children. Major Israeli news outlets and government press releases contain no evidence of such a program being considered or implemented. 

It's possible that this rumor gained momentum due to misunderstandings or misinterpretations of unrelated government initiatives. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, many countries, including Israel, implemented digital tracking via smartphones to help trace contacts and contain outbreaks. These measures, while controversial in some circles, relied on voluntary mobile applications and did not involve any form of physical microchipping. In May 2020, a comment by Israel's then-Prime Minister about tracking children’s movements for their safety was widely misreported and misconstrued as a proposal to implant microchips. The statement was quickly clarified by government spokespeople, emphasizing that no such plan existed and that the idea was metaphorical, not literal.

Microchipping humans is not a standard practice anywhere in the world, and the concept is often associated with science fiction or dystopian scenarios. While some private individuals in different countries have voluntarily implanted RFID chips for personal convenience or novelty, these instances are rare and not the result of government mandates.

In summary, there is no factual basis for the claim that Israel has announced intentions to start microchipping its citizens or children. The rumor likely stems from a misinterpretation of past statements and an amplification of fears regarding digital surveillance. As of the time of writing, there are no plans, official statements, or legislative proposals in Israel to introduce mandatory or widespread microchipping of any segment of the population. Social media users are encouraged to seek out reliable sources and official communications before sharing or acting on such claims.

A recent social media post asserts that “the BBC forgot to publish this statistic – 1,517 deaths from experimental vaccines in Britain and over 1 million side effects reported by over 330,000 people.” This claim is presented as an accusation of media omission regarding the reporting of vaccine safety data during the COVID-19 vaccination campaign in the United Kingdom. A careful examination of the statistics, their context, and the reporting standards of both health authorities and media outlets is necessary to assess the accuracy and relevance of these numbers.

The claim specifically refers to deaths and side effects allegedly caused by “experimental vaccines,” presumably referencing the COVID-19 vaccines authorized for emergency or conditional use in the UK since December 2020. The primary repository for vaccine safety data in the UK is the Yellow Card scheme, managed by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). The Yellow Card system collects voluntary reports of suspected side effects or adverse events following vaccination, regardless of whether a causal link to the vaccine has been established.

The figure of “1,517 deaths” likely originates from the cumulative total of death reports submitted to the Yellow Card scheme during the first two years of the COVID-19 vaccination rollout. However, it is crucial to understand that a report to the Yellow Card scheme does not confirm that the vaccine caused or contributed to the adverse event or death. The MHRA publicly states that the vast majority of reports are coincidental and reflect the high number of people vaccinated, many of whom are elderly or have pre-existing health conditions. Detailed investigations are carried out to determine if there is any pattern or credible evidence that suggests a causal relationship between vaccination and death, and to date, the MHRA and other health authorities worldwide have found that the benefits of COVID-19 vaccination far outweigh the risks.

Regarding the claim of “over 1 million side effects reported by over 330,000 people,” it is accurate that the Yellow Card scheme has received hundreds of thousands of reports of suspected side effects, ranging from mild symptoms like sore arms or headaches to more serious adverse events. As with the death reports, the existence of a report does not confirm that the vaccine caused the side effect. It is also important to note that increased public awareness and encouragement to report any and all symptoms following vaccination have led to higher numbers of reports, which is expected and desired for robust pharmacovigilance.

The post suggests a failure by the BBC to publish these figures. In reality, the BBC and other major news outlets have regularly reported on vaccine safety, including the existence and findings of the Yellow Card scheme. However, responsible journalism contextualizes these numbers, explaining the difference between a reported event and a confirmed case of vaccine-induced harm.

In summary, while the figures cited in the social media post are broadly in line with publicly available data from the UK’s vaccine safety monitoring system, they are presented without vital context. Reports of deaths and side effects are not evidence of causation. Health authorities continuously monitor vaccine safety and, so far, have found no evidence indicating that the COVID-19 vaccines used in Britain are responsible for large numbers of deaths or serious side effects when weighed against their demonstrated benefits in preventing illness and death from COVID-19.

A recent social media post claims, “The pandemic will go down in history as one of the biggest deceptions. Stay brave everyone.” This assertion suggests that the global COVID-19 pandemic was either exaggerated or fabricated and implies widespread deception by authorities or the media. In this article, we examine the context, background, and verifiable facts to assess the validity of this claim.

The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, was first identified in late 2019 in Wuhan, China. It rapidly spread across continents, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in January 2020 and a pandemic in March 2020. Governments worldwide implemented unprecedented measures, including lockdowns, travel restrictions, and mass vaccination campaigns, to curb the spread of the virus and reduce mortality.

The core claim in the social media post—that the pandemic was "one of the biggest deceptions"—echoes a narrative that has circulated on various online platforms since early 2020. This narrative typically alleges that the severity of the virus was exaggerated, that case and death numbers were manipulated, or that the pandemic was used as a pretext for government overreach.

Fact-checking the claim requires examining several key points:

1. **Epidemiological Evidence**: Independent health authorities from multiple countries, including the CDC, WHO, and national public health institutes, have consistently tracked COVID-19 cases and deaths using transparent methodologies. Excess mortality statistics, which compare deaths during the pandemic to averages from previous years, reveal significant increases in mortality across the globe during the pandemic period. These increases correlate with COVID-19 outbreaks.

2. **Medical Impact**: The medical community worldwide has documented the effects of COVID-19, including severe respiratory illness, long-term complications (commonly referred to as "long COVID"), and death, especially among vulnerable populations. Hospitals in numerous regions reported being overwhelmed during waves of infection, with medical staff sharing firsthand accounts of the virus’s impact.

3. **Scientific Consensus**: The overwhelming consensus among virologists, epidemiologists, and public health experts is that COVID-19 is a real, novel virus that caused a genuine global health crisis. While early responses and communication strategies were sometimes flawed, there is no credible evidence to support the theory that the pandemic was a manufactured deception.

4. **Addressing Misinformation**: While misinformation and conspiracy theories about the origins, severity, and management of the pandemic have circulated widely, these narratives often rely on misinterpretation of data, selective reporting, or unfounded speculation. Major investigations into data transparency and government responses have not revealed evidence of a coordinated global deception.

In conclusion, the claim that the COVID-19 pandemic will be remembered as "one of the biggest deceptions" is not supported by the available scientific, medical, and statistical evidence. The pandemic’s impact has been thoroughly documented by independent sources worldwide, and its consequences have been felt across societies, economies, and health systems. It is crucial for public discourse to be grounded in verified facts, especially when addressing issues of public health.

הצהרה לאומית עשויה להיחשב כהכרה, "הパンדמיקה תיכתב בהיסטוריה כמקרה אחד מהדמויות הגדושות ביותר. תחזו אומץ לכל." תובנה זו מציינת שパンדמיקה הקורונה-19 הייתה מוגזמת או הונדתה, ומערבת תביעה על השפעה נרחבת של תרגילים על ידי הרשויות או תקשורת. במאמר זה אנו בודקים את ההקשר, רקע, והעובדות הניתנות להערכה כדי לבדוק את תקפות הצהרה זו.

パンדמיקה הקורונה-19, שנגרמה על ידי וירוס הקורונה החדש SARS-CoV-2, נמצאה לראשונה בסוף 2019 במושבה וואן, סין. היא נפלה במהירות על פני כל היבשות, ובהמשך נרעה הארגון העולמי לבריאות (WHO) להכרה במשבר בריאותי עולמי בינלאומי בפברואר 2020, ובהמשך נרעה את הפסיקה של PANDEMIC במרץ 2020. מדינות מובילות ערכו צעדים בלתי נפוצים, כולל סגרים, הגבלות על נסיעות, ומבצעים עיקריים של חיסונים, כדי להפחית את התפשטות הווירוס וה mortaliteit.

הטענה היסודית בפרסומת לאומית – שパンדמיקה הייתה "מקרה אחד מהדמויות הגדושות ביותר" – מזכירה נרטיב שסirkulated על תשתית אינטנרט משנת 2020. נרטיב זה בדרך כלל מציין שהחומרה של הווירוס הוגזמה, שהמקרים וה mortaliteit נשלטו, או שהパンדמיקה הונתה כסיבוב עקירה של הרשויות.

לכבוד טענות יש לבדוק מספר נקודות עיקריות:

1. **האינפורמציה הפליטולוגית**: רשויות בריאות עצמאיות ממדינות רבות, כולל CDC, WHO, ומכונים לאומיים לבריאות ציבוריים, ערכו באופן קבוע את המקרים וה mortaliteit של הקורונה-19 באמצעות שיטות שקופות. הסטטיסטיקות על mortaliteit מוגזמת, שהשוות את המותים במהלך PANDEMIC למאvetים מממוצעים של שנים קודמות, מדגישות את הزيادة משמעותית של mortaliteit בכל העולם במהלך תקופת PANDEMIC. הزيادة הזו קשורה עם תפרעות הקורונה-19.

2. **ההשפעה המטרית**: הקהילה המטרית העולמית שמרה את השפעת הקורונה-19, כולל מחלה חמורה של ריאות, תופעות ארוכות טרף (שנוצרות לעיתים כ"קורונה ארוכה"), ומות, במיוחד בקרב קבוצות רגישות. במחוזות רבות נפלו מרחבי רפואת נפש בתקופות של תפרעות, עם צוותים רפואיים ששיתפו תובנות ראשוניות של השפעת הווירוס.

3. **הסכמה מדעית**: הסכמה מוחלטת על ידי מדענים לווירולוגיה, אפידמיולוגים, וחוקרי בריאות ציבוריים היא שקורונה-19 היא וירוס אמיתי, חדש, שנגרם למשבר בריאותי אמיתי על פני העולם. למרות שהר응ס והשיטות תקשורת בתחילתה היו לעיתים לא מדויקות, אין הוכחה מוסרית לתיאוריה שパンדמיקה הייתה מוניציפלית הונדה.

4. **ההתייחסות למידע שגוי**: למרות שמידע שגוי ותיאורים מפוצלים על מקורות, חומרה, וניהול PANDEMIC התרחשו בפיזור נרחב, נרטיבים אלו לרוב מותאמים לפרשנות שגויה של נתונים, דיווחים בודדים, או ספקולציות ללא בסיס. חקירות גדולות על שקיפות נתונים והרשות של הרשויות לא חשפו הוכחה לתרגלת הונדה עולמית.

בקיצור, הטענה שパンדמיקה הקורונה-19 תיכתב בהיסטוריה כ"מקרה אחד מהדמויות הגדושות ביותר" אינה נתמכת על ידי הוכחות מדעיות, מטריות, וסטטיסטיקות זמינות. השפעת PANDEMIC הוגדרה באופן מלא על ידי מקורות עצמאיים עולמיים, ותוצאותיה הרגישו בכל תחומים של תרבות, אירוח, ומערכות בריאות. חשוב מאוד להערכה ציבוריים להימצאות בעובדות הוכחות, במיוחד בעת טיפול בענייני בריאות ציבוריים.

A recent social media post has gone viral, claiming that a document from the Commission on Infectious Diseases to the British Government acknowledges that COVID-19 vaccines would lead to the emergence of a new variant capable of killing up to 35% of people, due to the vaccines' inability to prevent virus transmission. This alarming assertion has sparked widespread concern and confusion online. Here, we examine the origins of this claim, the relevant scientific context, and the veracity of the statement.

The claim appears to be rooted in a misunderstanding and misrepresentation of official documents and scientific discussion around COVID-19 vaccines and the evolution of the virus. The Commission on Infectious Diseases, as referenced in the post, is not a widely recognized or official advisory body to the British Government. The primary sources of advice to the UK Government on COVID-19 have been bodies such as the Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (SAGE), the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI), and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

No credible document from these bodies has claimed that COVID-19 vaccines would directly cause the emergence of a new variant that is both more deadly and capable of killing up to 35% of those infected. The figure of "35%" mortality is especially significant, as it suggests a death rate far higher than any observed with SARS-CoV-2 variants to date. Throughout the pandemic, the most severe variants have had case fatality rates far lower than this number, with early variants estimated at 1-3%, and Omicron and its subvariants significantly lower.

COVID-19 vaccines were developed and deployed to reduce severe illness, hospitalizations, and deaths. While it is true that the vaccines do not entirely prevent transmission — especially with new variants like Omicron — they remain highly effective at preventing severe outcomes. The scientific consensus is that widespread vaccination is one of the most effective tools for reducing the impact of the pandemic.

Concerns have been raised in the scientific community about "vaccine-driven" evolution, a theoretical scenario where widespread immunity might pressure the virus to evolve immune escape mutations. However, there is no evidence that COVID-19 vaccines have caused the emergence of more deadly variants. Variant evolution is a complex process influenced by many factors, including the scale of infection, viral mutation rates, and immunity in the population from both infection and vaccination.

The idea that vaccination would lead to a variant with a 35% fatality rate is not supported by any credible scientific evidence or official documentation. Experts continue to monitor for new variants and assess vaccine effectiveness, but current data do not support the scenario described in the social media post.

In summary, the claim that a formal document to the British Government admits COVID-19 vaccines would create a deadly new variant with a 35% mortality rate is unfounded. There is no public record of such a document, and the scientific evidence does not support this scenario. Vaccines remain a cornerstone of the public health response to COVID-19, and claims such as this risk undermining trust in proven interventions.

A recent social media post has sparked concern by claiming, “In case the second dose does not kill you, the third will surely work because it will be together with the flu vaccine.” This statement directly implies that COVID-19 vaccine booster shots, particularly when administered alongside the flu vaccine, are dangerous and potentially lethal. Given the significant impact of such messages on public perception and vaccine hesitancy, it is crucial to examine the facts and provide accurate information.

**Understanding the Vaccination Process**

COVID-19 vaccines, like other vaccines, undergo extensive clinical trials and rigorous safety evaluations before being authorized for public use. Initial vaccination regimens for COVID-19 often involved two doses, followed by booster shots as new variants emerged and studies showed waning immunity over time. Similarly, the flu vaccine is updated annually to target circulating strains and has been administered safely for decades.

**Co-Administration of Vaccines**

The claim that receiving a COVID-19 booster “together with the flu vaccine” poses a danger is not supported by scientific evidence. Health authorities in many countries, including national immunization programs, have recommended and permitted the co-administration of COVID-19 and influenza vaccines. This practice is based on data from clinical studies showing that the immune response to each vaccine remains robust and that side effects are similar to those experienced when either vaccine is given alone. The most commonly reported side effects—such as soreness at the injection site, mild fever, or fatigue—are generally short-lived and not dangerous.

**Safety and Monitoring**

Vaccine safety is monitored continuously, both in clinical trials and through national reporting systems once vaccines are in wide use. Adverse events are rare and are thoroughly investigated, with findings made publicly available. Serious side effects, such as severe allergic reactions, are exceedingly uncommon, and vaccination providers are trained to manage them. There is no evidence to support the assertion that receiving a second or third dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, either alone or with the flu vaccine, is “lethal” or significantly increases health risks.

**Addressing Vaccine Misinformation**

The spread of misinformation about vaccine safety can undermine public health efforts and potentially lead to increased illness, hospitalizations, and deaths from preventable diseases. The claim in the social media post relies on unfounded fears and lacks factual basis. COVID-19 vaccines and flu vaccines remain critical tools in reducing the impact of respiratory illnesses, especially among vulnerable populations.

**Conclusion**

The assertion that booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine—either singly or in combination with the flu vaccine—are fatal is not supported by scientific evidence or real-world data. Both vaccines have well-established safety profiles, and their combined administration is a recommended and effective approach to protecting individual and public health. It is important for individuals to seek information from trusted health sources and consult healthcare professionals when making decisions about vaccination.

A recent post circulating on Facebook makes several claims regarding vaccines, the behavior of viruses, and mask-wearing protocols for young children. The post asserts that vaccines are a source of mutations and diseases, questions why the virus persists despite widespread vaccination, and insists that masks should be worn by everyone, including children as young as two years old. To provide clarity, we examine each of these claims in detail, drawing on scientific understanding and public health guidance.

First, the claim that vaccines are a source of mutations and diseases is not supported by the current body of scientific evidence. Vaccines are designed to train the immune system to recognize and fight pathogens such as viruses or bacteria, without causing the diseases themselves. The concept that vaccines cause viral mutations is a misinterpretation of how viruses evolve. Viral mutations occur naturally as viruses replicate and spread among hosts, regardless of vaccination status. While it is true that selective pressure, such as that introduced by widespread vaccination, can influence which viral strains become more common, vaccines do not "create" mutations. Instead, vaccines help reduce the overall number of infections, thereby limiting the opportunities for the virus to mutate.

Additionally, vaccines undergo extensive testing for safety and efficacy before approval. Side effects, when they occur, are typically mild and temporary. Serious adverse reactions are rare. The assertion that vaccines are a significant source of new diseases is not substantiated by evidence; in fact, vaccines have played a crucial role in controlling and even eradicating many infectious diseases worldwide.

The second claim suggests that the virus should disappear even if not everyone is vaccinated. In reality, achieving the disappearance—or eradication—of a virus is complex. Vaccination reduces transmission by lowering the number of susceptible individuals, but unless a very high proportion of the population is immune, the virus can continue to circulate. Factors such as vaccine coverage, the infectiousness of the virus, and population movement all affect whether a virus persists. For many viruses, including those causing COVID-19, reaching complete eradication is challenging, particularly when vaccine uptake is incomplete and new variants emerge.

Finally, the post claims that masks must be worn by everyone, including two-year-olds. Mask guidance varies by country and evolves with new scientific findings. Early in the COVID-19 pandemic, some health authorities recommended masks for young children to reduce transmission risk. However, medical consensus generally advises caution with mask use in very young children, especially those under two years old, due to potential breathing difficulties and safety concerns. Most public health guidelines now recommend masks for children above a certain age—often two or older—mainly in high-risk settings or during outbreaks, while emphasizing the importance of proper fit and supervision.

In summary, the claims made in the Facebook post do not accurately reflect the scientific understanding of vaccines, viral persistence, or mask guidelines for children. Vaccines are safe and effective tools in preventing disease and limiting viral mutations, the disappearance of a virus depends on broad immunity, and mask recommendations for young children are nuanced and based on balancing safety and public health needs.

In recent years, discussions around COVID-19 vaccines have been rife with misinformation and polarized opinions. A social media post circulating widely states: "Anti-vaxxers are not the ones that cause blood clots. The vaccines do." This message encapsulates a recurrent claim found in online debates, raising concerns about vaccine safety and attributing adverse health effects solely to vaccination.

To assess this claim, it is essential to understand the background of vaccine development, the incidence of blood clots, and what current evidence suggests about causality.

**Context and Background**

Vaccines against COVID-19, including those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, Johnson & Johnson, and AstraZeneca, have undergone rigorous testing in clinical trials before receiving emergency use authorization and subsequent approval in many countries. The vast majority of vaccinated individuals experience mild side effects, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, or mild fever.

However, since the roll-out of COVID-19 vaccines, rare cases of blood clots have been reported, particularly in association with the Johnson & Johnson and AstraZeneca vaccines. These cases, known medically as thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), involve blood clots in combination with low platelet counts. Initial reports of these events prompted temporary pauses and further investigation by health authorities.

**Fact-Checking the Claim**

The social media post suggests that anti-vaxxers—individuals who refuse vaccination—do not cause blood clots, whereas the vaccines themselves do. This framing contains elements of truth but lacks necessary nuance and context.

It is accurate that individuals who do not receive vaccines cannot experience vaccine-induced side effects, including the rare blood clotting events associated with certain COVID-19 vaccines. In this sense, anti-vaxxers do not directly "cause" blood clots by refusing vaccination. However, the implication that vaccines broadly and commonly cause blood clots requires clarification.

The risk of developing blood clots after receiving a COVID-19 vaccine is extremely low. For example, the incidence of TTS after AstraZeneca vaccination was estimated to be approximately 1 in 100,000 to 1 in 250,000 doses, depending on age and location. For the Johnson & Johnson vaccine, the risk is similarly rare. These rates must be contrasted with the risk of blood clots associated with COVID-19 infection itself, which is much higher. COVID-19 is known to cause serious complications, including blood clots in the lungs, legs, and other organs, especially in hospitalized patients.

Health authorities have reviewed the available evidence and concluded that the benefits of vaccination far outweigh the risks, including those of rare blood clotting events. Where elevated risk has been identified (e.g., in younger women with the AstraZeneca or Johnson & Johnson vaccines), alternative vaccines have been recommended.

**Conclusion**

The claim that "the vaccines cause blood clots" is misleading without context. While there is a very small risk of rare blood clotting disorders following certain COVID-19 vaccines, this risk is much lower than the risk of blood clots from COVID-19 infection itself. Anti-vaxxers, by definition, do not experience vaccine side effects, but their refusal of vaccination may leave them more vulnerable to severe COVID-19 complications, including blood clots. The overall scientific consensus supports vaccination as a safe and effective public health measure, with extremely low risks of serious side effects in the general population.

近年来，关于新冠疫苗的讨论充斥着大量错误信息和两极化的观点。一条在社交媒体上广泛传播的帖子声称：“反疫苗人士不会导致血栓，是疫苗导致了血栓。”这一信息体现了在线辩论中反复出现的主张，引发了人们对疫苗安全性的担忧，并将不良健康影响归因于疫苗接种。

要评估这一主张，有必要了解疫苗的研发背景、血栓的发生率以及当前证据对因果关系的说明。

**背景与上下文**

针对新冠的疫苗，包括辉瑞-生物科技、莫德纳、强生和阿斯利康研发的疫苗，均在获得紧急使用授权和在许多国家正式批准之前，经历了严格的临床试验。绝大多数接种疫苗的人只会出现轻微的副作用，如注射部位疼痛、疲劳或轻度发烧。

然而，自新冠疫苗推广以来，已报告了罕见的血栓病例，尤其是与强生和阿斯利康疫苗有关的病例。这些病例在医学上被称为血小板减少症伴血栓形成（TTS），表现为血栓合并血小板减少。最初报告这些事件后，卫生当局暂停了疫苗接种并展开进一步调查。

**对这一主张的查证**

该社交媒体帖子声称，反疫苗人士（拒绝接种疫苗的人）不会导致血栓，而疫苗本身会导致血栓。这种表述包含部分事实，但缺乏必要的细致和上下文。

确实，未接种疫苗的人不会经历疫苗引起的副作用，包括与某些新冠疫苗相关的罕见血栓事件。从这个意义上说，反疫苗人士通过拒绝接种疫苗并不会直接“导致”血栓。然而，暗示疫苗普遍且常见地导致血栓的说法需要澄清。

接种新冠疫苗后出现血栓的风险极低。例如，接种阿斯利康疫苗后出现TTS的估计发生率为每10万至25万剂中约1例，具体取决于年龄和地点。对于强生疫苗，风险同样罕见。这些发生率必须与新冠感染本身导致的血栓风险进行对比，而后者要高得多。新冠感染已知会导致严重的并发症，包括肺、腿和其他器官的血栓，尤其是在住院患者中。

卫生当局已审查了现有证据，并得出结论，即接种疫苗的益处远大于风险，包括罕见的血栓事件。在已识别出较高风险的情况下（例如，年轻女性接种阿斯利康或强生疫苗），已推荐使用替代疫苗。

**结论**

“疫苗导致血栓”的说法在缺乏上下文的情况下是误导性的。虽然某些新冠疫苗后出现罕见血栓疾病的概率非常小，但这一风险远低于新冠感染本身导致的血栓风险。反疫苗人士，按定义，不会经历疫苗副作用，但拒绝接种疫苗可能使他们更容易受到严重新冠并发症的影响，包括血栓。总体科学共识支持接种疫苗作为一项安全有效的公共卫生措施，一般人群中严重副作用的风险极低。

In recent days, social media has been abuzz with claims about the rate of COVID-19 reinfections among those who have been revaccinated. A widely shared post asserts that the percentage of infected people who are revaccinated is "really very small, about 0.02 percent." The post goes on to allege that critics are attempting to discredit this statement from the Minister of Health by comparing national statistics with data from just one COVID-19 ward, specifically in Tetovo—a hospital described as "one of the most fulfilled in the country."

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to unpack both the official statement and the nature of the criticism.

**Background and Context**

Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccination rates and breakthrough infections have been closely monitored by health authorities worldwide. Revaccination, often referred to as receiving a booster dose, has been recommended to increase immunity, particularly in response to waning vaccine effectiveness and the emergence of new variants.

The Minister of Health’s statement that only 0.02 percent of revaccinated individuals have become infected appears intended to reassure the public about the continued effectiveness of booster doses in preventing COVID-19 infection. This figure, if accurate, would indeed indicate a very low incidence of breakthrough infections among those who have received additional vaccine doses.

**Fact-Checking the 0.02 Percent Claim**

The claim that only 0.02 percent of revaccinated individuals have been infected would suggest that, out of every 10,000 people who received a booster or additional dose, only two experienced a breakthrough infection. In practice, the exact rate of breakthrough infections can vary significantly based on factors such as the time period studied, the population’s age and health status, the dominant variant in circulation, and the overall vaccination coverage.

While many countries have reported low breakthrough infection rates among those who have received booster doses—especially compared to unvaccinated individuals—the exact figure of 0.02 percent is exceptionally low. In real-world conditions, especially during waves of highly transmissible variants, breakthrough infection rates have often been reported as higher, though still much lower than in the unvaccinated population.

**Analysis of the Criticism**

The post criticizes attempts to discredit the Minister’s statement by comparing national data with statistics from a single COVID-19 ward in Tetovo. Relying on data from one hospital, particularly one that is described as "one of the most fulfilled in the country," can indeed produce a skewed picture. Hospitals in regions experiencing surges or serving populations with specific health profiles may have different proportions of vaccinated or revaccinated patients compared to national averages.

Such localized data can be useful for understanding specific outbreaks but should not be generalized to represent the entire country. National statistics, when available and accurately compiled, provide a more comprehensive view of vaccine effectiveness and the incidence of breakthrough infections.

**Conclusion**

The core claim that only 0.02 percent of revaccinated individuals have been infected is likely an optimistic figure, potentially reflecting a best-case scenario or a specific time frame. While booster doses significantly reduce the risk of infection and severe illness, real-world data often show higher, though still low, breakthrough rates. Comparing national data with statistics from a single hospital can be misleading, and it is important to interpret such comparisons with caution. Ultimately, while the Minister’s statement may highlight the effectiveness of revaccination, the full picture is more nuanced and requires careful analysis of comprehensive data.

हाल के दिनों में सोशल मीडिया पर कोरोना वायरस के दोबारा संक्रमण की दर के बारे में दावे तेजी से चर्चा में रहे हैं, जो वैक्सीन के बाद फिर से टीकाकरण किए गए व्यक्तियों में हो रहे हैं। एक व्यापक रूप से साझा किए गए पोस्ट के अनुसार, फिर से टीकाकरण किए गए व्यक्तियों में संक्रमित लोगों की दर "बहुत छोटी है, लगभग 0.02 प्रतिशत" है। इस पोस्ट के आगे यह दावा करते हैं कि आलोचक इस बयान को अस्वीकृत करने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं, जिसमें राष्ट्रीय सांख्यिकीय आंकड़ों के साथ एक कोरोना वायरस अस्पताल के आंकड़ों की तुलना करते हैं, विशेष रूप से टेटोवो में एक अस्पताल के आंकड़ों की तुलना करते हैं, जिसे "देश के सबसे अच्छे अस्पतालों में से एक" के रूप में वर्णित किया गया है।

इन दावों की सटीकता का आकलन करने के लिए, आधिकारिक बयान और आलोचक के प्रकृति के बारे में विस्तार से जानना महत्वपूर्ण है।

**पृष्ठभूमि और संदर्भ**

कोरोना वायरस महामारी के दौरान, स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियों द्वारा टीकाकरण दर और टीका के बावजूद संक्रमण के मामलों की निगरानी तेजी से की गई है। पुनः टीकाकरण, आम तौर पर एक बूस्टर डोज के रूप में वर्णित किया जाता है, वैक्सीन के प्रभाव के धीमा होने और नए वेरिएंट के उदय के बारे में इम्यूनिटी को बढ़ाने के लिए सिफारिश किया गया है। स्वास्थ्य मंत्री के बयान के अनुसार, केवल 0.02 प्रतिशत पुनः टीकाकरण किए गए व्यक्तियों में संक्रमण हुआ है, जो बूस्टर डोज के प्रभाव के बारे में लोगों के लिए आश्वस्त करने के उद्देश्य से दिया गया है। यह आंकड़ा, यदि सही हो, तो वास्तविक रूप से बूस्टर डोज प्राप्त करने वाले व्यक्तियों में टीका के बावजूद संक्रमण के बहुत कम दर को दर्शाता है।

**0.02 प्रतिशत के दावे की जांच**

केवल 0.02 प्रतिशत पुनः टीकाकरण किए गए व्यक्तियों में संक्रमण हुआ है के दावे के अनुसार, 10,000 लोगों में से केवल दो व्यक्ति टीका के बावजूद संक्रमित हो सकते हैं। वास्तविक दर अध्ययन के समय अवधि, जनसंख्या की आयु और स्वास्थ्य स्थिति, प्रसारित वेरिएंट, और सामान्य टीकाकरण दर जैसे कारकों पर निर्भर कर सकती है।

कई देशों ने बूस्टर डोज प्राप्त करने वाले व्यक्तियों में ब्रेकथ्रू संक्रमण की दर के बारे में निम्न आंकड़े रिपोर्ट किए हैं, विशेष रूप से अटीके वाले व्यक्तियों के मुकाबले, लेकिन 0.02 प्रतिशत के ठीक आंकड़े बहुत कम है। वास्तविक दशाओं में, विशेष रूप से अत्यधिक संक्रामक वेरिएंट के लहरों के दौरान, ब्रेकथ्रू संक्रमण की दर अक्सर उच्च रही है, लेकिन अटीके वाले व्यक्तियों के मुकाबले बहुत कम है।

**आलोचक के आलोचना के विश्लेषण**

पोस्ट ने मंत्री के बयान को अस्वीकृत करने की कोशिश करने की कोशिश करते हुए राष्ट्रीय डेटा के साथ एक कोरोना वायरस अस्पताल के आंकड़ों की तुलना करने की आलोचना करता है। एक अस्पताल के डेटा पर आधारित विश्लेषण, विशेष रूप से एक अस्पताल जिसे "देश के सबसे अच्छे अस्पतालों में से एक" के रूप में वर्णित किया गया है, वास्तविक दृश्य को बदल सकता है। एक अस्पताल के आंकड़े जिस इलाके में लहर बढ़ रही है या विशिष्ट स्वास्थ्य प्रोफाइल वाली जनसंख्या सेवा करता है, तो टीकाकरण या पुनः टीकाकरण किए गए रोगियों के अनुपात के राष्ट्रीय औसत से भिन्न हो सकते हैं।

**निष्कर्ष**

A social media post has recently resurfaced, claiming that PCR tests for COVID-19 are fraudulent, alleging that these tests cannot distinguish between COVID-19 and common colds or flu. The post suggests that widespread acceptance of these so-called “fake tests” perpetuates the pandemic and calls for greater exposure of what it describes as “PCR test medical fraud.” This article examines the accuracy of these claims and provides context about PCR testing and its role in the pandemic.

Background on PCR Testing

The Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) test is a laboratory method used to detect genetic material from a specific organism, such as a virus. During the COVID-19 pandemic, PCR tests became the gold standard for diagnosing SARS-CoV-2 infection due to their high sensitivity and specificity. These tests work by amplifying segments of viral RNA present in a sample, allowing detection even when only a small amount of virus is present.

Are PCR Tests “Fake”?

The claim that PCR tests are “fake” is not supported by the available evidence. PCR technology has been widely used for decades to diagnose infections ranging from HIV to influenza. The protocols for COVID-19 PCR tests were developed to specifically identify unique genetic sequences found only in the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Laboratories carefully design primers—short pieces of DNA—that bind only to these sequences, minimizing the risk of cross-reactivity with other viruses.

Can PCR Tests Confuse COVID-19 with Colds or Flu?

The assertion that PCR tests cannot distinguish between COVID-19 and other respiratory illnesses, such as the common cold or influenza, is misleading. While it is true that respiratory viruses can cause similar symptoms, PCR tests are designed to identify the genetic material of specific pathogens. For example, a PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 will not give a positive result if only rhinovirus (the most common cause of colds) or influenza virus is present in the sample. Separate PCR tests exist for influenza and other respiratory viruses, and multiple tests can be run simultaneously to distinguish between them in cases of co-infection.

Limitations and Accuracy

No diagnostic test is perfect. PCR tests can sometimes produce false negatives if the sample is collected improperly or if the viral load is very low. Rarely, improperly designed tests or contamination can cause false positives, but these instances are exceedingly uncommon in well-regulated laboratories. Regulatory agencies require rigorous validation of tests before they can be used clinically.

The Role of PCR Testing in the Pandemic

PCR testing has been essential for identifying and isolating cases, tracking the spread of the virus, and informing public health decisions. Early detection of COVID-19 cases has helped prevent outbreaks and save lives. Suggesting that PCR tests are broadly fraudulent undermines efforts to control the pandemic and may contribute to public confusion and mistrust.

Conclusion

The claim that PCR tests cannot distinguish COVID-19 from colds or flu and are therefore a medical fraud is not supported by the scientific evidence or medical consensus. PCR tests for COVID-19 are specifically designed to detect SARS-CoV-2 and do not conflate results with other respiratory viruses. While no test is infallible, PCR testing remains a reliable tool in diagnosing COVID-19 and managing the public health response.

A video circulating on Facebook shows several individuals dressed in protective suits disinfecting a train station in Great Britain. The accompanying post alleges that these workers are only performing the cleaning for the benefit of cameras and media attention, rather than genuinely sanitizing the area. The post claims that the disinfection is staged and not conducted with the intention to actually clean or protect public health.

To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to consider the context in which such disinfection activities occur, particularly in the wake of public health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic. During periods of heightened concern about infectious diseases, public transport hubs like train stations are frequently targeted for enhanced sanitation measures. Cleaning crews are often equipped with protective clothing, sometimes referred to as "spacesuits," to shield themselves from potential contaminants and to comply with safety regulations.

The visual impact of these operations, especially when performed in public and heavily trafficked areas, has often attracted media coverage. Some cleaning activities are scheduled in coordination with media outlets to showcase efforts being made to ensure public safety and to reassure the public. This can result in photographs and videos of workers actively disinfecting facilities, which are then broadcast or shared on social media.

However, the claim that such cleaning efforts are solely for show, and not for actual disinfection, requires more scrutiny. Transport authorities and contracted cleaning services generally adhere to established protocols for sanitation, especially during outbreaks of infectious diseases. The use of protective suits, disinfectants, and systematic cleaning routines are standard procedures designed to minimize the risk of transmission. While it is true that some cleaning events may be timed for maximum visibility or public relations impact, it does not necessarily follow that the cleaning itself is fraudulent or ineffective.

There have been instances where skepticism arose regarding the authenticity of certain public sanitation demonstrations, particularly when the same workers or scenes are repeatedly featured in media coverage. Nevertheless, these cases are exceptions rather than the norm. Most public cleaning operations are conducted as part of ongoing efforts to maintain hygiene and public safety, regardless of whether cameras are present.

In the specific case of the video from Great Britain, without further evidence indicating that the workers did not actually disinfect the station, or that the cleaning was staged exclusively for the media, the core claim of the Facebook post remains unsubstantiated. Protective clothing and visible cleaning efforts are typical during public health crises, and their presence does not inherently imply deception. It is possible that the cleaning was both genuine and photographed for documentation or communication purposes.

In summary, while media coverage of cleaning activities in public spaces may sometimes be orchestrated for visibility, there is insufficient evidence to support the claim that workers at the train station in Great Britain acted only for the camera and did not actually disinfect the area. Public health protocols require genuine sanitation efforts, and visual documentation does not automatically equate to staged actions. Fact-checking such claims necessitates direct evidence of misconduct, which is lacking in this instance.

فیلمی که در فیسبوک در حال گردش است، تصویری از چند نفر دارای پوشاک حفاظتی است که در ایستگاه ریلی انگلستان در حال dezinfeksiyon هستند. پست همراه با این فیلم ادعا می‌کند که این کارکنان تنها به منظور دوربین و توجه رسانه‌ها انجام می‌دهند و در واقع مراقبت بهداشتی را انجام نمی‌دهند. پست ادعا می‌کند که dezinfeksiyon بطور تزیینی انجام شده و به منظور واقعی تمیز کردن یا حفاظت از سلامت عمومی انجام نشده است.

برای ارزیابی صحت این ادعاهای، لازم است با سبک انجام این فعالیت‌های dezinfeksiyon در محیط‌هایی مانند ایستگاه‌های ریلی در دوران بحران‌های بهداشتی مانند پاندمی کرونا، بررسی شود. در دورانی که نگرانی بیشتری درباره بیماری‌های عفونی وجود دارد، ایستگاه‌های مواصلات عمومی مانند ایستگاه‌های ریلی اغلب مورد توجه بیشتری برای اقدامات بهبود بهداشتی قرار می‌گیرند. تیم‌های تمیزی اغلب با پوشاک حفاظتی، گاهی اوقات به عنوان "پوشاک فضا" شناخته شده، دریافت می‌کنند تا از ممکن شدن آلودگی و رعایت مقررات ایمنی در برابر آلوده‌سازی‌های ممکن محافظت شوند.

تاثیر بصری این فعالیت‌ها به خصوص وقتی در مناطق عمومی و باریک بازدید شده است، اغلب توجه رسانه‌ها را جلب می‌کند. برخی از فعالیت‌های تمیزی با رسانه‌ها همکاری می‌کنند تا تلاش‌های انجام شده برای ایمنی عمومی و اطمینان افراد به نمایش گذاشته شود. این امر می‌تواند باعث شود تصاویر و فیلم‌هایی از کارکنان در حال dezinfeksiyon از اماکن به تصویر کشیده شود که سپس در رسانه‌ها یا شبکه‌های اجتماعی به اشتراک گذاشته می‌شود.

با این حال، ادعای اینکه این تلاش‌های تمیزی فقط برای نمایش و نه واقعی dezinfeksiyon است، نیاز به بررسی دقیق‌تر دارد. مقامات مواصلات و خدمات تمیزی اغلب به مقررات استاندارد بهداشتی متعهد هستند، به ویژه در دوران شیوع بیماری‌های عفونی. استفاده از پوشاک حفاظتی، ماده dezinfeksiyon و روتین‌های تمیزی به صورت سیستماتیک، روش‌های استانداردی هستند که برای کاهش ریسک انتقال بیماری طراحی شده‌اند. در حالی که این موضوع درست است که برخی از فعالیت‌های تمیزی ممکن است به منظور حداکثر توجه عمومی یا تأثیرات رسانه‌ای زمان‌بندی شوند، این امر به معنی این نیست که خود عملیات تمیزی تقلبی یا کارکردی ناکارآمد است.

در برخی موارد، شک در مورد صحت نمایش‌های بهداشت عمومی به ویژه وقتی همان کارکنان یا صحنه‌ها به طور مکرر در تغطیه رسانه‌ای به تصویر کشیده می‌شوند، به وجود می‌آید. با این حال، این موارد به جز استثناءات، قاعده‌های نیستند. اکثر فعالیت‌های تمیزی عمومی به عنوان بخشی از تلاش‌های مداوم برای حفظ بهداشت و امنیت عمومی انجام می‌شود، فارغ از اینکه دوربین در محل باشد یا نه.

در مورد ویدئوی واقعی از انگلستان، بدون اثبات بیشتری که نشان دهد کارکنان در واقع ایستگاه را dezinfeksiyon نکرده‌اند یا این عملیات فقط برای رسانه‌ها انجام شده است، ادعا اصلی پست فیسبوک هنوز غیرقابل اثبات است. پوشاک حفاظتی و تلاش‌های ظاهری در دوران بحران‌های بهداشتی رایج هستند و وجود آنها به خودی خود نشانه‌ای از تقلب نیست. احتمالاً تلاش در واقع واقعی بوده است و به منظور ثبت یا ارتباط با عمومی به تصویر کشیده شده است.

به طور خلاصه، در حالی که تغطیه رسانه‌ای از فعالیت‌های تمیزی در فضاها گاهی اوقات برای توجه بیشتر سازماندهی می‌شود، اثبات کافی برای ادعای اینکه کارکنان ایستگاه ریلی انگلستان فقط به منظور دوربین و نه واقعی dezinfeksiyon عمل کرده‌اند وجود ندارد. مقررات بهداشت عمومی نیاز به تلاش واقعی برای تمیز کردن دارد و توصیف بصری به خودی خود به معنی عملیات تزیینی نیست. بررسی واقعیت این ادعاهای نیاز به دلیل مستقیمی از تخلف دارد که در این مورد وجود ندارد.

A viral Facebook post has captured widespread attention, claiming to have been published 11 years ago and allegedly predicting the coronavirus pandemic. The post further asserts that the pandemic is fake, fueling conspiracy theories and misinformation online. As this content circulates widely, it is important to examine its authenticity, analyze the evidence and context, and provide a clear fact-check to help readers discern truth from falsehood.

The core of the claim centers around the supposed prophetic nature of the post, which reportedly dates back to 2013 (given the 11-year timeline from 2024). In the text, the author appears to reference a future global outbreak, implying knowledge of the COVID-19 pandemic years before its emergence. The post then goes further, labeling the pandemic as fraudulent and suggesting that the global response is based on deception.

To evaluate these claims, several factors require scrutiny. First, the technical aspects of Facebook’s timestamping and post history must be considered. While Facebook allows users to backdate posts on pages, regular user profiles do not have this functionality. Moreover, viral posts purporting to “predict” major events are a recurring phenomenon during times of crisis, often fabricated or altered to fit current narratives. In many instances, these posts are designed to provoke shock, skepticism, or fear, rather than relay factual information.

Fact-checking the timeline reveals that COVID-19 was first identified in late 2019, with initial cases reported in Wuhan, China. Prior to this, coronaviruses were known in medical literature, but no public discourse or media coverage in 2013 pointed to a specific, imminent pandemic of this nature. There is no verifiable evidence that any widely-shared Facebook post from 2013 accurately predicted the COVID-19 pandemic. Most such posts are edited, backdated, or manipulated screenshots intended to deceive viewers.

The second claim in the viral post—that the pandemic is “fake”—is also demonstrably false. The global impact of COVID-19 has been extensively documented, with millions of cases and deaths worldwide. Governments, health organizations, and independent researchers have all provided substantial evidence of the virus’s existence and its effects. While misinformation and skepticism have circulated since the pandemic’s onset, these narratives are not supported by credible scientific data.

The spread of posts like this one contributes to confusion and undermines public trust in legitimate health information. Social media platforms have become fertile ground for misinformation, especially during periods of uncertainty. Users are encouraged to approach such extraordinary claims with caution, verify sources, and consult reputable health authorities for accurate updates.

In summary, the viral Facebook post claiming to have predicted the coronavirus pandemic 11 years ago and asserting that the pandemic is fake fails under careful scrutiny. There is no credible evidence of a genuine, predictive post from 2013, and the assertion that the pandemic is fraudulent is contradicted by overwhelming scientific and medical documentation. As misinformation continues to circulate online, thorough fact-checking remains essential to maintaining an informed public.

article_content:
A recent social media post has circulated claims by Luis Martinez, an individual from Argentina, alleging that COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene oxide, a substance that he suggests causes systemic inflammation, the formation of "cytokine thrombus thrombi" (interpreted as blood clots involving cytokine storms), and lung damage. Martinez further claims that, after receiving the vaccine, individuals become magnetized, suggesting that metallic objects can stick to their skin. This article examines these assertions in detail, providing context, background, and a fact-based analysis.

**Background and Context**

Since the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines, a range of misinformation and conspiracy theories have proliferated online. Among the most persistent are claims regarding the ingredients in vaccines and purported side effects. Graphene oxide, a compound consisting of carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen atoms in a sheet-like structure, is a relatively new material with applications in industry and research, but it has become the focus of several vaccine-related conspiracy theories.

**Are COVID-19 Vaccines Made With Graphene Oxide?**

There is no evidence to support the claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene oxide. Vaccine manufacturers are required to disclose all ingredients for regulatory approval, and the published ingredient lists for the major vaccines—such as those from Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca, and Johnson & Johnson—do not include graphene oxide. The main components of these vaccines are either mRNA or adenoviral vectors, lipids, salts, sugars, and stabilizers. Regulatory bodies around the world, including those in Argentina, rigorously review and monitor vaccine contents and have found no trace of graphene oxide in any authorized COVID-19 vaccine.

**Claims of Systemic Inflammation and Blood Clots**

Martinez asserts that graphene oxide, allegedly present in vaccines, leads to systemic inflammation and the formation of blood clots through a "cytokine thrombus thrombi" process. While very rare cases of blood clots have been associated with certain adenovirus-based COVID-19 vaccines, these have been extensively studied and are not linked to graphene oxide or any undisclosed component. The vast majority of recipients do not experience such side effects, and when they do occur, they are believed to be immune-mediated rather than caused by a foreign material like graphene oxide.

**The “Magnetism” Phenomenon**

The claim that individuals become magnetic after vaccination—suggested by reports of coins or other metal objects sticking to the skin—has been widely debunked. Human skin is not magnetic, and COVID-19 vaccines do not contain any magnetic ingredients. Demonstrations of objects sticking to the skin are typically due to moisture, natural oils, or surface tension, not magnetic forces. No scientific evidence supports vaccine-induced magnetism.

**Conclusion**

The claims made by Luis Martinez regarding the presence of graphene oxide in vaccines, resultant inflammation, and post-vaccination magnetism have no factual basis. The ingredients of COVID-19 vaccines are well-documented, and the alleged phenomena described are not supported by scientific evidence. Misinformation of this nature can contribute to vaccine hesitancy and confusion, underlining the importance of relying on verified information from reputable sources.

Коронавирус пандемиясынан кейін вакциналардың құрамы мен жалған ақпараттар, әсіресе сілтеме арқылы құрылған теориялар басып шығып, интернетте өзгеріп отыр. **Коронавирус вакциналарында графен оксиді бар ма?**

Вакциналарда графен оксиді бар екеніне дәлел жоқ. Вакциналардың құрамын тексеру үшін өзгерістердің барлығын жариялау қажет, оның негізгі құрамы - Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca және Johnson & Johnson вакциналарының құрамында графен оксиді жоқ. **Жүйелі әріптесу және қан айналуынан тұратын тұжырымдар**

Мартинес вакциналарда графен оксидінің бар екенін айта отырып, оның жүйелі әріптесу және "цитокин тромб тромб" процесі арқылы қан айналуын қоздыратындығын айтады. Бірақ кейбір адено вирустық вакциналармен байланысты қан айналуының кездейсоқ жағдайлары анықталған, бірақ олар графен оксидіне немесе кез келген анықталмаған құрамға байланысты емес. Вакциналардың басқа көптеген азаматтары бұл әсерлерді түсінбейді, олар әріптесу арқылы болатын, графен оксиді сияқты басқа құрамдардан келмейді.

**"Магниттілік" құбылысы**

Вакцина алуға келген адамдар магниттеліп қалғанын айта отырып, құралдардың немесе басқа металл объектілердің қанатына түсуін ұсынған. Бұл ұсыныс әлі де ұрықтандырылған. Адамның қанаты магнитті емес, коронавирус вакциналарында магнитті құрамдар жоқ. Қанатына объектілердің түсуі әлі де қанаттың ылғалдылығы, табиғи қызыл қышқылдары немесе беттік керілімге байланысты, магниттік күштерге емес. Вакциналардан туындайтын магниттілікке дәлел жоқ.

**Қорытынды**

Луис Мартинес вакциналарда графен оксидінің болуы, оның нәтижесінде жүйелі әріптесу және вакцина алуға келген адамдардың магниттілігі туралы ұсыныстарының табылмайтындығын айтады. Коронавирус вакциналарының құрамы жетілдірілген, ұсынылған құбылыстарға дәлел жоқ. Бұндай жалған ақпараттар вакциналарға қатысты қатыспауға әкеледі және білімді тарату үшін үлкен маңыздылықты алады.

A social media post has gained attention with the claim that a 49-year-old woman in Kumanovo, North Macedonia, died after receiving her first dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. This assertion has sparked concern and debate, particularly among vaccine-hesitant individuals. In this article, we examine the veracity of the claim, provide relevant context, and analyze available information regarding the reported incident.

First, it is important to acknowledge that reports of adverse events following vaccination can generate significant public anxiety, especially when they involve fatalities. Vaccines, like any medical intervention, can be followed by side effects, ranging from mild to, in rare cases, severe. However, the occurrence of a death after vaccination does not automatically imply causation; careful investigation is necessary to determine whether the vaccine was related to the fatal outcome.

According to the claim, a 49-year-old woman from Kumanovo died after receiving her first dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. The post does not specify the type of vaccine administered, the time elapsed between vaccination and death, or any underlying health conditions the woman may have had. These details are crucial for a thorough assessment.

Local authorities in North Macedonia have previously reported incidents where individuals died in temporal proximity to vaccination. In such cases, standard public health protocols require a formal investigation, including autopsy and review of medical history, to establish the cause of death. Health officials typically release preliminary findings and, if necessary, guidance for the public.

Historically, the vast majority of deaths reported soon after vaccination have been found to be unrelated to the vaccine itself, often attributable to pre-existing health conditions or coincidental timing. Global health agencies, including the World Health Organization and national regulatory bodies, continuously monitor vaccine safety and investigate all reports of serious adverse events.

In the specific case of the alleged death in Kumanovo, local media and public health authorities did acknowledge that a 49-year-old woman passed away after receiving her first COVID-19 vaccine dose. However, health officials urged caution in drawing conclusions before the results of the autopsy and investigation were available. Initial statements suggested that the woman had underlying chronic health issues, which could have contributed to her death. As of the latest available information, there was no official confirmation that the vaccine caused or contributed to the fatality.

It is also important to note that, as of now, no COVID-19 vaccine approved for use in North Macedonia or elsewhere has been linked to widespread fatal adverse effects. Vaccines undergo rigorous testing and continuous monitoring to ensure their safety. Serious side effects are extremely rare, and the benefits of vaccination in preventing COVID-19 complications and deaths far outweigh the risks.

In summary, while it is true that a 49-year-old woman in Kumanovo died after receiving her first vaccine dose, there is no evidence at this time to support a direct causal link between the vaccination and her death. Investigations are ongoing, and conclusions should be based on official findings rather than speculation. The public is encouraged to rely on information from health authorities and medical professionals when evaluating vaccine safety.

സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയയിലെ ഒരു പോസ്റ്റ് ശ്രദ്ധ നേടിയിട്ടുണ്ട്, ഇത് നോർത്ത് മക്കഡോണിയയിലെ കുമാനോവോയിലെ 49 വയസ്സുകാരി കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനിന്റെ ആദ്യ ഡോസ് എടുത്തതിന് ശേഷം മരിച്ചതായി പ്രസ്താവിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഈ പ്രസ്താവന പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് വാക്സിന്‍ അസ്ഥിരരായ ആളുകളിൽ ആശങ്കയും ചർച്ചയും ഉണ്ടാക്കിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഈ ലേഖനത്തിൽ, ഈ പ്രസ്താവനയുടെ സത്യസന്ധത പരിശോധിക്കുക, സാമ്പത്തിക പരിസ്ഥിതിക്കുള്ള സാധ്യതകൾ അന്വേഷിക്കുക എന്നിവയുടെ പശ്ചാത്തലം വിശദമാക്കുകയും പ്രാപ്തമായ വിവരങ്ങളുടെ പരിശോധന നിർവഹിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും.

ആദ്യം, വാക്സിനേഷൻ ശേഷം ഉണ്ടാകുന്ന ദുരന്തങ്ങളെക്കുറിച്ചുള്ള റിപ്പോർട്ടുകൾ പൊതു ആശങ്കയെ ഉണ്ടാക്കാം, പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് മരണത്തെ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയ പക്ഷേ, വാക്സിനുകൾ മറ്റ് മെഡിക്കൽ പരിപാടികളുടെ പോലെ കാര്യങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ടാകാം, അതിന് പുറമേ, മിക്കവാറും നേരിട്ട് അപ്രത്യക്ഷമായ പരിണാമങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ടാകാം. എന്നാൽ, വാക്സിനേഷൻ ശേഷം മരണം ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുണ്ടാകാം എന്ന് അർത്ഥമാകുന്നില്ല, അത് അന്വേഷിക്കുവാൻ പൂർണ്ണമായ പരിശോധന ആവശ്യമാണ്, മരണത്തിന്റെ കാരണം തീർച്ചയായി പരിശോധിക്കുവാൻ വാക്സിനുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ടിരുന്നു എന്ന് തീർച്ചയായി പറയാൻ ആവശ്യമാണ്.

പ്രസ്താവന പ്രകാരം, കുമാനോവോയിൽ നിന്നുള്ള 49 വയസ്സുകാരി കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനിന്റെ ആദ്യ ഡോസ് എടുത്തതിന് ശേഷം മരിച്ചതായി പ്രസ്താവിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഈ പോസ്റ്റ് വാക്സിനുകൾ എന്താണ് എന്ന് വ്യക്തമല്ല, വാക്സിനേഷൻ മുതൽ മരണത്തിന് വരെ സമയം എന്താണ് എന്ന് വ്യക്തമല്ല, മുൻകാല ആരോഗ്യ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾ എന്താണ് എന്ന് വ്യക്തമല്ല. ഇതെല്ലാം പൂർണ്ണമായ പരിശോധനയ്ക്ക് ആവശ്യമാണ്.

നോർത്ത് മക്കഡോണിയയിലെ സ്ഥാനാന്തര അധികാരികൾ ഇതുപോലെ പ്രായോഗിക സമയത്ത് മരിച്ച പേരുകളെ റിപ്പോർട്ട് ചെയ്തിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഈ പക്ഷങ്ങളിൽ, സ്ഥാനാന്തര ആരോഗ്യ പ്രോട്ടോക്കോളുകൾ പ്രകാരം, മരണത്തിന്റെ കാരണം തീർച്ചയായി പരിശോധിക്കുവാൻ അനുവദിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു, അതിന് മൃതദേഹത്തിന് പരിശോധന നടത്തുക എന്നും ആരോഗ്യ ചരിത്രം പരിശോധിക്കുക എന്നും ആവശ്യമാണ്. ആരോഗ്യ അധികാരികൾ മുകളിൽ പ്രാഥമിക വിവരങ്ങൾ പുറത്തുവിടുകയും, ആവശ്യമായി പൊതുവില നിർദ്ദേശങ്ങൾ പുറത്തുവിടുകയും ചെയ്യും.

വാക്സിനേഷൻ ശേഷം പ്രായോഗിക സമയത്ത് റിപ്പോർട്ട് ചെയ്ത മരണങ്ങളുടെ പല പക്ഷങ്ങളും വാക്സിന്‍ തന്നെ കാരണമായിരുന്നിട്ടില്ല, അതിന് മുൻകാല ആരോഗ്യ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ സംയോഗം അല്ലെങ്കിൽ സാമ്പത്തിക സമയം കാരണമായിരുന്നു. ലോക ആരോഗ്യ സംഘടനയും രാഷ്ട്രീയ നിയന്ത്രണ സംവിധാനങ്ങളും മുഴുവൻ വാക്സിനുകളുടെ സുരക്ഷിതത പരിശോധിക്കുകയും എല്ലാ ഗുരുതരമായ ദുരന്തങ്ങളുടെയും റിപ്പോർട്ടുകളെ പരിശോധിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.

കുമാനോവോയിലെ പ്രസ്താവനയുടെ പ്രത്യേക സാഹചര്യത്തിൽ, സ്ഥാനാന്തര മാധ്യമങ്ങൾ ആണ് കുമാനോവോയിലെ 49 വയസ്സുകാരി കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനിന്റെ ആദ്യ ഡോസ് എടുത്തതിന് ശേഷം മരിച്ചതായി സമ്മതിച്ചു. എന്നാൽ, ആരോഗ്യ അധികാരികൾ അന്വേഷണത്തിന്റെ ഫലങ്ങൾ പുറത്തുവിട്ടതിനുമുമ്പ് നിർണ്ണായക നിഗമനങ്ങൾ കണ്ടെത്താൻ താത്പര്യം ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു. ആദ്യം പ്രസ്താവനകൾ ആ സ്ത്രീക്ക് മുൻകാല അസ്ഥിര ആരോഗ്യ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു, അത് മരണത്തിന് കാരണമായിരുന്നു എന്ന് കരുതാനായിരുന്നു. പക്ഷേ, അവസാനമായ ലഭ്യമായ വിവരങ്ങൾ അനുസരിച്ച്, വാക്സിന്‍ കാരണമായിരുന്നു അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മരണത്തിന് കാരണമായിരുന്നു എന്ന് ഔദ്യോഗികമായി സ്ഥാപിച്ചിട്ടില്ല.

അതുപോലെ, ഇതിനുമുമ്പ് നോർത്ത് മക്കഡോണിയയിൽ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മറ്റെന്തെങ്കിലും സ്ഥലത്ത് അംഗീകരിച്ചിരിക്കുന്ന കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനുകൾക്ക് വിപുലമായ മരണ പരിണാമങ്ങളുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ടിട്ടില്ല. വാക്സിനുകൾ സുരക്ഷിതതയുടെ Инспекцијата е во тек, а здравствени служби истакнуваат дека имаат предвидени здравствени состојби кои можат да се додаваат. Вакцините се проверени за безбедност, а ризикот од сериозни ефекти е веќе ретки, додека користењето им е од предност за спречување на смртта од болеста.

article_content:
Recently, a social media post has circulated claiming that the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has abolished the PCR test. The post suggests that the CDC has eliminated or discontinued the use of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing, a widely used method for detecting COVID-19. Given the importance of accurate information regarding public health practices, this article examines the validity of this claim and provides context for the CDC’s position on PCR testing.

PCR testing has been a cornerstone of COVID-19 diagnostics since the beginning of the pandemic. The test works by detecting genetic material from the virus in a patient’s sample, allowing for early and accurate identification of infection. Laboratories across the United States and globally have relied on PCR tests for their sensitivity and specificity, playing a critical role in tracking and controlling the spread of the virus.

The claim that the CDC has abolished the PCR test appears to stem from a misunderstanding of a CDC announcement made in mid-2021. At that time, the CDC notified clinical laboratories that it would withdraw its request for Emergency Use Authorization for its own CDC-developed PCR assay for SARS-CoV-2, which had been one of the first tests available in early 2020. However, this did not mean that PCR testing as a whole was eliminated or discontinued. Rather, the CDC encouraged laboratories to consider using multiplex assays capable of detecting both SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses, facilitating more efficient testing during respiratory virus season.

It is important to clarify that the CDC’s action did not affect the hundreds of other PCR-based tests that have been authorized and are routinely used in clinical and public health laboratories throughout the United States. PCR technology remains the gold standard for COVID-19 diagnosis due to its reliability. The CDC’s announcement was part of an effort to update testing protocols to reflect evolving scientific understanding and to ensure laboratories could distinguish between COVID-19 and other respiratory illnesses, such as the flu, which can present with similar symptoms.

Fact-checking analysis confirms that the CDC has not abolished PCR testing. The agency continues to support the use of PCR tests for the detection of COVID-19 and other pathogens. Health care providers, laboratories, and public health officials still utilize PCR assays as a primary method for diagnosing COVID-19 cases. The discontinuation of a single, specific CDC-developed test does not equate to the abandonment of PCR testing technology overall.

In summary, the claim that the CDC has abolished the PCR test is misleading and incorrect. The CDC continues to recognize PCR testing as a critical tool in the fight against COVID-19 and other infectious diseases. The agency’s actions reflect an ongoing commitment to improve and update testing strategies, not to eliminate effective diagnostic technologies. Individuals seeking COVID-19 testing or information should rely on official guidance from the CDC and trusted public health sources.

A bejegyzés szerint a CDC megszüntette vagy abbahagyta a polimeráz láncreakció (PCR) teszt használatát, amely a koronavírus (COVID-19) kimutatására szolgáló széles körben alkalmazott módszer. Mivel a publikus egészségügyi gyakorlatokkal kapcsolatos pontos információk fontosak, ez a cikk vizsgálja a kijelentés valóságtartalmát, és megadja a CDC álláspontját a PCR-tesztekkel kapcsolatban.

A PCR-teszt a járvány kezdete óta a COVID-19 diagnosztikájának alapköve. A teszt működése során a vírus génanyagát detektálja a beteg mintájában, így lehetővé teszi a fertőzés korai és pontos azonosítását. Az Egyesült Államokban és globálisan a laboratóriumok az érzékenység és specifikusság miatt számítanak a PCR-tesztekre, és kulcsfontosságú szerepet játszanak a vírus terjedésének nyomon követésében és kontrollálásában.

A kijelentés, miszerint a CDC megszüntette a PCR-tesztet, egyértelműen egy CDC-nyilatkozat félreértéséből ered, amely 2021 közepén történt. Ekkor a CDC tájékoztatta a klinikai laboratóriumokat, hogy visszavonja a saját kifejlesztett SARS-CoV-2-PCR-asszayához kapcsolódó válságként engedélyezett használat kérelmét, amely az egyik első teszt volt 2020 elején. Azonban ez nem jelentette azt, hogy a PCR-teszt általánosan megszűnt vagy abbahagyta a használatát. Inkább a CDC ösztönzötte a laboratóriumokat, hogy figyeljenek a SARS-CoV-2 és influenza vírusokat is képes felismerni multiplex asszayok használatára, így hatékonyabb tesztelést lehetővé téve a légúti vírusok időszakában.

Fontos megkülönböztetni, hogy a CDC cselekvése nem befolyásolta az ezerrel számolható más PCR-alapú tesztet, amelyek engedélyezve vannak, és rendszeresen alkalmazzák a klinikai és közegészségügyi laboratóriumokban az Egyesült Államokban. A PCR-technológia a koronavírus diagnosztikájának arany szabályozása, mivel megbízható. A CDC nyilatkozata részét képezte az egészségügyi vizsgálati protokollok frissítésének folyamatának, amely az evolúciós tudományos megértésre utal, és biztosította a laboratóriumoknak a COVID-19 és más légúti betegségek, például az influenza, különbségének felismerését, amelyek hasonló tüneteket okozhatnak.

A tények ellenőrzése megerősíti, hogy a CDC nem szüntette meg a PCR-tesztelést. Az intézmény továbbra is támogatja a PCR-teszt használatát a koronavírus és más patogének kimutatására. A egészségügyi szakemberek, laboratóriumok és közegészségügyi hivatalok továbbra is a PCR-asszayokat alkalmazzák a koronavírus eseteinek fő diagnosztikai módszereként. Egyetlen, a CDC által fejlesztett teszt megszüntetése nem jelenti a teljes PCR-tesztelési technológia elhagyását.

Összefoglalva a kijelentés, miszerint a CDC megszüntette a PCR-tesztet, téves és helytelen. A CDC továbbra is a koronavírus és más fertőző betegségek elleni harc során a PCR-tesztet fontos eszköznek tartja. Az intézmény cselekvései tükrözik a folyamatos kötelezettséget a tesztelési stratégiák javítására, nem a hatékony diagnosztikai technológiák megszüntetésére. A koronavírus tesztelésre vagy információkra kereső személyeknek a CDC és megbízható közegészségügyi források hivatalos útmutatóira kell támaszkodniuk.

A claim circulating on social media alleges that Covid-19 vaccines inject "metal powder" into the body, and that subsequent waves of the virus are stimulated through interaction with the 5G network. This assertion combines multiple conspiracy theories that have emerged during the pandemic, raising concerns about misinformation and its impact on public health.

To assess this claim, it is necessary to examine the scientific composition of Covid-19 vaccines and the nature of 5G technology, as well as investigate any plausible connection between the two.

Covid-19 vaccines, including those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, Johnson & Johnson, and others, do not contain "metal powder." The vaccines authorized for use globally are composed primarily of messenger RNA (mRNA) or adenoviral vectors, lipids, salts, sugars, and stabilizers. These ingredients are designed to stimulate the immune system to recognize and fight the virus that causes Covid-19. Detailed ingredient lists are publicly available, and none include metallic particles, powders, or substances that can interact with electromagnetic fields in the manner described by the social media post.

The notion that vaccines contain metals likely stems from misunderstandings about vaccine components or deliberate misinformation. Some vaccines, not related to Covid-19, have used trace amounts of aluminum salts as adjuvants to enhance immune response, but these are well-studied, safe, and not used in mRNA Covid-19 vaccines. Furthermore, the tiny quantities used in some vaccines do not render the body sensitive to electromagnetic fields or susceptible to any form of remote manipulation.

The second part of the claim involves 5G technology, the latest evolution in mobile telecommunications. 5G operates by transmitting data via radio waves, similar to previous generations of wireless technology but at higher frequencies and speeds. Scientific research has found no evidence that 5G radio waves can interact with biological tissues to stimulate viral activity, nor is there any plausible mechanism by which 5G signals could trigger a "new Covid wave" in vaccinated individuals or the general population.

Conspiracy theories about the link between 5G and Covid-19 gained traction early in the pandemic, fueled by fear and a lack of understanding of both the virus and telecommunications technology. These ideas have been widely debunked by experts in virology and physics, who explain that viruses cannot be "activated" or "spread" by radio waves or wireless signals. Covid-19 spreads through respiratory droplets and aerosols, not through electromagnetic frequencies.

In summary, the social media claim that Covid-19 vaccination involves injecting metal powder into the body, and that subsequent Covid waves are triggered by 5G networks, is not supported by scientific evidence. Covid-19 vaccines do not contain metals capable of interacting with 5G, and there is no credible mechanism by which wireless networks could influence viral activity. Misinformation of this kind can undermine public trust in vaccination and public health measures, making it essential to rely on verified scientific information when making health decisions.
