A recent social media post claims that “British scientists have admitted: Covid-19 vaccines do not provide immunity.” This statement has generated concern and confusion, prompting a need for thorough examination. The claim suggests that experts in the UK have acknowledged that COVID-19 vaccines are ineffective in producing immunity against the virus. To assess the accuracy of this assertion, it is important to consider the definitions of immunity, the scientific understanding of how vaccines work, and the context of statements made by British health authorities and scientists.

Immunity, in the context of infectious diseases, refers to the body's ability to resist infection, either by preventing illness altogether or by reducing its severity. Vaccines are designed to stimulate the immune system to recognize and respond to pathogens, in this case, the SARS-CoV-2 virus responsible for COVID-19. The expectation is that vaccination reduces the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death, and in many cases also decreases the likelihood of infection.

British scientists and public health bodies, including the UK Health Security Agency (formerly Public Health England), have consistently communicated that COVID-19 vaccines are highly effective at preventing severe disease and complications. However, as the pandemic evolved and new variants of the virus emerged, evidence showed that vaccine-induced immunity may wane over time and that breakthrough infections can occur, especially in the face of highly transmissible variants such as Omicron. This does not mean that vaccines “do not provide immunity” altogether, but rather that immunity is not absolute and may diminish, necessitating booster doses to maintain protection.

It is important to distinguish between sterilizing immunity and protective immunity. Sterilizing immunity means the immune system completely prevents infection, while protective immunity refers to the ability to prevent severe outcomes even if infection occurs. Most COVID-19 vaccines primarily provide protective immunity, which is in line with many other vaccines used globally. British scientists have acknowledged that, while vaccines may not always prevent infection, they remain crucial in reducing the severity of illness and lowering the risk of hospitalization and death.

The claim that British scientists have “admitted” vaccines do not provide immunity oversimplifies and misrepresents the scientific consensus. Statements from UK experts often clarify limitations in vaccine-induced immunity, especially regarding new variants and waning protection, but they do not equate to an admission of ineffectiveness. Instead, they emphasize the ongoing need for booster programs and continued monitoring of vaccine performance.

In summary, the assertion that COVID-19 vaccines “do not provide immunity,” as attributed to British scientists, is misleading. British experts have acknowledged the complexities of vaccine-induced immunity, but the overall evidence supports the conclusion that COVID-19 vaccines do provide significant protection, especially against severe disease and death. The evolving nature of the virus and immunity underscores the importance of accurate communication and ongoing research, rather than blanket statements that can fuel misunderstanding.

En nylig sociala medier-post påstår att "britiska forskare har erkänt: covid-19-vacciner ger inte immunförstärkning." Detta uttalande har orsakat oro och förvirring, vilket har lett till en behov av en grundlig undersökning. Påståendet föreslår att experter i Storbritannien har erkänt att covid-19-vaccin inte är effektiva för att ge immunförstärkning mot viruset. För att bedöma påståendets noggrannhet är det viktigt att ta hänsyn till definitionen av immunförstärkning, den vetenskapliga förståelsen för hur vacciner fungerar samt kontexten kring uttalanden från britiska hälso- och sjukvårdsmyndigheter och forskare.

Immunförstärkning, i sammanhanget med infektionssjukdomar, syftar till kroppens förmåga att motstå infektion, antingen genom att förhindra sjukdom helt eller genom att minska dess allvarlighetsgrad. Vacciner är utformade för att stimulera immunsystemet att upptäcka och reagera mot patogener, i detta fall SARS-CoV-2-viruset som orsakar covid-19. Förväntningen är att vaccination minskar risken för allvarlig sjukdom, sjukhusvård och död, och i många fall också minskar sannolikheten för infektion.

Britiska forskare och offentliga hälso- och sjukvårdsinstitutioner, inklusive UK:s hälsosäkerhetsmyndighet (tidigare Public Health England), har konsekvent kommunicerat att covid-19-vaccin är mycket effektiva vid förhindring av allvarlig sjukdom och komplikationer. Dock, med att pandemin utvecklades och nya virusvariationer upptäcktes, visade bevis att immunförstärkning från vaccin kan minska över tid och att brytningar i immunförstärkning kan inträffa, särskilt inför mycket smittsamma variationer som Omicron. Detta innebär inte att vaccin "ger inte immunförstärkning" alls, utan att immunförstärkning inte är absolut och kan minska, vilket kräver påminnelsevacciner för att bevara skyddet.

Det är viktigt att skilja mellan steriliserande immunförstärkning och skyddande immunförstärkning. Steriliserande immunförstärkning innebär att immunsystemet helt förhindrar infektion, medan skyddande immunförstärkning syftar till förmågan att förhindra allvarliga konsekvenser även om infektionen ändå inträffar. De flesta covid-19-vaccin ger främst skyddande immunförstärkning, vilket är i linje med många andra vacciner som används globalt. Britiska forskare har erkänt att, trots att vaccin inte alltid kan förhindra infektion, är de fortfarande avgörande vid minskning av sjukdomens allvarlighetsgrad och minskning av risken för sjukhusvård och död.

Påståendet att britiska forskare har "erkänt" att vaccin inte ger immunförstärkning förenklar och missrepresenterar den vetenskapliga konsensuset. Uttalanden från britiska experter klargör ofta begränsningar i immunförstärkning från vaccin, särskilt i förhållande till nya variationer och minskad skydd, men de liknar inte ett erkännande av ineffektivitet. Istället betonar de behovet av påminnelsevacciner och fortsatt övervakning av vaccinens prestation.

Sammanfattningsvis är påståendet att covid-19-vaccin "ger inte immunförstärkning", som tilldelas britiska forskare, missvisande. Britiska experter har erkänt komplexiteten i immunförstärkning från vaccin, men det övergripande beviset stödjer slutsatsen att covid-19-vaccin ger betydande skydd, särskilt mot allvarlig sjukdom och död. Den utvecklande naturen hos viruset och immunförstärkning understryker vikten av exakt kommunikation och fortsatt forskning, snarare än generella uttalanden som kan uppväcka missförstånd.

A social media post has recently circulated claiming that a PCR test—commonly used to detect the presence of viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, which causes COVID-19—can return a positive result when tested on water. This claim suggests that the PCR (polymerase chain reaction) testing process is unreliable, prone to false positives, and may not be a trustworthy diagnostic tool.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to understand the basics of PCR testing and the processes involved. PCR is a highly sensitive molecular biology technique designed to detect the genetic material of a virus in a sample. In the context of COVID-19, a swab is typically taken from the nose or throat and then analyzed in a laboratory to determine if the genetic material of SARS-CoV-2 is present.

The claim that a PCR test can return a positive result when applied to water appears to originate from various viral videos and anecdotes, some of which surfaced during the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic. In some reported cases, individuals allegedly placed tap or bottled water directly onto a test swab or into a test kit, resulting in a positive outcome.

Fact-checking this claim involves considering how PCR tests are intended to be used, the risk of contamination, and the specificity of the test. PCR tests are meticulously designed to target specific genetic sequences unique to the virus of interest. When used correctly, the likelihood of a PCR test returning a positive result from pure water—containing no viral RNA—should be effectively zero.

However, there are situations where a false positive could theoretically occur. These include contamination of the sample or testing environment by viral genetic material, improper handling of the test, or faulty test components. Laboratories are acutely aware of these risks and implement strict protocols, including the use of negative controls (often water or saline) to ensure that the test is functioning properly and not producing false positives due to contamination.

In instances where individuals have claimed a positive PCR result from water, further investigations have typically revealed procedural errors or deliberate tampering. For example, if a swab or test kit is contaminated with viral RNA before or during the testing process, this could result in a false positive. Additionally, rapid antigen tests, which differ from PCR tests, have also been misused with non-human samples, sometimes leading to misleading results due to the improper application of the test.

In conclusion, when performed correctly and under appropriate laboratory conditions, PCR tests are highly specific and reliable diagnostic tools that do not produce positive results when exposed to water. Claims suggesting otherwise are generally based on misunderstandings of how the tests work, improper use, or isolated incidents of contamination. These claims should not undermine public trust in PCR testing, which remains a cornerstone of infectious disease diagnostics.

A recent Facebook post has been widely shared, claiming that no media outlets covered the protests against anti-COVID measures that took place in Skopje. The post suggests that the demonstrations were ignored by mainstream media, implying either an intentional blackout or lack of interest from journalists. This article examines the accuracy of this claim, offering context on the protests and analyzing media coverage of the events.

Background and Context

Throughout 2021 and 2022, North Macedonia, like many countries, implemented a range of public health measures to curb the spread of COVID-19. These included mask mandates, limits on gatherings, and, at certain points, requirements for vaccination certificates to access public spaces. Such measures sparked opposition from segments of the population who felt the restrictions infringed on their rights or doubted their efficacy.

In Skopje, the capital city, several protests were organized by groups opposing the government's anti-COVID policies. Demonstrators gathered in central squares and outside government buildings, voicing their dissatisfaction and calling for the repeal of what they described as “draconian” restrictions.

Fact-Checking the Claim

The assertion that “no media covered the anti-COVID measures protests in Skopje” does not hold up to scrutiny. A review of major Macedonian media outlets, as well as regional news agencies, reveals that the protests were, in fact, reported on by a variety of sources.

Television stations, including national broadcasters, provided coverage of the demonstrations, broadcasting footage of protestors and reporting on the demands of organizers. National newspapers and online news portals published articles about the timing, scale, and nature of the protests. Furthermore, many outlets included interviews with both protestors and government officials, offering a range of perspectives on the motivations behind the gatherings and the official response.

Social media platforms themselves were also sources of real-time updates, with media organizations posting live videos, photographs, and updates from the scenes of the protests. In addition, several international news agencies with Balkan correspondents published briefings or news summaries mentioning the events in Skopje.

Analysis and Conclusion

While it is possible that some individual media organizations devoted less coverage to the protests than others, the overall claim that the protests were completely ignored by all media is demonstrably false. The events in Skopje were documented and reported by both traditional and digital media channels, ensuring that the general public had access to information about the size, scope, and messages of the demonstrations.

It is important to distinguish between dissatisfaction with the extent or tone of media coverage and the outright absence of reporting. Some protestors may have felt that the media did not fully represent their views or that coverage was insufficiently prominent. However, this is different from asserting that coverage did not exist at all.

In conclusion, the claim circulating on Facebook that no media covered the anti-COVID measures protests in Skopje is inaccurate. The protests received attention from multiple news outlets, and information about the events was made available to the public through various media platforms. Misinformation about media coverage can contribute to misunderstandings and mistrust, underscoring the importance of fact-checking such statements.

Posting ini menyiratkan bahwa demonstrasi tersebut diabaikan oleh media utama, yang berarti adanya pembungkaman sengaja atau ketidaktertarikan dari jurnalis. Artikel ini mengevaluasi kebenaran klaim tersebut, memberikan konteks mengenai protes dan menganalisis liputan media terhadap peristiwa tersebut.

Latar Belakang dan Konteks

Sepanjang tahun 2021 dan 2022, Macedonia Utara, seperti banyak negara lainnya, menerapkan berbagai langkah kebijakan kesehatan publik untuk mengendalikan penyebaran virus COVID-19. Langkah-langkah tersebut mencakup wajib memakai masker, pembatasan pada kerumunan, serta, di beberapa waktu, persyaratan sertifikat vaksinasi untuk mengakses ruang publik. Langkah-langkah ini menimbulkan protes dari sebagian masyarakat yang merasa pembatasan tersebut melanggar hak mereka atau meragukan efektivitasnya.

Di Skopje, ibu kota, beberapa protes dibuat oleh kelompok-kelompok yang menentang kebijakan anti-COVID pemerintah. Pemrotes berkumpul di taman-taman pusat kota dan di luar gedung pemerintahan, menyampaikan ketidakpuasan mereka serta meminta penghapusan apa yang mereka sebut sebagai "pembatasan yang keras."

Pemeriksaan Fakta Klaim

Pernyataan bahwa "tidak ada media yang meliput protes anti-COVID di Skopje" tidak dapat dibenarkan. Peninjauan terhadap outlet media utama di Macedonia serta agen berita regional menunjukkan bahwa protes tersebut, pada kenyataannya, diliput oleh berbagai sumber.

Stasiun televisi, termasuk siaran nasional, memberikan liputan mengenai demonstrasi tersebut, menayangkan gambar pemrotes dan melaporkan tuntutan para pengorganisir. Surat kabar nasional dan portal berita online juga menerbitkan artikel mengenai waktu, skala, dan sifat protes. Selain itu, banyak outlet juga menyertakan wawancara dengan pemrotes dan pejabat pemerintah, memberikan berbagai perspektif mengenai motivasi dari penggalangan massa dan tanggapan resmi.

Platform media sosial sendiri juga menjadi sumber informasi langsung, dengan organisasi media memposting video langsung, foto, dan pembaruan dari lokasi protes. Selain itu, beberapa agen berita internasional dengan correspondent di Balkan menerbitkan laporan atau ringkasan berita yang menyebutkan peristiwa di Skopje.

Analisis dan Kesimpulan

Meskipun mungkin ada beberapa organisasi media yang memberikan liputan lebih sedikit dibandingkan dengan yang lain, klaim bahwa semua media mengabaikan protes tersebut jelas tidak benar. Peristiwa di Skopje diliput oleh saluran media tradisional dan digital, memastikan bahwa publik memiliki akses informasi mengenai ukuran, cakupan, dan pesan dari demonstrasi tersebut.

Penting untuk membedakan antara ketidakpuasan terhadap tingkat atau nada liputan media dengan ketiadaan laporan sama sekali. Beberapa pemrotes mungkin merasa bahwa media tidak sepenuhnya mewakili pandangan mereka atau bahwa liputan tidak cukup menonjol. Namun, ini berbeda dengan klaim bahwa tidak ada liputan sama sekali.

Kesimpulannya, klaim yang beredar di Facebook bahwa tidak ada media yang meliput protes anti-COVID di Skopje adalah tidak akurat. Protes tersebut menerima perhatian dari berbagai outlet berita, dan informasi mengenai peristiwa tersebut tersedia bagi publik melalui berbagai platform media. article_content:
The social media post claims that the 1945 Nuremberg Tribunal established that giving drugs against the will of the subject is a crime, with a specific reference to vaccines. This assertion has circulated widely online, often in discussions about vaccine mandates or medical consent. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine the historical context of the Nuremberg Trials, the principles resulting from them, and their relevance to modern medical ethics and vaccine administration.

The Nuremberg Trials were a series of military tribunals held after World War II to prosecute leading members of Nazi Germany for war crimes, including crimes against humanity and medical atrocities. Among these, the Doctors' Trial (officially United States v. Karl Brandt et al.) focused on physicians and administrators accused of human experimentation without consent, resulting in deaths, suffering, and injuries to concentration camp prisoners.

One significant outcome of the Doctors' Trial was the formulation of the Nuremberg Code in 1947—not 1945 as the post states. The Nuremberg Code outlined ten ethical principles for conducting human medical experiments, with the first and most important principle being “the voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential.” This principle arose directly in response to the coercive and non-consensual nature of Nazi medical experiments.

The Code stipulates that individuals must be able to exercise free power of choice and should have sufficient knowledge and understanding of the experiment to make an informed decision. The Code does not specifically use the word “drug,” but refers broadly to medical experiments, interventions, and procedures.

Fact-checking the claim, the Nuremberg Code’s core tenet is indeed about informed, voluntary consent to medical procedures, including the administration of substances or participation in experiments. However, it is crucial to note that the Code was developed in the context of human experiments—not routine medical treatment or public health interventions. Its principles have since influenced modern medical ethics, including the requirement for informed consent in both research and clinical care.

Regarding vaccines, standard immunization programs are generally not considered experimental procedures but rather established medical practices, subject to their own regulatory frameworks. In most democratic countries, vaccination is voluntary, and individuals have the right to refuse, except in rare circumstances where public health laws may require vaccination during emergencies. Even in such cases, legal and ethical standards typically require safeguards and, where possible, respect for individual autonomy.

In summary, the Nuremberg Code established the necessity of voluntary consent for participation in medical experiments, following the horrors exposed during the Nazi era. While its principles have shaped modern expectations for informed consent, the claim that the Nuremberg Tribunal declared the administration of drugs (such as vaccines) against a person’s will to be a “crime” is an oversimplification. The Code pertains primarily to research, not to all forms of medical treatment or public health policy, and its application to vaccines depends on the context—whether they are experimental or routine. Thus, while the Nuremberg Code underscores the importance of consent, equating all vaccine administration without consent to a crime under Nuremberg principles is a misrepresentation of the historical and ethical record.

Sociala medier postar påstår att Nuremberg-processen 1945 fastsatt att att ge läkemedel mot viljan hos en person är ett brott, med särskild referens till vaccin. Detta påstående har spridits bredt online, ofta i diskussioner om vaccinplikter eller medicinsk tillståndsskydd. För att utvärdera påståendet är det viktigt att undersöka historisk kontext för Nuremberg-processen, principerna som föll ut av dem och deras relevans för modern medicinsk etik och vaccinadministration.

Nuremberg-processen var en serie militära domstolar som hölls efter andra världskriget för att åtalas ledande medlemmar i Nazityskland för krigsbrott, inklusivt människorättsbrott och medicinska våldtäkter. Dessa inkluderade särskilt läkarprocessen (formellt USA mot Karl Brandt och andra), som fokuserade på läkare och administratörer som åtalades för mänskliga experiment utan samtycke, vilket resulterade i döden, lidande och skador på koncentrationslagerfängelserna.

En viktig konsekvens av läkarprocessen var formulerandet av Nurembergskoden 1947 – inte 1945 som posten säger. Nurembergskoden utformade tio etiska principer för att utföra medicinska experiment på människor, med den första och viktigaste principen att "frivilligt samtycke från den mänskliga ärendet är absolut nödvändigt". Denna princip uppstod direkt i samband med den kraftiga och icke-samtyckande natur av nazistiska medicinska experiment.

Koden föreskriver att individer måste kunna utöva fri valmakt och ska ha tillräckligt med kunskap och förståelse för experimentet för att kunna göra ett informerat beslut. Koden använder inte specifikt ordet "läkemedel", men hänvisar bredt till medicinska experiment, ingrepp och procedurer.

Faktaundersökning av påståendet visar att Nurembergskodens kärnprincip verkligen handlar om informerat och frivilligt samtycke till medicinska procedurer, inklusive administrering av ämnen eller deltagande i experiment. Det är dock viktigt att notera att koden utvecklades i sammanhanget med mänskliga experiment – inte rutinmedicinsk behandling eller offentliga hälsoskyddsinterventioner. Principerna har sedan påverkat modern medicinsk etik, inklusive kravet på informerat samtycke i både forskning och klinisk vård.

Angående vaccin, är standardiserade immuniseringar generellt sett inte betraktade som experimentella procedurer utan snarare som etablerade medicinska rutiner, under sina egna regelverk. I de flesta demokratiska länder är vaccinering frivillig, och individer har rätt att vägrå, utom i sällsynta fall där offentliga hälsolagar kan kräva vaccinering under nödtilstånd. Även i sådana fall kräver lagar och etiska normer vanligtvis skydd och, så långt som möjligt, respekt för individens självbestämmande.

Sammanfattningsvis fastsattes av Nurembergskoden nödvändigheten av frivilligt samtycke till deltagande i medicinska experiment efter de skräck som avslöjades under nazistepoeten. Även om dess principer har format moderna förväntningar på informerat samtycke, är påståendet att Nuremberg-processen deklarerade att administrering av läkemedel (som vaccin) mot en persons vilja är ett "brott" en förenkling. Koden gäller främst forskning, inte alla former av medicinsk behandling eller offentlig hälsopolitik, och dess tillämpning på vaccin beror på sammanhanget – om de är experimentella eller rutinmässiga. Således understryker Nurembergskoden vikten av samtycke, men att lika alla vaccinadministreringar utan samtycke ska anses för brott enligt Nuremberg-principerna är en felaktig tolkning av historiska och etiska dokument.

On social media, a post has been circulating claiming that Mirlinda Azizi, described as a nurse from Kicevo, died from Covid-19 despite being fully vaccinated with two doses of the Pfizer vaccine. The post has garnered significant attention, sparking concerns and questions about vaccine effectiveness, the circumstances of her death, and the broader context of Covid-19 cases among vaccinated individuals.

To verify this claim, it is important to establish the facts surrounding the case, understand the background of Covid-19 vaccination efforts in North Macedonia, and clarify how vaccines function in preventing severe illness and death.

Kicevo is a municipality in North Macedonia, where Covid-19 vaccination campaigns have been ongoing since early 2021. Healthcare workers, including nurses, were among the first groups to receive the vaccine due to their elevated risk of exposure. The Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, known for its high efficacy rates, has been widely administered in the region.

The core claim is that Mirlinda Azizi, a nurse from Kicevo, died of Covid-19 after receiving two doses of Pfizer. Local news reports and official statements confirm that Mirlinda Azizi was indeed a nurse working in Kicevo. Her death was announced by healthcare authorities, and it was reported that she had contracted Covid-19 prior to passing away. Statements from colleagues and social media tributes further corroborate her role as a nurse and her recent death due to complications from Covid-19.

Regarding her vaccination status, multiple sources indicate that Azizi had received two doses of the Pfizer vaccine. The timeline of her vaccination and infection is not fully detailed in public records; however, it is widely acknowledged that she was considered fully vaccinated at the time she contracted Covid-19.

While the post accurately reports her profession, location, vaccination status, and cause of death, it is crucial to place these facts in context. Covid-19 vaccines, including Pfizer, are highly effective at preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death. However, no vaccine provides 100% protection, and breakthrough infections—cases where vaccinated individuals contract the virus—can occur, particularly among those with underlying health conditions, compromised immune systems, or high exposure risk.

Statistical data show that deaths among fully vaccinated individuals are rare but possible, especially as variant strains of the virus circulate and immunity may wane over time. Healthcare workers, due to their constant exposure, may be at higher risk for contracting the virus even after vaccination.

The case of Mirlinda Azizi is a tragic example of a breakthrough infection resulting in fatality. It underscores the importance of continuing public health measures, booster vaccinations for vulnerable groups, and the need for ongoing monitoring of vaccine effectiveness. While her death is a sobering reminder that vaccines do not guarantee absolute protection, they remain the most effective tool for reducing the risk of severe outcomes from Covid-19.

In summary, the social media post about Mirlinda Azizi's death is factually accurate. She was a nurse from Kicevo, died from Covid-19, and had received two doses of the Pfizer vaccine. This case highlights the importance of understanding the limits of vaccine protection and the continued need for vigilance in combating Covid-19.

article_content:
A recent social media post has claimed that “most of the patients admitted here to the Infectious Diseases Clinic are patients who received two doses of vaccines, and there are no registered patients who have had covid and become infected again.” This statement has garnered significant attention and concern, given the ongoing debates about COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness and the nature of reinfection. Here, we examine the accuracy of these claims, provide context, and analyze available evidence.

**Understanding the Claims**

The post makes two primary assertions: first, that the majority of patients currently hospitalized for COVID-19 at an Infectious Diseases Clinic are fully vaccinated with two doses; and second, that no patients who had previously contracted COVID-19 have been readmitted due to reinfection.

**Context and Background**

COVID-19 vaccines were developed to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death—not necessarily to prevent all infections. As the pandemic has progressed, new variants have emerged, some of which can partially evade immune protection provided by vaccines or previous infection. While breakthrough infections (cases where vaccinated individuals contract the virus) do occur, vaccines have consistently shown to reduce the severity of symptoms and rates of hospitalization and death, even against newer variants.

Regarding reinfection, early in the pandemic, it was believed that recovering from COVID-19 provided strong, though not absolute, protection against subsequent infection. With the advent of new variants, cases of reinfection have been documented, though the risk remains lower compared to those who have neither been infected nor vaccinated.

**Fact-Checking the Core Claims**

*Claim 1: Most patients admitted to the clinic are vaccinated with two doses.*

Data from multiple countries indicate that the majority of individuals hospitalized with COVID-19, especially during surges driven by new variants, are unvaccinated or partially vaccinated. However, in populations with very high vaccination rates, the absolute number of breakthrough hospitalizations can increase simply because the vast majority of people are vaccinated. This is a statistical effect known as the “base rate fallacy,” where the denominator (total number of vaccinated individuals) is so large that even a small rate of breakthrough cases can constitute a majority of hospitalizations. Nevertheless, per capita, unvaccinated people remain at significantly higher risk of severe disease and hospitalization.

Without specific data from the named Infectious Diseases Clinic, it is not possible to verify the claim that “most” hospitalized patients received two vaccine doses. However, generalized data does not support the idea that vaccinated individuals are disproportionately represented among severe cases relative to their numbers in the population.

*Claim 2: No patients who had COVID-19 are being reinfected and registered as patients again.*

There are documented cases worldwide of COVID-19 reinfection, including instances severe enough to warrant hospitalization. While prior infection does confer immunity, it is not absolute, especially as the virus evolves. The absence of reinfected patients in one clinic at a particular time does not mean reinfection does not occur. It may reflect local trends, reporting practices, or the timing of data collection.

**Conclusion**

The claim that most hospitalized patients are fully vaccinated oversimplifies complex data and may be misleading without broader context. The assertion that no reinfected patients are registered does not align with broader epidemiological evidence. Immunity from vaccination and previous infection both offer protection, but neither is absolute. Accurate interpretation of hospitalization data requires careful consideration of population-level vaccination rates, variant circulation, and local infection history.

Nauja socialinio tinklo paskyroje teigė, kad „dauguma pacientų, įtraukti čia į Infekcinių ligų kliniką, yra pacientai, gavę dvi vakcinos dozes, ir neregistruota pacientų, kurie buvo sergę koronavirusu ir vėl jį ėmė“, ši teiga sukelia didelę dėmesį ir rūpestį, nes tęsiasi debatai apie vakcinos efektyvumą ir vėlsergimo pobūdį. Štai mes nagrinėjame šių teigiamų tikslumą, suteikiame kontekstą ir analizuojame prieinamą įrodymą.

**Supratimas teigiamų sakinio**

Paskyroje yra dvi pagrindinės teigiamosios išvados: pirmiausia, kad dauguma pacientų, kurie dabar ligonių įstaigose yra sergę koronavirusu, yra pilnai vakcinuoti dvi dozes; antra, kad neregistruota pacientų, kurie anksčiau buvo sergę koronavirusu ir vėl jį ėmė, dėl vėlsergimo.

**Kontekstas ir pagrindinė informacija**

Koronaviruso vakcinos buvo sukurtos, kad sumažintų ligos sunkumą, ligonių įstaigų įtraukimą ir mirštamumą – ne tik kad visiškai išvengtų infekcijos. Kuo ilgiau truko pandemija, tuo daugiau atsirado naujų variantų, kurių kai kurie galėjo išvengti imuninės apsaugos, kurią suteikia vakcina ar ankstesnė infekcija. Nors tarp vakcinuotų asmenų gali atsirasti ligos atvejai (atsitiktinės infekcijos), vakcinos visada rodo, kad sumažina simptomų sunkumą, ligonių įtraukimų ir mirties dažnumą, net naujais variantais.

Dėl vėlsergimo, pradžioje pandemijos laikotarpiui buvo tikėta, kad išgyvenus koronavirusą suteikia stiprų, bet neabsoliutų apsaugą nuo tolesnių infekcijų. Naujų variantų atsiradimo metu įrašyti vėlsergimo atvejai, nors rizika yra mažesnė nei tiems, kurie nei nebuvo infektyvūs, nei nebuvo vakcinuoti.

**Tikrinant pagrindines teigiamas**

*Teiginys 1: Dauguma pacientų, įtraukta į kliniką, yra vakcinuoti dvi dozes.*

Kelių šalių duomenys rodo, kad dauguma ligonių, sergančių koronavirusu, ypač per šių naujų variantų viršijimų laikotarpį, yra nevakcinuoti arba dalinai vakcinuoti. Tačiau populiacijose su labai aukšta vakcinavimo kiekiu, absoliutus ligonių įtraukimų skaičius gali išaugti tiesiog todėl, kad dauguma žmonių vakcinuoti. Tai statistinis efektas, vadinamas „pagrindinio rodiklio klaidą“, kurioje denominacija (vakcinuotų žmonių visumas) yra tokia didelė, kad net mažas ligos atvejų procentas gali sudaryti daugumą ligonių. Tačiau per capita, nevakcinuoti žmonės vis dar yra labiau pažeidžiami sunkiai ligos ir ligonių įtraukimui.

Be konkrečių duomenų iš nurodytos Infekcinių ligų klinikos, negalima patvirtinti teiginio, kad „dauguma“ ligonių gavo dvi vakcinos dozes. Tačiau bendri duomenys ne patvirtina, kad vakcinuoti asmenys būtų per daug atstovaujantys sunkių ligų atvejų, lyginant su jų populiacijoje skaičiumi.

*Teiginys 2: Neregistruota pacientų, kurie buvo sergę koronavirusu, vėl jį ėmė.*

Pasaulio šalyse dokumentuota koronaviruso vėlsergimo atvejai, įskaitant atvejus, kuriuos reikėjo įtraukti į ligonių įstaigas. Nors anksčiau sergusios infekcija suteikia imuninę apsaugą, ji nėra absoliutinė, ypač kai virusas vystosi. Neregistruoti vėlsergimo pacientai vienoje klinikos laikotarpiui nereiškia, kad vėlsergimo nėra. Tai gali atspindėti vietos tendencijas, ataskaitų praktikas arba duomenų surinkimo laiką.

**Išvada**

Teiginys, kad dauguma ligonių yra pilnai vakcinuoti, pernelyg paprasta ir gali būti išvengta be plačiosios konteksto. Teiginys, kad neregistruota vėlsergimo pacientų, neatitinka platesnio epidemiologinio įrodymo. Imuninės apsaugos, gautos vakcinuojant ir anksčiau sergant, abu suteikia apsaugą, bet nei viena nėra absoliutinė. Tiksli ligonių įtraukimo duomenų interpretacija reikalauja atsargaus įvertinimo populiacijos vakcinavimo lygmenų, variantų kruopščiai perleidimo ir vietos infekcijos istorijos.

article_content:
A recent social media post has circulated a video in which a doctor claims that the spike protein produced by COVID-19 vaccines circulates throughout the body, accumulates in organs, and acts as a toxin. The doctor further states that when spike protein is injected into laboratory animals, it causes the same diseases seen in COVID-19, specifically affecting the heart, lungs, and cardiovascular system. The post concludes by questioning why “toxins” would be injected into humans. This article examines these claims in detail, offering background and a thorough fact-check.

**Background: Understanding the Spike Protein and Vaccines**

The COVID-19 vaccines authorized for use in many countries, including mRNA vaccines (such as those made by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna), work by instructing cells to produce a harmless piece of the spike protein found on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This spike protein triggers an immune response, teaching the body to recognize and fight the actual virus if exposed in the future. Importantly, the spike protein produced by the vaccine is not the entire virus; it cannot cause COVID-19.

**Claim 1: The Spike Protein Circulates and Accumulates in Organs**

The claim suggests that the spike protein made after vaccination leaves the injection site, travels through the bloodstream, and ends up in various organs, potentially causing harm. Research shows that after vaccination, the spike protein is produced locally in muscle cells near the injection site and is quickly broken down by the body’s immune system. Small amounts of spike protein or its fragments may enter the bloodstream temporarily, but studies indicate that these levels are extremely low and short-lived. There is no credible evidence that the spike protein produced by vaccines accumulates in organs or causes lasting harm.

**Claim 2: Injecting Spike Protein Causes COVID-19-Like Diseases in Animals**

The assertion that injecting spike protein into animals causes COVID-19-like diseases is misleading. While laboratory studies have examined the effects of the spike protein in animals, these studies typically use much higher concentrations than what is produced after vaccination. Furthermore, the spike protein alone, without the rest of the virus, does not cause COVID-19. A social media post making the rounds claims: “Take care of your children. They secretly want to vaccinate them. It is a crime. Vaccines are poisonous.” The post contains several serious allegations regarding vaccination practices, the intent of health authorities, and the safety of vaccines. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context and evaluating the available evidence.

First, the post suggests that there is a covert effort to vaccinate children without parental knowledge or consent. In most countries, vaccination policies for children are governed by strict regulations. Typically, parental consent is required for minors to receive vaccinations, except in certain public health emergencies or specific legal circumstances where different consent protocols may apply. While there have been discussions and rare instances in some regions regarding adolescent consent for certain vaccines (such as the HPV vaccine), it is not standard practice to vaccinate children “secretly,” and any such actions would generally violate established medical ethics and legal requirements.

The post further claims that vaccinating children without parental consent is a criminal act. Laws regarding medical consent for minors vary by country and jurisdiction. In most cases, administering medical treatment to a child without the consent of a parent or legal guardian, outside of emergencies or specific legal exceptions, can carry legal consequences. However, authorized vaccination programs conducted through schools or public health agencies typically operate transparently, with consent forms and information provided to parents or guardians well in advance. There is no credible evidence of widespread, systematic illegal vaccination of children.

Another significant claim made in the post is that “vaccines are poisonous.” Vaccines undergo rigorous testing for safety and efficacy before they are approved for use by regulatory authorities. These assessments involve multiple phases of clinical trials, as well as continuous monitoring once vaccines are in use. While vaccines, like any medical intervention, can cause side effects, the vast majority are mild and temporary, such as soreness at the injection site or mild fever. Serious adverse reactions are rare. The main ingredients in vaccines—such as weakened or inactivated viruses, proteins, adjuvants, and preservatives—are present in safe amounts and are carefully regulated. The overwhelming scientific consensus is that vaccines are a safe and effective means of preventing many infectious diseases.

The claim that vaccines are “poisonous” misrepresents their purpose and safety profile. Vaccines have played a critical role in controlling and eradicating diseases such as smallpox, polio, and measles, saving millions of lives worldwide. The benefits of vaccination in preventing serious illness, disability, and death far outweigh the risks of rare adverse effects.

In summary, the social media post contains several inaccurate and misleading claims. There is no substantiated evidence of secret or illegal vaccination of children on a broad scale, nor is there credible scientific support for the assertion that vaccines are poisonous. Parents concerned about vaccination are encouraged to consult healthcare providers and rely on information from reputable health organizations.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that three substances—graphene oxide, spike protein, and the enzyme luciferase—are being omitted from an unspecified list, raising concerns regarding their presence in products or technologies, often in the context of vaccines or medical interventions. Such assertions have circulated widely online, particularly since the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines, prompting questions about the accuracy and implications of these claims. This article examines each component individually, providing context, background, and a thorough fact-checking analysis.

**Graphene Oxide**

Graphene oxide is a material derived from graphite and is known for its unique chemical and physical properties, such as high conductivity and strength. It has applications in various fields, including electronics, energy storage, and biomedical research. Some social media posts allege that graphene oxide is a hidden ingredient in COVID-19 vaccines or other medical products. However, there is no credible evidence to support the claim that graphene oxide is present in any of the approved COVID-19 vaccines or commonly used pharmaceutical products. Regulatory agencies and manufacturers list all ingredients in vaccines and these lists do not include graphene oxide. While research into potential medical uses of graphene oxide exists, such as its use in drug delivery systems or biosensors, it has not been approved for use in vaccines administered to the public.

**Spike Protein**

The spike protein refers to a structural protein found on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which facilitates entry into human cells. In the context of COVID-19 vaccines, particularly mRNA vaccines, small segments of genetic code instruct human cells to produce a harmless version of the spike protein to stimulate an immune response. This allows the body to recognize and defend against the actual virus if exposed. Some social media posts suggest that spike proteins themselves are dangerous or are being concealed from the public. In reality, the spike protein generated by mRNA vaccines is not infectious and is rapidly broken down by the body’s immune system. The inclusion of the spike protein mechanism is openly disclosed in vaccine information, and its role is fundamental to vaccine efficacy. Scientific consensus maintains that the spike protein produced via vaccination is safe for the vast majority of people.

**Luciferase**

Luciferase is an enzyme found in various organisms, such as fireflies, that emits light through a biochemical reaction. In biomedical research, luciferase is frequently used as a marker in laboratory studies to visualize and measure cellular processes, but it is not an ingredient in any authorized COVID-19 vaccine or other routine vaccines. The claim that luciferase is secretly included in vaccines or medical products is unfounded. Its use in research does not translate to its presence in products administered to humans. Some confusion may arise from early-stage experiments or patents mentioning luciferase in the development of vaccine technologies, but these do not pertain to ingredients used in approved products.

**Conclusion**

The social media post suggesting that graphene oxide, spike protein, and luciferase are omitted from ingredient lists reflects a broader trend of misinformation and misunderstanding regarding biomedical technologies. Available evidence indicates that graphene oxide and luciferase are not present in approved vaccines or pharmaceutical products. The spike protein, meanwhile, is intentionally produced in the body as part of the mechanism of certain vaccines, and its role is transparently communicated. Public health agencies and manufacturers maintain clear records of vaccine ingredients, and claims of hidden substances are not supported by credible scientific evidence.

**ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ്**

ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ് ഗ്രാഫൈറ്റിൽ നിന്നുള്ള ഒരു പദാർത്ഥമാണ്, അത് അതിന്റെ പ്രത്യേക രാസപരിശോധന അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഭൗതിക പ്രതിഭാസങ്ങൾ, ഉയർന്ന പ്രവഹനശക്തി അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ശക്തി എന്നിവയുടെ കാരണം അറിയപ്പെടുന്നു. ഇത് വിവിധ മേഖലകളിലും ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു, എന്നാൽ ഇലക്ട്രോണിക്സ്, ഊർജ്ജ സംഭരണം, ബയോമെഡിക്കൽ പഠനങ്ങൾ എന്നിവയിലും. ചില സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയ പോസ്റ്റുകൾ ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ് കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനുകളിലും മറ്റ് ആരോഗ്യ ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിലും ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ടെന്ന് ആരോപിക്കുന്നു. എന്നാൽ, അത് അപ്പോ അപ്പോ അംഗീകൃത കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനുകളിലും സാധാരണ ഔഷധ ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിലും ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടില്ല എന്ന് പ്രാമാണിക തെളിവ് ഉണ്ടായിട്ടില്ല. വാക്സിനുകളിലെ എല്ലാ ഘടകങ്ങളും നിയമപരമായ സംവിധാനങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഉൽപ്പാദകർ പട്ടികപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു, അതിൽ ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ് ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടില്ല. അതിന്റെ ആരോഗ്യ ഉപയോഗത്തിനുള്ള പഠനങ്ങൾ അപ്പോ അപ്പോ മരുന്ന് വിതരണ സംവിധാനങ്ങളിൽ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ബയോസെൻസറുകളിൽ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു, എന്നാൽ അത് സാധാരണ പൊതു ജനങ്ങൾക്ക് വാക്സിനുകളിൽ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു എന്ന് അംഗീകരിച്ചിട്ടില്ല.

**സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീൻ**

സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീൻ എന്നത് SARS-CoV-2 വൈറസിന്റെ മുഖഭാഗത്ത് കണ്ടെത്തിയ ഒരു സംവിധാനമാണ്, അത് മനുഷ്യ സെല്ലുകളിൽ പ്രവേശിക്കുന്നതിന് സഹായിക്കുന്നു. കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനുകളുടെ സാഹചര്യത്തിൽ, പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് mRNA വാക്സിനുകളിൽ, മനുഷ്യ സെല്ലുകൾക്ക് ഒരു സുരക്ഷിതമായ സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനിന്റെ പകർപ്പ് ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്ന ചെറിയ മാന്ദ്യം പ്രതികരണം പ്രക്രിയ നടത്താൻ പ്രവേശിക്കുന്നു. ഇത് അവർ വാസ്തവത്തിൽ വൈറസിനെ പരിചയപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിന് പ്രതിരോധം നല്കുന്നതിന് അവർ പ്രതികരിക്കുന്നു. ചില സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയ പോസ്റ്റുകൾ സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനുകൾ തന്നെ ആരോഗ്യ പ്രശ്നങ്ങൾക്ക് കാരണമാകുന്നതാണ് അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അത് പൊതു ജനങ്ങൾക്ക് വിവരം നൽകാൻ മറന്നിട്ടുണ്ട്. വാസ്തവത്തിൽ, mRNA വാക്സിനുകളിൽ ഉണ്ടാകുന്ന സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനിന് പ്രകോപനം ഉണ്ടാകാത്തതാണ്, അത് ശരീരത്തിലെ പ്രതിരോധ സംവിധാനത്തിൽ വേഗം വിഘടിക്കുന്നു. വാക്സിനിന്റെ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിൽ സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനിന്റെ ഉപയോഗം സാധാരണ ജനങ്ങൾക്ക് പ്രായോഗികമായി പ്രതികരിക്കുന്നു. വാക്സിനിന്റെ പ്രായോഗികതയുടെ പ്രാധാന്യം കാണിക്കുന്നതിന് അത് പുറത്തിറക്കിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. വിദഗ്ദ്ധർ പരിശോധനയിൽ സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീനിന്റെ ഉപയോഗം പൊതുവെ സുരക്ഷിതമാണ് എന്ന് സമഗ്രമായി പ്രാമാണികമായി പറയുന്നു.

ലൂസഫർസ് പ്രകൃതിയിലെ പല ജീവികളിലും ഉണ്ടാകുന്ന ഒരു എൻസൈം ആണ്, പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് ഫയർഫ്ലൈക്കിലെ പോലുള്ളവയിൽ അത് ബയോകെമിക്കൽ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിനാലുള്ള പ്രകാശം ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്നു. ബയോമെഡിക്കൽ പഠനത്തിൽ, ലൂസഫർസ് ലേബർട്ടറി പരീക്ഷണങ്ങളിൽ പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് സെല്ലുകളുടെ പ്രവർത്തനങ്ങൾ കാണിക്കുന്നതിന് പരിശോധന ചെയ്യുന്നതിനുള്ള ചിഹ്നമായി ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു, എന്നാൽ അത് ഒരു അനുമോദിത കൊവിഡ്-19 വാക്സിനിലും അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മറ്റ് പ്രതിസന്ധി വാക്സിനിലും ഉള്ളതാണ്. വാക്സിനുകളിലോ ആരോഗ്യ ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിലോ ലൂസഫർസ് ഗൂഢാലോചനയിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടില്ല എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് തെറ്റായ വാദമാണ്. അതിന്റെ ഉപയോഗം പരിശോധനയിൽ അത് മനുഷ്യർക്ക് നൽകുന്ന ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തുന്നതിന് പരിവർത്തനം ചെയ്യുന്നില്ല. കൂടാതെ, വാക്സിനുകളുടെ തുടര്‍പ്പെടുത്തൽ പ്രക്രിയയിലെ കുറിച്ചുള്ള പ്രാചീന പരീക്ഷണങ്ങളിലോ പേറ്റന്റുകളിലോ ലൂസഫർസ് പരാമർശിക്കപ്പെട്ടിട്ടുണ്ടെങ്കിലും അത് അംഗീകൃത ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിലെ ഘടകങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ സാധാരണ പ്രവർത്തനങ്ങളിലെ ഘടകങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ പൊതുവെ പ്രവർത്തനങ്ങളിലെ ഘടകങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അതിന് പുറത്ത് പ്രവർത്തനങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മറ്റ് കാര്യങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അത് പരിശോധനയിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടില്ല.

**പരിഗണനയിലെ വിവരങ്ങൾ**

ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ്, സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീൻ എന്നീ മൂന്ന് ഘടകങ്ങൾ അവയുടെ ഘടകപട്ടികകളിൽ പുറത്തിറക്കപ്പെട്ടിട്ടില്ല എന്ന് സോഷ്യൽ മീഡിയ പോസ്റ്റ് പറയുന്നു, ഇത് ബയോമെഡിക്കൽ തകനാട്ടുകളിൽ പരിശോധന പ്രതിഫലങ്ങളിൽ വ്യാപകമായ അസത്യ വാദങ്ങളും അപ്രത്യക്ഷ മനസ്സിലെ അന്തരങ്ങളും പ്രതിഫലിക്കുന്നു. ലഭ്യമായ തെളിവുകൾ ഗ്രാഫീൻ ഓക്സൈഡ് അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ലൂസഫർസ് അംഗീകൃത വാക്സിനുകളിലോ ഔഷധ ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങളിലോ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടില്ല. സ്പൈക്ക് പ്രോട്ടീൻ എന്ന് പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് ചില വാക്സിനുകളുടെ പ്രവർത്തനത്തിലെ ഘടകമായി തന്നെ ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്നു, അതിന്റെ പങ്ക് പ്രത്യക്ഷമായി പ്രഖ്യാപിക്കുന്നു. പൊതു ആരോഗ്യ സംവിധാനങ്ങൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഉൽപ്പാദകർ വാക്സിനിന്റെ ഘടകങ്ങളുടെ പട്ടികകൾ സൂക്ഷിക്കുന്നു, അത് അസത്യമായ തെളിവുകൾ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അവ സമർത്ഥമായ വിദ്യാഭ്യാസ തെളിവുകളിൽ പ്രതിഫലിക്കുന്നില്ല.

A widely shared social media post claims that Bill Gates stated, “I expect 700,000 deaths as a result of vaccination against the Covid-19.” This striking allegation has generated concern and confusion, prompting a need for careful fact-checking and context.

Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft and a philanthropist heavily involved in global health initiatives, has been a prominent voice in discussions about the Covid-19 pandemic and vaccination efforts. However, the claim that Gates predicted or expected 700,000 deaths as a direct result of Covid-19 vaccination is misleading and does not accurately reflect his public statements or scientific consensus.

The origin of this claim traces back to an interview Bill Gates gave in April 2020, at a time when Covid-19 vaccines were still in development and regulatory agencies were considering the risks and benefits of accelerated approval processes. In the interview, Gates discussed the possibility of adverse reactions to new vaccines, a standard concern in vaccine development. He referenced the need to ensure that safety testing was thorough, noting that if a vaccine is administered to billions of people, even rare side effects could affect a number of individuals.

Gates did not state, nor imply, that he “expected” 700,000 deaths from vaccination. Rather, he cited a hypothetical calculation: if a vaccine caused severe side effects in one in 10,000 recipients, vaccinating the entire world population could lead to approximately 700,000 cases of adverse effects—not deaths. Notably, adverse effects can range from mild to severe, and the vast majority are not fatal. Gates’ comments highlighted the importance of robust safety protocols, not an expectation of mass casualties.

Since the rollout of various Covid-19 vaccines, health authorities and regulatory agencies around the world have closely monitored vaccine safety. While some rare side effects have been identified, the number of deaths directly attributable to Covid-19 vaccines is exceedingly small, especially compared to the millions of lives saved by preventing severe disease, hospitalization, and death from the virus itself.

Health experts emphasize that, like all medical interventions, vaccines are associated with rare risks, but these are far outweighed by their benefits. The assertion that Bill Gates expected 700,000 deaths as a result of vaccination misinterprets his comments and lacks any basis in medical data or official reports.

In summary, the claim circulating on social media distorts a statement about hypothetical side effects into an alarming and inaccurate prediction. Bill Gates did not say or suggest that 700,000 people would die from Covid-19 vaccination. Instead, he advocated for careful safety assessment while supporting the rapid development and global distribution of vaccines. The overwhelming evidence supports the safety and efficacy of Covid-19 vaccines, and claims to the contrary misinform the public and undermine vital public health efforts.

מאחורי הצוות ה التطعيمים לكورونا, רגילים ועוסקים בתקופת הפקת التطعيمים监控 את בטיחות التطعيمים. למרות שמצטברות כמה תופעות לוואי נדירות, מספר הوفيات שהותקפו באופן ישיר מה التطعيمים הקורונאיים הוא זניח במיוחד, במיוחד בהשוואה למיליונים של חיים שיצרו במניעה של מחלות חמורה, חירום רפואי, ומוות מה冠状病毒 עצמו.

לסיכום, הטענה שהפכה למשהו מפורסם במדיה חברתית מוטיעה את תיאור תופעות לוואי מיתומה לטענה מפחידת ובלתי נכונה. גיטס לא אמר או סיפק ש700,000 אנשים יموו מה التطعيم נגד הקורונה. במקום זאת, הוא תמך בבדיקה מדויקת של בטיחות, תוך שיתוף הפעולה בהירות בتطوير מהיר והפצת التطعيمים. הראות הדרמטית תומכת בטיחות ויעילות של التطعيمים נגד הקורונה, וטענות ההפוכה מזוייפות את הציבור ומכהות את מאמצי הבריאות הלא מודעים.

article_content:
A recent social media post is circulating with alarming claims regarding COVID-19 vaccines and the ongoing evolution of the virus. The post asserts that "people are starting to die from the vaccine," and that authorities are attributing these deaths to "another mutation in the Covid-19 worse than the previous ones." It further alleges that "the unvaccinated are to blame for the deaths." This fact-checking article examines the accuracy and context of these statements.

First, it is important to clarify the scientific and public health consensus regarding COVID-19 vaccines and their safety. Vaccines authorized or approved for use have undergone rigorous clinical trials and are continually monitored for safety. Serious side effects from COVID-19 vaccines are extremely rare. The vast majority of adverse effects are mild and temporary, such as soreness at the injection site or mild flu-like symptoms. While there have been rare reports of severe reactions, such as myocarditis or blood clotting disorders, these cases are exceptional and are far outweighed by the benefits of vaccination in preventing COVID-19, severe illness, and death.

The claim that "people are starting to die from the vaccine" lacks substantiated evidence. Health authorities globally, including in regions with high vaccination rates, have not detected any spike in mortality attributable to the vaccines themselves. Most reported deaths following vaccination have been thoroughly investigated and are overwhelmingly found to be coincidental or related to underlying health conditions. There is no credible data to suggest that the vaccines are causing widespread fatalities.

The second part of the post claims that authorities are blaming these alleged deaths on a new COVID-19 mutation "worse than the previous ones." While it is true that new variants of the virus continue to emerge, this is a normal aspect of viral evolution. Some variants have shown increased transmissibility or partial resistance to immunity, but current evidence does not support the assertion that a new mutation is causing a surge in deaths, nor that such deaths are being misattributed to natural causes when they are actually vaccine-related.

Finally, the post alleges that "the unvaccinated are to blame for the deaths." Public health messaging has occasionally highlighted that unvaccinated individuals are at higher risk of contracting and transmitting COVID-19, which can contribute to outbreaks and strain healthcare systems. However, blaming any single group for pandemic-related deaths oversimplifies a complex situation. Factors such as access to healthcare, underlying medical conditions, and community transmission dynamics all play significant roles.

In summary, the claims made in the social media post are misleading and not supported by current scientific evidence. COVID-19 vaccines remain a critical tool in controlling the pandemic and have saved millions of lives worldwide. Ongoing monitoring and transparent reporting continue to ensure vaccine safety. The emergence of variants is being closely tracked, and there is no substantiated link between vaccination and a rise in deaths. Public discourse benefits from factual, nuanced information rather than fear-based or divisive assertions.

article_content:
A social media post has been circulating, claiming that vaccinated individuals are at risk of contracting a new virus, can transmit it, and thus should be isolated from society. The post further asserts that the unvaccinated are not dangerous, whereas the vaccinated are. These statements have created confusion and concern among the public, prompting a need for thorough fact-checking and clarification.

First, it is crucial to understand the basic principles of how vaccines work and the nature of viral transmission. Vaccines are designed to stimulate the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens, thereby reducing the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death. With most viruses, including those targeting respiratory systems, vaccines do not always provide absolute immunity but significantly decrease the likelihood of severe outcomes. It is true that vaccinated individuals, particularly with newer variants of viruses, may experience breakthrough infections; however, these cases are generally milder compared to those in unvaccinated individuals.

Regarding transmission, scientific observations have confirmed that both vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals can transmit viruses. Vaccines typically reduce the amount of virus in the body (viral load), which can, in turn, reduce the likelihood of passing the virus to others. However, transmission is still possible, especially with highly contagious variants. Therefore, the claim that vaccinated people are uniquely dangerous or pose a greater risk of spreading the virus is not supported by the majority of scientific evidence. In fact, studies have shown that unvaccinated individuals tend to be at higher risk of contracting and transmitting the virus due to a lack of immune protection.

The assertion that "the unvaccinated are not dangerous" is misleading. Public health data consistently show that unvaccinated populations are more likely to suffer serious illness and are more likely to transmit the virus, especially during outbreaks. The risk they pose is not only to themselves but also to others, particularly those who cannot be vaccinated due to medical reasons or those with compromised immune systems.

The suggestion that vaccinated individuals should be isolated from society is unsupported and contrary to public health guidance. Isolation is typically recommended for individuals who are actively infected and contagious, regardless of vaccination status. Blanket isolation of vaccinated people would not only be impractical but also unjustified based on current scientific understanding.

In summary, while vaccinated individuals can contract and transmit viruses, they generally do so at lower rates and with less severe outcomes than their unvaccinated counterparts. The portrayal of the vaccinated as a danger to society, and the unvaccinated as harmless, is inaccurate and misrepresents the available evidence. Effective public health strategies continue to prioritize vaccination as a key tool in controlling the spread and impact of infectious diseases.

ମୂଳରେ, ଟିକାକରିତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିମାନେ ଭାଇରସ ପ୍ରାପ୍ତ ଓ ପ୍ରଚାର କରିପାରନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅପରିହାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ରୋଗରେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ତୁଳନାତ୍ମକ ପରିମାଣରେ କମ୍ ଭାରୀ ଫଳାଫଳ ରହିଛି। ଟିକାକରିତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିମାନଙ୍କୁ ସମାଜର ବିପଦ ବିଷୟରେ ବିବେଚନା କରାଯାଇଛି, ଯେତେବେଳେ ଟିକା ନାହାଁନ୍ତି ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିମାନଙ୍କୁ ଅପରିହାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ହେବାର ବିପଦରେ ନାହାଁନ୍ତି, ଏହା ଅପ୍ରମାଣିତ ଏବଂ ବିଜ୍ଞାନର ପ୍ରମାଣରେ ଭୁଲ ବୁଝାଇଛି। ପ୍ରାପ୍ତ ପ୍ରମାଣର ପ୍ରଭାବକୁ କମାଇବା ପାଇଁ ପ୍ରାଥମିକ ପ୍ରଜାରେ ଟିକାକରଣକୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶିତ କରାଯାଇଛି।

According to the publisher of the video, the altercation is said to have stemmed from a misunderstanding related to vaccination certificates and the implementation of new anti-COVID measures.

Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, North Macedonia and neighboring regions have implemented various public health measures to mitigate the spread of the virus. These measures have included requirements for vaccination certificates or negative test results for entry into certain public venues, which have occasionally led to confusion and disputes.

The claim centers on a fight allegedly triggered by disagreements over vaccination certificates—documents that have become increasingly important for access to public spaces. Such certificates are intended to prove an individual’s vaccination status and are mandated in some areas as part of broader anti-COVID policies. The introduction of these rules has, in some instances, led to confrontations between customers, business owners, and staff, particularly when enforcement is unclear or contentious.

Upon reviewing the video, which shows a chaotic scene with individuals shouting and physically confronting each other inside a pastry shop, it is difficult to ascertain the specific cause of the fight from the footage alone. The video does not include clear audio or visible documentation of vaccination certificates being checked or disputed. Furthermore, there is no official statement from local authorities or the pastry shop itself confirming the reasons behind the altercation.

Social media commentary, both from the original publisher of the video and subsequent commenters, suggests that the fight may have been related to COVID-19 regulations, specifically the requirement for vaccination certificates. However, social media posts are not always reliable sources of factual information, as they can be influenced by personal biases, incomplete details, or attempts to sensationalize events.

In this instance, while it is plausible that heightened tensions over anti-COVID measures and vaccination requirements could have contributed to the dispute, there is insufficient direct evidence to conclusively state that the fight was caused by issues surrounding vaccination certificates. It is possible that other factors, such as personal disagreements or unrelated misunderstandings, played a role.

In summary, although the video shows a physical altercation in a pastry shop in Centar Zupa and social media users have speculated that it was related to vaccination certificates and new anti-COVID measures, there is no definitive proof linking the fight to these regulations. Without official confirmation or further evidence, the claim remains unverified and should be treated with caution. The situation highlights the ongoing challenges of enforcing public health measures and the potential for misinformation to spread in the absence of clear facts.

A widely shared social media post claims that Dr. Sean Brooks, described as an internal medicine specialist with over 23 years of experience, has issued a dire warning regarding COVID-19 vaccines. According to the post, Dr. Brooks alleges that everyone who has received a COVID-19 vaccine will die within six months to five years and will become sterilized, unable to have children. The post questions how many more medical specialists will be ignored on this subject.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to review the credentials of Dr. Brooks, the content of his warnings, and the scientific evidence related to COVID-19 vaccines and their safety.

First, there is scant evidence that Dr. Sean Brooks is a licensed internal medicine specialist or that he has 23 years of experience in that field. Publicly available information indicates that Dr. Sean Brooks has presented himself as an author and commentator, but not as a practicing physician or an expert in internal medicine. There is no record of him being affiliated with major medical institutions or holding medical licenses in the United States. This raises questions about the authority and expertise underpinning the statements attributed to him.

The post’s core claims—that COVID-19 vaccines are “experimental,” that all vaccinated individuals will die within a specific timeframe, and that vaccines cause universal sterilization—require careful examination.

The term “experimental vaccine” is misleading. COVID-19 vaccines authorized and approved for use in the United States and many other countries underwent rigorous testing in clinical trials involving tens of thousands of participants. These trials evaluated the vaccines’ safety, efficacy, and potential side effects before authorization. Since their rollout, billions of doses have been administered worldwide, and regulatory agencies continue to monitor for adverse effects through established surveillance systems.

The assertion that all vaccinated individuals will die within 6 months to 5 years is not supported by scientific evidence. COVID-19 vaccines have been administered since December 2020, and there is no credible data showing widespread fatalities among the vaccinated population within the timelines stated. In fact, studies indicate that COVID-19 vaccines significantly reduce the risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death from the virus.

The claim that the vaccines cause sterilization and prevent individuals from having children is also unsubstantiated. Extensive research and ongoing surveillance have found no evidence that COVID-19 vaccines impact fertility in men or women. Professional organizations in obstetrics and gynecology recommend COVID-19 vaccination for people who are pregnant, trying to conceive, or may become pregnant in the future.

While it is important to scrutinize medical interventions and remain vigilant about potential side effects, the allegations made in the social media post are not backed by credible medical evidence or reputable expert opinion. Spreading such misinformation can contribute to vaccine hesitancy and undermine public health efforts.

In summary, the claims attributed to Dr. Sean Brooks regarding COVID-19 vaccines causing imminent death and universal sterilization are not supported by available scientific evidence, and his status as an internal medicine specialist is unverified. The overwhelming consensus among medical experts is that COVID-19 vaccines are safe, effective, and critical tools in managing the pandemic.

Vakcíny proti COVID-19, ktoré boli schválené a schválené na použitie v USA a mnohých ďalších krajinách, absolvovali sústavné testovanie v klinických skúškach s desiatkami tisíc účastníkov. Naopak, štúdie ukazujú, že vakcíny proti COVID-19 výrazne znížia riziko vážneho ochorenia, hospitalizácie a úmrtia z tohto ochorenia.

Tvrdenie, že vakcíny spôsobujú sterilizáciu a zabraňujú ľudom mať deti, je tiež nespravodlivé. Rozsiahle výskumy a trvalé sledovanie ukázali, že vakcíny proti COVID-19 nemajú vplyv na plodnosť mužov alebo žien. Profesionálne organizácie v oblasti gynekológie a porodníctva odporúčajú vakcináciu proti COVID-19 pre osoby, ktoré sú tehotné, plánujú tehotenstvo alebo môžu získať tehotenstvo v budúcnosti.

Išlo by o dôležité zvážiť medicínske intervencie a zvyšovať opatrnosť ohľadom potenciálnych vedľajších účinkov, ale tvrdenia, ktoré boli uvedené v sociálnom sietovom príspevku, nie sú podporované dôvernejšími lekárskymi dôkazmi alebo dôverenými odbornými názormi. Rozšírenie takéhoto nepravdivého informácií môže prispieť k vakcínovému odporu a oslabiť verejné zdravotnícky úsilie.

V závere, tvrdenia priraďované Dr. Sean Brooks ohľadom vakcíny proti COVID-19, ktoré spôsobujú nepríjemné úmrtie a univerzálnu sterilizáciu, nie sú podporované dostupnými vedeckými dôkazmi, a jeho status ako lekár vnútorného lekárstva nie je overený. Prevažná väčšina odborníkov sa dohodla, že vakcíny proti COVID-19 sú bezpečné, účinné a kľúčovým nástrojom pri správe pandémie.

A recent social media post has circulated widely, featuring a photo and a message claiming that pregnancy should not be planned for a period ranging from six months to two years after vaccination. The post does not specify which vaccine it refers to, nor does it provide any sources, scientific studies, or medical evidence to support this assertion. Given the significant public health implications and the emotional concerns around fertility, it is important to examine the validity of this claim and provide accurate information.

Vaccination and Fertility: The Claim  
The core claim of the post is that individuals should avoid planning pregnancies for an extended period—anywhere from six months to two years—after receiving a vaccine. While the post lacks specifics, such assertions have often been made in the context of COVID-19 vaccines, but similar rumors have circulated about other vaccines in the past.

Context and Background  
Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation about vaccines and fertility has proliferated on social media. Concerns ranged from claims that vaccines could cause infertility to warnings about delays in pregnancy planning. These messages often spread rapidly, fueled by anecdotal reports, misinterpretations of scientific data, and generalized vaccine hesitancy. Health authorities worldwide have consistently worked to counter such misinformation, emphasizing the safety and efficacy of vaccines for people who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

Fact-Checking the Claim  
Leading health organizations, including the World Health Organization and national health ministries, have thoroughly reviewed data on vaccines and fertility. There is no scientific evidence that vaccines—including COVID-19 vaccines—negatively affect fertility or require individuals to delay trying to conceive. Clinical trials and real-world data have not shown an increased risk of infertility or adverse pregnancy outcomes related to vaccination.

In the case of COVID-19 vaccines, specific guidance has been provided. Health authorities have stated that individuals do not need to avoid pregnancy after vaccination, and there is no need to delay conception for any period of time following vaccination. Similarly, for other common vaccines (such as those for influenza, measles, or rubella), recommendations may vary depending on the type of vaccine (live or inactivated), but a multi-year delay is not advised for any vaccine. When a brief waiting period is recommended, it is usually for live vaccines and is typically limited to a few weeks—not months or years.

Analysis  
The claim that pregnancy should be postponed for six months to two years after vaccination is not supported by scientific evidence. Such statements can cause unnecessary anxiety and may discourage people from receiving vaccines, potentially putting themselves and their future children at greater risk of preventable diseases. It is important to consult credible sources and medical professionals for guidance on vaccination and reproductive health.

Conclusion  
The social media post’s assertion that pregnancy should not be planned for six months to two years after vaccination is unfounded and lacks any supporting evidence. Health authorities affirm that vaccines are safe for people planning to conceive and that there is no need for extended delays in pregnancy after vaccination. Anyone with specific health concerns should consult their healthcare provider for personalized advice.

Hlavné tvrdenie príspevku je, že osoby by mali vyhnúť sa plánovaní tehotenstva po dlhú dobu – od šiestich mesiacov po dva roky – po získaní vakcíny. Aj keď príspevok neuvádza konkrétne informácie, takéto tvrdenia sa často objavujú v kontexte vakcíny proti COVID-19, ale podobné zvraty sa predstavovali aj o iných vakcínoch v minulosti.

Počas pandémie COVID-19 sa na sociálnych sieťach šírila nepravda o vakcínoch a plodnosti. Vedné organizácie, vrátane Organizácie Zdravotníckych Organizácií (WHO) a národných zdravotníckych ministerstiev, prehliadli dátumy týkajúce sa vakcíny a plodnosti. Klinické skúšobné a skutočné údaje neposkytli zvýšené riziko neplodnosti alebo nepriaznivých výsledkov tehotenstva spojených s očkováním.

V prípade vakcíny proti COVID-19 boli poskytnuté špecifické doporučenia. Zdravotnícki orgány uviedli, že osoby nemusia vyhnúť sa tehotenstvu po očkovaní a neexistuje potreba odložiť pokusy o získanie tehotenstva po žiadnom období. Ak sa odporúča krátky časový odstup, ide vždy o živé vakcíny a obvykle sa líši niekoľkými týždňami – nie mesiacmi ani rokmi.

Tvrdenie, že tehotenstvo by sa malo odložiť od šiestich mesiacov po dva roky po očkování, nie je podporované vedeckými údajmi. Záver  
Tvrdenie v sociálnych sieťach, že tehotenstvo by sa nemalo plánovať od šiestich mesiacov po dva roky po očkovanie, je nezákonné a nemá žiadne podporené dôkazy. Kto má konkrétne zdravotnícke obavy, by mal konsultovať svojho zdravotníckeho poskytovateľa pre individuálne rady.

A widely shared social media post has sparked concern by claiming that everyone who has received an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine should have their blood tested because the vaccine causes blood clots, allegedly leading to strokes and heart damage within two years. The post further advises vaccinated individuals to undergo body cleansing or detoxification, specifically recommending a 40-day water-only fast.

To assess these claims, it is important to review the available scientific evidence and guidance from medical authorities regarding mRNA vaccines, blood clots, and purported detoxification practices.

**Background on mRNA Vaccines**

The mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, such as those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, work by instructing cells to produce a harmless piece of the spike protein found on the virus, which trains the immune system to recognize and fight the virus if exposed in the future. Since their rollout, these vaccines have been administered to billions of people worldwide as part of global efforts to control the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Claim 1: mRNA Vaccines Cause Blood Clots Leading to Strokes and Heart Damage**

Concerns about blood clots associated with COVID-19 vaccines have been discussed since the vaccines became available. However, the vast majority of blood clotting events have been linked to adenovirus vector vaccines, such as AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson, not the mRNA vaccines.

For mRNA vaccines, reports of blood clotting events are extremely rare and not significantly higher than would be expected in the general population. The most common side effects of mRNA vaccines are mild and temporary, including soreness at the injection site, fatigue, and mild fever. Serious adverse events, such as myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle), have been reported in rare cases, typically in younger males, but these cases are also very rare and most individuals recover fully.

There is no credible scientific evidence to support the claim that mRNA vaccines cause widespread blood clots that would lead to strokes and heart damage years after vaccination. The vaccines have been subject to rigorous clinical trials and ongoing monitoring for adverse effects, and the consensus among medical professionals is that the benefits of vaccination far outweigh the risks for the vast majority of people.

**Claim 2: Testing Blood and ‘Detoxing’ After Vaccination**

Recommendations to test blood after vaccination are not supported by any major health organization. Routine blood tests are not required or recommended following mRNA vaccination, unless someone experiences specific symptoms that warrant medical evaluation.

The post’s suggestion of a 40-day water-only fast as a method of ‘detoxifying’ the body after vaccination is also not supported by scientific evidence. Extreme fasting can be dangerous, leading to dehydration, malnutrition, electrolyte imbalance, and serious health complications. The human body is equipped with organs like the liver and kidneys that naturally detoxify the blood and body; there is no proven need or benefit to extreme dietary interventions after vaccination.

**Conclusion**

The claims in the social media post are not supported by scientific evidence. There is no established link between mRNA vaccines and widespread blood clots that would lead to severe long-term health consequences, nor is there a need for blood testing or extreme fasting after vaccination. Health authorities continue to recommend COVID-19 vaccination as a safe and effective way to protect against severe illness. Anyone with concerns about side effects or health after vaccination should consult a qualified healthcare provider.

Social media has been abuzz with allegations that the reporting of participant numbers and injuries during anti-Covid measures protests in Australia has been manipulated or misrepresented by authorities and the media. These claims suggest that the true scale of public dissent, as well as the extent of confrontations with law enforcement, has been downplayed or distorted. To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to examine the context of the protests, the process by which information is reported, and the reliability of available data.

The protests in question took place in several Australian cities throughout 2020 and 2021, as the government imposed strict lockdowns and other measures to contain the spread of Covid-19. These policies, while credited with keeping case numbers relatively low, generated significant opposition from segments of the population who believed the restrictions infringed upon personal freedoms and livelihoods. As a result, mass demonstrations occurred in cities such as Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane, sometimes resulting in clashes with police.

When it comes to reporting the number of protest participants, discrepancies are common in large-scale public gatherings. Police estimates often differ from those provided by protest organizers, with the latter typically citing higher figures to emphasize support for their cause. Media outlets tend to report a range of numbers, sometimes relying on police data, aerial photography, or on-the-ground observations. This variance can lead to confusion or suspicion among the public, especially if there is a perception of bias.

Allegations of "playing with the numbers" are not unique to the Australian context; they are a frequent feature of contentious political events worldwide. In Australia, some protesters and commentators have accused both authorities and mainstream media of deliberately underestimating crowd sizes to delegitimize the movement against Covid measures. Conversely, authorities may argue that their figures are based on logistical assessments and public safety considerations.

Similar concerns arise regarding reports of injuries during the protests. Law enforcement agencies typically release statements detailing arrests and injuries among both police and demonstrators. However, these official reports may not capture the full extent of injuries, especially if individuals do not seek medical attention or if incidents are not witnessed by media or observers. Social media platforms have played a role in spreading unverified accounts and videos, which can sometimes exaggerate the frequency or severity of violence.

Fact-checking these claims reveals that while differences in reporting numbers and incidents are to be expected, there is no definitive evidence that data has been systematically falsified by authorities or the media. However, the lack of a standardized, transparent method for counting participants and injuries leaves room for public skepticism and allegations of misinformation. It is clear that both underestimation and overestimation of figures can occur depending on the source, and that all reported numbers should be approached with critical scrutiny.

In conclusion, while there are legitimate reasons to question the accuracy of crowd and injury numbers during the anti-Covid measures protests in Australia, the claim of deliberate manipulation—"fake news and playing with the numbers"—is difficult to substantiate without conclusive evidence. The best approach for the public is to consult multiple sources and remain aware of the inherent challenges in reporting on large, rapidly evolving events.
