Spletne omrežja so bila zasedena z trditi, da je poročanje o številu udeležencev in poškodb med protesti proti ukrepom proti koronavirusu v Avstraliji predstavljeno ali zmanjšano s strani uradov in medijev. Te trditve predpostavljajo, da je resnična obseg javnega nasprotovanja ter stopnja nasilja s policijo zmanjšan ali deformiran. Za oceno natančnosti teh trditev je pomembno raziskati kontekst protestov, proces poročanja in zanesljivost dostopne podatkov.

Protesti, o katerih je govorilo, so se odvijali v več avstralskih mestih v letih 2020 in 2021, ko je vlada vvedla stroge karantenske ukrepe in druge ukrepe za omejitev razširjanja koronavirusa. Ti ukrepi, čeprav so bili pripisani nizkih številk okuženih, so generirali veliko nasprotovanja med delom prebivalstva, ki so verjeli, da so omejitve vplivali na osebne svobode in življenjski standard. Zaradi tega so se pojavile masovne demonstracije v mestih kot so Melbourne, Sydney in Brisbane, včasih pa so se dogodili nasilni stikovi s policijo.

Ko gre za poročanje števil udeležencev, so razlike pogosto pogostih v večjih javnih sestankih. Policija pogosto daje različne ocene od tistih, ki jih ponujajo organizatorji protestov, kateri pogosto navedejo višje številke, da poudarijo podporo svojemu pristopu. Mediji običajno poročajo o številu udeležencev, pogosto se osredotočajo na podatke policije, zrakoplovno fotografijo ali terenske opazovanja. Ta variacija lahko povzroči zmedo ali sume med javnostjo, še posebej če obstaja percepcija naključnosti.

Trditve o "igri z številki" niso zlasti značilne samo za avstralski kontekst; so pogosto prisotne pri težkih političnih dogodkih po vsem svetu. V Avstraliji so nekateri protestniki in komentatorji obtožili uradov in glavnega medija, da namerno podcenjujejo številke skupin, da bi zmanjšali legitimnost pokreta proti ukrepom proti koronavirusu. Nasprotno, uradni osebi lahko trdijo, da so njihovi podatki temelječi na logističnih ocenah in varnostnih razmerah.

Podobne zadeve se pojavijo tudi glede poročanj o poškodbah med protesti. Policije običajno objavljajo izjave, ki opisujejo aretacije in poškodbe med policijo in demonstrantmi. Vendar pa te uradne poročila morda ne zaznamujejo celotnega obsega poškodb, še posebej če posamezniki ne potrebujejo zdravstvene pomoči ali če se dogodki ne zaznamujejo s strani medijev ali opazovalcev. Spletne omrežja so igrala vlogu razširjanja neverificiranih zapisov in videozapiskov, ki so včasih povečali frekvenco ali resnost nasilja.

Pregled trditev z izkušnje in raziskavami pokazuje, da razlike v poročanju števil in dogodkov so pričakovane, vendar ni zanesljivih dokazov, da so podatki sistematično lažno predstavljeni s strani uradov ali medijev. Vendar pa manjka standardiziran, transparenten način štetja udeležencev in poškodb, kar omogoča javni skepticizem in trditve o nepravilnem poročanju. Jasno je, da se lahko številke podcenjujejo ali preobčutijo glede na vir, in da morajo vse poročane številke biti podvržene kritičnemu pregledu.

Zaključek: medtem ko so obstajali zasluženi razlogi za vprašanje natančnosti števil udeležencev in poškodb med protesti proti ukrepom proti koronavirusu v Avstraliji, trditev o namerno manipulaciji – "falsifikacije in igri z številki" – je težko potrditi brez končnih dokazov. Najboljši pristop za javnost je, da se posvetuje več virov in ostane zaveden izjemno težavam pri poročanju na velikih, hitro spreminjajočih se dogodkih.

A video circulating on Facebook shows a woman, identified as a doctor, at a recent anti-Covid protest making several contentious claims about the coronavirus pandemic. In the video, she asserts that the coronavirus “does not exist and is just the flu,” and goes further to allege that the entire pandemic was fabricated due to PCR tests, which she claims “do not distinguish between influenza and Covid-19.”

These statements echo a series of widely debunked conspiracy theories and misunderstandings about both the nature of Covid-19 and the scientific methods used to detect it. This article examines the veracity of these claims and provides key background information to help clarify the facts.

**Claim 1: “The coronavirus does not exist and is just the flu.”**

Covid-19, caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, was first identified in late 2019 and has since been recognized by medical authorities worldwide, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The virus has been isolated, sequenced, and studied extensively in laboratories around the globe. Its genetic structure is distinct from influenza viruses, which cause the flu.

Covid-19 and influenza are both respiratory illnesses, but they are caused by entirely different viruses. While symptoms may overlap—such as fever, cough, and fatigue—Covid-19 has been found to cause more severe disease in some populations and has a different pattern of transmission and complications, including unique symptoms like loss of taste and smell.

Furthermore, excess mortality data and hospital records from around the world provide extensive evidence of the impact of Covid-19, which cannot be explained by influenza alone. The notion that “coronavirus does not exist” is not supported by scientific evidence or the global medical consensus.

**Claim 2: “The pandemic was caused by PCR tests that do not distinguish between influenza and Covid-19.”**

PCR (polymerase chain reaction) tests are a cornerstone of modern molecular biology and have been used for decades to detect genetic material from various pathogens, including viruses. The PCR tests designed for Covid-19 specifically target unique genetic sequences found only in SARS-CoV-2, making them highly specific for the coronavirus.

While false positives and negatives can occur with any diagnostic test, the design and validation of Covid-19 PCR tests include rigorous steps to ensure they do not react to influenza or other common respiratory viruses. Laboratories use control samples and sequence matching to rule out cross-reactivity. Influenza viruses have different genetic markers, and standard PCR protocols can distinguish between them and SARS-CoV-2.

It is inaccurate to claim that the pandemic was merely the result of misidentified flu cases. The scale of illness, patterns of transmission, and the international response—including the development of Covid-19-specific vaccines—reflect the recognition of a new and distinct viral threat.

**Conclusion**

The assertions made in the Facebook video—questioning the existence of the coronavirus and the accuracy of PCR testing—do not align with established scientific knowledge or the global experience of the pandemic. Covid-19 is a real and distinct disease, and PCR tests are designed to specifically detect it, not influenza. Misinformation of this nature can undermine public health efforts and spread unnecessary fear and confusion. It is crucial to rely on credible sources and scientific expertise when evaluating such claims.

Une vidéo circulant sur Facebook montre une femme, identifiée comme médecin, lors d'une manifestation récente contre le Covid-19, affirmant plusieurs déclarations contestables sur la pandémie du coronavirus. Dans cette vidéo, elle affirme que le coronavirus « n’existe pas et n’est qu’une grippe », et va même plus loin en accusant le fait que la pandémie entière ait été inventée à cause des tests PCR, qu'elle affirme « ne pas distinguer entre la grippe et le Covid-19 ».

Ces déclarations reflètent une série de théories du complot largement démenties et de malentendus concernant à la fois la nature du Covid-19 et les méthodes scientifiques utilisées pour le détecter. Cet article examine la véracité de ces affirmations et fournit un contexte clé pour clarifier les faits.

**Affirmation 1 : « Le coronavirus n’existe pas et n’est qu’une grippe. »**

Le Covid-19, causé par le nouveau coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, a été identifié pour la première fois fin 2019 et a depuis été reconnu par les autorités médicales mondiales, y compris l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) et le Centre pour le contrôle et la prévention des maladies (CDC). Ce virus a été isolé, séquencé et étudié de manière approfondie dans des laboratoires à travers le monde. Sa structure génétique est distincte de celle des virus de la grippe, qui provoquent la grippe.

Le Covid-19 et la grippe sont tous deux des maladies respiratoires, mais ils sont causés par des virus entièrement différents. Bien que les symptômes puissent se chevaucher – tels que la fièvre, la toux et la fatigue – le Covid-19 a été constaté provoquer des formes plus graves de maladie chez certaines populations, et présente un mode de transmission et des complications différents, notamment des symptômes uniques comme la perte de l'odorat et du goût.

De plus, les données sur la mortalité excédentaire et les dossiers hospitaliers à travers le monde fournissent une preuve abondante de l'impact du Covid-19, qui ne peut être expliqué uniquement par la grippe. L'idée que « le coronavirus n’existe pas » n'est pas appuyée par des preuves scientifiques ou par le consensus médical mondial.

**Affirmation 2 : « La pandémie a été causée par les tests PCR qui ne distinguent pas entre la grippe et le Covid-19. »**

Les tests PCR (réaction en chaîne du polymérase) sont un pilier de la biologie moléculaire moderne et ont été utilisés pendant des décennies pour détecter l'ADN ou l'ARN de divers pathogènes, y compris les virus. Les tests PCR conçus pour le Covid-19 ciblent spécifiquement des séquences génétiques uniques présentes uniquement dans le SARS-CoV-2, ce qui les rend hautement spécifiques pour le coronavirus.

Bien que des faux positifs et faux négatifs puissent survenir avec n'importe quel test diagnostique, la conception et la validation des tests PCR pour le Covid-19 incluent des étapes rigoureuses pour s'assurer qu'ils ne réagissent pas à la grippe ou à d'autres virus respiratoires courants. Les laboratoires utilisent des échantillons de contrôle et des correspondances de séquences pour éliminer toute réactivité croisée. Les virus de la grippe possèdent des marqueurs génétiques différents, et les protocoles PCR standard peuvent les distinguer du SARS-CoV-2.

Il est inexact de prétendre que la pandémie résulte uniquement de cas de grippe mal identifiés. L'échelle de la maladie, les schémas de transmission et la réponse internationale – y compris le développement de vaccins spécifiques au Covid-19 – reflètent la reconnaissance d'une menace virale nouvelle et distincte.

**Conclusion**

Les affirmations faites dans la vidéo de Facebook – remettant en question l'existence du coronavirus et la fiabilité des tests PCR – ne correspondent pas à la connaissance scientifique établie ni à l'expérience mondiale de la pandémie. Le Covid-19 est une maladie réelle et distincte, et les tests PCR sont conçus pour le détecter spécifiquement, pas la grippe. Une telle désinformation peut affaiblir les efforts de santé publique et propager une peur et une confusion inutiles. Il est crucial de se fier à des sources fiables et à l'expertise scientifique lors de l'évaluation de telles affirmations.

On August 22, a Sunday and officially a non-working day, social media saw the circulation of photos apparently taken at the "Mother Teresa" complex of clinics. The images depict an empty ambulance parking lot and a seemingly deserted area in front of the Covid-19 section of the clinics. Accompanying the photos, the post alleges that the absence of ambulances and visible activity is evidence the Covid-19 pandemic is a government sham.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is crucial to examine both the content of the post and relevant contextual factors.

First, the "Mother Teresa" complex of clinics is among the largest healthcare facilities in the country, serving thousands of patients annually. Like most hospitals, it operates with varying levels of visible activity depending on the day and time. August 22, 2021, fell on a Sunday—a day traditionally associated with reduced staffing, fewer scheduled appointments, and minimal elective procedures. Many administrative and outpatient services also observe limited hours on weekends.

The photos in question show a lack of ambulances and people in the parking areas near the Covid-19 section. However, there are several plausible explanations for this scenario that do not support the conclusion that Covid-19 is a government-created sham. Ambulances are dispatched to emergencies and may not be stationed at the hospital at all times; their absence in the parking lot does not necessarily indicate a lack of patients or emergencies, but rather that vehicles may be out on calls or parked elsewhere. Additionally, the Covid-19 ward itself is a restricted area, with protocols limiting patient movement and non-essential personnel access for infection control. The absence of crowds or visible activity is consistent with these safety measures.

Furthermore, Covid-19 patient surges tend to fluctuate based on public health conditions. While some periods see high numbers of hospitalizations, others are marked by lower patient counts, especially if public health measures are effective or if infection rates temporarily decrease. A snapshot of one area on a single day cannot capture the overall impact of the pandemic or the workload experienced by healthcare staff over time.

The claim that the pandemic is a government sham based solely on images of an empty parking lot is not supported by the broader context. Covid-19 has been documented globally, with millions of confirmed cases and deaths. The clinical staff at "Mother Teresa" and other hospitals have repeatedly reported overwhelming workloads during surges, and numerous patients have described their experiences receiving treatment for the virus.

In conclusion, while the photos do show a quiet scene at the clinic on a Sunday, this is not evidence that the pandemic is fabricated. The lack of ambulances and people is consistent with typical weekend operations and infection control protocols. Fact-checking the claim reveals it is based on a misinterpretation of limited visual evidence, ignoring the complexities of hospital operations and the documented reality of Covid-19’s impact on healthcare systems and society as a whole.

Mnoho administratívnych a ambulatívnych služieb má obmedzené hodiny v sobotu a nedelu.

Základným problémom sú fotografe, ktoré ukazujú nedostatok ambulancií a ľudí v parkovacích miestach v blízkosti oddelenia na COVID-19. Však existujú niekoľko pravdepodobných vysvetlení pre tento scenár, ktoré neukazujú, že pandémia na COVID-19 je vládny podvod. Ambulancie sú posielané na nouzové prípady a nemusia byť stacionované v nemocnici vždy; ich chýba v parkovacích miestach nemusí znamenať nedostatok pacientov alebo nouzových prípadov, ale skôr, že vozidlá môžu byť výrazne výslužbe alebo parkované iného miesta. Navyše, samotné oddelenie na COVID-19 je obmedzené oblasti, kde sú protokoly, ktoré obmedzujú pohyb pacientov a nevyžadovaného personálu pre kontrolovanie infekcie. Nedostatok ľudí alebo viditeľnej aktivity je v súlade s týmito bezpečnostnými opatreniami.

Krom toho, výskyt pacientov na COVID-19 sa môže meniť v závislosti od zdravotníckych podmienok. Niektoré obdobia sú spojené s vysokým počtom hospitalizácií, iné s nižším počtom pacientov, najmä ak sú účinné zdravotnícky opatrenia alebo ak sa infekčné rýchlosti dočasne znížia. Náhľad jedného miesta na jeden deň nemôže zachytiť celkový vplyv pandémie alebo záťaž, ktorú zdravotnícke zariadenia zažili počas času.

Tvrdenie, že pandémia na COVID-19 je vládny podvod, založené výhradne na obrazoch prázdneho parkovacieho miesta, nie je podporované širším kontextom. Pandémia na COVID-19 bola dokumentovaná na celom svete s miliónmi potvrdených prípadov a úmrtí. Klinický personál v komplexi klinik „Mater Teresa“ a iných nemocniciach opakované zaznamenali prehrozene vysoké záťaže počas vrcholov, a mnoho pacientov popisuje svoje skúsenosti s liečbou tohto vírusu.

Záverom, aj keď fotografie ukazujú ticho na nemocnici v nedele, to nie je dôkaz, že pandémia je falošná. Nedostatok ambulancií a ľudí je v súlade s typickými výkonmi v sobotu a protokolmi na kontrolovanie infekcií. Overenie tohto tvrdenia ukazuje, že je založené na chybnom výklade obmedzeného vizuálneho dôkazu, ignoruje komplexnosť výkonov nemocníc a dokumentovanú realitu vplyvu pandémie na zdravotnícke systémy a spoločnosť ako celok.

A recent video circulating on Facebook, reportedly from an anti-vaccine protest in Skopje, North Macedonia, has reignited debates around the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccination campaigns. In the video, demonstrators can be heard claiming that the coronavirus does not exist and that vaccines are part of a global scheme to microchip and monitor the population.

The video’s core claims—that COVID-19 is a fabrication and that vaccines are being used for population surveillance—are not new. Such narratives have been present since the beginning of the pandemic and have found renewed momentum in online communities skeptical of government and scientific authorities. Understanding the roots and veracity of these assertions is crucial for public health and informed discourse.

First, the claim that the coronavirus does not exist is contradicted by overwhelming scientific and medical evidence. COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, was first identified in late 2019 and has since led to millions of deaths and significant social and economic disruption worldwide. The genetic sequence of the virus has been mapped by researchers globally, and the existence of COVID-19 is confirmed through diagnostic tests, epidemiological data, and clinical observation in hospitals. Health agencies and independent researchers have documented the spread, symptoms, and impact of the virus across diverse populations.

The assertion that vaccines are being used to microchip the population is a conspiracy theory that has been widely debunked by health experts and technologists. COVID-19 vaccines—including mRNA vaccines and viral vector vaccines—underwent rigorous clinical trials before being approved for emergency use. The ingredients of these vaccines are publicly available and do not include microchips or any form of tracking technology. The logistics of inserting a microchip undetectably through a standard vaccine needle are not supported by current technological capabilities. Furthermore, regulatory agencies closely monitor vaccine safety and composition.

The persistence of such conspiracy theories can be attributed to a mixture of distrust in institutions, the rapid spread of misinformation on social media, and the anxiety caused by a global health crisis. In North Macedonia, as in many countries, public protests have become a venue for expressing skepticism about official narratives, often fueled by viral videos and posts that lack scientific grounding.

Public health experts warn that misinformation about COVID-19 and vaccines undermines efforts to control the pandemic. Vaccine hesitancy, driven by unfounded fears, has been identified as a significant barrier to achieving widespread immunity and ending the public health emergency. Authorities urge citizens to seek information from reliable sources and consult healthcare professionals regarding the safety and efficacy of vaccines.

In summary, the claims made in the Facebook video from the Skopje protest—that coronavirus does not exist and that vaccines are tools for microchipping and monitoring—are not supported by scientific evidence. Such misinformation poses risks to public health and highlights the need for responsible communication and critical evaluation of sources, especially in times of crisis.

A recent social media post has raised concerns about COVID-19 vaccines, asking: “How can we, the unvaccinated, protect ourselves and not get infected by the vaccinated? We know that everyone who is vaccinated is infected by the vaccines!” This post reflects persistent myths and misunderstandings about COVID-19 vaccines, their safety, and their effects. Here, we break down the claims and provide evidence-based analysis.

**Claim 1: The vaccinated pose an infection risk to the unvaccinated**

The primary question in the post suggests that vaccinated individuals may spread COVID-19 to unvaccinated individuals, potentially implying that vaccination itself causes a person to become infectious. In reality, the vaccines authorized and used worldwide for COVID-19 do not contain live virus in a form that can cause COVID-19. The most widely used vaccines (such as mRNA vaccines and non-replicating viral vector vaccines) teach the body’s immune system to recognize and fight the virus without introducing the whole, live virus.

Vaccinated individuals are not “infected” by the vaccine. Rather, their immune systems are trained to defend against the actual virus if it is encountered in the future. After vaccination, people do not shed live virus nor do they pose a risk of infecting others simply because they have been vaccinated. The only way a vaccinated person could transmit the virus is if they become infected with COVID-19 itself, which can still occur, though at reduced rates and with typically milder symptoms compared to unvaccinated individuals.

**Claim 2: Everyone who is vaccinated is “infected by the vaccines”**

This statement is scientifically inaccurate. Infection refers to the invasion and multiplication of a pathogen such as a virus or bacteria. COVID-19 vaccines do not contain live SARS-CoV-2 virus and cannot cause infection with COVID-19. The mRNA and vector-based vaccines use genetic instructions to teach the body to recognize the spike protein found on the coronavirus, but these components do not replicate or cause disease.

It is possible for vaccinated individuals to experience side effects such as fever, fatigue, or muscle aches. These are signs of the immune system responding—not evidence of infection. The confusion may arise from misinformation or misunderstanding of the biological processes involved in vaccination.

**Protecting the unvaccinated**

The best way for unvaccinated individuals to protect themselves is to follow public health guidance: maintain good hand hygiene, wear masks in crowded or indoor settings, and practice physical distancing, especially when community transmission is high. Vaccination remains the most effective tool to prevent severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19.

**Conclusion**

The claims in the social media post are not supported by scientific evidence. Vaccinated individuals do not become infected with COVID-19 from the vaccines, nor do they become a source of infection to others due to vaccination. The risk of infection comes from exposure to people who are actively infected with COVID-19, regardless of their vaccination status, although the likelihood and severity of illness is lower among the vaccinated. The spread of misinformation can hinder efforts to control the pandemic and protect public health.

A recent social media post claims that drinking baking soda and one fruit daily for seven days can prevent viruses. This assertion, while appealing for its simplicity and natural approach, requires careful examination to determine its validity and safety. With increasing interest in home remedies and alternative health practices, it's important for the public to understand what is and isn’t supported by scientific evidence.

The post’s core message is straightforward: consuming a beverage made with baking soda and fruit for a week will prevent viral infections. This idea seems to draw on two popular notions—that baking soda can “alkalize” the body and that fruit provides immune-boosting nutrients. However, the science behind these concepts is more nuanced.

Baking soda, or sodium bicarbonate, is commonly used as an antacid to relieve heartburn and indigestion. It works by neutralizing stomach acid, but its effects are temporary and localized to the digestive system. Some alternative health advocates believe that increasing the body’s alkalinity can ward off diseases, including viral infections. However, medical experts agree that the body tightly regulates its pH levels, and dietary intake has minimal impact on overall blood pH. Excessive consumption of baking soda can lead to serious health risks such as metabolic alkalosis, electrolyte imbalance, and high blood pressure due to its sodium content.

The mention of adding “one fruit” daily likely refers to the general health advice of consuming fruits for their vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Fruits like oranges, berries, and kiwis are rich in vitamin C, which supports immune function. While adequate intake of vitamins from fruits is beneficial for overall health and immune response, eating fruit alone cannot prevent viral infections. No single fruit or seven-day regimen can act as a shield against viruses such as the common cold, influenza, or COVID-19.

Prevention of viral infections relies on proven strategies: vaccination, regular handwashing, avoiding close contact with sick individuals, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle that supports the immune system. While diet plays a role in supporting immune health, there is no evidence that baking soda, alone or in combination with fruit, can prevent viruses or offer protection if consumed for a week.

The viral post does not specify which viruses are being targeted, nor does it provide any scientific rationale or clinical evidence for its claim. Additionally, drinking baking soda regularly—especially in large amounts—can be dangerous and is not recommended by health authorities.

In summary, the claim that drinking baking soda and one fruit daily for seven days can prevent viruses is not supported by medical science. While fruit consumption is a healthy habit, baking soda should only be used for its intended purposes and under guidance from a healthcare provider. Viral prevention is best achieved through established public health measures and a balanced diet, rather than unproven remedies circulating online.

یک پست اخیر در شبکه‌های اجتماعی ادعا می‌کند که نوشیدن یک چای میکس شده از سدیم بیکربنات و یک میوه به مدت هفت روز می‌تواند ویروس‌ها را جلوگیری کند. این ادعا، با اینکه به دلیل سادگی و رویکرد طبیعی خود جذاب است، نیاز به بررسی دقیقی دارد تا اثربخشی و امنیت آن را تعیین کنیم. با افزایش علاقه عمومی به روش‌های محلی درمان و روش‌های دیگری برای سلامتی، مهم است که عموم مردم بدانند چه چیزی به واقع توسط داده‌های علمی پشتیبانی می‌شود و چه نه.

محتوای اصلی این پست به این صورت است: نوشیدن یک نوشیدنی با سدیم بیکربنات و میوه به مدت هفت روز می‌تواند عفونت‌های ویروسی را جلوگیری کند. این ایده به نظر می‌رسد که از دو مفهوم محبوب استفاده می‌کند: اینکه سدیم بیکربنات می‌تواند بدن را "کلیه‌تر" کند و اینکه میوه‌ها مواد مغذیی هستند که به تقویت ایمنی کمک می‌کنند. با این حال، علم پشت این مفاهیم پیچیده‌تر است.

سدیم بیکربنات یا سدیم بیکربنات به طور معمول به عنوان یک ضد اسید استفاده می‌شود تا از قرچک و ناپایداری گوارش جلوگیری کند. این مواد کار می‌کنند که اسید معده را متعادل می‌کنند، اما اثرات آن موقتی و محدود به سیستم گوارش است. برخی از پروپانسیون‌های سلامتی گزینه‌های دیگر معتقدند که افزایش کلیه‌تی بدن می‌تواند از بیماری‌ها، از جمله عفونت‌های ویروسی، جلوگیری کند. با این حال، متخصصان پزشکی موافقت می‌کنند که بدن به طور چشم‌بندی سطح pH خود را تنظیم می‌کند و مصرف غذایی تأثیر کمی بر pH خون کلی دارد. مصرف زیاد سدیم بیکربنات می‌تواند خطرات جدی سلامتی مانند آلکالوز متابولیک، اختلالات الکترولیتی و فشار خون بالا به دلیل محتوای نatrium آن ایجاد کند.

اشاره به افزودن "یک میوه" در روز احتمالاً به توصیه عمومی مصرف میوه‌ها برای اینکه آن‌ها به ویتامین، معدنی و آنتی اکسیدان‌های مفید است اشاره دارد. میوه‌هایی مانند لیمو، میوه‌های قرمز و موز پر از ویتامین C هستند که به عملکرد ایمنی کمک می‌کنند. در حالی که مصرف کافی ویتامین از میوه‌ها برای سلامتی کلی و پاسخ ایمنی مفید است، مصرف میوه به تنهایی نمی‌تواند عفونت‌های ویروسی را جلوگیری کند. هیچ یک از میوه‌های یکسان یا رژیم هفت روزه نمی‌تواند به عنوان یک حفاظت در برابر ویروس‌هایی مانند سرماخوردگی، گریپ یا کووید 19 عمل کند.

جلوگیری از عفونت‌های ویروسی به روش‌های ثابت احیا می‌شود: واکسیناسیون، شستشوی دست‌ها، اجتناب از تماس نزدیک با افراد بیمار و حفظ یک رژیم سالم که به سیستم ایمنی کمک می‌کند. در حالی که رژیم غذایی به تقویت سلامت ایمنی می‌پردازد، هیچ داده‌ای وجود ندارد که نشان دهد سدیم بیکربنات به تنهایی یا با میوه، می‌تواند ویروس‌ها را جلوگیری کند یا در صورت مصرف به مدت هفت روز حفاظت ایمنی ارائه دهد.

این پست ویروسی نه به ویروس‌هایی که هدف قرار داده است اشاره می‌کند، نه هیچ توجیه علمی یا داده کلینیکی برای ادعای خود ارائه می‌دهد. علاوه بر این، مصرف منظم سدیم بیکربنات، به ویژه در مقادیر زیاد، خطراتی دارد و توسط مقامات سلامت توصیه نمی‌شود.

به طور خلاصه، ادعا که مصرف سدیم بیکربنات و یک میوه در روز به مدت هفت روز می‌تواند عفونت‌های ویروسی را جلوگیری کند، توسط علم پزشکی پشتیبانی نمی‌شود. در حالی که مصرف میوه یک عادت سالم است، سدیم بیکربنات فقط برای مقاصد مورد نظر خود و تحت نظارت پزشک می‌تواند استفاده شود. جلوگیری از عفونت ویروسی بهترین راه از طریق اقدامات بهداشت عمومی ثابت و رژیم غذایی تعادلی به جای روش‌های غیرآزمایشی که در اینترنت پخش می‌شوند است.

A recent social media post has made alarming claims about medical professionals, asserting that “Doctors are Masons and they perform rituals and mass murders of patients! That's why they die, and not Covid.” This statement raises serious concerns, both due to its accusations against the medical community and its implications about the causes of death during the Covid-19 pandemic. In this article, we break down the core claims, provide factual context, and analyze the evidence.

**Understanding the Claims**

The post makes two core allegations: 
1. That doctors, as a group, are members of the Freemasons—a centuries-old fraternal organization often shrouded in conspiracy theories—and perform secret rituals.
2. That doctors are responsible for the deaths of patients, particularly during the Covid-19 pandemic, suggesting intentional harm or “mass murders,” rather than deaths being caused by the virus itself.

**Background: Freemasonry and the Medical Profession**

Freemasonry is a fraternal organization that traces its roots to the local fraternities of stonemasons. While some doctors, like individuals in any profession, may be Freemasons, there is no evidence to support the claim that all or most doctors are Masons, or that the medical profession is linked to this organization in a systemic way. Freemasonry is not inherently secretive, nor is it associated with criminal or ritualistic behavior, despite persistent conspiracy theories.

**Medical Practice, Ethics, and Oversight**

The suggestion that doctors, as a group, perform “rituals” or engage in “mass murders” is not supported by any credible evidence. Medical professionals are regulated by strict ethical codes, licensing bodies, and oversight mechanisms designed to protect patient safety. Hospitals and clinics operate under local, national, and often international standards of care. Individual doctors found guilty of malpractice or criminal behavior are subject to disciplinary action, loss of license, and legal prosecution.

**Covid-19 and Patient Mortality**

The post implies that patient deaths, particularly during the Covid-19 pandemic, are due to doctors’ actions rather than the virus itself. However, the global Covid-19 pandemic has been extensively documented by scientists, public health agencies, and governments around the world. The primary cause of death among Covid-19 patients has been the virus and its complications, as confirmed by medical records, autopsies, and epidemiological studies. While there have been isolated cases of medical error or mismanagement, these are rare and not indicative of any widespread conspiracy or intentional harm.

**The Dangers of Misinformation**

Such posts contribute to misinformation and can undermine public trust in healthcare professionals. During a global health crisis, this kind of narrative can discourage people from seeking care, following public health guidance, or accepting vaccines and treatments. It is important to rely on verified information from reputable sources when assessing claims about medical care and the pandemic.

**Conclusion**

The claim that doctors are Masons who perform rituals and “mass murders” of patients, rather than deaths being caused by Covid-19, is not supported by facts. There is no credible evidence linking the medical profession to Freemasonry in any conspiratorial sense, nor is there evidence to suggest that doctors are intentionally causing patient deaths. Most deaths during the pandemic have been due to the virus itself, and healthcare professionals have played a vital role in treating and saving lives.

الصوفية هي منظمة تعاونية تعود أصولها إلى الجمعيات المحلية للمasons (الصُّناع). على الرغم من أن بعض الأطباء، مثل الأفراد في أي مهنة أخرى، قد يكونون من الصوفية، إلا أنه لا يوجد دليل يدعم الادعاء بأن كل أو معظم الأطباء من الصوفيين، أو أن المهنة الطبية مرتبطة بهذه المنظمة بطريقة نظامية. الصوفية ليست في الأصل سرية، ولا ترتبط بأي سلوك جنائي أو سريري، رغم أن نظريات المؤامرة تستمر في انتشارها.

**ممارسة الطب، الأخلاقيات، والرقابة**

الادعاء بأن الأطباء كمجموعة يمارسون "شعائر" أو يرتكبون "قتل جماعي" لا يدعمه أي دليل موثق. يُنظم المهنيون الطبيون بقوانين أخلاقية صارمة، وأجهزة رقابة، وآليات مراقبة مصممة لحماية سلامة المرضى. تعمل المستشفيات والعيادات تحت معايير رعاية محلية ووطنية، وأحيانًا دولية. يتم إجراء إجراءات إجرائية ضد الأطباء الذين يُعاقبون على سوء السلوك أو السلوك الجنائي، وتُفقد ترخيصهم، ويعتقلون قانونيًا.

**كوفيد-19 ومعدل الوفيات**

تشير المشاركة إلى أن وفات المرضى، وخاصة خلال جائحة كوفيد-19، ناتجة عن أفعال الأطباء وليس عن الفيروس نفسه. ومع ذلك، تم تسجيل جائحة كوفيد-19 بشكل واسع من قبل العلماء ووكالات الصحة العامة والحكومات في جميع أنحاء العالم. السبب الرئيسي لوفاة المرضى الذين عانوا من كوفيد-19 هو الفيروس ومضاعفاته، كما أثبتته السجلات الطبية، والتحاليل المصلحية، والدراسات الوبائية. على الرغم من وجود حالات من أخطاء طبية أو إدارية منفصلة، إلا أن هذه الحالات نادرة ولا تعكس أي مؤامرة واسعة النطاق أو ضرر متعمد.

**خطورة المعلومات الزائفة**

هذه المشاركات تساهم في انتشار المعلومات الزائفة وتحلل الثقة العامة في المهنيين الطبيين. خلال أزمة صحية عالمية، يمكن أن تؤدي هذه الأفكار إلى تقليل حث المواطنين على طلب العلاج، أو الالتزام بتعليمات الصحة العامة، أو قبول التطعيمات والعلاجات. من المهم الاعتماد على المعلومات الموثقة من مصادر موثوقة عند تقييم الادعاءات المتعلقة بالرعاية الطبية والوباء.

**الخاتمة**

الادعاء بأن الأطباء هم صوفيين يقومون بشعائر و"قتل جماعي" للمرضى، بدلًا من أن الوفاة ناتجة عن كوفيد-19، لا يدعمه أي حقائق. لا يوجد دليل موثق يربط المهنة الطبية بالصوفية من حيث المؤامرة، ولا يوجد دليل يشير إلى أن الأطباء يقومون بقتل المرضى عن قصد. معظم الوفيات خلال الجائحة كانت بسبب الفيروس نفسه، وساهم المهنيون الطبيون بشكل كبير في علاج المرضى وإنقاذ حياتهم.

A recent social media post has raised concerns about the use of digital thermometers, particularly those that measure temperature from the forehead. The post alleges that these devices are deliberately used to target the pineal gland, described as a "chakra" and a "center for communication with higher realms," and suggests that there is a hidden agenda, especially when it comes to children.

To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to first understand how forehead thermometers work, what the pineal gland is, and whether there is any scientific evidence supporting the assertion that using such thermometers affects the pineal gland or spiritual communication.

Digital forehead thermometers, also known as infrared thermometers, have become increasingly common, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, as a non-contact method to screen for fever. These devices use infrared technology to detect the surface temperature of the skin on the forehead. The process is quick, harmless, and does not involve any physical penetration or "drilling" into the skin or underlying structures. It is widely used in medical settings, schools, and public places due to its safety and efficiency.

The pineal gland is a small endocrine gland located deep within the brain, roughly at the center of the head. It is responsible for the production of melatonin, a hormone that regulates sleep-wake cycles. The location of the pineal gland is not immediately beneath the forehead; it sits near the center of the brain, well-protected by bone and tissue. The notion that an external thermometer on the forehead could physically affect the pineal gland is not supported by anatomical evidence.

Some spiritual and esoteric traditions refer to the pineal gland as the "third eye" or associate it with a chakra believed to be involved in psychic or spiritual experiences. However, these interpretations are not recognized by mainstream science or medicine, and there is no empirical evidence that the pineal gland serves as a literal communication center with "higher realms."

The claim that forehead thermometers are specifically designed to "drill" into the pineal gland, especially in children, is unfounded. The measurement of body temperature via the forehead is based on convenience and practicality, as the area is easily accessible and provides a reliable estimation of core body temperature. The process involves detecting infrared radiation emitted from the skin and does not emit any form of energy capable of penetrating the skull or influencing internal organs or glands.

In conclusion, the assertion that digital forehead thermometers are used to target the pineal gland or interfere with spiritual communication lacks scientific basis. The devices are safe for all ages, including children, and are not capable of affecting brain structures or chakras. Concerns about their use are not supported by current medical knowledge or practice.

A social media post circulating widely claims that the COVID-19 pandemic was manufactured as part of a conspiracy to destroy small businesses and the economy, making people dependent on government aid. The post further alleges that doctors who speak out publicly are bribed to promote false narratives, while those who attempt to expose so-called fraud are censored on social networks. According to this theory, the ultimate aim is to make citizens more easily controlled by governments, who can then implement unpopular policies under the guise of emergency measures.

To assess the validity of these claims, it is important to examine each element of the post in detail.

The suggestion that the pandemic was “created” as part of a deliberate plan to harm the economy and small businesses does not align with the consensus among global health experts. COVID-19 was declared a pandemic by the World Health Organization in March 2020, following the rapid worldwide spread of a novel coronavirus. There is no credible evidence supporting the idea that the virus was intentionally released or that the pandemic was staged for political or economic purposes. Most scientific investigations point to a natural origin for the virus, and the massive disruptions to healthcare systems, economies, and societies worldwide have affected nearly all countries, governments, and populations, making a coordinated global conspiracy highly implausible.

The claim that doctors who speak publicly are bribed, and that dissenting voices are systematically censored, is also not supported by available evidence. While there have been instances of misinformation being removed from social media platforms, these actions have typically targeted content that spreads demonstrably false information about COVID-19 treatments, vaccines, or the severity of the disease. Many doctors, scientists, and healthcare workers have voiced a wide range of opinions about pandemic management, with robust debates taking place in scientific journals, the media, and online. There is no verifiable proof of a coordinated campaign to bribe doctors for supporting official narratives. However, social media companies have implemented policies to limit the spread of misinformation, particularly when it poses a risk to public health.

Regarding the economic impact, it is true that the pandemic and resulting public health measures—such as lockdowns and restrictions—have disproportionately affected small businesses and certain sectors. Governments around the world introduced various forms of financial aid to support individuals and enterprises during closures. While increased dependence on government support has been a consequence for some, there is no evidence that this was the intended purpose of pandemic policies. Most government actions aimed to balance public health needs with economic considerations, and many countries have since implemented measures to help businesses recover and reopen.

The assertion that governments are using pandemic-induced dependence to force through unpopular decisions is speculative and not substantiated by concrete examples. In democratic societies, major policy changes continue to be subject to public debate, legislative processes, and, in many cases, judicial review.

In summary, the claims made in the social media post reflect a conspiracy theory that lacks credible evidence. While the pandemic has undeniably caused economic hardship and prompted an increase in state intervention, there is no substantiated link to a deliberate plot to create dependency or suppress dissenting medical voices. Fact-checking and public scrutiny remain essential, but extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, which is not present in this case.

Učestvuje široko širena društvena mreža koja tvrdi da je pandemija COVID-19 stvorena kao deo konspiracije da bi se uništila malo poslovanje i ekonomija, što bi povećalo zavisnost ljudi od državnog pomoći. Poruka dodatno tvrdi da su liječnici koji javno govore isplati oni koji promoviraju lažne priče, dok oni koji pokušavaju otkriti pretpostavljeno podmetanje cenzurirani su na društvenim mrežama. Prema ovoj teoriji, cilj je povećati kontrolu nad građanima, pa bi države mogli implementirati nepopularne politike pod okriljem hitnih mjera.

Da bi se procijenila valjanost ovih tvrdnji, važno je detaljno analizirati svaku komponentu poruke.

Predlog da je pandemija „stvorena“ kao deo zamišljenog plana za štetu ekonomiji i malim poslovima ne odgovara konsenzusu među globalnim zdravstvenim stručnjacima. Pandemija je proglasila Svetovna zdravstvena organizacija u martu 2020. godine, nakon brzog širenja nove koronavirusa širom svijeta. Nema pouzdanih dokaza koji podržavaju ideju da je virus namjerno oslobodjen ili da je pandemija organizirana za političke ili ekonomske svrhe. Većina znanstvenih istraživanja ukazuje na prirodni porijeklom virusa, a ogromne prekide u zdravstvenim sustavima, ekonomijama i društvenim strukturama širom svijeta uključile su gotovo sve zemlje, vlade i populacije, što čini koordinirano globalno konspiraciju izuzetno nevjerojatnom.

Tvrdnja da su liječnici koji javno govore isplati, a da se nezavisne glasove sistematski cenzuriraju, također nema podršku dostupnim dokazima. Iako su postojale primjere uklanjanja nepravilnih informacija s društvenih mreža, ti podaci su tipično ciljali sadržaj koji širi očito lažne informacije o liječenju, vakcinama ili ozbiljnosti bolesti. Mnogi liječnici, znanstvenici i zdravstveni radnici su iznosili široku pažnju o upravljanju pandemijom, s jakim raspravama u znanstvenim časopisima, medijima i online. Nema potvrđenih dokaza o koordiniranoj kampanji za kupovinu liječnika da bi podržavali službene priče. Međutim, društvene mreže su implementirale politike za ograničavanje širenja lažnih informacija, posebno kada predstavljaju opasnost za javno zdravlje.

U vezi s ekonomskim uticajem, istina je da pandemija i slijedeće javno zdravstvene mjere, poput zatvaranja i ograničenja, nisu imala jednake učinke na malo poslovanje i određene sektore. Vlade širom svijeta uvedele različite oblike financijske pomoći za podršku pojedincima i preduzećima tokom zatvaranja. Iako je povećana zavisnost od državne podrške bila posljedica za neke, nema dokaza da je to bila namjena pandemije politika. Većina vlada djelovala je kako bi izbalansirala potrebe javnog zdravlja i ekonomskih razmatranja, a mnoge zemlje su nakon toga implementirale mjere za pomoć preduzećima da se oporave i ponovno otvore.

Uvjet da vlade koriste zavisnost izazvanu pandemijom za prisilno provođenje nepopularnih odluka je spekulativna i nema konkretnih primjera. U demokratskim društvima, značajne političke promjene nastavljaju biti podložne javnoj raspravi, zakonskom postupku i, u mnogim slučajevima, sudskom pregledu.

Uzimanje u obzir, tvrdnje iz društvene mreže odražavaju konspirativnu teoriju koja nema pouzdanih dokaza. Iako pandemija sigurno izazvala ekonomski teškoća i dovela do povećanja državne intervencije, nema potvrđenog povezivanja s namjernim planom za stvaranje zavisnosti ili potiskivanje nezavisnih medicinskih glasova. Provjera istinitosti i javna kontrola ostaju esencijalne, ali izuzetno tvrdi zahtijevaju izuzetne dokaze, što nije prisutno u ovom slučaju.

A recent social media post has been circulating widely, claiming that in Australia, "every child tested positive will be forcibly taken away from their parents," and warning that similar measures could be implemented elsewhere if not opposed. This statement has caused concern and alarm among parents and the broader public. A careful examination of the claim, the context in which it arose, and the actual policies implemented in Australia reveals a much more nuanced picture.

The claim appears to reference Australia’s COVID-19 pandemic response, particularly the procedures in place during periods of high infection rates in 2020 and 2021. Australia, especially states like Victoria and New South Wales, implemented some of the world’s strictest lockdowns and quarantine measures in an attempt to curb the spread of the coronavirus. Part of their strategy included rigorous contact tracing, mandatory quarantine for positive cases, and, in some instances, the use of quarantine facilities for people who could not safely isolate at home.

The core of the social media post—the assertion that every child testing positive is forcibly separated from their parents—misrepresents the actual public health policy and what occurred in practice. While there were isolated cases where children were temporarily separated from parents, particularly in situations where parents were seriously ill, hospitalized, or otherwise unable to care for their children during isolation, there was never a blanket policy of forcibly removing all COVID-positive children from their families. In fact, public health authorities emphasized keeping families together where possible, recognizing the importance of parental care and the psychological impact of separation.

In some specific instances, such as in managed quarantine hotels or facilities, families were required to isolate together, and protocols were put in place to minimize risk to others. When separation was necessary—such as when a parent was hospitalized and the child was not infected—efforts were typically made to ensure the child was cared for by another family member, guardian, or, in rare cases, by trained staff in a safe environment. These cases were handled with sensitivity and on a case-by-case basis, rather than through any broad or automatic enforcement.

The spread of the claim that every COVID-positive child in Australia was forcibly removed from their parents likely stems from misinterpretations of news reports or viral clips of official briefings, where public health officials discussed possible procedures in exceptional circumstances. These statements were often taken out of context, leading to widespread misinformation.

In summary, the claim that every child in Australia who tested positive for COVID-19 was forcibly taken away from their parents is false. While strict quarantine and isolation measures were in place, family separation was avoided whenever possible and only occurred in exceptional circumstances to protect the health and safety of all involved. Panic-inducing statements like the one circulating on social media do not reflect the reality of Australian public health policy.

هسته اصلی این پست در شبکه‌های اجتماعی، ادعا که هر کودکی که مثبت به کرونا تشخیص داده شود به طور اجبار از والدینش جدا می‌شود، این سیاست‌های بهداشت عمومی واقعی را نمی‌تواند توصیف کند و به واقعیت اتفاقاتی که رخ داده است نیز نزدیک نیست. در حالی که در موارد منفرد کودکان به طور موقت از والدینشان جدا شده‌اند، به ویژه در مواقعی که والدین به دلیل بیماری جدی، در بیمارستان بودند یا به دلیل دیگر عوامل قادر به مراقبت از کودکانشان نبودند، هرگز سیاستی به صورت کلی برای اجباری کردن تمام کودکان مثبت کرونا از خانواده‌هایشان وجود نداشت. در واقع، مقامات بهداشت عمومی تأکید کردند که به اندازه امکان خانواده‌ها را به هم نزدیک نگه دارند، به دلیل اهمیت مراقبت والدین و تأثیر روانی جدایی.

A social media post has circulated criticizing Venko Filipce, the former Minister of Health of North Macedonia, for recommending that children wear masks and undergo COVID-19 testing. The post asserts that children "cannot catch COVID at all," and questions the rationale for imposing such public health measures on minors.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to analyze the scientific understanding of COVID-19 transmission in children, the rationale behind health protocols in schools, and official guidelines during the pandemic.

**Background and Context**

During the global COVID-19 pandemic, health authorities worldwide implemented various measures to reduce viral transmission, including the use of face masks and regular testing in schools. These measures were often controversial, with some critics arguing that children were not at significant risk from COVID-19 and therefore should not be subject to restrictions or protocols such as masking and testing.

Venko Filipce, as Health Minister, was responsible for implementing North Macedonia’s pandemic response, which included guidelines for schools and children. The social media post in question reflects a broader skepticism seen in some communities about the necessity of these measures for children.

**Can Children Catch COVID-19?**

The core claim in the post is that children "cannot catch COVID at all." This statement is not supported by scientific evidence. From the early stages of the pandemic, research has demonstrated that children of all ages can become infected with SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. While children tend to experience milder symptoms compared to adults, and severe cases are less common, they are not immune to infection. There have been documented cases of children developing serious complications, such as Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C), and, in rare cases, fatalities.

Moreover, children can carry and transmit the virus to others, including those who are more vulnerable due to age or underlying health conditions. This capacity for transmission was a key concern for public health officials aiming to prevent outbreaks in schools and communities.

**Masking and Testing Policies**

The recommendation for children to wear masks and undergo testing was based on reducing the spread of COVID-19 within schools and preventing outbreaks that could affect students, staff, and their families. Mask-wearing was shown in multiple studies to lower the risk of respiratory virus transmission, especially in indoor or crowded environments like classrooms. Testing allowed for early detection of cases, including among asymptomatic individuals, which is crucial in containing spread before larger outbreaks occur.

These measures were generally aligned with guidance from international health organizations, which recommended masking and testing as part of a layered approach to pandemic control in schools, especially during periods of high community transmission.

**Conclusion**

The claim that children cannot catch COVID-19 is false. Scientific evidence confirms that children can and do contract the virus, and while the risk of severe illness is lower than in adults, it is not zero. Public health policies recommending masks and testing for children were based on available scientific data and aimed at protecting not only children themselves but also the broader community. Such measures were not arbitrary, but part of a comprehensive strategy to manage the pandemic’s impact.

Sebuah postingan media sosial telah berpusing mengkritik Venko Filipce, mantan Menteri Kesehatan Macedonia Utara, atas rekomendasinya kepada kanak-kanak untuk memakai masker dan menjalani ujian kencing batu (testing) untuk COVID-19. Postingan ini menyatakan bahawa kanak-kanak "tidak dapat menjangkiti COVID-19 sama sekali," dan mempertanyakan rasionaliti mengenai pengenalan langkah-langkah kesihatan awam terhadap kanak-kanak.

Untuk menilai kebenaran klaim ini, penting untuk menganalisis pemahaman saintifik mengenai penularan COVID-19 pada kanak-kanak, rasionaliti protokol kesihatan dalam sekolah, dan garis panduan rasmi semasa pandemik.

**Latar Belakang dan Konteks**

Semasa pandemik global COVID-19, pihak berkuasa kesihatan di seluruh dunia telah melaksanakan pelbagai langkah untuk mengurangkan penularan virus, termasuk penggunaan masker dan ujian kencing batu (testing) secara rutin di sekolah. Langkah-langkah ini sering kontroversi, dengan sebahagian pihak mengkritik bahawa kanak-kanak tidak berisiko besar terhadap COVID-19 dan oleh itu tidak sepatutnya terdedah kepada pembatasan atau protokol seperti memakai masker dan ujian kencing batu (testing).

Venko Filipce, sebagai Menteri Kesehatan, bertanggungjawab melaksanakan tindakan respons pandemik Macedonia Utara, termasuk panduan untuk sekolah dan kanak-kanak. Postingan media sosial yang diperkatakan mencerminkan keraguan yang lebih luas yang dilihat dalam beberapa komuniti mengenai keperluan langkah-langkah ini untuk kanak-kanak.

**Kanak-kanak Dapat Menjangkiti COVID-19?**

Klaim utama dalam postingan ini ialah bahawa kanak-kanak "tidak dapat menjangkiti COVID-19 sama sekali." Pernyataan ini tidak disokong oleh bukti saintifik. Sejak awal pandemik, kajian menunjukkan bahawa kanak-kanak dalam semua usia boleh terjangkit dengan SARS-CoV-2, virus yang menyebabkan COVID-19. Walaupun kanak-kanak cenderung mengalami simptom yang lebih ringan berbanding orang dewasa, dan kes yang serius kurang umum, mereka tidak imun terhadap infeksi. Terdapat kes yang direkodkan mengenai kanak-kanak yang mengalami komplikasi serius, seperti Sistem Inflamasi Multisistem pada Kanak-kanak (MIS-C), serta kematian dalam kes-kes yang jarang berlaku.

Selain itu, kanak-kanak boleh membawa dan menular virus kepada orang lain, termasuk mereka yang lebih rentan disebabkan usia atau keadaan kesihatan yang sedia ada. Kemampuan menular ini menjadi kebimbangan utama pihak kesihatan awam untuk mencegah wabak di sekolah dan komuniti.

**Kebijakan Memakai Masker dan Ujian Kencing Batu (Testing)**

Rekomendasi untuk kanak-kanak memakai masker dan menjalani ujian kencing batu (testing) adalah berdasarkan usaha mengurangkan penyebaran COVID-19 di sekolah dan mencegah wabak yang boleh mempengaruhi pelajar, staf, dan keluarga mereka. Memakai masker telah ditunjukkan dalam kajian-kajian berbilang untuk mengurangkan risiko penularan virus pernafasan, terutamanya dalam ruang dalam atau ramai seperti kelas. Ujian kencing batu membolehkan pengesan awal kes, termasuk individu yang tidak menunjukkan simptom, yang penting untuk mengawal penyebaran sebelum wabak yang lebih besar berlaku.

Langkah-langkah ini secara umumnya selaras dengan panduan dari organisasi kesihatan antarabangsa, yang menasihati penggunaan masker dan ujian kencing batu (testing) sebagai sebahagian daripada pendekatan lapisan untuk mengawal pandemik di sekolah, terutamanya semasa tempoh penularan komuniti yang tinggi.

**Kesimpulan**

Klaim bahawa kanak-kanak tidak dapat menjangkiti COVID-19 adalah salah. Bukti saintifik menunjukkan bahawa kanak-kanak boleh dan memang terjangkit virus ini, dan walaupun risiko penyakit yang serius lebih rendah berbanding orang dewasa, ia bukanlah sifar. Kebijakan kesihatan awam yang menasihati penggunaan masker dan ujian kencing batu (testing) untuk kanak-kanak berdasarkan data saintifik yang ada dan bertujuan melindungi bukan sahaja kanak-kanak itu sendiri, tetapi juga komuniti yang lebih luas. Langkah-langkah ini bukanlah sewenang-wenangnya, tetapi sebahagian daripada strategi menyeluruh untuk mengurangkan dampak pandemik.

article_content:
A recent social media post has sparked alarm among parents by claiming that authorities will arrive unannounced, accompanied by strong police security, to forcibly vaccinate children without parental consent. The author of the post warns families to be vigilant, suggesting a scenario where law enforcement acts as enforcers for what the post describes as a covert, aggressive public health initiative.

This claim has caused considerable concern, leading to widespread sharing and discussion. To assess the accuracy of this statement, it is important to examine both the context of vaccination policies and the realities of law enforcement involvement in public health initiatives.

**Background and Context**

Vaccination programs are a cornerstone of public health efforts worldwide. In most countries, including the United States and across Europe, vaccines for children are administered with parental consent, either through school-based programs, healthcare providers, or public clinics. Vaccines are considered one of the most effective ways to prevent infectious diseases and protect community health.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccination campaigns intensified, sometimes with mobile units and pop-up clinics. However, even at the height of public health emergencies, standard procedure has required parental or guardian consent for the vaccination of minors.

**Law Enforcement and Vaccination**

The claim that police will accompany health officials to forcibly vaccinate children raises serious questions. In democratic societies, law enforcement officers may be present at certain events to ensure public order or to provide protection if there is a credible threat. However, there is no evidence to support widespread or systematic use of police to enforce vaccination by force. Authorities do not have the legal mandate to enter private homes unannounced and vaccinate children against the wishes of their parents.

In rare cases, law enforcement has been involved when there are court orders regarding the welfare of a child, such as when a child is at risk due to medical neglect. These situations are exceptional and require judicial oversight, not unilateral action by health officials or police.

**Analysis of the Claim**

The core assertion of the post—that authorities will act as “assassins” and forcibly vaccinate children with police backup, without any warning or consent—is not supported by available evidence or by established vaccination protocols. Such an approach would violate multiple legal and ethical standards, including the right to bodily autonomy and parental rights.

Public health authorities have consistently emphasized the importance of consent and transparency in vaccination campaigns. While there are mandates in some regions that require certain vaccines for school attendance, these are enforced through administrative measures, such as exclusion from school, not through forced medical procedures.

**Conclusion**

The narrative presented by the social media post is highly misleading and not grounded in fact. There is no basis for the claim that children will be forcibly vaccinated by authorities with police presence, nor is there any evidence of such practices occurring on a broad scale. Parents are encouraged to seek information from official health sources and consult with healthcare providers regarding vaccinations for their children.

article_content:
A video circulating on social media features Dr. Robert Malone, a scientist involved in early mRNA technology research, making several alarming claims about COVID-19 vaccines. Malone asserts that "the vaccine makes the virus more contagious than if there were no vaccine," calls the phenomenon "the worst nightmare for vaccinologists," and suggests that "virus mutations fleeing vaccines are more likely to be developed in the vaccinated than in the unvaccinated." He concludes by insisting, "we have to stop the vaccination process." These statements have sparked widespread concern and confusion online. Here, we examine the scientific validity of these claims and provide the necessary context.

First, Dr. Malone’s claim that vaccines make the virus more contagious than if there were no vaccine is not supported by the current body of scientific evidence. The purpose of COVID-19 vaccines is to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death from infection. While breakthrough infections—cases in which vaccinated individuals still contract COVID-19—can occur, studies consistently show that vaccinated people are less likely to become infected in the first place and, if infected, are less likely to transmit the virus to others compared to the unvaccinated. The assertion that vaccines increase overall contagiousness contradicts both laboratory and real-world data.

Malone’s reference to "the worst nightmare for vaccinologists" alludes to a theoretical concept known as "antibody-dependent enhancement" or concerns about "leaky" vaccines leading to vaccine-driven viral evolution. While it is true that, in rare instances, vaccines can theoretically apply selective pressure on viruses to evolve, this is not unique to COVID-19 vaccines and has not been observed at a scale that outweighs the benefits of vaccination. In practice, widespread vaccination campaigns have been essential tools in controlling or eradicating other viral diseases such as measles and polio.

The claim that "virus mutations fleeing vaccines are more likely to be developed in the vaccinated than in the unvaccinated" also requires scrutiny. Viral mutations arise as the virus replicates, and the largest reservoir for replication is among unvaccinated populations, where the virus spreads more freely. While selective pressure exists in any population with immunity—whether from infection or vaccination—current evidence indicates that most significant new variants have emerged in areas with high transmission and low vaccination coverage. Therefore, halting vaccination would likely result in increased transmission and more opportunities for the virus to mutate, not fewer.

Finally, the call to "stop the vaccination process" is at odds with global health recommendations. Leading health agencies worldwide, including the World Health Organization and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, continue to advocate for vaccination as the most effective means of controlling the spread of COVID-19 and preventing severe outcomes.

In summary, Dr. Malone’s statements in the video are not substantiated by scientific evidence. Vaccination remains a cornerstone of public health efforts against COVID-19. The suggestion that vaccines are making the virus more dangerous or that vaccination should be stopped is misleading and not supported by current research or expert consensus.

اولین ادعای مالون این است که واکسن‌ها باعث می‌شود ویروس بیشتر قابل انتقال باشد، اما این ادعای از نظر داده‌های علمی فعلی پشتیبانی نمی‌شود. هدف واکسن‌های کووید-19 کاهش خطر ابتلا به بیماری جدی، بستری شدن و مرگ است. در حالی که ابتلاهای "فراگیر" (که در آن افراد واکسینه هم ابتلا می‌کنند) ممکن است اتفاق بیفتد، مطالعات ثابت کرده‌اند که افراد واکسینه شده احتمال ابتلا به ویروس را در ابتدا کمتر دارند و در صورت ابتلا، احتمال انتقال آن به دیگران نیز کمتر است. ادعای اینکه واکسن‌ها افزایش کلی قابلیت انتقال ویروس را می‌کنند با هر دو داده‌های آزمایشگاهی و واقعی در تضاد است.

اشاره مالون به "سیاه‌ترین خواب دشمنان واکسن" به یک مفهوم نظری یعنی "افزایش وابسته به آنتی بادی" یا نگرانی‌هایی درباره "واکسن‌های یکنواخت" که به ایجاد تغییرات ویروسی مرتبط با واکسن منجر می‌شود، اشاره دارد. اگرچه در ندرستی، احتمالاً واکسن‌ها می‌توانند فشار انتخابی بر روی ویروس را اعمال کنند و این فرآیند در نتیجه تغییرات ویروسی باشد، اما این موضوع به طور خاص در واکسن‌های کووید-19 نیست و این فشار انتخابی در مقیاسی که به نفع واکسیناسیون باشد مشاهده نشده است. در عمل، کامپانی‌های واکسیناسیون گسترده به ابزارهای حیاتی در کنترل یا از بین بردن بیماری‌های ویروسی دیگر مانند کوچک‌کردن و پولیو تبدیل شده‌اند.

ادعای اینکه "تغییرات ویروسی که از واکسن فرار می‌کنند، در افراد واکسینه شده بیشتر از افراد غیرواکسینه شده تولید می‌شوند" نیز نیاز به بررسی دارد. تغییرات ویروسی در هنگام تکثیر ویروس ایجاد می‌شود و بزرگترین منبع تکثیر در جوامع غیرواکسینه است، که در آن ویروس بیشتر انتقال می‌یابد. اگرچه فشار انتخابی در هر جوامعی با ایمنی وجود دارد (چه از عفونت چه از واکسن) اما داده‌های فعلی نشان می‌دهد که اغلب نوین تغییرات ویروسی در مناطقی که انتقال بالا و واکسیناسیون پایین است به وجود آمده است. بنابراین، متوقف کردن واکسیناسیون به احتمال زیاد باعث افزایش انتقال و فرصت بیشتری برای تغییرات ویروسی خواهد شد، نه کاهش آن.

در نهایت، ادعای "متوقف کردن فرآیند واکسیناسیون" با پیشنهادهای جهانی سلامت در تضاد است. سازمان‌های سلامت جهانی، از جمله سازمان سلامت جهانی و مرکز کنترل و پیشگیری از بیماری‌ها، همچنان به واکسیناسیون به عنوان روش مؤثرترین برای کنترل انتشار کووید-19 و جلوگیری از نتایج جدی اشاره می‌کنند.

در نتیجه، اظهارات مالون در فیلم از نظر داده‌های علمی پشتیبانی نمی‌شود. واکسیناسیون هنوز هم یکی از اساسی‌ترین اقدامات سلامت عمومی در برابر کووید-19 است. ادعای اینکه واکسن‌ها باعث خطر بیشتری برای ویروس می‌شوند یا واکسیناسیون را متوقف کنیم، به نظر گمراه کننده و بدون پشتیبانی از پژوهش‌های فعلی و توافق نظر اندیشمندان است.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming, “Denmark will lift the restrictive measures because it will consider Covid-19 as a flu.” This post suggests that the Danish government has decided to end Covid-19 restrictions on the basis that it now regards the virus as equivalent to seasonal influenza. To evaluate the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine Denmark’s public health policy decisions, the government’s statements, and the broader context of pandemic management in the country.

Background and Context

Denmark has been at the forefront of Covid-19 policy shifts in Europe, frequently adjusting its approach in response to changing circumstances. Since the beginning of the pandemic, Denmark implemented a range of restrictive measures, including lockdowns, mask mandates, and vaccine requirements. These measures were periodically tightened or relaxed according to infection rates, hospital capacity, and vaccination coverage.

In early 2022, Denmark announced significant changes: the country would lift most of its Covid-19 restrictions, including the use of vaccine passports, mask mandates, and limits on indoor gatherings. The government justified these changes by citing high vaccination rates, widespread immunity, and the reduced severity of illness caused by the Omicron variant.

Fact-Checking the Claim

The core claim in the social media post has two components: that Denmark is lifting restrictive measures, and that it is doing so because it now considers Covid-19 equivalent to the flu.

First, it is accurate that Denmark lifted nearly all Covid-19 restrictions. As of early 2022, the government officially declared that Covid-19 was no longer classified as a “socially critical disease,” a legal designation that allowed for special emergency powers. This move effectively ended most public restrictions, although some recommendations for vulnerable groups and health care settings remained.

However, the assertion that Denmark is lifting restrictions because it considers Covid-19 as “a flu” oversimplifies and misrepresents the government’s position. Danish authorities did not equate Covid-19 with influenza in terms of severity or public health impact. Instead, the government cited several reasons for lifting restrictions: the milder symptoms associated with the Omicron variant, high levels of immunity in the population, and a manageable burden on the healthcare system. The decision was described as a transition to managing Covid-19 as an ongoing health issue, rather than an acute social emergency.

Government officials have been careful to note that Covid-19 is still potentially dangerous, especially for vulnerable groups. The comparison to seasonal influenza relates more to the management and monitoring of the disease, rather than a statement about their equivalence in all respects.

Conclusion

While it is true that Denmark lifted most of its Covid-19 restrictions, the claim that this was done because the government now simply considers Covid-19 “as a flu” is misleading. The decision was based on a combination of high immunity rates, the characteristics of the Omicron variant, and the capacity of the healthcare system—not a formal reclassification of Covid-19 as equivalent to influenza. Covid-19 continues to be monitored and managed as a distinct public health concern, albeit with fewer emergency restrictions.

article_content:
A recent social media post has resurfaced concerns about the COVID-19 vaccines, specifically those produced by Pfizer. The post claims that these products are “not vaccines,” are “not approved,” and that even Pfizer admits this. It further alleges that the side effects are more severe than the common cold and may persist for life, including increased risks of cancer that could be attributed to the vaccine years later. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context and clarity on each point.

The first assertion is that the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine is “not a vaccine.” This is incorrect by both scientific and regulatory definitions. Vaccines are substances used to stimulate the body’s immune response against diseases. The Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, known as Comirnaty, uses messenger RNA (mRNA) to instruct cells to produce a protein similar to the spike protein of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, triggering an immune response. Although mRNA vaccines are a newer technology, they fit the established definition of a vaccine—namely, they prepare the immune system to recognize and fight the pathogen if exposed in the future.

The claim that the Pfizer vaccine is “not approved” also misrepresents the regulatory status. In the early stages of the pandemic, COVID-19 vaccines were distributed under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) to expedite access during a global health crisis. However, the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine has since received full approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for individuals 12 years and older, and similar approvals have been granted in many other countries. The approval process involved a rigorous review of safety and efficacy data from large clinical trials and real-world use. Pfizer has not stated that its vaccine is “not approved.” In fact, the company has publicly communicated its approval status.

The post suggests that side effects from the vaccine are “not as mild as the common cold” and may be lifelong. Most reported side effects of the Pfizer vaccine are mild and short-lived, including fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and soreness at the injection site. Serious side effects are extremely rare. Long-term effects are monitored continuously, and current evidence does not support claims that the vaccine causes persistent or lifelong health problems for the majority of recipients.

Finally, the post alleges that “for the next 10 years if you get cancer, they will tell you that it should be so,” implying the vaccine will be used as a scapegoat for future health issues like cancer. There is no scientific evidence linking mRNA vaccines to increased cancer risk. Monitoring and surveillance systems remain in place to detect any potential long-term side effects, and so far, no credible signals indicate an association between the vaccine and cancer development.

In summary, the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine is a vaccine by scientific and regulatory standards, is fully approved for use in several countries, and has a strong safety profile based on extensive studies and ongoing monitoring. Claims to the contrary are not supported by current scientific evidence.

A social media post circulating widely claims that the World Health Organization (WHO) now considers a child’s attendance at school as “informed consent” for vaccination, stating that parental presence is not required. This assertion has sparked concern among parents and guardians who worry about their rights and the procedures surrounding childhood immunizations. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine WHO’s actual guidelines, the concept of informed consent, and how vaccination programs are typically conducted in schools.

**Understanding Informed Consent and WHO Guidelines**

Informed consent is a foundational principle in medical ethics. It requires that individuals, or their legal guardians in the case of minors, are given adequate information about a medical intervention, including its benefits, risks, and alternatives, and that they voluntarily agree to proceed. For children, laws and regulations in most countries require parental or guardian consent before any medical procedure, including vaccinations.

The WHO provides guidance to countries on best practices for vaccination programs, especially in settings with limited resources or where large-scale immunization campaigns are needed, such as during outbreaks. WHO’s position is that national laws and policies take precedence in determining consent procedures. In some contexts, particularly where there is high community awareness and engagement (for example, when parents are informed ahead of time and have the opportunity to opt out), some countries have considered attendance at school as an indication of implied consent. However, WHO does not mandate or universally endorse this practice.

**School-Based Vaccination Programs: International Practice**

School-based vaccination programs are common worldwide for their effectiveness and reach. In most cases, schools distribute consent forms to parents ahead of vaccination days. These forms explain the vaccines being offered and request a signature from a parent or guardian. Children whose parents do not consent are typically not vaccinated at school.

The claim that WHO now says parental presence is not required and that mere attendance at school is considered “informed consent” oversimplifies and misrepresents WHO’s recommendations. The organization acknowledges that in certain emergency or resource-limited situations, some countries have adopted implied consent approaches. However, WHO also emphasizes that parents and guardians should be informed, and national policies must be respected.

**Fact-Checking the Core Claim**

There is no evidence that WHO has changed its policy to universally endorse school attendance as sufficient for informed consent to vaccination, nor that parental presence or explicit consent is no longer required. WHO’s guidance continues to stress the importance of informing parents and obtaining consent in accordance with national laws. In most jurisdictions, explicit parental consent remains a legal requirement, and schools are expected to communicate with families prior to any immunization activities.

**Conclusion**

The claim circulating on social media exaggerates and distorts the WHO’s position on informed consent for school-based vaccinations. While some countries may use implied consent approaches under specific circumstances, WHO does not mandate or broadly recommend that simple school attendance be treated as informed consent for vaccination. Parents should expect to receive information and have the opportunity to give or withhold consent before their children are vaccinated at school. As always, local regulations and procedures should be consulted for the most accurate guidance.

**Forståelse af informeret samtykke og WHO's retningslinjer**

Informeret samtykke er en grundlæggende princip i medisk etik. Det kræver, at individer, eller deres juridiske våben i tilfælde af mindreårige, får tilstrækkeligt information om en medicinsk intervention, herunder dens fordele, risikoen og alternativer, og at de frivilligt samtykker til at gennemføre proceduren. WHO giver retningslinjer til lande om bedste praksis for vaccineringssprog, især i situationer med begrænset ressourcer eller hvor store vaccinationskampagner er nødvendige, som under udbrud. WHO's holdning er, at nationale love og politikker har primært ansvar for at fastlægge samtykkeproceduren. I nogle kontekster, især hvor der er høj samfundskendskab og engagement (fx når forældre informeres i forvejen og har mulighed for at afvise), har nogle lande overvejet skolegang som et tegn på tilsyneladende samtykke. **Skolebaserede vaccineringssprog: International praksis**

Skolebaserede vaccineringssprog er almindelige i hele verden på grund af deres effektivitet og omfang. I de fleste tilfælde distribuerer skoler samtykkeformulare til forældre foran vaccinationsdage. Disse formulare r forklarer de tilbudte vacciner og beder om et undertegn fra en forælder eller våben. Børn, hvis forældre ikke samtykker, vaccineres typisk ikke i skolen.

Påstanden, at WHO nu siger, at forældrenes tilstedeværelse ikke er påkrævet og at blot skolegang betragtes som "informeredt samtykke", forenkler og misrepræsenterer WHO's anbefalinger. Organisationen erkender, at i visse nødsituationer eller i ressourcerstyrede områder har nogle lande adopteret tilsyneladende samtykke. Dog understreger WHO også, at forældre og våben skal informeres, og at nationale politikker skal respekteres.

**Faktagenkaldning af den centrale påstand**

Der er ingen beviser for, at WHO har ændret sin politik til at universelt anerkende skolegang som tilstrækkelig for informeret samtykke til vaccination, eller at forældrenes tilstedeværelse eller eksplisit samtykke ikke længere er påkrævet. WHO's retningslinjer fortsætter med at understrege vigtigheden af at informere forældre og opnå samtykke i overensstemmelse med nationale love. I de fleste juridiske områder er eksplisit forældresamtykke stadig en juridisk forudsætning, og skoler forventes at kommunikere med familier inden for enhver immuniseringssprog.

**Konklusion**

Påstanden, der spredes via socialmedie, forstærker og forvrænger WHO's holdning til informeret samtykke ved skolebaserede vaccineringssprog. Selvom nogle lande muligvis bruger tilsyneladende samtykke i bestemte situationer, anerkender WHO ikke, at simpel skolegang skal behandles som informeret samtykke til vaccination. Forældre bør forvente at modtage information og have mulighed for at give eller afvise samtykke inden deres børn vaccineres i skolen. Som altid bør lokale regler og procedurer konsulteres for den mest præcise vejledning.
