A social media post has recently garnered attention by claiming, “The vaccinated are full of toxins.” This statement suggests that individuals who have received vaccines carry harmful or toxic substances in their bodies as a result of vaccination. This article examines the scientific basis of this claim, provides context about vaccine ingredients, and evaluates the safety profile of commonly administered vaccines.

Vaccines are a cornerstone of public health, preventing the spread of infectious diseases such as measles, polio, influenza, and COVID-19. The process of vaccination involves introducing a harmless component or inactivated version of a pathogen into the body, prompting the immune system to build a defense against the disease. To achieve this, vaccines contain active ingredients (antigens) and other components known as excipients, which may include stabilizers, preservatives, and adjuvants.

The claim that vaccinated individuals are “full of toxins” hinges on the misunderstanding and misrepresentation of these ingredients. Vaccine ingredients are carefully selected to ensure safety and efficacy. Some of the most commonly discussed ingredients include aluminum salts (used as adjuvants to boost immune response), trace amounts of formaldehyde (used to inactivate viruses or detoxify bacterial toxins), and thimerosal (a mercury-based preservative, now rarely used). These substances are present in extremely small amounts, much lower than levels people are typically exposed to in their daily environment.

Scientific studies and regulatory reviews have repeatedly shown that the ingredients used in vaccines do not accumulate in the body at toxic levels. The human body is capable of processing and eliminating these substances efficiently. For example, the amount of aluminum in vaccines is far less than what people ingest through food and water. Concerns about mercury are largely outdated, as thimerosal has been removed from most childhood vaccines for decades, and the type of mercury it contains (ethylmercury) is processed by the body much more rapidly than the more dangerous methylmercury found in some fish.

Furthermore, vaccines undergo rigorous testing in clinical trials and are subject to continuous monitoring once approved for public use. Regulatory agencies such as the Food and Drug Administration and the World Health Organization evaluate vaccines for both short-term and long-term safety, ensuring that any potential risks are outweighed by the benefits of disease prevention.

In summary, the assertion that “the vaccinated are full of toxins” lacks scientific support. The ingredients in vaccines are present in minuscule, carefully regulated amounts that are proven to be safe for human use. The benefits of vaccination in preventing serious illness and death far outweigh the extremely low risks associated with vaccine ingredients. Misinformation about vaccine safety can undermine public health efforts and lead to lower vaccination rates, increasing the risk of disease outbreaks. It is crucial to rely on scientifically accurate information when making health decisions.

Социјална мрежа је недавно присвојила пажњу од стране изјаве која тврди: „Вакцинирани су пунови токсинима.“ Ова изјава подразумева да је особа која је добила вакцину у телу имала штетне или токсичне субстанце као последица вакцинације. Ово чланак прегледа научну основу ове изјаве, даје контекст о састојцима вакцина и процени безбедносни профил обичних вакцина.

Вакцине су један од основних елемената јавног здравља, предуздимају ширење инфективних болести као што су орепс, полиомелитис, грипа и коронавирус. Процес вакцинације укључује уводење безбедног компонента или инактивиране верзије патогена у тело, што изазива имунолошку систем да сазна како да се одбани болест. За то, вакцине садрже активне састојке (антигене) и друге компоненте познате као експандери, који могу укључивати стабилизаторе, конзерванте и адјувањанте.

Алтернативна изјава да је „вакцинирани пунови токсинима“ зависи од неправилног разумевања и несанице о овим састојцима. Састојци вакцина су одабрани са пажњом да би се осигурала безбедност и ефикасност. Неки од најчешће дискутираних састојака су алуминијумски соли (коришћени као адјувањанти да би се убрзао имунски одговор), праћећи количине формалдехида (коришћен за инактивирање вируса или детоксикацију бактеријских токсина), и тимерозол (конзервант базиран на ртут, сада ретко коришћен). Ове субстанце су присутне у екстремно малим количинама, много мањим од нивоа изложености који људи уобичајено имају у свом дnevном животу.

Научни истраживања и регулаторни прегледи су многократно показали да састојци који се користе у вакцина не аккумулишу у телу на токсичним нивоима. Човечко тело је способно да обради и избацује ове субстанце ефикасно. На пример, количина алуминијума у вакцина је много мања од количине коју људи узимају кроз храну и воду. Брине о ртутима су углавном устарели, јер је тимерозол био уклоњен из већине детских вакцина пре неколико деценија, а врста ртута коју садржи (етилртут) је брже обрађује телом него већи ризик од метилртута који се налази у неким рибама.

Додатно, вакцине претходно премашићу строга испитивања у клиничким испитивањима и након одобривања за јавно коришћење, настављају се непрестано праћење. Регулаторни агенције као што су Фуд и Дрог Администрација и Светска здравствена организација процени вакцине по безбедности кратког и дугог термина, осигуравајући да било који потенцијални ризици биће оштећени од користи од превенције болести.

У закључку, тврдња да „вакцинирани су пунови токсинима“ не има научног подршке. Састојци вакцина су присутни у минималним, строго регулисаним количинама које су доказане као безбедне за људско коришћење. Користи од вакцинације у превенцији тешких болести и смртних случајева углавном превазилазе екстремно ниске ризике повезане са састојцима вакцина. Неврачено информације о безбедности вакцина могу да подржију јавно здравствене напоре и довести до нижих стопа вакцинације, што повећава ризик од епидемија болести. Важно је да се приликом одлучивања о здравству користи научно тачна информација.

In April 2021, a social media post circulated widely, claiming that the Pentagon had announced the development of a microchip designed to be inserted into the human body to detect the presence of a virus. The claim sparked significant concern and speculation, fueling existing anxieties about privacy, government surveillance, and emerging medical technologies. To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to examine the facts surrounding the Pentagon’s involvement in medical technology and what was actually stated by officials at the time.

The context for this claim originates from a segment aired in April 2021 on a prominent television news program, which featured retired Colonel Dr. Matt Hepburn, a physician and infectious disease expert associated with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), a research arm of the U.S. Department of Defense. During the segment, Dr. Hepburn discussed a range of medical innovations developed by DARPA scientists to help prevent and combat infectious diseases, particularly in military settings where close quarters can allow viruses to spread rapidly.

One of the technologies showcased was a tiny sensor that could be placed under the skin. The description given was that this sensor could continuously monitor certain biochemistry in the body and could potentially detect the onset of infection, such as a viral illness, before the onset of symptoms. The intended application was to provide early warning for service members, allowing for prompt isolation and treatment to prevent outbreaks, especially on naval ships where containment is challenging.

However, the claim that the Pentagon “declared” it has a “microchip that will be inserted into the body” to register if a person “has a virus” misconstrues both the purpose and the nature of the technology. First, the device is not a “microchip” in the way that term is popularly used, which often conjures images of tracking devices or invasive implants. Instead, the sensor is described as a small, tissue-like gel, similar to a glucose monitor used by people with diabetes. It is not a tracking device and does not collect or transmit personal data beyond the biological markers it is designed to monitor.

Second, the device was not created for mass public use nor was there any discussion of mandatory insertion into the general population. The project was focused on voluntary use by military personnel to manage health risks specific to their operational environment.

Finally, the sensor does not directly “register if the person has a virus.” Instead, it monitors biomarkers that can indicate the early stages of an infection, prompting further diagnostic testing. It is not a standalone diagnostic tool for any specific virus, including COVID-19.

In conclusion, while the Pentagon’s DARPA did present a novel under-the-skin sensor in April 2021, the claim that it declared a microchip would be inserted into the body to register viral infections broadly misrepresents the facts. The technology is an early-warning health tool for military settings, not a general-use microchip, and is not intended for mass implantation or real-time infection detection. This social media post takes elements of truth and distorts them, resulting in a misleading and inaccurate portrayal of the Pentagon’s medical research efforts.

A social media post circulating widely claims: “MASS VACCINATION IS NOT a cure for the virus, it is NOT IMMUNIZATION, nor will it get you back to normal. They lie to you if they tell you otherwise.” This statement raises concerns about the effectiveness and purpose of mass vaccination campaigns against infectious diseases, particularly in the context of recent global efforts to address the COVID-19 pandemic. To evaluate the accuracy of this claim, it is important to analyze each assertion in detail and provide relevant context.

First, the claim that “mass vaccination is not a cure for the virus” is technically accurate. Vaccines are not designed to cure illnesses that have already developed in the body. Instead, they are preventive tools, aiming to prepare the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens before an individual is exposed to them. This is a fundamental distinction in medicine: cures treat existing disease, while vaccines prevent disease from occurring.

The post goes on to state that mass vaccination “is NOT IMMUNIZATION.” This is misleading. Vaccination is the process of introducing a vaccine into the body to stimulate the immune system to produce immunity to a specific disease. Immunization refers to the actual process by which a person becomes protected against a disease through vaccination. In practice, the terms “vaccination” and “immunization” are often used interchangeably. While no vaccine is 100% effective for every individual, mass vaccination campaigns are a proven method for achieving widespread immunity in populations, reducing disease transmission, severity, and mortality.

The assertion that vaccination “will not get you back to normal” requires nuanced consideration. Mass vaccination has historically played a pivotal role in controlling and, in some cases, eradicating infectious diseases—such as smallpox and polio—allowing societies to return to normal functioning. During the COVID-19 pandemic, mass vaccination was a key strategy recommended by public health authorities worldwide. While vaccines alone cannot guarantee an immediate return to pre-pandemic normalcy, they significantly reduce the risk of severe illness and death, and, when combined with other public health measures, can contribute to the lifting of restrictions and the resumption of everyday activities.

Finally, the claim that “they lie to you if they tell you otherwise” implies deliberate misinformation by health officials and experts. There is no evidence to support the idea that the medical and scientific community is systematically deceiving the public about the role of vaccines. Public health messaging acknowledges both the strengths and limitations of vaccines, emphasizing that while they are not cures, they are among the most effective preventive measures available.

In summary, while the post contains elements of truth—such as vaccines not being cures—it presents a misleading and incomplete picture of the role and effectiveness of mass vaccination. Vaccines are a cornerstone of public health, providing immunization and helping societies manage and recover from infectious disease outbreaks.

article_content:
A recent social media post has claimed that the Vaccine Safety Committee decided against vaccinating children, but the government ignored this scientific advice and proceeded to authorize vaccinations for children. The post further alleges that doctors in Great Britain receive £12.58 for every vaccine administered, suggesting that financial incentives are motivating health professionals to vaccinate children, rather than public health considerations. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context and a fact-based analysis.

First, it is important to clarify the role and recommendations of the Vaccine Safety Committee. In the United Kingdom, vaccine recommendations for children are made by the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI), an independent expert advisory committee. Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, the JCVI has issued guidance on the vaccination of various age groups, including children. The committee’s recommendations have often been cautious, particularly regarding the vaccination of children, balancing the risks and benefits in the context of available evidence.

At certain points, the JCVI did initially express reservations about offering COVID-19 vaccines to children aged 12-15, citing the relatively low risk of severe illness in this age group and the need for further data on vaccine safety and effectiveness. However, the JCVI later updated its guidance as more data became available and as the wider benefits of vaccination (including reduced transmission and protection of vulnerable populations) were considered. Ultimately, the UK government, taking into account JCVI advice and additional input from chief medical officers, authorized the vaccination of children in specific age groups. This was not a case of the government wholly disregarding scientific advice; rather, it involved weighing multiple factors and expert opinions in a dynamic public health situation.

The second claim in the post concerns financial incentives for doctors. In the UK, general practitioners (GPs) and other healthcare providers are commonly paid a set fee per vaccine administered as part of national immunization programs. The figure of £12.58 per dose is accurate and reflects the standard payment made to doctors for administering a COVID-19 vaccine. This fee is intended to cover costs associated with delivering the vaccine, including staff time, facilities, and administration, and is standard practice for many NHS vaccination programs. There is no evidence to suggest that this payment is an unusual or excessive financial incentive, nor that it is the primary motivation for recommending vaccination.

The implication that “everything revolves around money” and that health professionals are behaving unethically is not supported by evidence. The decision to vaccinate children was based on an evolving understanding of the risks and benefits, with input from a range of experts and authorities. Payments to doctors for administering vaccines are commonplace and are designed to ensure the logistics of large-scale immunization campaigns are feasible and efficient.

In summary, while it is true that doctors receive a standard fee per vaccine dose and that initial scientific debate occurred regarding vaccinating children, the portrayal of the situation as driven by financial motives and government disregard for science does not reflect the complex reality of public health decision-making during the pandemic.

article_content:
A social media post circulating online makes several sweeping claims about the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccines. The post alleges that the pandemic is a fabricated event designed to instill fear, that reports of deaths from COVID-19 lack transparency, and that vaccines are more dangerous than the illness itself. This article examines these assertions in detail, providing context and factual analysis.

The first claim suggests that “everything is just a big lie to terrorize people to think it is true,” implying that the pandemic is a hoax. COVID-19, a respiratory disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, was first identified in late 2019. Since then, millions of cases and deaths have been reported worldwide. Governments, health agencies, and scientific communities have deployed extensive resources to track the spread, develop treatments, and manage public health responses. The pandemic’s impact is evidenced by overwhelmed healthcare systems, economic disruptions, and the unprecedented global mobilization for vaccine development. While misinformation and confusion have surrounded the pandemic, the overwhelming consensus among scientists is that COVID-19 is a real and serious public health issue.

The post further claims that “they wash the brains of the people to be vaccinated,” implying widespread manipulation or coercion. Public health campaigns have indeed promoted vaccination as a primary tool to reduce transmission and severity of COVID-19. These campaigns are rooted in evidence showing that vaccines reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death. While some individuals remain hesitant or skeptical, vaccine recommendations are based on rigorous clinical trials and ongoing safety monitoring. No credible evidence supports the notion that people are being “brainwashed” on a mass scale; rather, health authorities attempt to inform and protect populations based on scientific data.

Another assertion in the post is that reported COVID-19 deaths lack transparency, stating “There is never a name, surname, or address of the dead.” Typically, public health agencies report aggregate data to respect privacy and confidentiality. However, families, news outlets, and local reports have frequently shared personal stories and obituaries of individuals lost to COVID-19. While not every death is individually documented in public databases, the overall data collection methods are designed to provide an accurate picture of the pandemic’s toll.

The post claims, “if there is someone dead, it certainly has nothing to do with the Covid-19,” suggesting that COVID-19 deaths are misattributed. In reality, the cause of death on official death certificates is determined by medical professionals, often following hospitalizations and diagnostic testing. While comorbidities can contribute to outcomes, COVID-19 is listed when it is a significant factor.

Finally, the post asserts that “vaccines are much more dangerous and deadly than the flu, which they called Covid-19.” COVID-19 is distinct from influenza, with different causative viruses and patterns of severity. Vaccines authorized for COVID-19 have undergone extensive testing and monitoring, with serious side effects being rare. By contrast, COVID-19 itself has caused widespread severe illness and death, particularly before vaccines became widely available.

In summary, the claims made in the social media post do not align with the established facts regarding COVID-19, its impact, or the safety and effectiveness of vaccines. The pandemic is a real and significant global health crisis, and the tools used to combat it—including vaccination—are based on scientific evidence and rigorous study.

మొదటి వాదన అనేక విషయాలు మానవులకు భయం కలిగించడానికి ప్రమాదకరంగా ఉంటాయని చెబుతుంది, అంటే పాండెమిక్ ఒక ప్రమాదకరమైన ఘటన అని అనిపిస్తుంది. కోవిడ్-19 కోవిట్ వైరస్ ద్వారా కారణం అయిన శ్వాస వ్యవస్థ వ్యాధి, 2019 చివరి వరకు గుర్తించబడింది. అప్పటి నుండి ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా కోటికి పైగా కేసులు మరియు మరణాలు నమోదు చేయబడ్డాయి. ప్రభుత్వాలు, ఆరోగ్య ఏజెన్సీలు మరియు విప్లవ సమాజం వ్యాప్తంగా విస్తృత వనరులను ఉపయోగించి విస్ఫోటనం నియంత్రణ, చికిత్స అభివృద్ధి మరియు ప్రజా ఆరోగ్య సమాధానాలను పరిపోషించడానికి ప్రయత్నించాయి. ఈ పాండెమిక్ ప్రభావం వైద్య సంస్థలు విస్ఫోటనం కుదిరించడం, ఆర్థిక వ్యవస్థ దెబ్బతినడం మరియు వ్యాక్సిన్ అభివృద్ధికి అంతర్జాలం వ్యాప్తంగా విస్తృత ప్రయత్నం వల్ల చూపబడింది. విస్ఫోటనం సంబంధించి తప్పు సమాచారం మరియు అస్థిరత ఉండింది, కానీ విప్లవ సమాజం విషయంలో శాస్త్రవేత్తలు కోవిడ్-19 ఒక వాస్తవం మరియు ముఖ్యమైన సామాజిక ఆరోగ్య సమస్య అని సాధారణంగా అనుమానించారు.

ఈ పోస్ట్ ఇంకా వాదిస్తుంది అనేక మంది వ్యక్తులు వ్యాక్సిన్ వేయించడానికి వారి మానసిక శక్తిని ప్రభావితం చేస్తారని, అంటే విస్ఫోటనం కోసం విస్టార్ లేదా విస్టార్ ఉంటుందని అనిపిస్తుంది. ప్రజా ఆరోగ్య కార్యక్రమాలు కోవిడ్-19 వ్యాప్తిని తగ్గించడం మరియు వ్యాధి విస్ఫోటనం నుండి విప్లవ సమాజం చికిత్స చేయడం కోసం వ్యాక్సిన్ వేయించడం ప్రధాన ఉపయోగంగా ప్రచారం చేస్తున్నాయి. ఈ కార్యక్రమాలు వ్యాక్సిన్ విస్ఫోటనం కారణం చికిత్స ప్రమాదాలు, ఆస్పత్రుల్లో అంతరాయం మరియు మరణాల ప్రమాదాలను తగ్గించడానికి ప్రమాణాలు ఉన్నాయని చెప్పడం ద్వారా నిరూపించబడింది. కొందరు వ్యక్తులు వ్యాక్సిన్ అందించడానికి విస్టార్ లేదా విస్టార్ కోసం విస్టార్ ఉండిందని అనుకుంటారు, కానీ వ్యాక్సిన్ అందించడానికి సంబంధించిన విషయాలు విస్టార్ లేదా విస్టార్ కోసం నిరూపించబడలేదు. విప్లవ సమాజం విస్టార్ లేదా విస్టార్ కోసం సాంకేతిక సమాచారం ఆధారంగా విప్లవ సమాజం ప్రజల రక్షణ కోసం వివరించడానికి ప్రయత్నిస్తున్నారు.

ఈ పోస్ట్ మరో వాదన కోవిడ్-19 మరణాలు అస్పష్టంగా ఉండాలని చెబుతుంది, అంటే "ఏ వ్యక్తి మరణించినా, అది కోవిడ్-19 కు సంబంధించినది కాదు". సాధారణంగా ప్రజా ఆరోగ్య ఏజెన్సీలు గుర్తించడం కోసం సంప్రదాయం డేటాను కూడా వివరిస్తుంది. కానీ కుటుంబాలు, సమాచార సంస్థలు మరియు స్థానిక న్యూస్ పత్రికలు కోవిడ్-19 కారణంగా మరణించిన వ్యక్తుల వ్యక్తిగత కథలు మరియు ప్రముఖతలు వివరించడం కోసం సాధారణంగా ప్రయత్నిస్తాయి. అయితే ప్రతి మరణం ప్రాముఖ్యత ఉన్న ప్రాంతీయ డేటా బేస్ లో వివరించబడలేదు, కానీ మొత్తం డేటా సేకరణ విధానం పాండెమిక్ ప్రమాదం విస్ఫోటనం చూపించడానికి సరిపోయే ప్రమాదాన్ని నిర్ణయిస్తుంది.

ఈ పోస్ట్ చెబుతుంది "ఎవరైనా మరణించినా అది కోవిడ్-19 కు సంబంధించినది కాదు", కోవిడ్-19 మరణాలు తప్పుగా నమోదు చేయబడినట్లు అనిపిస్తుంది. సాధారణంగా అధికారిక మరణాల సంఖ్య నిర్ణయించడానికి వైద్యులు ప్రముఖ పాత్ర వహిస్తారు, ఇది సాధారణంగా ఆస్పత్రుల పరిశీలన మరియు నిర్ధారణ పరీక్ష తరువాత జరుగుతుంది. కొంతమంది వ్యక్తులు మరణాల కారణం అయిన వాటికి సంబంధించిన ఇతర వ్యాధులు కూడా కారణం అవుతాయి, కానీ కోవిడ్-19 అంతా ముఖ్యమైన కారణంగా నమోదు చేయబడుతుంది.

చివరిగా, ఈ పోస్ట్ అందుకు వచ్చిన వాదన అనేక వ్యాక్సిన్లు బహుమతి మరియు చికిత్స కంటే కోవిడ్-19 కంటే ఎక్కువ ప్రమాదకరం మరియు ప్రమాదకరంగా ఉంటాయని చెబుతుంది. కోవిడ్-19 ఇన్ఫ్లూంజా కంటే వేరైన వైరస్ కారణంగా ఉంటుంది మరియు విస్ఫోటనం విధంగా ఉంటుంది. కోవిడ్-19 కోసం అనుమతించబడిన వ్యాక్సిన్లు విస్తృత పరీక్ష మరియు పరిశీలన కోసం ప్రయత్నించాయి, ఇవి ప్రమాదకరమైన ప్రమాదాలు సాధారణంగా కొంచెం ఉంటాయి. వ్యాక్సిన్ కంటే కోవిడ్-19 చాలా విస్ఫోటనం మరియు మరణాలకు కారణం అయింది, ఇది వ్యాక్సిన్ విస్టార్ కు ముందు కూడా విస్టార్ కు చేరింది.

కొన్ని సార్లు, సోషల్ మీడియా పోస్ట్ చేసిన వాదనలు కోవిడ్-19 విషయంలో స్థాపించిన వాస్తవాలు, ఇంకా వ్యాక్సిన్ సురక్షితత్వం మరియు ప్రభావవంతత్వం విషయంలో స్థాపించిన వాస్తవాలతో అనుగుణం కాదు. ఈ పాండెమిక్ ఒక వాస్తవం మరియు ప్రముఖమైన ప్రపంచ ఆరోగ్య సమస్య అయినప్పటికీ, ఇది అంటువ్యాధి కోసం ఉపయోగించిన ఉపకరణాలు - వ్యాక్సిన్ వంటివి - విప్లవ సమాజం పై విప్లవ సమాజం ఆధారంగా నిరూపించబడిన శాస్త్రీయ సమాచారం మరియు విస్టార్ పరీక్షలపై ఆధారపడి ఉన్నాయి.

A recent social media post claims, “Here is how a doctor receives a vaccine, first in the left shoulder, then in the right shoulder on the same day.” This assertion raises questions about standard medical practices for vaccine administration, particularly regarding the number of doses, the anatomical site, and the timing of injections.

To begin, vaccines are typically administered via intramuscular injection, most often into the deltoid muscle of the upper arm. Medical guidelines and protocols are designed to ensure both the efficacy and safety of vaccinations. For most routine vaccines, a single dose is given in one arm, although in some cases—such as during multi-vaccine appointments or for certain vaccines requiring more than one injection simultaneously—a patient may receive more than one shot during the same visit.

However, receiving two doses of the same vaccine in both shoulders on the same day is not standard medical practice. Most vaccines, including commonly administered ones like the influenza, COVID-19, and hepatitis vaccines, require only one dose per visit or, when a multi-dose series is needed, the doses are spaced out over days, weeks, or months. The exception is when a patient is receiving different vaccines at the same appointment. For example, during a well-child visit, multiple vaccines may be scheduled for the same day, with each administered in a different arm to reduce discomfort and facilitate identification in case of an adverse reaction.

For adult patients, some vaccines such as the COVID-19 vaccine may be administered alongside another vaccine, like the flu shot, during a single visit. In such cases, the injections are typically given in opposite arms, but each arm receives a different vaccine, not two doses of the same vaccine. Medical professionals are trained to ensure that the same vaccine is not administered twice in one day, as this could constitute an overdose and potentially lead to increased risk of adverse reactions.

The social media post does not specify which vaccine is being referenced, nor does it clarify whether the doctor is receiving two separate vaccines or two doses of the same vaccine. If the scenario described involves two doses of the same vaccine administered in each shoulder on the same day, this would be inconsistent with established vaccination protocols. Alternatively, if the doctor is receiving two different vaccines—one in each arm—this would align with accepted medical practice for co-administration, as recommended by health authorities.

In summary, the claim that a doctor receives a vaccine “first in the left shoulder, then in the right shoulder on the same day” is misleading unless it refers to the administration of two different vaccines. Receiving two doses of the same vaccine on the same day, one in each arm, does not reflect standard practice and may pose unnecessary risks. For individuals scheduled to receive multiple vaccines, medical staff will typically administer each vaccine in a separate arm when possible, but never more than the recommended dose of any single vaccine in one appointment. Patients are advised to consult qualified healthcare professionals if they have concerns about vaccine administration procedures.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that, as part of repressive measures designed to force vaccination, North Macedonia is refusing to hospitalize unvaccinated individuals. The post further asserts that this policy results in a "double profit" for the unvaccinated, though it does not clarify what such a profit entails. This article examines the veracity of these claims by evaluating government policies, available public health data, and the context of COVID-19 vaccine mandates in North Macedonia.

Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, many countries implemented various strategies to encourage vaccine uptake, ranging from public information campaigns to vaccine mandates for certain professions or activities. Some countries considered or enacted restrictions on access to public spaces for unvaccinated individuals, particularly during periods of high transmission. However, the claim that North Macedonia or any other government is systematically refusing to hospitalize unvaccinated people is a serious allegation that warrants closer scrutiny.

First, no official policy in North Macedonia prohibits hospitals from providing care to the unvaccinated. The country's Ministry of Health has repeatedly stated that access to emergency medical care, hospitalization, and treatment for COVID-19 or any other condition remains available to all citizens, regardless of their vaccination status. During the height of the pandemic, North Macedonia's healthcare system, like those in other nations, experienced severe strain due to rising case numbers and limited resources. In such situations, hospitals sometimes had to triage patients based on the severity of their condition and the availability of beds, but triage decisions have been based on clinical urgency, not vaccination status.

Additionally, there have been no credible reports from international organizations, local health authorities, or reputable news outlets confirming that unvaccinated individuals are being systematically refused hospitalization in North Macedonia. Medical ethics and international law require that emergency healthcare be provided without discrimination, and there is no evidence that these standards have been officially breached in the country.

The notion of a "double profit" for the unvaccinated is unclear and not substantiated within the post. It may imply that unvaccinated individuals somehow benefit by avoiding both vaccination and hospitalization, but this interpretation is speculative. In reality, unvaccinated individuals face a higher risk of severe illness and hospitalization from COVID-19, as demonstrated by global and local health data.

In conclusion, the claim that North Macedonia has implemented a policy of refusing hospitalization to unvaccinated people as a coercive measure is unfounded. Available evidence indicates that healthcare access remains open to all, regardless of vaccination status. While governments have encouraged vaccination to protect public health, refusing essential medical care based on vaccination status would contradict both medical ethics and legal obligations. Social media users should be cautious about unverified claims that can spread misinformation and undermine public trust in healthcare systems.

कोरोना वायरस महामारी के दौरान, कई देशों ने वैक्सीन लेने के प्रोत्साहन के लिए विभिन्न रणनीतियों को अपनाया, जैसे कि सार्वजनिक सूचना अभियान या निश्चित व्यवसायों या गतिविधियों के लिए टीका आवश्यकता के लिए। कुछ देशों ने अटीका वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए पब्लिक स्थानों पर प्रतिबंध लगाने की बात विचार की या उनको लागू कर दिया गया, विशेष रूप से उच्च प्रसार अवधि के दौरान। हालांकि, उत्तर मैकेडोनिया या किसी अन्य सरकार के अटीका वाले व्यक्तियों को अस्पताल में भर्ती न करने के दावे के आरोप के आधार पर एक गंभीर आरोप है जिसकी गहरी जांच की आवश्यकता है।

पहले, उत्तर मैकेडोनिया में कोई आधिकारिक नीति नहीं है जो अस्पतालों को अटीका वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए चिकित्सा सेवा प्रदान करने से रोकती है। देश के स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय ने बार बार कहा है कि आपातकालीन चिकित्सा सेवा, अस्पतालीकरण और कोरोना वायरस या किसी अन्य बीमारी के लिए उपचार सभी नागरिकों के लिए उपलब्ध है, चाहे वे टीकाकरण के लिए अटीका हों या नहीं। महामारी के शिखर पर, उत्तर मैकेडोनिया के स्वास्थ्य चिकित्सा प्रणाली के जैसे अन्य देशों की तरह उत्पन्न मामलों की बढ़ती संख्या और सीमित संसाधनों के कारण भारी दबाव था। इस तरह के स्थितियों में, अस्पतालों को बार बार रोगी के गंभीरता के आधार पर बेड की उपलब्धता के अनुसार रोगियों को आपातकालीन चिकित्सा सेवा देने के लिए त्रिएज निर्णय लेने पड़े, लेकिन इन निर्णयों का आधार चिकित्सा आवश्यकता की गंभीरता नहीं बल्कि वैक्सीनेशन के अवस्था पर आधारित रहे हैं।

इसके अलावा, अंतरराष्ट्रीय संगठनों, स्थानीय स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियों या विश्वसनीय समाचार संस्थानों के कोई विश्वसनीय रिपोर्ट नहीं हैं जो बताते हैं कि अटीका वाले व्यक्तियों को उत्तर मैकेडोनिया में प्रणालीसह अस्पतालीकरण के लिए रोक दिया जा रहा है। आपातकालीन चिकित्सा सेवा के बिना भेदभाव बिना दिया जाए इस विषय पर चिकित्सा नैतिकता और अंतरराष्ट्रीय कानून के आवश्यकताएं हैं, और देश में इन मानदंडों के उल्लंघन के बारे में कोई सबूत नहीं है।

"द्वितीय लाभ" के बारे में धारणा स्पष्ट नहीं है और पोस्ट में समर्थन नहीं है। इसका अर्थ हो सकता है कि अटीका वाले व्यक्ति टीका लेने और अस्पताल में भर्ती न करने से दोनों लाभ प्राप्त करते हैं, लेकिन यह अनुमान अनुमानित है। वास्तविकता में, अटीका वाले व्यक्ति को कोरोना वायरस से गंभीर बीमारी और अस्पतालीकरण के अधिक खतरा होता है, जैसा कि वैश्विक और स्थानीय स्वास्थ्य डेटा दिखाते हैं।

निष्कर्ष में, उत्तर मैकेडोनिया में अटीका वाले व्यक्तियों को अस्पताल में भर्ती न करने की नीति के आरोप के आधार पर आधार नहीं है। उपलब्ध साक्ष्य इंगित करते हैं कि स्वास्थ्य सेवा सभी के लिए खुली रहती है, चाहे वे टीकाकरण के लिए अटीका हों या नहीं। हालांकि सरकारों ने सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य के संरक्षण के लिए टीकाकरण के प्रोत्साहन किया है, लेकिन टीकाकरण के आधार पर आवश्यक चिकित्सा सेवा के अनुमति के लिए यह चिकित्सा नैतिकता और कानूनी बाध्यताओं के खिलाफ होगा। सोशल मीडिया उपयोगकर्ता अनुचित दावों के लिए जांच करने के लिए सावधान रहें क्योंकि यह गलत सूचना के प्रसार को बढ़ावा दे सकते हैं और स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली में जनता के भरोसे को कम कर सकते हैं।

A recent social media post has sparked concern and confusion among residents of Skopje, North Macedonia, claiming that “more than 200 flights on Camtrail over Skopje” have sprayed the area with “unknown chemicals,” and that this alleged activity has gone unreported by television or mainstream media. The post raises questions about transparency, public health, and the spread of information in the digital age. To address these concerns, it is necessary to examine the claim in detail, analyze available evidence, and provide context regarding the topic of so-called “chemtrails.”

The core assertion in the post is twofold: first, that over 200 flights have passed over Skopje in a single day, dispersing unknown substances; and second, that this activity is being intentionally ignored by the media. This claim ties into the longstanding “chemtrail” conspiracy theory, which suggests that governments or other organizations are deliberately dispersing chemicals into the atmosphere for nefarious purposes, often citing visible trails left by airplanes as evidence.

To evaluate the first part of the claim, it is important to understand normal aviation activity over Skopje. The city is home to an international airport and is located along several major flight paths connecting Europe, the Middle East, and beyond. It is not uncommon for dozens or even hundreds of flights to traverse the airspace above Skopje daily, especially when accounting for both commercial and cargo traffic. The trails often observed in the sky—known as contrails (short for condensation trails)—are formed when hot, humid air from jet engines mixes with colder air at high altitudes, creating visible streaks of water vapor or ice crystals. These are a normal byproduct of aviation and are well understood by atmospheric scientists.

The claim that these flights are “spraying unknown chemicals” lacks credible evidence. No substantiated scientific studies or official reports support the existence of a coordinated effort to disperse harmful chemicals over populated areas from commercial or military aircraft. The substances composing contrails are primarily water vapor, with trace amounts of other engine byproducts. While air pollution from aviation is a legitimate concern, it differs significantly from the notion of deliberate chemical spraying.

The second part of the social media claim suggests a media blackout on this alleged phenomenon. In practice, mainstream media outlets report on events and issues substantiated by evidence or of significant public interest. The absence of coverage on “chemtrail” spraying over Skopje reflects the lack of credible evidence supporting such events, rather than a coordinated effort to suppress information.

Misinformation about “chemtrails” has circulated online for decades, often gaining traction in times of uncertainty or when people observe unusual weather patterns. It is understandable that visible phenomena like contrails can prompt questions, especially if people are not familiar with atmospheric science. However, the preponderance of scientific understanding and available data does not support the claim that Skopje, or any other city, is subject to mass chemical spraying by aircraft.

In conclusion, while the social media post reflects real concerns about transparency and environmental safety, the specific claims regarding 200 “Camtrail” flights and chemical spraying over Skopje are not supported by credible evidence. The visible trails in the sky are a routine result of air traffic and atmospheric conditions, and the lack of media coverage corresponds to the scientific consensus on the issue. Residents are encouraged to seek information from authoritative sources and remain critical of extraordinary claims that lack substantiation.

Ce post soulève des questions sur la transparence, la santé publique et la diffusion de l'information à l'ère numérique. Pour répondre à ces préoccupations, il est nécessaire d'examiner la revendication en détail, d'analyser les preuves disponibles et de fournir un contexte concernant le sujet des « traînées chimiques ».

L'assertion centrale du post est double : d'abord, que plus de 200 vols ont traversé Skopje en une seule journée, dispersant des substances inconnues ; et ensuite, que cette activité est intentionnellement ignorée par les médias. Cette revendication s'inscrit dans la théorie du complot des « traînées chimiques », qui suggère que des gouvernements ou d'autres organisations dispersent délibérément des produits chimiques dans l'atmosphère à des fins nuisibles, souvent en citant les traînées visibles laissées par les avions comme preuve.

Pour évaluer la première partie de cette revendication, il est important de comprendre l'activité aérienne normale au-dessus de Skopje. La ville abrite un aéroport international et se trouve le long de plusieurs itinéraires aériens majeurs reliant l'Europe, le Moyen-Orient et au-delà. Il est courant que des dizaines, voire des centaines de vols traversent l'espace aérien au-dessus de Skopje quotidiennement, surtout lorsqu'on tient compte à la fois du trafic commercial et du fret. Les traînées souvent observées dans le ciel, connues sous le nom de « traînées de condensation » (abrégé en « traînées »), se forment lorsque l'air chaud et humide des moteurs d'avion se mélange à l'air plus froid à haute altitude, créant des bandes visibles de vapeur d'eau ou de cristaux de glace. Ce sont un produit normal de l'aviation et sont bien connus par les scientifiques de l'atmosphère.

La revendication selon laquelle ces vols « pulvérisent des substances inconnues » ne possède pas de preuves crédibles. Aucune étude scientifique avérée ou rapport officiel ne soutient l'existence d'une tentative coordonnée pour disperser des produits chimiques nuisibles sur les zones habitées à partir d'avions commerciaux ou militaires. Les substances composant les traînées de condensation sont principalement de la vapeur d'eau, avec des quantités traces d'autres sous-produits des moteurs. Bien que la pollution de l'air liée à l'aviation soit une préoccupation légitime, elle diffère considérablement de l'idée d'une pulvérisation délibérée de produits chimiques.

La seconde partie de la revendication sur les réseaux sociaux suggère un manque de couverture médiatique sur ce phénomène allégué. En pratique, les médias d'information principaux rapportent des événements et des questions qui sont avérés ou d'intérêt public significatif. L'absence de couverture sur la « pulvérisation de traînées chimiques » au-dessus de Skopje reflète l'absence de preuves crédibles de tels événements, plutôt qu'une tentative coordonnée de censurer l'information.

L'information erronée sur les « traînées chimiques » circule en ligne depuis des décennies, souvent gagnant en popularité pendant les périodes de doute ou lorsque les gens observent des phénomènes météorologiques inhabituels. Il est compréhensible que des phénomènes visibles comme les traînées de condensation puissent susciter des questions, surtout si les gens ne sont pas familiers avec la science atmosphérique. Cependant, le prédominant des connaissances scientifiques et des données disponibles ne soutient pas la revendication selon laquelle Skopje, ou toute autre ville, est soumise à une pulvérisation massive de produits chimiques par les avions.

En conclusion, bien que le post sur les réseaux sociaux reflète des préoccupations réelles concernant la transparence et la sécurité environnementale, les revendications spécifiques concernant les 200 « vols Camtrail » et la pulvérisation de substances chimiques au-dessus de Skopje ne sont pas soutenues par des preuves crédibles. Les traînées visibles dans le ciel sont un résultat courant du trafic aérien et des conditions atmosphériques, et l'absence de couverture médiatique correspond à la consensus scientifique sur le sujet. Les résidents sont encouragés à consulter des sources autoritatives et à rester critiques face aux revendications extraordinaires qui manquent de preuves.

A recent social media post claims that injections offered as vaccines are “something completely different,” suggesting they may have nefarious effects, such as making people “habitually” dependent on needles and even metaphorically “turning you into needles.” The post continues to assert that individuals who received vaccines are now sick again and allegedly dying from the very disease they were vaccinated against. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context and fact-based analysis.

**Background on Vaccines and Injections**

Vaccines have been a cornerstone of public health for over a century. They are designed to stimulate the body’s immune system to recognize and combat pathogens, such as viruses or bacteria, often by introducing a harmless component of the pathogen (like a protein or an inactivated virus). Standard regulatory and safety protocols govern the production and administration of vaccines, and they are subject to rigorous testing before approval for public use.

**Analysis of the Claim: “Vaccines are something completely different”**

The claim that vaccines offered “as an excuse” are actually “something completely different” is vague and not supported by any evidence. The composition and purpose of vaccines, especially those developed for COVID-19, influenza, and other diseases, are well-documented and publicly available. Regulatory agencies require detailed disclosure of ingredients, mechanisms of action, and clinical trial results.

The suggestion that vaccines are being misrepresented or are delivering unknown substances is a common theme in vaccine misinformation but lacks substantiation. Ingredients in vaccines are not secret, and there is no credible evidence to suggest that vaccines contain hidden substances or are designed for purposes other than disease prevention.

**Claim: “Vaccines will become your habit, will turn you into needles”**

The statement that vaccines will become a “habit” and metaphorically “turn you into needles” seems to play on fears of dependency or addiction. Vaccines are generally administered on a schedule determined by public health authorities based on the nature of the disease and immunity duration. For example, annual flu shots are recommended because influenza strains change year to year. COVID-19 vaccines have required boosters due to waning immunity and emerging variants.

However, receiving recommended vaccine boosters is not a sign of addiction or habit but rather a public health measure, similar to routine dental checkups or seasonal allergy medication. There is no mechanism in vaccines that creates physical or psychological dependency.

**Claim: “The vaccinated are sick again and allegedly dying of the disease they were vaccinated against”**

Breakthrough infections—cases where vaccinated individuals contract the disease—can occur, especially as immunity wanes or new variants emerge. However, extensive data show that vaccinated individuals are significantly less likely to experience severe illness, hospitalization, or death compared to unvaccinated individuals. Vaccines are not 100% effective at preventing all infections, but they remain highly effective at reducing the most serious outcomes.

Claims of widespread death among vaccinated individuals from the same disease are not supported by available public health data. Reports of deaths following vaccination are investigated thoroughly, and no evidence has established a causal link between receiving a vaccine and dying from the targeted disease at rates higher than in unvaccinated populations.

**Conclusion**

The social media post in question repeats several commonly circulated but unsubstantiated claims regarding vaccines. Vaccines are rigorously tested, transparent in their composition, and proven to reduce the severity and incidence of infectious diseases. While breakthrough infections can occur, the vast majority of serious cases and deaths occur among the unvaccinated. There is no evidence to suggest that vaccines are addictive, habit-forming, or misrepresented in their purpose or content.

A viral social media post claims that breastfeeding mothers who receive vaccinations “kill their newborns,” raising alarm and confusion among new mothers and their families. This article examines the claim, providing context from medical experts and public health guidance to determine its accuracy.

The post’s wording suggests that vaccinated breastfeeding mothers are directly responsible for the deaths of their newborns, implying that vaccines are lethal when transmitted through breast milk. This statement is not only alarming but also runs counter to the guidance provided by leading health organizations worldwide.

First, it is important to understand the purpose of recommending vaccinations for breastfeeding mothers. Vaccines are designed to protect individuals and those around them from infectious diseases. For many vaccines, including those developed for COVID-19, influenza, and other common illnesses, public health agencies have specifically studied their safety profiles in pregnant and breastfeeding women. The overwhelming consensus is that these vaccines are safe for both mother and baby.

When a breastfeeding mother is vaccinated, her body produces antibodies against the targeted disease. Some of these antibodies can pass through breast milk, potentially providing additional protection for the infant, whose immune system is still developing. There is no evidence that vaccines themselves, or any harmful components, are secreted into breast milk in quantities that could harm a newborn. Instead, the transfer of antibodies is considered beneficial and may even reduce the risk of infection in young infants.

The claim that vaccinated breastfeeding mothers “kill their newborns” is not supported by scientific evidence. Large-scale surveillance and post-marketing studies have not found an increased risk of mortality or severe adverse effects among infants breastfed by vaccinated mothers. Health authorities, including governmental and international organizations, monitor vaccine safety closely and would issue warnings if credible evidence supported any such risk.

It is also critical to recognize the damage that misinformation can cause. The spread of such claims may discourage mothers from receiving vaccines, potentially leaving both mothers and infants vulnerable to serious, preventable diseases. Vaccine hesitancy fueled by unfounded fears can undermine public health efforts and lead to outbreaks of diseases previously kept in check by widespread immunization.

In summary, the claim that breastfeeding mothers “kill their newborns” by receiving vaccinations is false and unsupported by scientific research. Vaccination during breastfeeding is considered safe and, in some cases, beneficial for the newborn. Mothers are encouraged to consult with healthcare providers for accurate information and guidance regarding vaccines during breastfeeding.

A claim circulating on social media alleges that Covid-19’s “primary goal is to establish a new world order.” This assertion suggests that the global pandemic was either engineered or manipulated with the intent of restructuring world power or governance. In this article, we examine the origins of this claim, provide context about the pandemic, and evaluate the available evidence.

The phrase “new world order” is often used in conspiracy theories to describe a supposed secret plan among powerful elites to establish an authoritarian global government. These theories have been linked to various events throughout history, especially times of crisis or uncertainty, such as wars, economic downturns, or pandemics.

Covid-19, a respiratory illness caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, was first identified in late 2019 in Wuhan, China. Since then, it has caused widespread illness, loss of life, and significant disruptions to societies and economies worldwide. In response, governments have implemented public health measures such as lockdowns, travel restrictions, and vaccination campaigns. International organizations such as the World Health Organization have coordinated global responses to the pandemic.

The claim that Covid-19’s “primary goal” is to establish a new world order implies intentionality behind the pandemic, either from the virus itself or from human actors. Scientifically, viruses do not have goals; they are biological entities that spread and mutate according to natural processes. The overwhelming consensus among epidemiologists and virologists is that SARS-CoV-2 likely emerged from a natural zoonotic spillover, meaning it jumped from animals to humans, as has happened with other viruses in the past.

Some proponents of the “new world order” theory point to the unprecedented government interventions and global coordination during Covid-19 as evidence of a larger agenda. For example, they cite restrictions on movement, mandates for digital health passes, and changes in economic policy as steps toward centralized control. However, public health experts and policymakers explain that these measures were enacted in response to the urgent need to control the spread of a novel, deadly virus and to protect public health.

No credible evidence supports the claim that Covid-19 was intentionally released or used as a tool to implement a global authoritarian regime. Investigations into the origins of the virus have not found proof of deliberate engineering for such a purpose. The measures introduced during the pandemic have been widely debated and, in many countries, subject to democratic processes and legal challenges.

In conclusion, while the claim that Covid-19’s “primary goal is to establish a new world order” taps into longstanding fears of global conspiracies, it lacks a factual basis. The pandemic has prompted extraordinary responses from governments and societies, but these actions reflect efforts to manage a public health crisis rather than evidence of a covert plan to reshape world governance. As with any major global event, it is important to critically evaluate extraordinary claims and rely on verifiable evidence.

В социалните мрежи се циркулира тврдба, според която „основна цел на ковид-19 е да се установи нова светска редовна система“. Ова изјава подразбира, дека глобалниот пандемичен кризис е или еднакво измислен, или е направен со намера да се промени светската моќ или управувањето. Во овој член, ја истражуваме порочната настана на оваа тврдба, даваме контекст за пандемијата и ја евалуираме достапната доказа.

Фразата „нова светска редовна система“ често се користи во конспиративни теории за да се опише таа претпоставена тајна план на моќни елита за да се установи авторитарна светска влада. Овие теории се поврзани со различни настани во историјата, особено во времиња на криза или несигурност, како што се војни, економски спадови или пандемии.

Ковид-19, дишна болест која е предизвикана од новиот коронавирус SARS-CoV-2, беше прво идентифициран во крајот на 2019 година во Вухан, Кина. Од тогаш, тоа доведе до широка болест, загуба на животи и значителни нарушувања на друштвата и икономиите по цел свет. Во одговор, владини премиери имплементираа здравствени мерки како што се локални затвори, ограничување на патувањето и кампанија за вакцинација. Меѓународни организации како што е Светската здравствена организација (СЗО) координираат глобални одговори на пандемијата.

Тврдбата дека „основна цел“ на ковид-19 е да се установи нова светска редовна система има подразбирање на намера зад пандемијата, или од самата вирус, или од човечки агенти. Научно, вирусите немаат цели; тие се биолошки ентуитети кои се распространуваат и мутираат според природни процеси. Поголемиот консензус меѓу епидемиолозите и вирусологите е дека SARS-CoV-2 веројатно е излезал од природна зоонозна спиловер, што значи дека е прескакнат од животни на човечките, како што е било случај со други вируси во минатото.

Некои проповедници на теоријата за „нова светска редовна система“ го цитираат неочекуваните владини интервенции и глобална координација по време на ковид-19 како доказ за постоење на постоечки план. На пример, ги цитираат ограничувањето на движењето, обврзите за цифрови здравствени сертификати и промени во икономската политика како чекори кон централизирано управување. Меѓутоа, здравствени експерти и политичари објаснуваат дека овие мерки се воведени во одговор на утврдената потреба да се контролира распространувањето на нов, опасен вирус и за заштита на јавното здравство.

Нема достоверни докази кои поддржуваат тврдбата дека ковид-19 е намерено испуштен или користен како инструмент за имплементирање на глобален авторитарен режим. Инспекцијата за порочната настана на вирусот не е пронашла докази за намерен инженерски дизајн за таква цел. Мерките воведени по време на пандемијата се широко дискутирани и во многу земји се подвргнуваат на демократски процеси и правни прашања.

Во заклучок, доколку тврдбата дека „основна цел на ковид-19 е да се установи нова светска редовна система“ се врз основа на долготрајни страхи од глобални конспирации, тоа не има фактичка основа. Пандемијата ја извокала неочекувани одговори од влади и друштва, но овие акции се резултат на општествени напори да се управува со јавно здравствено криза, а не докази за тајен план да се промени светското управување. Како и со секој голем глобален настан, е важно да се критички процесираат неочекувани тврдби и да се користат докази кои се потврдени.

Reports have recently circulated on social media claiming that North Macedonia has documented its first case of a person infected with Covid-19 for a third time. This claim has sparked considerable attention and concern among the public, raising questions about the nature of Covid-19 reinfections and the current situation in North Macedonia.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to understand the medical and epidemiological context surrounding Covid-19 reinfection. Since the beginning of the pandemic, it has been established that most individuals who contract Covid-19 develop some level of immune response, which can provide protection against future infections. However, it is also known that immunity can wane over time, and new variants of the virus may partially evade previously acquired immunity, making reinfections possible.

Globally, cases of individuals testing positive for Covid-19 more than once have been documented since at least 2020. The majority of reinfections involve a second episode, often months after the initial infection. Third infections are considerably rarer but have been reported in several countries, particularly as the virus has mutated and new variants such as Omicron have become prevalent. Factors such as underlying health conditions, age, immune system function, and vaccination status can influence susceptibility to reinfection.

In North Macedonia, the health authorities have monitored suspected cases of reinfection, especially as the pandemic has progressed and the population has experienced multiple waves of Covid-19. While instances of double reinfection have been recorded, the claim of a third infection — that is, one individual testing positive for Covid-19 three separate times — would mark a notable development in the country’s pandemic records.

Upon investigation, local health officials have confirmed that there is indeed a documented case of a person in North Macedonia being infected with Covid-19 for a third time. According to available information, the individual had previously recovered from two separate confirmed episodes of Covid-19 and recently tested positive for a third time. This person’s case was reviewed by epidemiologists to rule out false positives, chronic infection, or prolonged viral shedding, which can sometimes be mistaken for reinfection. The intervals between the episodes and the presence of symptomatic illness during each infection were key factors in determining this as a true third reinfection case.

This occurrence aligns with global trends, where third infections, though rare, have been observed as the coronavirus evolves. It highlights the ongoing challenges posed by Covid-19, including the limits of natural and vaccine-induced immunity and the importance of ongoing surveillance. Health experts in North Macedonia emphasize that such cases, while uncommon, reinforce the need for booster vaccinations, adherence to public health guidelines, and continued vigilance.

In summary, the social media claim that North Macedonia has recorded its first case of a person infected with Covid-19 for the third time is accurate. It reflects a broader global phenomenon and serves as a reminder of the unpredictable nature of the virus and the importance of robust public health measures.

Nuo pandemijos pradžios yra įrodyta, kad dauguma žmonių, susikrovę virusą, kuriuos infekcija atsiranda, susiformuoja tam tikras imuninės atsparumo lygmenys, kurie gali apsaugoti nuo ateityje galimų infekcijų. Tačiau taip pat žinoma, kad imuninė atsparumas gali prarasti savo jėgą laikui bėgant, o nauji viruso variantai gali dalimis išvengti iš anksto susikrovoto imuninio atsparumo, todėl atkūrimas yra galimas.

Pasauliniu lygmeniu atkūrimų atvejai, kai žmogus išgyvena daugiau nei vieną Covid-19 infekciją, buvo įrašyti nuo 2020 metų. Dauguma atkūrimų apima antrąją infekciją, dažnai mėnesius po pirmosios. Trečiosios infekcijos yra labai retos, tačiau jie buvo pranešti keliuose šalyse, ypač kai virusas mutavo ir nauji variantai, tokie kaip Omicronas, tapo populiarūs. Susiję su atkūrimu veiksniai, tokie kaip esminės sveikatos problemas, amžius, imuninės sistemos veiklos lygis ir vakcinacijos būklė, gali veikti atkūrimo tikimybę.

Šiaurės Makedonijoje sveikatos institucijos stebėjo įtariamus atkūrimo atvejus, ypač kai pandemija klostėsi ir populiacija patyrė kelis Covid-19 bangas. Nors dvigubo atkūrimo atvejai buvo įrašyti, trečiojo atkūrimo – t. y. vieno žmogaus trikartinės Covid-19 infekcijos – įrašymas būtų svarbus šalies pandemijos istorijoje.

Po tyrimo vietos sveikatos oficialiai patvirtino, kad šiaurės Makedonijoje yra įrašytas atvejis, kai žmogus buvo infekcijos su Covid-19 trečią kartą. Pagal prieinamą informaciją, šis asmuo anksčiau išgyveno dvi atskirus patvirtintus Covid-19 infekcijos atvejus ir nedidelio laiko atėjus, vėl buvo teigiamas testas. Šio asmeninio atvejo buvo peržiūrėti epidemiologai, kad būtų išvengta klaidingų teigiamų rezultatų, chroniškų infekcijų ar ilgalaikio viruso išsiskirstymo klaidų, kurios kartais gali būti palaikomos kaip atkūrimas. Tarp epizodų intervalai ir simptomų buvimas kiekvienoje infekcijoje buvo svarbūs veiksniai, nustatant šį atvejį kaip tikrą trečią atkūrimo atvejį.

Šis įvykis atitinka pasaulinius trendus, kuriuose trečiosios infekcijos, nors retos, yra pastebėtos, kai koronavirusas evoliucijos. Jis atskleidžia tęstinį Covid-19 sukeltus iššūkius, įskaitant natūralaus ir vakcinacijos sukurtų imuninio atsparumo ribas ir svarbą nuolatinių stebėjimo sistemų. Šiaurės Makedonijos sveikatos ekspertai pabrėžia, kad tokie atvejai, nors reti, primena reikalingumą papildomų vakcinacijų, laikytis sveikatos apsaugos rekomendacijų ir tęsti pasitikėjimą.

Claims have circulated on social media suggesting that politicians and VIP individuals receive imitation versions of vaccines, rather than the authentic doses administered to the general public. This assertion taps into longstanding public skepticism about elites receiving preferential treatment, especially during major public health crises. To address this claim, it is important to consider the origins of such rumors, the procedures in place for vaccine administration, and any available evidence supporting or refuting the idea.

The context for these allegations often emerges during mass vaccination campaigns, such as those seen during the COVID-19 pandemic. During this period, vaccines were rolled out globally at an unprecedented speed. In many countries, politicians and high-profile figures received their vaccine shots in public, often broadcasted on television or streamed online. The intent was to build public trust in the vaccines and encourage uptake by demonstrating their safety and efficacy.

Despite these efforts, skepticism persisted. Some social media users began circulating videos and images purporting to show inconsistencies during these public vaccinations—such as syringes with covered needles, unclear vials, or camera angles that obscured the process. These posts often concluded, without concrete proof, that the individuals involved were not receiving real vaccines but instead saline or another harmless imitation.

Examining the logistics of vaccine administration provides important context. Vaccination programs, especially those involving public officials, are typically conducted under strict medical supervision. The process is usually overseen by healthcare professionals trained in proper handling and administration. Vaccines are usually drawn from the same batches supplied to the wider population, and the chain of custody is maintained to ensure safety and authenticity.

There have, however, been rare instances where officials have been accused of bypassing standard protocols. These isolated cases, though, usually involve queue-jumping or early access rather than substitution with imitation vaccines. Investigations into such incidents have rarely found evidence that VIPs receive fake or saline shots in place of real vaccines.

Fact-checking organizations and health authorities have repeatedly addressed these claims. They point out that there is no credible, documented evidence to support the idea that imitation vaccines are systematically administered to politicians or celebrities. Mistakes in the administration process—such as improper technique or camera misdirection—have occasionally occurred, but these are not proof of intentional deception.

The spread of such claims can be attributed to a mix of factors, including distrust of authorities, viral misinformation, and isolated incidents misrepresented as widespread practice. The visual ambiguity of some vaccination videos also fuels suspicion, despite the lack of substantiating evidence.

In conclusion, the assertion that politicians and VIPs systematically receive imitation vaccines does not hold up under scrutiny. While skepticism is natural, especially in times of crisis, available evidence and standard medical procedures indicate that high-profile individuals receive the same vaccines as the general public. The perpetuation of this claim appears to be based more on speculation and misinterpretation than on verifiable fact.

ਇਹ ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ਾਂ ਹਾਲਾਂ ਵੀ ਸ਼ੱਕ ਦੀ ਮੌਜੂਦਗੀ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ। ਕੁਝ ਸੋਸ਼ਲ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਉਪਭੋਗਕ ਇਹ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਅਤੇ ਛੋਟੇ ਛੇਤੀ ਛੇਤੀ ਤਸਵੀਰਾਂ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ ਜੋ ਇਸ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਅਸਥਿਰਤਾ ਦਾ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਕਿਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਸੀਟੀ, ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਏ ਵੈਲੀਅਮ ਅਤੇ ਕੈਮਰਾ ਦੇ ਕੋਣ ਜੋ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਛੁਪਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਹ ਪੋਸਟ ਆਮ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸਪੱਸ਼ਟ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਸੰਬੰਧਿਤ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਲਕਿ ਸੈਲੀਨ ਜਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਹਾਨੀਕਾਰਕ ਨਕਲੀ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਦੀ ਵੰਡ ਦੀ ਲੋਗਿਸਟਿਕਸ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਨਾ ਇਸ ਸਾਰੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇ ਲਈ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ। ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ, ਖਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਜਦੋਂ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਸ਼ਾਸਨ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਤਾਂ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਤਹਿਤ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਿਗਿਆਨੀਆਂ ਦੁਆਰਾ ਨਿਯੰਤ੍ਰਿਤ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਦੀ ਸਹੀ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ। ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਆਮ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਹੀ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਦੀ ਸੀਰੀਜ਼ ਨੂੰ ਬਰਕਰਾਰ ਰੱਖਦੇ ਹਨ।

ਹਾਲਾਂ ਕਿ, ਕੁਝ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਧਿਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਮਾਨਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਦੀ ਛੋਟ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਆਰੋਪ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਹ ਛੋਟੇ ਮਾਮਲੇ, ਹਾਲਾਂ ਕਿ, ਸਿਰਫ ਲੈਣ ਦੀ ਛੋਟ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਦੀ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਹੀ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ, ਨਕਲੀ ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਦੇ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਨੂੰ ਬਦਲਣ ਦੇ ਨਹੀਂ। ਇਸ ਵਿਸ਼ੇ 'ਤੇ ਜਾਂਚ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਕਈ ਘਟਨਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਵਿਅਕਤੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਕਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੈਲੀਨ ਸੰਸਕਰਣ ਦੇ ਬਦਲੇ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਹੈ ਦੀ ਕੋਈ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਿਆ।

ਇਹ ਦਾਅਵੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਕਾਰਨਾਂ ਕਾਰਨ ਫੈਲਦੇ ਹਨ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਅਧਿਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਅਸਥਿਰਤਾ, ਵਾਇਰਲ ਗਲਤ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਮਾਮਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਗਲਤ ਵਿਵਰਣ ਨਾਲ ਸਾਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਨ। ਕਈ ਵੈਕਸੀਨ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਿਸ਼ਟ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੀ ਗਲਤ ਦੇਖਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨਿਰੀਖਣ ਵੀ ਸ਼ੱਕ ਨੂੰ ਧੁੰਦਦੇ ਹਨ, ਹਾਲਾਂ ਕਿ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਸੰਭਾਵਨਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਕੋਈ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਣ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।

article_content:
A recent social media post has sparked controversy after alleging that the death of a woman is being misrepresented, with suggestions that her death was caused by a vaccine despite a lack of supporting medical evidence, documentation, or proof that she had even received a vaccination. This claim raises important questions about the responsible reporting of medical information, the spread of misinformation, and the need for factual accuracy in public discourse.

The core assertion in the post is that the woman’s death is being “abused”—that is, used or manipulated to support a narrative linking her passing to vaccination efforts, without any substantiated medical basis. According to the post, there is neither documentation confirming her vaccination status nor medical proof directly implicating a vaccine as the cause of death.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is necessary to explore how deaths are typically investigated and reported in the context of vaccine safety. When an individual dies after receiving a vaccine, health authorities generally undertake a thorough investigation. This includes reviewing the person’s medical records, vaccination history, autopsy reports, and other relevant documentation. Only after careful examination can experts determine if there is a plausible causal relationship between the vaccine and the death.

In this case, the post alleges a lack of such documentation or evidence, implying that any conclusions about the vaccine’s involvement are premature or unfounded. If there is indeed no verified record that the woman was vaccinated, and no medical evaluation linking the vaccine to her death, then attributing her passing to vaccination is speculative at best. It is crucial to distinguish between temporal association—the fact that an event occurred after vaccination—and causation, which requires robust scientific investigation.

The post also highlights the risks of spreading unsubstantiated claims, particularly in the emotionally charged context of illness and death. Using a tragic event to advance a particular agenda, absent evidence, can contribute to public confusion and erode trust in health authorities and scientific processes. It is especially important during a public health crisis that information about vaccine safety and adverse events is communicated transparently, accurately, and based on thorough investigation.

In summary, the social media post brings attention to a real and pressing issue: the potential for misinformation when deaths are linked to vaccines without proper evidence. The claim that the woman’s death is being misused—without medical basis or documentation to support the connection to vaccination—appears to be founded on the absence of concrete proof. This underscores the need for careful fact-checking and responsible communication, ensuring that public discussion around vaccine safety is guided by facts rather than speculation or insinuation.

A social media post has been circulating, alleging that medical personnel in Australia are intentionally withholding medicine from unvaccinated individuals, leading to their deaths. The post claims, in essence, that unvaccinated patients are being denied necessary treatments for diseases, resulting in fatal outcomes. This assertion has sparked concern and outrage among some communities, prompting a closer examination of the claim’s validity.

To understand the context, it is important to recall that the COVID-19 pandemic placed extraordinary pressure on healthcare systems worldwide, including Australia. During the height of the pandemic, governments and health organizations strongly encouraged vaccination as a key measure to reduce the severity and spread of the virus. Some public health measures, such as vaccine mandates for certain professions or entry to specific venues, were implemented to protect vulnerable populations and maintain healthcare system capacity.

However, the suggestion that medical personnel in Australia are systematically denying unvaccinated individuals life-saving treatment is a serious and concerning allegation. Australia’s healthcare system, both public and private, is regulated by strict ethical and legal standards. Medical professionals are bound by the principles of medical ethics, including providing care without discrimination based on vaccination status, race, religion, or other factors unrelated to clinical need.

Throughout the pandemic, official health guidance in Australia always emphasized that all patients, regardless of vaccination status, should receive appropriate medical care. While some elective procedures were postponed during times of extreme hospital strain, urgent and emergency care remained available to all. In some cases, unvaccinated individuals were at higher risk of severe illness from COVID-19 and thus required more intensive medical intervention. Hospitals and clinics continued to treat these patients according to established clinical protocols, which prioritize medical need and urgency.

There have been occasional reports of frustration among healthcare workers over the increased burden placed on the system by unvaccinated patients. Some unverified anecdotes online have claimed instances of delayed care or negative attitudes. However, there is no substantiated evidence to support the widespread or systematic denial of medicine or treatment to unvaccinated Australians. Regulatory bodies overseeing healthcare professionals in Australia would treat such breaches of duty with utmost seriousness, as they violate professional codes of conduct and the law.

Furthermore, no specific medicine exists that universally “cures the disease” referenced in the post—likely COVID-19. Treatments for COVID-19, including antiviral medications and supportive therapies, are provided based on clinical assessment and eligibility, not solely on vaccination status.

In summary, the claim that medical personnel in Australia are killing unvaccinated individuals by withholding medicine is not supported by credible evidence. Healthcare workers remain committed to treating all patients ethically and professionally, regardless of vaccination status. It is important for the public to rely on verified information and to approach alarming social media posts with a critical eye.

အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို နားလည်ရန် အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ကျန်းမာရေးစနစ်များအား နှိမ်နက်စွာ ဖြစ်ပွားခဲ့သော ကူးစက်မှုကို ပြန်လည်သုံးသပ်ရန် လိုအပ်သည်။ ကူးစက်မှုအရှိန်အဝါကြီးအတွင်း အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ကျန်းမာရေးစနစ်များကို အထူးသဖြင့် အလုပ်သမားများအတွက် ဆေးထိုးခြင်းကို တောင်းဆိုခြင်းနှင့် အခြားနေရာများသို့ ဝင်ရောက်ခြင်းကို တောင်းဆိုခြင်း အပါအဝင် ကူးစက်မှုကို ကန့်သတ်ရန် အစိုးရနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေးအဖွဲ့အစည်းများက မျှော်လင့်ထားခဲ့ကြသည်။ အကျုံးဝင်သော အထူးကုသမှုများကို ကန့်သတ်ခြင်းနှင့် နေထိုင်သူများအား ကာကွယ်ရန် ပြဿနာရှိသော လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်းများကို ကာကွယ်ရန် အတွက် ကျန်းမာရေးစနစ်၏ အရည်အချင်းများကို ထိန်းသိမ်းရန် အစီအစဉ်များကို အကောင်အထည်ဖော်ခဲ့သည်။

သို့သော် အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ကျန်းမာရေးပညာရှင်များက ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား သက်သေများကို ဆိုင်ရာ ကုသမှုများကို ဖျက်သိမ်းခြင်းအား သတ်မှတ်ခြင်းသည် အထူးသဖြင့် အဓိကအားဖြင့် ပြဿနာဖြစ်ပွားခြင်းအား မှတ်တမ်းတင်ခြင်းဖြစ်သည်။ အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ကျန်းမာရေးစနစ် မိမိတို့၏ ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုနှင့် မျှော်လင့်ချက်များအပေါ် အခြေခံကာ ပြဿနာဖြစ်ပွားမှုများအား အမှီအခိုင်အမြဲတည်ထားသည့် အကြံပြုချက်များကို ထိန်းသိမ်းရန် တာဝန်ရှိသည်။ မိမိတို့၏ ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုအပေါ် အခြေခံကာ ရောဂါသည်းခံနိုင်စွမ်းအားနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေးအခြေခံအကြံပြုချက်များအပေါ် အခြေခံကာ တာဝန်ကို ပေးအပ်သည့် ပြဿနာများကို ပေးအပ်ရန် ပြဿနာဖြစ်ပွားခြင်းအား တာဝန်ရှိသည်။

ကူးစက်မှုအရှိန်အဝါကြီးအတွင်း အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ပြဿနာဖြစ်ပွားခြင်းအား အကြံပြုချက်များက ပေးအပ်သည့် အခြေခံအကြံပြုချက်များကို ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသခြင်းများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းကို အပ်နှံခဲ့သည်။ သို့သော် အကြံပြုချက်များကို အထူးသဖြင့် အမှီအခိုင်အမြဲတည်ထားသည့် အကြံပြုချက်များကို ပေးအပ်ခြင်းနှင့် မျှော်လင့်ချက်များကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ပေးအပ်ခြင်းနှင့် ပတ်သက်၍ ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား အကြံပြုချက်များကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား ပေးအပ်ခြင်းများကို ရှိပါသည်။ သို့သော် ကျန်းမာရေး ပညာရှင်များအား ပိုမိုအားကောင်းမွန်စွာ ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား အထူးသဖြင့် ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား ပေးအပ်ခြင်းများကို မှတ်တမ်းတင်ခြင်းမရှိပါ။ အိုးစတားနိုင်ငံတွင် ကျန်းမာရေးပညာရှင်များကို ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား တာဝန်ရှိသည့် စီမံခန့်ခွဲမှုအဖွဲ့များသည် အထူးသဖြင့် ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား ရှိပါက အလွန်အမှန်တကယ် အထူးသဖြင့် အရာရှိတာဝန်များကို အထူးသဖြင့် ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား အကြံပြုချက်များနှင့် ဥပဒေအား အထူးသဖြင့် ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုမရှိသော လူများအား ကုသမှုများကို နှိမ်နက်ခြင်းများအား ဖြစ်ပေါ်စေခြင်းကို တာဝန်ရှိသည်။

A recent social media post circulating widely claims that, as of October 20, 2021, Covid-19 vaccines are no longer needed or mandatory, citing confirmation from authorities. The post further asserts that the European Union (EU) has authorized five therapies for the treatment of Covid-19, which will be available in all hospitals to treat SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes Covid-19). It also claims that vaccines were only permitted as a "temporary experimental device." This article examines these claims in detail, providing context, background information, and a thorough fact-checking analysis.

First, the claim that Covid-19 vaccines would no longer be needed or mandatory from October 20, 2021, is misleading. As of that date, the approach to Covid-19 vaccination policy varied significantly across EU member states and globally. No EU-wide or global health authority announced an end to vaccine recommendations or mandates as of October 2021. Some countries did implement or relax mandates based on changing epidemiological conditions, but vaccination continued to be a cornerstone of public health strategies to control the pandemic. The decision to mandate or recommend vaccination remained under the jurisdiction of individual countries, often taking into account local transmission rates, healthcare capacity, and vaccine uptake.

The post further claims that "the EU has authorized 5 therapies for the treatment of Covid-19, which will be available in all hospitals." While it is true that, throughout 2021, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the European Commission worked to identify and evaluate potential Covid-19 treatments, the process of authorization is rigorous and ongoing. By late 2021, several therapies, such as monoclonal antibodies and antiviral drugs, were under review or had received conditional approval for use in certain patient populations. However, the assertion that five therapies had been fully authorized and made available in all hospitals by October 20, 2021, is an overstatement. Authorization and distribution of therapeutics depend on regulatory approval, production capacity, and distribution logistics, which can vary between countries and institutions.

The post also refers to Covid-19 vaccines as merely "temporary experimental devices." This characterization is inaccurate. Covid-19 vaccines authorized for use in the EU and elsewhere underwent rigorous clinical trials, demonstrating safety and efficacy before being granted emergency use or conditional marketing authorization by regulatory agencies. These authorizations are based on substantial evidence, including data from large-scale clinical trials and ongoing monitoring of vaccine safety and effectiveness in real-world settings. While “emergency use” or “conditional approval” indicates that regulators are continuing to monitor long-term outcomes, it does not mean the vaccines are experimental in the sense implied by the post.

In conclusion, the social media post in question contains several misleading or inaccurate claims. Covid-19 vaccines remained a central part of public health strategies beyond October 2021, with mandates and recommendations determined by individual countries. The authorization and deployment of Covid-19 therapies were progressing, but the blanket statement that five therapies were available in all hospitals by that date is not supported by the facts. Finally, describing vaccines as "temporary experimental devices" misrepresents the extensive regulatory processes and scientific evidence that underpin their use. Readers are urged to consult official sources and public health authorities for accurate information about Covid-19 vaccines and treatments.
